### Finding 95 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a whitespace-only value, a real data-entry shape, was reported "placed" on the real Form of Offer/MBD1, with its own read-back verification vacuously passing, while the printed form showed nothing at all)

**Where:** non-SANRAL pack rotation this cycle (notify was being actively worked by a sibling this
exact morning - two digest-label fixes landed mid-cycle - so avoided it; `process_general_jobs.py`/
`process_pack_jobs.py`/`fingerprints/Conventional_Consultant_Tender.json` stayed avoided too, still
in-flight on open PR `#170`). `engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py` - the flat (non-fillable) PDF form
filler for municipal MBD editions and CIDB-style returnables, 1000+ lines, zero dedicated test file
anywhere in the repo before this pass (confirmed by grep: only `test_form_field_audit.py` touches
it, and only `values_for()`'s own Klipcorp-default audit - none of `fill_flat_pdf()`/
`place_text_fields()`/`place_captions()` had ever run under test).

**What was tested:** read the whole file, since it had never had a dedicated adversarial pass.
`place_text_fields()`/`place_captions()` both gate "is there a real value to place" with a bare
`if not value:`. Asked the standard question for that shape of guard: does `not value` really
exclude everything that should count as "nothing to place"? `values_for()` can produce a non-None,
non-empty string straight from a company/signatory record with no normalization
(`signatory_name_upper = (s.get("name") or "").upper() or None` - `.upper()` on an all-whitespace
string is still all-whitespace, which is truthy) - a realistic data shape (leading/trailing spaces
left over from a copy-paste into a name field) that `not value` does not catch.

**Finding (CONFIRMED, severe).** Traced the full consequence, then reproduced it end to end against
a real synthetic MBD1 page (built with reportlab, already a test-only dependency in this repo's own
CI): a whitespace-only signatory name sails past the `if not value:` guard (not `not value`:
non-empty strings are always truthy); Helvetica's own space-character width is non-zero, so `_fit()`
"fits" it fine; the overlay write types invisible blank space onto the page; and
`verify_placements()`'s own read-back check (`want in got`, after stripping ALL whitespace from
both sides for comparison) reduces `want` to the empty string for a whitespace-only value - which is
a substring of literally anything, so the write is reported `verified = True` regardless of what is
actually on the printed page. End to end, confirmed with the real pipeline (not reasoned about in
the abstract): `fill_flat_pdf()` reported `{"status": "placed", "value": "   "}` for the
`sbd1.contact_person` field (the same `signatory_name`/`signatory_name_upper` path feeds the real
Form of Offer's own signatory-name field too) - exactly the "silent wrong data" risk this module's
own docstring says it exists to prevent ("nothing is assumed to have worked"). A company whose
signatory's name is a data-entry glitch would see "placed" on the report and have no reason to
check the actual printed page, where the field is blank.

**Fix:** changed both guards from `if not value:` to `if not (value or "").strip():` - rejects a
whitespace-only value as "missing" (same reason, same wording, as a genuinely absent one) while
leaving a real value's own internal/surrounding whitespace untouched (a name like "Jane Smith", or
even "  Jane Smith  ", is still placed exactly as given - only an ALL-whitespace value is now
caught). `place_choices()` was checked too and is naturally immune (`ans not in ("yes", "no")` can
never accidentally match whitespace).

**Verified red-then-green against the real pipeline, not a stub.** New file
`engine/general/test_fill_flat_pdf.py`: builds a real, minimal synthetic MBD1 page with reportlab
(the real "INVITATION TO BID" heading, "NAME OF BIDDER"/"POSTAL ADDRESS"/"VAT REGISTRATION NUMBER"
needed for `find_form_pages()`'s own detection, a real dotted leader line after "CONTACT PERSON:"),
then runs the REAL `fill_flat_pdf()` end to end. Reverted the fix (`git apply -R`): the whitespace-
only and tab/newline-only cases both failed exactly as predicted (`status: "placed"`, the real
written-but-invisible value); the empty-string/`None`/real-name/whitespace-padded-real-name cases
(unchanged behaviour) correctly stayed green throughout, confirming the fix is precise. Restored:
`ALL PASSED`, 10/10 checks. `engine/test_form_field_audit.py` (the sibling consumer of this same
file) re-run clean, `0 failure(s)`, no regression. Wired into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml`) - reportlab
is already installed earlier in the same job for `test_general_bridge.py`'s own fixtures.

**Regression:** `engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py` (two guard conditions), new
`engine/general/test_fill_flat_pdf.py` (10 checks), `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` (one
new step). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 96 (coverage-gap closure, no bug fixed - a dangling signatory_person_id answer leaves the signatory blank rather than falling back, a real but untested behaviour, flagged as a design question not decided here)

**Where:** rotation this cycle, after PR #170 merged (unblocking `process_general_jobs.py`, no
longer in-flight). Picked the brand-new signatory-fallback logic `gather_pack_inputs()` gained in
that PR (2026-10-28, a real fix for Mzansi/RFP165's "Not on file" incident) - fresh code is always
worth a QA pass of its own, and the merge PR's own test coverage (3 cases: fallback fires, explicit
pick wins, nobody on file) left one real path untested.

**What was tested:** `gather_pack_inputs()`'s signatory logic is `if sid: ... (look up that one
person, by id+company_id) ... else: (company-wide fallback, first person with a signatory_capacity)`.
Asked the standard question: what happens when `sid` is truthy but the lookup finds nobody - a
genuinely possible data shape (a stale/dangling `tender_answers.signatory_person_id` reference)?
Checked whether migration `0044`'s own deletion-cleanup trigger (which explicitly deletes this exact
`tender_answers` row when the referenced person is deleted, specifically because there's no real FK
to cascade automatically - `signatory_person_id` is stored as generic text in a key-value table, not
an actual foreign key column) rules this out: it only fires on a person's own deletion, not on a
cross-company mismatch or any other way the reference could go stale.

**Finding (CONFIRMED behaviour, not a bug - a real, previously-untested path).** Reproduced
directly: an explicit `signatory_person_id` pointing to a person id that doesn't resolve at this
company (`client.select("people", {"id": sid, "company_id": ...})` returns empty) leaves `person =
None`, and because this is still inside the `if sid:` branch, the company-wide fallback is never
reached - `signatory` stays `None` even when a real Director IS on file at that exact company. Not
a crash, not silently wrong data (it's an honest "missing," matching this codebase's own
"never silently substitute" discipline) - but a genuinely different outcome from the sibling "nobody
has a signatory_capacity at all" case, and one the merge PR's own test suite never exercised.

**Not fixed - flagged as a design question.** Whether a dangling pick SHOULD fall back to the
company's own designated signatory, or whether staying blank (and visibly so, on the Tender
Workspace) is the safer choice precisely because the original intent was a SPECIFIC person, not
"whoever else is available," is a real product call - the same "flag, don't silently decide for
Sarel" discipline this session applies to every judgment call of this shape. Realistic trigger
likelihood is low (requires the dangling reference to arise some way other than person deletion,
which migration 0044 already cleans up), so this doesn't rise to the severity of a "fix now" finding
either way.

**What was done**: locked in the CURRENT behaviour with 2 new checks in the existing
`test_gather_pack_inputs_signatory_fallback()` (same function the merge PR's own 3 cases live in,
extended rather than duplicated) - confirms `answers` still records the dangling value as-is (not
silently dropped from the pack job's own audit trail) and that `signatory` stays `None` without
raising. Verified: `0 failure(s)`, all 6 checks in this function (3 original + 2 new + the "answers
still records it" check) pass; `test_build_general_pack.py`/`test_general_bridge.py` re-run clean,
no regression. Already wired into CI.

**Regression:** `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py` only (2 new checks inside an existing
test function, additive). No production code touched - this pass closed a test-coverage gap on a
real, previously-undocumented behaviour, not a code bug.

### Finding 97 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a corrupted/truncated SANRAL fingerprint baseline file raised a raw JSONDecodeError straight out of the real intake job, instead of the clean "error" status every OTHER failure mode in the same function already reports)

**Where:** intake rotation this cycle. `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s `check_fingerprint()` -
compares a tender's uploaded Technical Submission workbook against the stored baseline for its
SANRAL family, called from the real production intake path
(`engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `register_sanral_tender()`, with no try/except of its
own around the call) and from `opportunity_requirements.py`'s own per-tender classification.

**What was tested:** the function already has a clear, established pattern: `fingerprint.
build_fingerprint(technical_path)` is wrapped in its own try/except returning a clean `{"status":
"error", ...}`, and a missing baseline file returns `{"status": "no_baseline", ...}` honestly. Asked
whether the ONE remaining read in the same function - `json.load(open(path))`, loading the stored
baseline itself - follows the same discipline. It didn't: no guard at all.

**Finding (CONFIRMED, moderate).** Reproduced directly: a corrupted/truncated baseline JSON file
(the exact kind of file PR #170's own fingerprint-regeneration work just replaced one of, and the
kind a bad merge or an interrupted write could produce) makes `check_fingerprint()` raise a raw
`json.JSONDecodeError` instead of returning a status dict. Traced the real production consequence:
`process_general_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` DOES have its own top-level `except Exception` around
the whole job (confirmed by reading it), so this doesn't crash the worker or hang anything - but it
turns a specific, already-anticipated failure mode into a confusing raw-exception message on that
one job, instead of the clear, actionable "could not read the stored baseline" text every sibling
failure mode in this exact function already produces. The same asymmetric-guard shape (one branch
of a function handles a failure cleanly, a sibling branch doesn't) already found and fixed
independently in three other files this session (Findings 82/83/84).

**Fix:** wrapped `json.load(open(path))` in the identical try/except pattern already used two lines
above it for `build_fingerprint()`, returning `{"status": "error", "detail": f"could not read the
stored '{family}' baseline: {e}"...}`.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test
`test_check_fingerprint_no_baseline_match_mismatch_and_corrupted_baseline` - the first dedicated
test for `check_fingerprint()` at all - covers all four real outcomes: no baseline yet, a genuine
match (the real workbook's own freshly-written fingerprint), a genuine mismatch (a tampered copy),
and the corrupted-file case. Reverted the fix (`git apply -R`): only the corrupted-file case failed,
raising the exact predicted `JSONDecodeError`; the other three stayed green, confirming the test is
precise. Restored: `0 failure(s)`. `engine/test_fingerprint.py`/`engine/general/
test_general_bridge.py` re-run clean, no regression. Already wired into CI.

**Regression:** `engine/intake/classify_tender.py` (one new try/except), `engine/intake/
test_classify_tender.py` (1 new test function, 5 checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 98 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor - a readiness-change whose field_provenance row's tender_pack went missing was dropped from the seen store with zero trace, unlike the identical shape of problem elsewhere in the same codebase)

**Where:** compliance/reminders rotation this cycle (Finding 91, the disabled "Compliance deadline
reminder check-in" trigger, is still open and unchanged since the pass that found it - `list_triggers`
confirmed `enabled: false`, `updated_at: 2026-10-27T20:30:13Z`, same as before; re-decided nothing,
that stays Sarel's call). Looked past that already-reported gap for something new in the same area
and found this in `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`'s `find_readiness_changes()`/
`save_readiness_seen_db()` - the field_provenance "readiness changed" pipeline `main()`'s live mode
runs for real every day.

**What was tested:** `find_readiness_changes()` reads `field_provenance` rows, then separately reads
the `tender_packs` those rows point to, and fills an `owners` dict mapping each `prov::<id>` seen-key
to that pack's `company_id`. `field_provenance.tender_pack_id` is `not null` and `references
tender_packs(id) on delete cascade` (0002/0001), so in normal operation this always resolves - the
one way it doesn't is the narrow window between those two separate Supabase reads: a tender_pack
deleted in between leaves `owners[key]` as `None`. Reproduced directly (no race needed to prove the
code path - the end state is the same either way): a `field_provenance` row whose `tender_pack_id`
doesn't resolve to any row in `tender_packs`. `find_readiness_changes()` still returns the item (with
`company_id: None`, which every per-company `own()` filter downstream then drops - correctly, since
there's no company to send it to). But `save_readiness_seen_db()` had `... and owners.get(k)` as a
silent filter in its list comprehension - the row is skipped with **no print, no alert, nothing**.
Compare `watch_deadlines.save_seen_db()` (the sibling seen-store writer, same shared mechanism this
whole area is built on): it prints `"  (seen key {k!r} has no company - not stored)"` for the exact
same shape of problem. The asymmetry is the bug - not a crash, but a seen-store write that quietly
writes one row fewer than the run found changes for, with no way for whoever reads the run's own
output to know why.

**Fix:** `save_readiness_seen_db()` now prints the same `"(seen key {k!r} has no company - not
stored)"` message `save_seen_db()` already uses, in the same place in the loop, before skipping the
row - behavior is unchanged (the row still isn't written, correctly), only visibility changed.

**Verified red-then-green:** added `test_orphaned_field_provenance_owner_not_silently_dropped()` to
`engine/notify/test_digest_live.py`, calling `find_readiness_changes()`/`save_readiness_seen_db()`
directly against an orphaned row (4 checks: the change still surfaces with `company_id: None`, its
owner is recorded as unknown not guessed, the row is genuinely not written, and the skip is now in
the run's own stdout). `python3 test_digest_live.py`: `0 failure(s)`. Revert-and-confirm-red: `git
diff engine/notify/daily_digest.py > /tmp/finding98.patch`, `git apply -R`, re-ran - exactly the
visibility check failed (`''` instead of the message), the other 3 new checks stayed green; restored,
re-ran clean. Already wired into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml:164`). Regression-checked
`engine/notify/test_digest_opt_in.py`, `test_send_digest_emails.py`, `test_record_heartbeat.py`,
`test_send_pack_ready_email.py`, and every `engine/compliance/test_*.py` file - all still pass.

**Regression:** `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (one function's internal loop restructured, no
behavior change besides the new print), `engine/notify/test_digest_live.py` (1 new test function, 4
checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 99 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a malformed timestamp on ANY ONE stuck job crashed every bridge's own stale-job-recovery sweep, blocking every OTHER genuinely stuck job's recovery AND every brand-new pending job in that queue, repeatedly, until a human fixed the one bad row by hand)

**Where:** worker/job-queue rotation this cycle. `fail_stale_jobs()`/`fail_stale_uploads()` - the
"a worker died mid-job, don't leave the row stuck in 'generating'/'extracting'/'classifying' forever"
safety net every one of the six queue-consuming bridges has its own copy of:
`engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`, `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`,
`engine/narrative/process_narrative_jobs.py`, `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`,
`engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`, `engine/onboarding/process_onboarding_jobs.py`.

**What was tested:** every one of the six functions above parses a stuck row's own
`started_at`/`claimed_at`/`extraction_claimed_at`/`classification_claimed_at` with a bare
`datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(...)` call - no try/except anywhere. Reproduced directly (a
`FakeClient`/`FakeDB` row with `started_at: "not-a-real-timestamp"` alongside a genuinely, separately
stale row for a different company): the malformed row's `ValueError` raised straight out of the
function, and since `fail_stale_jobs()`/`fail_stale_uploads()` is each bridge's own **first** call in
its job-processing entrypoint (`process_pending()` for pack/general, `poll_once()` for
cv/cv_extract/onboarding, the main loop body for narrative), the exception aborted everything after
it in that pass too - not just the other genuinely stuck job (confirmed never recovered), but every
brand-new, perfectly healthy pending job in that SAME queue, for every company, every cycle, until a
human manually fixed the one corrupted DB row. In `--loop` mode (`run_bridges.py`/`poll_forever`) this
surfaces as a `critical` system alert for a non-zero exit (not silent), but the underlying queue stays
completely stalled regardless - exactly the "one malformed item aborts the whole run for everyone, not
just the one with bad data" bug class `watch_deadlines.days_until()` was fixed for (QA pass,
2026-10-23), found here independently, repo-wide, across every queue consumer in the codebase.
Realistic cause: a hand-edited row (a hotfix, a bad migration backfill, a manual DB correction) - these
timestamp columns are always system-written via `_now_iso()` at claim time, so this never occurs
without outside interference, but when it does the blast radius is the entire queue, not one row.

**Fix:** each function now wraps its own `fromisoformat()` parse/compare in a `try/except ValueError`,
recording a `"warning"` system alert naming the bad value and skipping just that one row - matching
`watch_deadlines.days_until()`'s own established pattern exactly (warning severity, not error; alert,
never a guess; the sweep continues for every other row).

**Verified red-then-green, per file:** for each of the six, built/extended a test with a genuinely
stale row (must still be recovered), a fresh row (must stay untouched), and a malformed-timestamp row
(must not crash, must get its own warning alert, must stay as-is) -
`engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (**new file - `process_pack_jobs.py` had no test touching its
job-queue logic at all before this pass**), `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py` (extended),
`engine/narrative/test_process_narrative_jobs.py` (extended), `engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py`
(extended), `engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` (extended), `engine/onboarding/
test_process_onboarding_jobs.py` (extended). For each file: reverted that file's own production fix
(`git apply -R`), re-ran - exactly the malformed-timestamp case failed (the real `ValueError` traceback,
confirming the exact predicted crash), every other check in that file stayed green; restored, re-ran -
clean again. Wired `test_process_pack_jobs.py` into CI (new step, `bridge-worker-ci.yml`, right after
the existing `test_sync_functions.py` step) - validated the YAML with `python3 -c "import yaml;
yaml.safe_load(...)"` before committing (Finding 92/95's own lesson). The other five test files were
already wired in. Regression-checked every other `engine/pack/test_*.py`,
`engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py`, and every file in this write-up's own "Verified" list above - all
still pass.

**Regression:** six production files (one `try/except` added per `fail_stale_jobs`/
`fail_stale_uploads`, no other behavior change), five existing test files extended (1 new row + updated
checks each), one new test file (`engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py`, first ever for this bridge's
job-queue logic), one CI workflow file (one new step). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 100 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a corrupted SANRAL fingerprint baseline raised a raw JSONDecodeError out of the real pack build's own STEP 1, and that raw exception was misclassified as a worker crash instead of the clean, actionable refusal process_pack_jobs.py's own handler already distinguishes)

**Where:** SANRAL pack rotation this cycle. `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`'s `check_template()` -
`build_submission_pack()`'s own first step, called before anything else, for every company's real
pack build.

**What was tested:** `check_template()` reads the stored fingerprint baseline for the workbook's
template family and diffs it against the current workbook (`fingerprint.diff()`), raising a clean
`ValueError` on a genuine mismatch ("SANRAL may have changed the template..."). The baseline file read
itself (`json.load(open(store_path))`) had no try/except. Reproduced directly against a real sample
workbook (`templates/samples/R.334-030-2025.1F_ran.xlsm`): a corrupted baseline file (the exact shape
a bad merge or an interrupted fingerprint regeneration - PR #170's own regeneration script - would
produce) raised a raw `JSONDecodeError` straight out of `check_template()`. Checked
`process_pack_jobs.py`'s own exception handling around `build_submission_pack()`
(`process_job()`, ~line 703): it explicitly distinguishes a `ValueError` ("the confirm gate / a filler
refusing on purpose... recorded as a warning") from any other exception ("anything else is a crash" -
`error` severity). A raw `JSONDecodeError` is itself a `ValueError` subclass in Python, so it wasn't
rejected outright - but its message is the bare internal parser detail
("Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes..."), nothing like this function's own other,
deliberately actionable refusal messages, and nowhere near as diagnosable for whoever reads the failed
job. **Independent, second occurrence of Finding 97's exact bug class** (`engine/intake/
classify_tender.py`'s `check_fingerprint()`) - same unguarded `json.load(open(path))` next to an
already-careful sibling, this time in the pack-assembly path itself rather than the intake pre-check,
so the practical blast radius is larger: it blocks the real pack BUILD, company-wide, for the affected
template family, not just an advisory intake classification.

**Fix:** wrapped the baseline read in `try/except`, raising the same clean, actionable `ValueError`
shape `check_template()`'s own other two guards already use (names the family, says what to do -
"Re-run engine/fingerprint.py to regenerate the baseline").

**Verified red-then-green:** new file `engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` (`check_template()` had no
dedicated test at all before this pass) - no-baseline/match/mismatch/corrupted-baseline against the
real sample workbook, plus a control case for the "unfillable family" guard. Revert-and-confirm-red:
reverting the fix made exactly the 2 checks that assert the fix's own clean wording fail (with the raw
parser detail in their place), the other 4 stayed green - note `json.JSONDecodeError` being itself a
`ValueError` subclass means an `isinstance` check alone can't distinguish fixed from unfixed here; the
real signal, and what the test asserts, is the message content. Restored, `0 failure(s)`. Wired the
new test file into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml`, next to `test_process_pack_jobs.py`) - validated the
YAML with `yaml.safe_load` before committing. Regression-checked every other `engine/pack/test_*.py`
file, `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py`, `engine/test_fingerprint.py`, and
`engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` - all still pass.

**Regression:** `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` (one `try/except` added, no other behavior change),
new file `engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` (first dedicated test for `check_template()` ever), one
CI workflow file (one new step). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 101 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a whitespace-only value was written as invisible spaces into a real non-SANRAL SBD form and logged "confirmed", the third independent occurrence of Finding 95's exact bug class)

**Where:** non-SANRAL pack rotation this cycle. `engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py`'s
`fill_sbd_document()` - the real SBD 1/4/6.1/8/9 field-filling logic used on every non-SANRAL general
tender submission - and its five low-level writer functions (`fill_cells`, `fill_phone_cells`,
`fill_blank_paragraphs`, `fill_line_above_caption`, `fill_dotted_paragraph_count`).

**What was tested:** every one of those five writer functions writes whatever `value` it's given
straight into the document with no guard of its own; `fill_sbd_document()`'s own ~15 call sites each
gate the call with a bare `if val else 0` / `if val:` style truthiness check, and `_log_fill()`
(the function EVERY one of those call sites funnels through to decide "confirmed" vs "missing")
checks `if value and n:`. A value that is non-empty but entirely whitespace - the same realistic
data-entry shape Finding 95 found in `fill_flat_pdf.py`'s `place_text_fields()`/`place_captions()`
(a copy-paste glitch into a company field) - is truthy by Python's own rules, so none of these guards
catch it. Reproduced directly with the real pipeline, no stub: `fill_sbd_document()` against a
synthetic docx with a bidder table ("NAME OF BIDDER" / blank cell) and a dotted "POSTAL ADDRESS:
........" paragraph, `legal_name`/`postal_address` both set to `"   "` - the bidder cell was written
with literal spaces (no longer blank, but nothing legible either), the dotted paragraph's own dots
were overwritten with invisible spaces too, and `log.entries` showed `{"status": "confirmed", "value":
"   "}` for both fields - the exact same "silent wrong data" shape as Finding 95, now independently
confirmed in this file's own, separate writer functions (not shared code with `fill_flat_pdf.py` at
all - a genuinely independent occurrence of the bug class, the third this session: Finding 95
`fill_flat_pdf.py`, this one `fill_sbd_docx.py`).

**Fix:** added a shared `_has_value(v)` helper (`bool(str(v or "").strip())`) and a guard at the top
of each of the five writer functions (`if not _has_value(value): return 0`) - the lowest common point
that covers every one of `fill_sbd_document()`'s ~15 call sites at once, rather than patching each
call site individually. Also made `_log_fill()`'s own classification whitespace-aware
(`_has_value(value)` in place of the bare `value` checks) as defense in depth, which turned out to
have a second, welcome effect: with the writer now returning 0 for a whitespace-only value, a
whitespace-only field now falls all the way through to `_log_fill()`'s own generic "No value on
file." message (the same message a genuinely absent value gets) instead of the misleading "Label not
found in this buyer's edition" a bare `n == 0` would otherwise have produced.

**Verified red-then-green against the real pipeline.** Extended `engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py`
with `test_whitespace_only_value_is_never_placed_or_confirmed` (10 new checks): plain-spaces and
tab/newline-only values against both writer shapes (the bidder table cell and the dotted paragraph)
- both must stay untouched and both must log "missing", not "confirmed" - plus a control case
proving a real value (even one with incidental surrounding whitespace, e.g. `"  Mzansi Roads & Civils
(Pty) Ltd  "`) is still placed exactly as given and logged confirmed, so the fix doesn't over-correct.
Revert-and-confirm-red: reverting made exactly the 8 new checks tied to the two whitespace-only cases
fail (the real written-but-invisible text and the wrongly-"confirmed" log entries both showed up
exactly as predicted), the real-value control case stayed green throughout. Restored, `0 failure(s)`.
Already wired into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml:255`) - no new CI step needed. Regression-checked
`engine/test_form_field_audit.py` (`0 failure(s)`) and `engine/general/general_harness.py --no-pack`
(`84 clean, 7 flagged, 0 failed` - confirmed by running the SAME harness against the unmodified
baseline that the 7 flagged `*_eskom_e3689: changed ['roles']` entries are pre-existing drift,
unrelated to this fix, not a regression it introduced).

**Regression:** `engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py` (one new helper + five one-line guards + one
classification fix, no other behavior change), `engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` (1 new test
function, 10 checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 102 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a corrupted/unopenable image upload broke OCR silently as far as system_alerts was concerned, unlike every OTHER OCR-infrastructure failure in the same module)

**Where:** CV rotation this cycle (`generate_cv.py` was already re-checked clean by a sibling pass
earlier today; picked `engine/ocr/scan_ocr.py` instead - the shared OCR module `extract_cv_fields.py`'s
own `read_cv_text()` calls for image uploads with no text layer, genuinely untouched: confirmed by
grep that no dedicated test file for this module existed anywhere in the repo before this pass).

**What was tested:** `ocr_image_file()`'s own `Image.open(path)` call is wrapped in try/except - when
it fails (a corrupted upload, a file renamed to an image extension that isn't really one, a Pillow
incompatibility), the function sets `res["error"]` to a clear reason and returns early. Checked
whether this reaches `_alert_failures()` - the one place every OTHER OCR-infrastructure break in this
module (Tesseract missing/unstartable, a PDF page `pdftoppm` couldn't render, a page OCR errored or
timed out) is reported to `system_alerts`, per the module's own docstring ("Broke = Tesseract missing
or unstartable... or a page that couldn't be rendered... One alert per document, never raises"). It
didn't - the early `return res` happens before the function's own closing `_alert_failures(res, path)`
call.

**Finding (CONFIRMED).** Reproduced directly (`available()` monkeypatched to force the Tesseract-
present branch, isolating the exact failure under test): a corrupted PNG upload returned the correct
`res["error"]` ("the image could not be opened (UnidentifiedImageError)") but recorded **zero**
`system_alerts` entries - confirmed by sink. The PDF path's exact analogue ("the page could not be
rendered to an image for OCR") IS already matched by `_alert_failures()`'s own string check, so this
is a genuine asymmetry between the two input types, not a design choice. The user-facing outcome was
never wrong - `extract_cv_fields.read_cv_text()` already checks `if not res["read"]:` and raises a
clean `ExtractionFailed` either way - only the operator-visible alert was missing, so a real, repeated
instance of this (a library incompatibility, a corrupted-upload bug affecting many uploads) would have
been invisible to Sarel while every sibling OCR failure mode was reported. Scoped moderate, not severe:
no data-correctness or crash risk, purely an observability gap.

**Fix:** added the missing `_alert_failures(res, path)` call in that one early-return branch, matching
every other failure path in the same two functions (`ocr_image_file`/`ocr_pdf_pages`).

**Verified red-then-green.** New file `engine/ocr/test_scan_ocr.py` (first dedicated test for this

control and the non-alert checks stayed green. Restored, `0 failure(s)`. Wired into CI
(`bridge-worker-ci.yml`, right after the existing CV AI-extraction step that already installs

`engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` and `engine/onboarding/test_classify_documents.py` (both
indirect consumers of this module) - both still `ALL PASSED`.

file `engine/ocr/test_scan_ocr.py` (first dedicated test for this module ever, 8 checks), one CI

### Finding 103 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a SANRAL closing date typed as literal text instead of a numeric Excel serial was silently dropped during intake AND falsely refused during key-position suggestion, while the real pack build read it fine - two independently-written copies of the same helper function had drifted apart)

**Where:** intake rotation this cycle. `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py`'s `_excel_date()` -
imported and reused as-is by `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s `read_setup()` - versus
`engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`'s own, separately written `_excel_date()`.

**What was tested:** `Workbook.cached()` (`engine/sanral_fill.py`) reads a cell's raw XML value
directly - a genuine Excel date is stored as a plain numeric serial (date FORMATTING is only a
display style, never part of the cell's own `<v>` value), but a cell someone typed as literal text
(an apostrophe-prefixed `'2026-05-01` to stop Excel's own autoformat, a paste-as-values from a
different locale) comes back as a plain string instead - a real, if uncommon, way SETUP!C3 can
legitimately hold a perfectly valid date. Compared `suggest_pack._excel_date(serial)` (`return
datetime.date(1899, 12, 30) + datetime.timedelta(days=int(serial))` - only ever tries `int()`)
against `assemble_pack._excel_date(v)` (checks `isinstance(v, (int, float))` first, falls back to
`datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(v)[:10])` for anything else) - two independently written copies of
conceptually the same "decode SETUP!C3" logic that had quietly drifted apart.

**Finding (CONFIRMED), reproduced end to end against a real sample workbook, not reasoned about in
the abstract:** took a copy of `templates/samples/R.334-030-2025.1F_ran.xlsm`, used `Workbook.
set_value()` to rewrite its own SETUP!C3 cell to the literal text `"2026-05-01"` (confirmed the real
fixture's own C3 was a plain numeric serial beforehand), saved it, and ran the real pipeline against
it: `classify_tender.read_setup()` returned `closing_date: None` - silently treating a perfectly
valid date as unreadable, so intake never shows the user the workbook's own closing date and
`discrepancies()` never checks it against what they typed (the `if setup.get("closing_date") and
...` guard short-circuits on `None`); `suggest_pack.suggest()` raised `ValueError: ...SETUP!C3
(closing date) is '2026-05-01', not a readable Excel date` - a **false alarm** blocking key-position
candidate suggestions entirely for a perfectly fine tender; `assemble_pack.check_template()`'s own
caller (the real pack BUILD) read the exact same cell correctly and proceeded normally. The same
tender's same cell: silently wrong in one place, falsely blocked in another, correct in a third.

**Fix:** widened `suggest_pack._excel_date()` to try `datetime.date.fromisoformat()` on anything
that isn't already numeric, matching `assemble_pack._excel_date()`'s own breadth - while preserving
its existing raise-on-genuinely-bad-input contract (both of its callers already catch and handle
that correctly; widening what counts as *successfully parseable* needed no change to either
caller). Also added `not isinstance(serial, bool)` to both functions: `bool` is a subclass of `int`
in Python, so a stray `True`/`False` in this cell (a checkbox mistakenly placed there) would
otherwise have silently become the bogus date `1899-12-31` in both functions rather than being
rejected as the obviously-wrong type it is - confirmed this was ALSO a (separate, smaller) latent
bug in `assemble_pack._excel_date()`, fixed there too for consistency between the two functions,
not just the one this pass started from.

**Verified red-then-green, against both consumers, with the real pipeline where it mattered.**
`engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py`: `_excel_date()` directly (numeric unchanged;
text-typed and whitespace-padded text-typed now parsed; `None`/`""`/garbage/`True`/`False` still
raise) plus an integration check that `suggest()` no longer falsely refuses a text-typed closing
date and the real date reaches `pack_suggestions.json` (9 new checks). `engine/intake/
test_classify_tender.py`: a real copy of the fixture workbook with its own SETUP!C3 rewritten to
text, confirming `read_setup()` now reads it instead of silently returning `None` (2 new checks,
including a sanity check that the unmodified fixture's own C3 really is numeric first). Revert-and-
confirm-red: reverting reproduced the exact predicted failures in both files (a raw `ValueError`
traceback in `suggest_pack`'s own direct `_excel_date()` check; `closing_date: None` in
`classify_tender`'s), every other check stayed green. Restored, both `0 failure(s)`. Already wired
into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml` already runs both test files - no new step needed). Regression-
checked `engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py`, `test_process_pack_jobs.py`, `test_sync_functions.py`,
and `engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py` (`_excel_date()` widened, same
raise-on-bad-input contract), `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` (one added `isinstance` guard, no
other behavior change), `engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py` (1 new test function, 9
checks), `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` (1 new test function, 2 checks). No schema or
other call-site changes.

### Finding 104 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a failure on ANY ONE discovered release aborted requirement-classification for every OTHER release still queued in the same run, with zero system_alerts visibility either way)

**Where:** discovery rotation this cycle (avoided `notify` - a sibling pass was actively working it
this exact run, two commits in a row on the same bug class; avoided `engine/discovery/
score_outlook.py` specifically - open PR `#172` touches it). `engine/discovery/
opportunity_requirements.py`'s `classify_all()` - the "classify every discovered-but-not-yet-pursued
release's documents" sweep (`classify_release()` run once per release, a Supabase `select`/`upsert`
each, plus the real `classify_tender.classify_documents()`/`check_fingerprint()` pass per release).

**What was tested:** the per-release loop had no try/except of any kind, and the whole file had
**zero `system_alerts` integration** - confirmed by grep, unlike every other `engine/` script.
Reproduced directly with a fake client whose `select()` raises for the middle of three queued
releases (simulating a transient Supabase network blip, the same realistic cause every other
instance of this bug class in this codebase has had): the exception raised straight out of
`classify_all()`, and the third, perfectly fine release was never even attempted - confirmed by a
second check that the crash happens precisely at that call site, with every prior release's own
check still green. Same bug class this codebase has fixed independently several times this session
(`watch_deadlines.days_until()`, every bridge's own `fail_stale_jobs()`/`fail_stale_uploads()` -
Finding 99) - a single bad or transiently-unreachable item must never cost every OTHER item its own
chance to run, in the same batch.

**Fix:** wrapped the per-release call in `try/except Exception`, recording a new `"discovery"`-
sourced `system_alerts` entry naming the real `release_key` and incrementing a new `summary["errors"]`
counter, then `continue`-ing to the next release rather than letting the exception propagate. Added
the missing `import system_alerts` (and its `sys.path` entry) to this file for the first time.

**Verified red-then-green, against the real pipeline (the existing test file's own `Fake`
PostgREST+Storage server, real committed sample workbooks).** Extended `engine/discovery/
test_opportunity_requirements.py` with case 8: seeds a `"crash-release"` release (sorts
alphabetically before the already-seeded `"sanral-full-release"`), monkeypatches
`classify_release()` to raise specifically for it, and confirms `classify_all()` still (a) counts it
as an error rather than crashing, (b) still classifies the already-seeded release that sorts AFTER
it in the same run, and (c) records exactly one `system_alerts` entry naming the real release key (3
new checks, on top of the file's existing 7 scenarios). Revert-and-confirm-red (the loop body only,
keeping the new import so the test file itself still loads): reverting reproduced the exact
predicted crash, at the exact call site, with every prior check in the file having already passed
green. Restored, `All checks passed.`. Already wired into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml:367` already
runs this test file). Regression-checked `engine/discovery/test_download_discovered_documents.py`
and `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` (both touch the same shared helpers/fixtures) - both pass.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/opportunity_requirements.py` (one `try/except` added around the
per-release loop body, one new import, no other behavior change), `engine/discovery/
test_opportunity_requirements.py` (1 new scenario, 3 checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 105 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a real, correctly-detected pricing model was silently discarded and replaced with a generic label whenever a numbered deliverables list was also present - the ordinary, common real-world shape this exact feature exists to classify well; plus two brand-new test files from the same merge were missing from CI)

**Where:** non-SANRAL pack rotation this cycle, picked up opportunistically while orienting from the
freshly-merged PR #172 ("Document Vault fixes, Bids pipeline overhaul, **Manifest v2 engine**,
Dashboard widgets") - `engine/general/requirements.py`'s brand-new `extract_pricing_schedule()`
(`MANIFEST_VERSION` 1 -> 2 in that same merge), never reviewed by this standing QA process before
this pass.

**What was tested:** the function's own header comment explicitly promises `type` "reuses
`tender_enrichment.py`'s existing `extract_pricing_model()` ... never a second, independently-
computed pricing-model classification." The actual code did the opposite: `"type": "fixed_deliverables"
if deliverables else model` - whenever a numbered deliverables list was found (`deliverables`
non-empty), `type` was hardcoded to the generic string `"fixed_deliverables"`, **unconditionally
discarding** whatever real pricing model `extract_pricing_model()` had already correctly detected
from the document's own text. The two tests already committed in the same merge
(`test_fixed_deliverables_extracted_with_vat`, `test_lump_sum_without_a_deliverables_list_reuses_the_
existing_classifier`) each covered exactly one signal in isolation - neither one's fixture text
combined both, so this never surfaced.

**Finding (CONFIRMED), reproduced directly:** fed `extract_pricing_schedule()` a realistic combined
text - "This is a lump sum contract... SCHEDULE OF PRICES / Pricing Schedule / 1. Site establishment
and mobilisation / 2. Design development phase / ..." (a tender stating its pricing basis AND
listing a numbered schedule under it, which is the *ordinary*, expected real shape for this exact
field, not a rare edge case) - and confirmed `extract_pricing_model()` alone correctly says
`"lump_sum"`, while `extract_pricing_schedule()`'s own `type` came back `"fixed_deliverables"`
instead - a generic label not even in `extract_pricing_model()`'s own documented enum
(`lump_sum`/`schedule_of_rates`/`boq_based`/`cost_reimbursable`/`remeasurement`/`time_based`),
silently losing a real, commercially-meaningful fact (the contract's actual pricing basis) that was
already correctly read.

**Fix:** `"type": model or ("fixed_deliverables" if deliverables else None)"` - the real model now
wins whenever one was detected (matching the function's own documented promise); `"fixed_deliverables"`
is used only as a weaker fallback label when no real model keyword was present at all, exactly
preserving both pre-existing tests' own expectations.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_a_stated_pricing_model_together_with_a_deliverables_list_
keeps_the_real_model` to `engine/general/test_requirements_manifest_v2.py` (3 new checks: the
deliverables list is still found, `type` is the real `lump_sum` not the generic label, VAT is still
read correctly alongside it). Revert-and-confirm-red: reverting made exactly the one `type`-assertion
check fail (`'type': 'fixed_deliverables'` instead of `'lump_sum'`), every other check in the file -
including both pre-existing pricing-schedule tests - stayed green. Restored, `0 failure(s)`.
Regression-checked `engine/general/general_harness.py --no-pack` against the real eTenders corpus
(`84 clean, 7 flagged, 0 failed` - the same pre-existing, unrelated `*_eskom_e3689: changed
['roles']` drift already confirmed in Finding 101's own regression check, not a new issue this fix
introduced).

**Also found, while confirming CI wiring for the above (same "CI-wiring-gap" bug class as Findings
87/88/89/92):** PR #172's own merge added TWO new test files - `engine/general/
test_requirements_manifest_v2.py` (this finding's own test home) and `engine/discovery/
test_score_outlook_functionality.py` (the sibling structured-functionality-breakdown feature added
in the same merge) - **neither was wired into `bridge-worker-ci.yml`**, so both would have silently
never run in CI despite passing locally (confirmed: both run clean standalone). Added both as new
CI steps, next to their natural siblings (`test_requirements.py`, `test_score_outlook.py`) -
validated the YAML with `yaml.safe_load` before committing (Finding 92/95's own lesson).

**Regression:** `engine/general/requirements.py` (one `type` expression changed, no other behavior
change), `engine/general/test_requirements_manifest_v2.py` (1 new test function, 3 checks), one CI
workflow file (two new steps, for the two test files this same upstream merge had already added but
never wired in).

### Finding 106 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a transient failure marking ONE system alert as reported crashed the alerting system's own report, silently hiding every OTHER alert - including a critical one in the real repro - from the exact Claude-scheduled check-in that emails Sarel)

**Where:** worker/job-queue rotation this cycle. `engine/alerts/check_system_alerts.py`'s `check()` -
the consumer side of this app's one real failure-notification mechanism (`system_alerts.record()`
is the write side), run by the "System alerts check-in" Claude-scheduled trigger that reads this
script's own `--out` JSON to compose Sarel's alert email.

**What was tested:** `check()`'s `mark_reported()` loop (marking every newly-surfaced alert as
reported, so it isn't re-reported next run) had no try/except at all. Asked the now-familiar
question for this exact shape (already found and fixed independently several times this session:
`watch_deadlines.days_until()`, Finding 99's six `fail_stale_jobs()`/`fail_stale_uploads()`
bridges, Finding 104's `opportunity_requirements.classify_all()`) - what happens to the OTHER,
unrelated alerts in the same batch if marking ONE of them as reported fails (a transient Supabase
PATCH blip, or the alert row got resolved/deleted between `open_alerts()`'s read and this write)?

**Finding (CONFIRMED, severe).** Reproduced directly with a minimal client (three alerts - one
`critical`, one `error`, one `warning` - all genuinely new): a simulated transient failure marking
just the middle (`error`) alert as reported raised straight out of `check()`. `main()`'s own
try/except catches that, prints an error, and returns exit code 1 - **with no `--out` file written
at all**. The Claude-scheduled trigger that emails Sarel from this exact file gets NOTHING that
run: not the failing alert, and not the `critical` one either, even though it was already correctly
identified as new before the failure. The one system that exists specifically to catch "something
went wrong" going completely blind, in exactly the scenario ("something going wrong") it exists
for, is the highest-stakes occurrence of this bug class found this session - scored severe, not
moderate, on that basis (CI/UX impact alone would be moderate; the ops-blindness consequence here
is severe).

**Fix:** wrapped each `mark_reported()` call in its own `try/except`, logging (not re-raising) a
warning naming the alert and the real exception when one PATCH fails, then continuing to mark and
report every other alert in the batch. An alert whose own mark fails simply stays eligible to be
reported again next run (its `reported_at` stays unset) - never lost, and no worse than the
pre-existing "flaky write, retried next cycle" tolerance every other fixed instance of this bug
class in this codebase already has.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_check_survives_a_failed_mark_reported` to `engine/alerts/
test_system_alerts.py` (a minimal direct client, not the file's own `FakeSupabase` HTTP stand-in,
since this needs to fail one specific PATCH which that fake has no hook for): 3 new checks - `check()`
still returns all three alerts including the one whose own mark failed; `open_unresolved_total` is
unaffected; the two alerts whose PATCH succeeded were genuinely marked, the failing one wasn't.
Revert-and-confirm-red: reverting reproduced the exact predicted crash (a raw `RuntimeError`
traceback at the exact `mark_reported()` call site), with every one of this test file's own
pre-existing Part 1 checks (fingerprinting, the real CV/general bridge subprocess runs, run_bridges.py's
own critical-alert path, the full reported/still_occurring/resolved lifecycle) having already passed
green first. Restored, `0 failure(s)`. Already wired into CI (`bridge-worker-ci.yml:243`).
Regression-checked `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py`, `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py`,
`engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py`, and `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/alerts/check_system_alerts.py` (one `try/except` added around the per-alert
mark_reported call, no other behavior change), `engine/alerts/test_system_alerts.py` (1 new test
function, 3 checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 107 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate-severe - a person with "projects": null on file crashed candidate scoring for EVERY position on the tender, not just that one person's suggestion)

**Where:** CV rotation this cycle. `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py`'s `candidate_person_text()`,
called by `score_candidate()` inside `rank_candidates()` (once per position, over every person in
the profile) - the CLI path `suggest()` reads straight from a company's own `profile.json` file with
no per-person try/except around any of it.

**What was tested:** `generate_cv.py` already has an explicit, commented fix for this exact field
("a row with an explicit `"projects": null`... sails through and crashes `sorted()` below" -
`person.get("projects") or []`, in both `build_sanral_keyperson()` and `build_world_bank()`).
Checked whether `suggest_pack.py`'s own, separately-written `candidate_person_text()` - which reads
the identical `profile.json` shape - had the same guard. It didn't: line 130 was still
`person.get("projects", [])`, which only substitutes `[]` when the key is **absent**, not when it's
present with `None` - and oddly, the function's own comment already claimed this was "found... 2026-10-18"
and fixed, describing the exact bug, while the code itself never carried the fix through.

**Finding (CONFIRMED).** Reproduced directly: `candidate_person_text({"name": "X", "projects": None,
"qualifications": {}})` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. Confirmed the full
blast radius with `rank_candidates()`: a two-person `people` dict where only ONE person has
`"projects": None` and the other has a normal projects list - the call crashes for **both**
candidates, not just the person with no projects on file. Since `suggest()` calls `rank_candidates()`
once per required position with no try/except at all, one person entered with just a name (a
signatory-only director - a real, plausible profile shape, not a contrived one) would abort
`pack_suggestions.json` generation for the **entire tender**, for every position, not just fail to
suggest that one person. Same "one bad item aborts the whole batch" bug class that's been the
dominant theme this session (`watch_deadlines.days_until()`, Finding 99's six bridges' stale-job
sweeps, Finding 104's `opportunity_requirements.classify_all()`, Finding 106's `check_system_alerts.check()`)
and the same "one sibling function guards, the twin doesn't" shape as Findings 97/100/101/103 -
this time the twin that was missing the guard is `suggest_pack.py`'s own separate copy of logic
`generate_cv.py` had already fixed for the identical field.

**Fix:** `person.get("projects") or []` - identical one-line change to the pattern `generate_cv.py`
already uses in both its builders, degrading an explicit `null` the same as an absent key, never
crashing on it.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_a_person_with_projects_explicitly_null_does_not_crash_scoring_for_everyone_else`
to `engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py`: a two-candidate `rank_candidates()` call (one
signatory-only person with `"projects": None`, one real candidate) - both are still scored (the
null-projects person correctly scores 0 rather than being silently dropped or crashing the call).
Revert-and-confirm-red: reverting the fix reproduced the exact predicted `TypeError` on only the
new check, with every other pre-existing check in the file (tie-break ordering, the blank-SETUP!C3
guard, the text-typed-Excel-date parsing) still green. Restored, `0 failure(s)`.
Regression-checked `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (the SANRAL pack bridge's own separate
`rank_candidates()`/`score_candidate()` copy, which already had this guard via its own `adapt_person()`
always building `"projects"` as a list - untouched, still green), `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py`,
and `engine/cv/test_process_cv_jobs.py` - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py` (one line, `candidate_person_text()`'s
`projects` read), `engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py` (1 new test function, 2 checks). No
schema or other call-site changes - `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s live Supabase-backed path
was never exposed to this bug (its own `adapt_person()` always builds a list), so this only affects
the `suggest_pack.py --profile` CLI path reading a hand-maintained `profile.json` directly.

### Finding 108 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a company's own disciplines, written as a bare string instead of a list in a hand-maintained profile.json, were silently shredded into individual characters and never matched any real tender again)

**Where:** discovery rotation this cycle. `engine/discovery/assess_tender.py`'s `load_company_profile()`
- the one function every CLI/manual-profile caller (`engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s `--profile`
path, this module's own CLI) uses to turn a hand-maintained `profile.json` into the dict
`assess_fit()`/`estimate_score_outlook()` score against.

**What was tested:** `"disciplines": company.get("disciplines", [])` had no type check at all. This
function's own docstring says these files are hand-maintained ("`config/test_companies/<company>.json`,
or that company's own exported profile"), and every OTHER field on `company` in a real profile
genuinely IS a bare string (`bee_level`, `black_ownership_pct`, ...) - so typing `"disciplines":
"roads_civil"` instead of `["roads_civil"]` is a realistic, easy mistake to make hand-editing this
file, not a contrived one. Checked what `taxonomy.fit_overlap()` - the function this value is fed
straight into - actually does with a bare string.

**Finding (CONFIRMED).** `fit_overlap()`'s own `set(company_disciplines or [])` does not reject a
bare string - Python iterates a string into its INDIVIDUAL CHARACTERS, so `"roads_civil"` becomes
`{'r','o','a','d','s','_','c','i','v','l'}`, which never equals any real category slug. Reproduced
directly: a company profile with `"disciplines": "roads_civil"` (not `["roads_civil"]`) scored its
own `road_maintenance` tender - a tender that genuinely is that company's own discipline - as
`"outside the company's disciplines"` / `not_a_fit`, silently, with no error, no crash, and no
warning at all. This is exactly the "silent wrong data is the main risk" failure mode this module's
own `find_delivery_address()`/`find_closing_time()` docstrings already name as the thing to guard
against everywhere else in this file - just unguarded here. The live Discovery fan-out's own
`company_profiles.py` always builds `disciplines` as a real list (`sorted()` of a set comprehension),
so the live, automated discovery feed can never hit this; only this CLI/manual-profile path can - but
that is exactly the path `classify_tender.py`'s own intake flow (and any manual fit check) uses.

**Fix:** `load_company_profile()` now normalises the field: a bare string becomes a one-item list
(the obviously intended reading of the typo - an empty string becomes `[]`, not `[""]`); anything
else that is neither a list nor a string (an int, a dict, ...) becomes `[]` with a loud `WARNING`
printed, matching this codebase's existing "never silently guess, say so" convention rather than
shredding it into something worse than empty. A genuine list passes through completely unchanged.

**Verified red-then-green.** Created `engine/discovery/test_assess_tender.py` - no dedicated test for
`load_company_profile()` existed at all before this pass, confirmed by a repo-wide search. 4 new test
functions, 5 checks: a bare-string discipline is wrapped into a one-item list and then genuinely
matches via `taxonomy.fit_overlap()`; an empty string normalises to `[]`, not `[""]`; a wrong-typed
value (an int) falls back to `[]` without crashing; a real list is passed through unchanged (control).
Revert-and-confirm-red: reverting reproduced all 3 predicted failures exactly (the bare-string case,
the blank-string case, the wrong-type case) with the control case still green; restored, `0 failure(s)`.
Regression-checked `engine/discovery/test_taxonomy.py`, `engine/discovery/test_discovery_fanout.py`,
and `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/assess_tender.py` (`load_company_profile()`'s own `disciplines`
read, ~15 lines, no other behavior change), `engine/discovery/test_assess_tender.py` (new file, 4
test functions, 5 checks). No schema or other call-site changes - the live Discovery fan-out's own
`company_profiles.py` was never exposed to this bug in the first place.

### Finding 109 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - daily_digest.py's own --mode local was unconditionally wired to the wrong object, so document-expiry and person-credential-expiry sections were silently empty for every company, every run, no matter what was really on file)

**Where:** notify rotation this cycle. `engine/notify/daily_digest.py`'s `main()` (`--mode local` setup
block), feeding `local_document_expiry()`/`local_person_credential_expiry()` (same file).

**What was tested:** `main()`'s local-mode block does `profile = assess_tender.load_company_profile
(args.profile)` then passes that SAME `profile` straight into `local_document_expiry(profile, ...)`
and `local_person_credential_expiry(profile, ...)`. Those two functions read `profile.get("company",
{})` / `profile.get("key_people", [])` - the RAW profile.json's own top-level shape (the same one
`suggest_pack.py`/`generate_cv.py` read directly from the same file). But `assess_tender.
load_company_profile()` is a TRANSFORMING function: it returns a completely different, flatter dict
(`disciplines`/`bee_level`/`black_ownership_pct`/`has_cidb_grading`/`offices` only) - confirmed by
reading its own `return` statement - with no `"company"` or `"key_people"` key at all.

**Finding (CONFIRMED).** Reproduced directly: `assess_tender.load_company_profile()`'s real output,
fed into `local_document_expiry()`, returns `[]` regardless of what the underlying profile.json
actually contains, because `profile.get("company", {})` always hits the "absent" default (that key
genuinely never exists on the transformed dict) - same for `key_people`. This means `--mode local`'s
document-expiry and person-credential-expiry digest sections are unconditionally empty, silently, for
every company, every run - not a rare edge case, the ONLY possible outcome via this wiring. The
existing dedicated test for `local_person_credential_expiry()` (`engine/compliance/
test_watch_person_credentials.py`) masked this completely: it hand-builds a `{"key_people": [...]}`
fixture directly and calls the function with it, which exercises the function's OWN logic correctly
but never exercises `main()`'s actual wiring that feeds it the wrong object in a real run. Confirmed
`--mode live` (the only mode the real scheduled workflow, `.github/workflows/daily-digest.yml`, ever
runs) was never exposed to this at all - it reads these two sections straight from Supabase via
`watch_deadlines.find_due_documents()`/`find_due_person_credentials()`, a completely separate code
path. `--mode local` is explicitly the dev/offline-only convenience path (also the one `mode` falls
back to automatically whenever the Supabase env vars aren't set) - not what runs in production, but
exactly the path a developer would reach for to verify a change to either of these two sections
offline, and it silently couldn't.

While fixing this, also found and fixed the identical "null present, not missing" gap this session's
dominant bug class has already hit repeatedly (Finding 107's `suggest_pack.py`): `profile.get
("company", {})`/`profile.get("key_people", [])` only substitute the default when the key is ABSENT,
not when it's present with `None` - a real profile.json shape (the same file's `"key_people"`/
`"projects"` keys already needed this exact fix elsewhere). Once the wiring fix makes these two
functions receive the REAL raw profile for the first time, this gap becomes newly reachable too, so
fixed both together.

**Fix:** `main()` now re-reads the raw profile JSON directly (with the same graceful OSError/
JSONDecodeError degrade `assess_tender.load_company_profile()`'s own read already has) and passes
THAT to `local_document_expiry()`/`local_person_credential_expiry()`, instead of the already-
transformed `assess_tender.load_company_profile()` result (which is still used for the fit-assessment
profile, unchanged). Both functions' own `"company"`/`"key_people"` reads changed from `.get(key, {})`/
`.get(key, [])` to `.get(key) or {}`/`.get(key) or []`, degrading an explicit `null` the same as absent.

**Verified red-then-green.** Extended `engine/compliance/test_watch_person_credentials.py`'s existing
digest-routing section with 5 new checks: a control case (the TRANSFORMED profile correctly finds
nothing, demonstrating the bug's premise), the RAW profile.json shape finding both the company
document and the key person's registration (demonstrating the fix), and `"company"`/`"key_people"`
explicitly `null` degrading to empty rather than crashing. Revert-and-confirm-red: reverting reproduced
the exact predicted `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` at the exact predicted
line, with every pre-existing check in the file (including the two checks that don't exercise the
null-safety guard) still green; restored, `0 failure(s)`. Regression-checked `engine/notify/
test_digest_live.py`, `engine/notify/test_digest_opt_in.py`, and `engine/compliance/
test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (`main()`'s local-mode profile read, plus two `.get()`
calls in `local_document_expiry()`/`local_person_credential_expiry()`), `engine/compliance/
test_watch_person_credentials.py` (5 new checks in the existing digest-routing section). No schema
or other call-site changes - `--mode live` (the real scheduled run) was never exposed to this bug.

### Finding 110 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - a signatory's name or company's own legal name containing a literal backslash silently corrupted a signed SANRAL declaration, or crashed the whole SANRAL/non-SANRAL pack build outright, via re.sub()'s own backreference syntax)

**Where:** SANRAL pack rotation this cycle. `engine/fill_a_forms.py`'s `fill_declaration_blanks()`
(the real SANRAL pack build path, via `assemble_pack.py` -> `run_forms_pipeline.py` -> `fill_a_forms.
main()`), and independently, `engine/general/fill_sbd_docx.py`'s `fill_dotted_paragraph_count()` (the
non-SANRAL/general pack's own Treasury SBD form filler, called from `fill_sbd_document()` for every
SBD1/4/6.1/7/8/9 free-text field across every general-tender submission).

**What was tested:** both functions passed an f-string built from a free-text company/signatory value
(the person's own name, the company's legal name) straight to `re.sub()`/`re.subn()` as the
**replacement** argument. Python's `re.sub`/`subn` treat a STRING replacement's own backslashes
specially - `\1` is a backreference to a captured group, `\9`/`\g<bad>` raise `re.error` outright for
an invalid or malformed group reference - a well-known but easy-to-miss gotcha with this exact shape
(`pattern.sub(f"...{value}...", text)`). Checked what happens when a signatory's name or a company's
legal name - both plain free text any company member can set, and in the signatory name's case also a
field the CV AI-extraction pipeline can propose a value into - contains a literal backslash (a pasted
Windows file-path fragment, an OCR misread, a plain typo).

**Finding (CONFIRMED, severe).** Reproduced directly in both files:
- `fill_a_forms.py`: a signatory name of `"John\1 Doe"` (a backslash followed by an EXISTING group
  number in the pattern) silently corrupted the output to `"I, the undersigned, JOHNI, the undersigned,
  DOE hereby declare"` - the regex's own matched `"I, the undersigned,"` text spliced straight into the
  middle of the name, in a document meant to be signed and submitted to SANRAL, with **no error at
  all**. A name of `"John\9 Doe"` (no group 9 in this pattern) instead raised a raw, uncaught
  `re.error`/`PatternError: invalid group reference 9`, aborting `fill_declaration_blanks()` - and
  therefore the entire SANRAL pack build for that company - with no indication of the real cause.
- `fill_sbd_docx.py`: a bidder/company name of `"Smith\1 Construction"` raised the same `re.error`
  (this pattern has no capture groups at all, so any `\<digit>` is automatically invalid) straight out
  of `fill_dotted_paragraph_count()`, aborting the whole non-SANRAL SBD form fill.

Scored severe rather than moderate specifically for the silent-corruption case in `fill_a_forms.py`:
unlike every other bug this session found that corrupts internal data or crashes a build loudly, this
one can put fabricated text directly into a document meant to be wet-signed and submitted to a
government buyer, with nothing anywhere - not a log line, not a warning, not a crash - to indicate it
happened. The crash case in both files is also real and would abort an entire pack build with a
confusing, unrelated-looking `re.error` traceback instead of this codebase's own established
"name the field, degrade honestly" discipline.

**Fix:** both call sites now pass a **callable** (`lambda m: f"..."`) as the replacement instead of a
literal f-string - a callable's return value is used by `re.sub`/`subn` completely verbatim, with
zero backslash processing, exactly the convention this same `fill_a_forms.py` file's own `fill_footer()`
already correctly uses for the identical name/position/company values two functions below the fixed
one (confirmed by reading it: it was never vulnerable, which is how this specific function's own gap
stood out against it).

**Verified red-then-green.** New file `engine/test_fill_a_forms.py` (no dedicated test for this module
existed at all before this pass, confirmed by a repo-wide search) - 3 test functions, 5 checks: an
ordinary name still fills exactly as before (control); a name with a backslash-digit backreference is
placed verbatim, not spliced with the regex's own matched text; a name with an unresolvable backslash
escape doesn't raise and abort the fill. Extended `engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` with 1 new
test function, 6 checks (3 value shapes x 2 checks each: a backreference-shaped value, a named-group-
shaped value, and a plain control value with no backslash). Revert-and-confirm-red on both files:
reverting reproduced the exact predicted `re.error`/corrupted-output failures (2 failures in each
file's new test, matching the two distinct failure modes - corruption and crash), with every other
check in both files staying green; restored, `0 failure(s)` in both. Regression-checked
`engine/pack/test_assemble_pack.py` and `engine/general/test_requirements.py` - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/fill_a_forms.py` (one `.subn()` call, f-string -> lambda), `engine/general/
fill_sbd_docx.py` (one `.sub()` call, f-string -> lambda), `engine/test_fill_a_forms.py` (new file, 3
test functions, 5 checks), `engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` (1 new test function, 6 checks). No
schema or other call-site changes - both fixes are return-value-identical for every input that didn't
already trigger the bug.

### Finding 111 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a tender's own real minimum-years requirement for a key position silently disappeared whenever the C3.1.11 table's qualification-alternatives couldn't be phrase-split, even though the individual years figures were still right there in the text)

**Where:** this cycle's own lead, picked up from the standing solution-architect review's own honest,
explicitly-unconfirmed note in `docs/specs/System-Status.md` ("one inconclusive lead on
`key_person_minimums.py` noted, not fixed" - that pass couldn't construct or confirm a real failing
case in the time it had). `engine/discovery/key_person_minimums.py`'s `extract_key_person_minimums()`
- the C3.1.11(d) key-person minimum-requirements table parser feeding the real compliance check
(`app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`).

**What was tested:** when a position's row offers several qualification/years alternatives (e.g.
"None specified: 20 years" / "National Diploma: 10 years" / "Pr Techni Eng: 5 years" - the real,
documented R.396 Senior Materials Technician shape), the parser only builds the structured
`alternatives` list when `len(numeric) > 1 and len(quals) > 1` - i.e. only when its OWN phrase-
splitting (`qual_new`/`DANGLE`-based) manages to separate the qualification column into as many
phrases as there are years values. Constructed two real-world-plausible layouts where that splitting
fails while the years values themselves are still individually readable: (1) a qualification phrase
ending in a dangling connector word ("None specified **or**") right before a line-wrapped
continuation - a genuine `pdftotext -layout` artifact this same file's own `DANGLE` list already
exists to handle elsewhere, just not for this exact row shape; (2) an all-lowercase qualification
column (`qual_new` requires an uppercase first letter to recognise a new phrase).

**Finding (CONFIRMED).** In both constructed cases, `alternatives` stayed `[]` as designed (the
phrase-split genuinely couldn't separate them) - but `years_text`/`years_min`/`years_under` fell
through to `(None, None)` UNCONDITIONALLY (`ymin, yunder = _years(years_text) if len(numeric) == 1
else (None, None)` - and since `len(numeric) == 3` here, always the `None, None` branch), even though
`years_text` itself was a perfectly legible string (`"10 5"` / `"20 10 5"`) and every individual
numeric fragment (20, 10, 5) was independently parseable. The row's real stated minimum (5 years,
same position, same real-world figures as the documented R.396 example) was silently discarded to
`None` - a compliance check reading `years_min` for this position would see "no minimum stated"
instead of the real "5 years minimum", exactly the "silent wrong data is the main risk" failure mode
this session has found repeatedly elsewhere, just in a file with zero prior QA attention until the
architect pass's own read.

**Fix:** when `alternatives` couldn't be built but `len(numeric) > 1`, take the lowest of the
individually-parsed numeric fragments as the row's own `years_min` - the same "the lower bound is the
binding minimum" rule the `alternatives` branch immediately above already applies (`min(a["years_min"]
for a in alternatives ...)`). `alternatives` itself stays `[]` (honest: which qualification pairs with
which years figure is genuinely lost), but the overall minimum-years compliance signal - the one
figure the actual check reads - is recovered rather than silently dropped.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `part1b()` to `engine/discovery/test_key_person_minimums.py`: both
constructed layouts, 6 checks total (one row read, `alternatives == []` confirming the premise, and
`years_min == 5` confirming the fix, for each of the two trigger shapes). Revert-and-confirm-red:
reverting reproduced the exact predicted 2 failures (`years_min` back to `None`) with every other
check - including both "alternatives genuinely empty" premise checks, and all of the existing Part
1/2/3 real-fixture tests - still green; restored, `0 failure(s)`. Regression-checked
`engine/general/test_requirements.py` (a real consumer of this module) - all pass.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/key_person_minimums.py` (one `elif` branch added, ~15 lines, no
other behavior change - every row that already had `len(numeric) <= 1` or successfully-built
`alternatives` is byte-for-byte unaffected), `engine/discovery/test_key_person_minimums.py` (1 new
test function, 6 checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 112 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a tender document that couldn't actually be read came back silently blank with no reason, instead of flagged unreadable, whenever its saved file had no recognized extension)

**Where:** this cycle's "intake" rotation. `engine/general/requirements.py`'s `read_document()` - the
dispatcher every tender document goes through (pdf/docx/doc/txt) before `extract_requirements()`
builds the manifest that `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`'s `run_extraction()` relies on for
both the SANRAL/general route decision and the "none of this tender's documents could be read" loud
failure.

**What was tested:** `collect_documents()` decides a document's `format` purely from the SAVED FILE's
own extension (`os.path.splitext(path)[1]`). The file a tender document is saved under is named by
`process_general_jobs.download_tender_documents()`, which only appends a fallback `.pdf` when there is
NO dot at all in the title's last 6 characters - so a real, buyer-published title like `"SBD Forms Part
A.1"` or `"Addendum No.1"` keeps its own trailing `.1` as the "extension" (format `"1"`), and a scanned
notice uploaded directly as a raw `.jpg`/`.png` (not wrapped in a `.pdf`) keeps that extension too.
`read_document()`'s `if/elif` chain only had branches for `pdf`/`docx`/`doc`/`txt` - any other format
fell through all of them with `text` left at `""` and, critically, `doc["unreadable"]` never set at
all (the one `if not doc.get("unreadable") and fmt in ("pdf", "docx", "doc") and ...` scanned-image
check that would otherwise catch a near-empty read doesn't apply either, since its own `fmt in (...)`
guard excludes anything outside that same three-format list).

**Finding (CONFIRMED).** Reproduced directly: a file saved as `"SBD Forms Part A.1"` containing real,
perfectly good bytes came back `{"format": "1", "text": "", "unreadable": None}` - indistinguishable,
to every downstream consumer, from a genuinely-empty-but-successfully-read document. `chars == 0`
correctly keeps it out of the `readable` list, so `run_extraction()` still fails loudly when it's the
only document - but `intake_rec["unreadable_documents"]` (built by filtering on `d["unreadable"]`
being truthy) silently omits it, and the loud failure message's own `d['unreadable'] or 'no text
found'` fallback shows a generic, unhelpful "no text found" instead of the real reason (wrong/missing
file extension) - exactly the "silent wrong answer, not an empty one" failure mode `run_extraction()`'s
own module comment already names as the thing to never produce, just one dispatch level further in
than that comment's own guard reaches. The same gap affects a raw scanned image uploaded directly
(`.jpg`/`.png`), not only the mis-detected-extension case.

**Fix:** added an explicit `else` branch to `read_document()`'s format dispatch: any format not in
`pdf`/`docx`/`doc`/`txt` now sets `doc["unreadable"] = f"not a format this can read ({fmt or 'no file
extension'}) - re-upload it as a PDF or Word document"`, so it is correctly counted in
`unreadable_documents`, correctly excluded from `readable`, and reported with its real reason rather
than a generic fallback. Scoped to `read_document()` only - the weaker upstream `.pdf`-fallback
heuristic in `download_tender_documents()` is left as-is (a separate, more speculative improvement:
guessing a buyer's REAL intended extension from a title is not a "contained issue" fix), since this
fix alone closes the actual defect (a document that can't be read must never be silently treated as if
it were read and found empty).

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `check_unrecognized_format_is_flagged_not_silently_blank()` to
`engine/general/test_requirements.py`: the exact trailing-`.1` title case and a raw `.jpg` case, both
via `read_document()` directly and via the full `extract_requirements()` manifest. Revert-and-confirm-
red: reverting reproduced the exact predicted 3 failures (`unreadable` back to `None`/falsy in all
three assertions) with every other check - including the premise checks (`format == "1"`, `text ==
""`) and every pre-existing check in the file - still green; restored, `0 failure(s)`. Regression-
checked `engine/general/test_requirements_manifest_v2.py`, `engine/general/test_submission_plan.py`,
and `engine/general/test_fill_sbd_docx.py` (real downstream consumers of this manifest shape) - all
pass.

**Regression:** `engine/general/requirements.py` (one `else` branch added to `read_document()`'s
format dispatch, ~10 lines including comment - every document whose format was already `pdf`/`docx`/
`doc`/`txt`/`zip` is byte-for-byte unaffected), `engine/general/test_requirements.py` (1 new test
function, 6 checks). No schema or other call-site changes.

### Finding 113 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - the daily digest email's "Listing changes" section (cancellations, closing-date moves, new addenda) showed only the tender's own generic title on every single line, with the one fact that section exists to report - WHAT changed - never reaching the sent email at all)

**Where:** this cycle's "notify" rotation, following up on `send_digest_emails.py`'s own disclosed,
honest gap ("`listing_changes`/`tender_updates`/`reassessed_tenders` weren't traced key-by-key here -
... not a full per-section audit, flagged as such in `app/AGENTS.md`") the same way this session has
repeatedly turned a disclosed-but-unconfirmed gap into a confirmed fix or a ruled-out conclusion
(Finding 111 most recently). `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py`'s `render_text()`.

**What was tested:** `render_text()`'s per-item text comes from one shared fallback chain: `item.get
