### Finding 156 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `watch_tender_updates.py`'s own eTenders/OCDS
failure path had no `system_alerts.record()` call at all, unlike the SANRAL failure path right
next to it in the same function, so a pursued eTenders tender whose release drops out of every
day-window this watch tries would silently stop getting ANY addendum/closing-date/briefing alert,
forever, with zero visibility to Sarel)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py` (`check_tender()`), the 4th watch of the same
shape as `watch_new_tenders.py`/`watch_deadlines.py`/the daily digest - reports addenda, closing-
date changes and briefing-date changes ONLY to companies actively pursuing a tender.

**How this was found.** This pass's own priority was the 4 sibling direct-buyer readers named in
the immediately-preceding pass (2026-11-07r) as unreachable-or-unverified for the DBSA-shaped
reused-reference `ocid` collision - see below for that result. With time remaining, continued the
discovery-pipeline read into a slice not yet covered by any prior pass: the tender-change/update-
tracking subsystem (`watch_tender_updates.py`, `tender_changes.py`, `tender_updates.py`,
`detail.py`) - none of which the 2026-11-07r fan-out/scoring slice touched.

Read `check_tender()`'s two source branches side by side - eTenders (`tender.get("ocid")`) and
SANRAL (`tender.get("source") == "sanral"`) - since they handle the structurally identical case
(this run's attempt to re-read the tender's real source failed) right next to each other in the
same function, an obvious place to check they actually behave the same way. They don't:

```python
if tender.get("ocid"):
    ...
    release, day = ocds.find(tender["ocid"], known_day, _discovered_day(client, tender), today)
    if not release:
        new_state["last_error"] = f"OCDS release {tender['ocid']} not found in the windows read"
        client.upsert("tender_watch_state", [{**state, **new_state}], "tender_id")
        log(f"  {tender.get('contract_no') or tender['id']}: {new_state['last_error']}")
        return []
elif tender.get("source") == "sanral" and tender.get("slug"):
    try:
        ...
    except Exception as e:
        new_state["last_error"] = f"SANRAL page could not be read ({e})"
        system_alerts.record("tender_updates", f"A pursued SANRAL tender's page could not be read: ...",
                             "error", exc=e, context={...})
        ...
        return []
```

The SANRAL branch calls `system_alerts.record(..., "error", ...)` on failure - a real alert
`/admin` shows and Sarel sees (`system_alerts.py`'s own docstring: "Sarel... a fail must be
emailed to me and flagged for me to review"). The OCDS branch, on the equivalent failure (the
tender's release can't be found in ANY of the day-windows `OcdsDays.find()` tries - the
`WALK_BACK_DAYS=21` walk-back exhausted, or the feed's own re-dating/pagination means today's
windows simply don't carry it), does **not** call `system_alerts.record()` at all - it only writes
`last_error` into `tender_watch_state`, confirmed by `grep -rn "last_error"` across all of `app/`
and `engine/` to be a column **nothing else in the codebase ever reads** (no admin page, no
digest, nothing - the only other `last_error` match anywhere is `app/lib/workflowRegistry.ts`'s
own unrelated field of the same name for a completely different subsystem).

**The real consequence.** A company actively pursuing an eTenders tender whose release drops out
of every window this watch tries would silently stop getting ANY addendum/closing-date/briefing
alert for it, forever - and this never shows up as a "failure" anywhere a human would see: it
doesn't raise (so it's never in `run()`'s own per-tender `failed` list, which only catches an
actual exception), it's just a plain `return []` with nothing new to report that run, indistin-
guishable from a tender that's genuinely had no updates. The identical failure mode for a SANRAL
tender has always alerted. This is the exact dominant bug class this whole review has tracked
(an external-read failure silently treated as a false-safe "nothing here" state) - just one level
removed from the usual shape, since it's not a discarded exception but a discarded **negative
result** (release not found) from a call that itself didn't fail.

**Zero test coverage, confirmed before writing one.** `ls test_*.py` in `engine/discovery/` - every
other module in this subsystem with real logic has a test file (`test_tender_changes.py`,
`test_tender_updates.py`, `test_discovery_downgrades.py`, etc.); `watch_tender_updates.py` (600+

### Finding 157 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `tender_changes.run()`'s own live read of the
eTenders portal's Cancelled tab failing used to only log a local WARNING and fall back to
`cancelled=[]`, silently zeroing out ALL cancellation and cancelled-tender re-advertisement
detection for the whole run with zero visibility to Sarel; plus a second, independent finding - the
higher-traffic of its two real callers, `watch_new_tenders.py`'s daily fan-out, had no alert at all
on any OTHER failure from the same call, unlike `daily_digest.py`'s own identical call site)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/tender_changes.py` (`run()`), `engine/discovery/watch_new_tenders.py`
(`main()`'s own call site around `tender_changes.run()`).

**How this was found.** Continuing 2026-11-07s's own backlog note: the tender-change/update-
tracking subsystem (`watch_tender_updates.py`, `tender_changes.py`, `tender_updates.py`,
`detail.py`) had been read but not yet audited line-by-line for siblings of Finding 156's own bug
shape. `detail.py`, `tender_updates.py` and `watch_tender_updates.py` itself (re-read in full) all
came back clean - the first two have no failure path of their own to alert on, the third's one real
gap was already Finding 156. `tender_changes.py` had the real one:

```python
cancelled = res.get("cancelled")
if cancelled is None:
    import etenders_portal
    since = datetime.datetime.now(sh.SAST) - datetime.timedelta(days=lookback_days)
    try:
        cancelled = etenders_portal.fetch_releases("cancelled", since=since, log=log)
    except Exception as e:
        log(f"  WARNING: portal Cancelled tab failed: {e}")
        cancelled = []
```

Confirmed (`grep -rn "cancelled" gov_sources.py watch_new_tenders.py daily_digest.py` - zero hits)
that `res.get("cancelled")` is ALWAYS `None` at both of `run()`'s two real call sites, so this
live-fetch branch runs on every real invocation, not a rare fallback path. The module's own
docstring states plainly that the OCDS feed "can't show this" (a cancellation) - this Cancelled-tab
read is the ONLY signal `cancellations()` has, and part of what `readvertisements()` matches
cancelled-but-relisted bid numbers against. A failed fetch here silently zeroes out an entire
change-detection category - every cancellation, every cancelled-tender re-advertisement match - for
the whole run, across every tender and every company, with only a `log()` line (stdout, not
necessarily monitored) and no `system_alerts.record()` call. Three lines below, in the same file's
`detect()` function, an almost identical per-listing failure already calls
`system_alerts.record("tender_changes", ..., "warning", ...)` - the asymmetry this whole review
tracks, one call further removed than the usual shape: not a discarded exception on one record, but
an entire source read for the whole run, right next to a working alert for a narrower case.

**The second finding, found while tracing whether either caller would have caught it.** Neither of
`run()`'s two real callers ever sees this specific failure (the catch above swallows it before it
can raise) - but checking whether either WOULD catch some OTHER exception from `run()` (a snapshot/
change-store write failure, say) found they are not symmetric. `daily_digest.py`
(`engine/notify/daily_digest.py:815-828`) already wraps its call to `tender_changes.run()` and
calls `system_alerts.record("digest", ..., "error", exc=e)` on any exception. `watch_new_tenders.py`
(`engine/discovery/watch_new_tenders.py:493-497` - the DAILY scheduled fan-out, `daily-discovery.yml`,
the higher-traffic of the two) wraps the identical call but only `print()`s a local WARNING, no
alert. A real failure reaching `run()` from the daily fan-out would have gone to Sarel even less
reliably than from the once-daily digest.

**Fix.** `tender_changes.run()`'s Cancelled-tab catch now calls `system_alerts.record("tender_changes",
f"...{type(e).__name__}: {e} - no cancellations or cancelled-tender re-advertisement matches were
detected this run...", "error", exc=e, context={"lookback_days": lookback_days})` before the
existing `cancelled = []` fallback - the fallback itself (the run must continue regardless) is
unchanged, only the silence is fixed. `watch_new_tenders.py`'s own call site gained
`system_alerts.record("discovery", f"...{type(e).__name__}: {e}", "error", exc=e)`, matching
`daily_digest.py`'s own identical call site's shape and severity.

**Verified genuinely, red-then-green.** Added `test_cancelled_tab_fetch_failure_alerts_sarel()` to
`engine/discovery/test_tender_changes.py`: monkeypatches `etenders_portal.fetch_releases` to raise,
calls `tc.run()` with no `'cancelled'` key in `res` (exercising the live-fetch branch exactly as
both real callers do), captures alerts via `system_alerts.set_sink()`. Isolated the fix with `git
stash` and re-ran: **red** - `run()` correctly did not raise (the must-continue behaviour was
already intact), but zero alerts were recorded. Restored the fix (`git stash pop`) and re-ran:
**green** - exactly one alert, severity `error`, naming the real exception and explaining what went
undetected. Full regression: `test_tender_changes.py` (6/6 pass, including the new test),
`test_discovery_fanout.py` and `test_gov_sources.py` re-run in full (both clean); the complete
`engine/` per-file test loop (`find . -maxdepth 2 -name "test_*.py"`, real exit codes, not
string-grep) - **86 files, 0 failures** (the genuine current count from `find` itself - this pass
added a test function to an existing file, not a new file). `py_compile` clean on both edited
source files. `ruff check` on the three touched files: 23 warnings, all pre-existing `BLE001`
"blind except" style (20 already there before this pass; the 3 this pass adds follow the exact same
deliberate, already-pervasive broad-except convention used throughout this file and its siblings) -
`ruff` is not wired into any CI gate for `engine/`, confirmed by grepping every workflow file, so
this is a style note, not a regression.

**Regression:** `engine/discovery/tender_changes.py` (+19 lines, one `system_alerts.record()` call
+ explanatory comment in `run()`'s Cancelled-tab catch). `engine/discovery/watch_new_tenders.py`
(+11 lines, one `system_alerts.record()` call + explanatory comment in `main()`'s own
`tender_changes.run()` call site). `engine/discovery/test_tender_changes.py` (+1 new test
function, `test_cancelled_tab_fetch_failure_alerts_sarel`). No other file touched.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - small, narrow, does not touch RLS/money paths/hard-stop gates, and
does not change what the production worker image installs/copies.

### Finding 160 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`'s own 4 metric-count
functions caught their own Supabase read failure and then returned a plain `0` anyway, so the
daily email Sarel reads every morning could not tell "nothing happened" apart from "the read itself
broke")

**Area:** `app/scripts/send-founder-digest.ts` (`countNewSignups24h()`, `countActiveSubscriptions()`,
`countClosingWithin48h()`, `countScoutBacklog()`), `app/lib/emailTemplatesTier3.ts`
(`founderDailyDigestEmail()`).

**How this was found.** With the pagination-cap/anon-grant/discovery/tender-change angles this
chain has already closed, picked up the Tier 3 founder-digest/Scout-alert surface
(`lib/scoutAnomalyAlerts.ts`, `scripts/send-scout-alerts.ts`, `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts`,
`lib/emailTemplatesTier3.ts`) as a slice this review had read for a *different* bug class before
(the `countClosingWithin48h()` 1000-row pagination-cap fix, `1acf0c1`) but never for this review's
own dominant bug class - a discarded Supabase error read as a false-safe "nothing here" state.
`lib/scoutAnomalyAlerts.ts` (pure candidate-selection, no I/O) and `scripts/send-scout-alerts.ts`
(every real failure path already `console.error`s and `process.exit(1)`s, or skips just the one
alert whose own `claim_notification` call failed, never silently zeroing the whole batch) both read
clean. `scripts/send-founder-digest.ts` did not.

**The bug.** All 4 of its count functions follow the identical shape:

```ts
async function countScoutBacklog(supabase: SupabaseService): Promise<number> {
  const { count, error } = await supabase.from("system_alerts").select("id", { count: "exact", head: true }).is("resolved_at", null);
  if (error) {
    console.error("founder-digest: could not count the system_alerts backlog", error);
    return 0;
  }
  return count ?? 0;
}
```

`console.error()` gives an operator watching the GitHub Actions log something to see - but
`founderDailyDigestEmail()` (`lib/emailTemplatesTier3.ts`), the one real consumer, only ever
receives the plain number that function call resolves to. A transient Supabase blip, an RLS/grant
regression, or a renamed column on any one of the 4 underlying tables (`companies`,
`company_subscriptions`, `tender_packs`/`tenders`, `system_alerts`) would render as "0 new company
signups", "0 active paid subscriptions", "0 active bids closing within 48h" or "0 flagged" in
Sarel's own 07:00 SAST inbox - identical, byte for byte, to the genuinely healthy or genuinely quiet
day the digest exists to report on. The worst instance is `countScoutBacklog()`: a broken read of
the alerts table would tell Sarel "Scout backlog: 0 - all clear" on the exact morning the alerting
pipeline itself needs his attention, the one metric in this email whose entire job is to surface
that something elsewhere is broken.

**Fix.** All 4 functions now return `number | null` - `null` on a real read failure, never folded
into `0`. `founderDailyDigestEmail()`'s 4 corresponding fields are now `number | null` too; a `null`
renders as its own "Couldn't load" value (the same wording convention `app/AGENTS.md`'s own
error-banner entries already use for this exact page-level distinction), gets the same `warning`
emphasis a real nonzero count already gets, and - since the subject line and the HTML's lead
sentence previously interpolated `closingWithin48h`/`scoutBacklogCount` directly as numbers - falls
back to "Daily digest - some metrics couldn't load" rather than literally printing the word "null".
A visible line ("One or more counts above couldn't be read this run - check the Admin Console and
the worker logs rather than trusting 'Couldn't load' as zero.") is added to the email body whenever
any of the 4 is `null`, and omitted entirely when all 4 succeed - confirmed by test, not by reading
the template's own prose.

**Verified genuinely, red then green.** Neither `send-founder-digest.ts`'s count functions nor
`emailTemplatesTier3.ts` had any test coverage before this pass (confirmed: no `*.spec.ts` existed

### Finding 161 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py` gated a
time-critical, per-bid-pack notification on the unrelated "new tenders discovered" digest opt-in,
so any company member who never opted into that digest silently never got told their own bid pack
was ready)

**Area:** `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py` (`send_pack_ready_email()`'s recipient filter).

**How this was found.** Reading `send_pack_ready_email.py` end to end as part of this chain's
continuing sweep of the notification engine (the same module PR #181 fixed the worker-image
delivery path for). Its recipient lookup calls `company_notification_recipients()` and then
filtered the result on `r.get("daily_digest_opt_in")` - identical in shape to
`lib/notificationRecipients.ts`'s own `operationalRecipients()`. But that flag (migration 0073) is
specifically the "new tenders discovered" digest opt-in, default off, surfaced in
`app/app/company/Notifications.tsx` under a toggle literally labelled "Turn on daily digest" -
confirmed by reading that component's own header comment ("digest email only ... Narrowed to 'new
opportunities only'") and `daily_digest.py`'s own real digest sender, the only other place in the
codebase this flag legitimately gates anything. `lib/notificationRecipients.ts` already drew this
exact distinction on 2026-10-30, adding a second, unfiltered `criticalBidRecipients()` specifically
for "critical, bid-specific" alerts (corrigenda, returnables blockers, closing-deadline reminders)
with its own header comment spelling out why: "the opt-in flag is a preference about the
discovered-tenders digest only ... gating these three on it would mean a company's own bidding
team silently misses an addendum or a closing deadline unless someone found and clicked a toggle
described as a generic 'daily digest'." A pack-ready notification - this module's own header
comment says instant delivery matters because "teams are often working against tight
courier/print deadlines" - is exactly as time-critical and exactly as per-bid as those three, but
this Python sender had duplicated the wrong (digest-gated) TypeScript pattern instead of the
right (ungated) one.

**Consequence.** Any company member who never opted into the unrelated "new tenders discovered"
digest - the default state for every member, since that opt-in is off until explicitly turned on -
never received the "your bid pack is ready" email at all, regardless of whether PR #181's
worker-image fix is deployed. Not a transient/intermittent gap: for a company where nobody has
ever clicked "Turn on daily digest," 100% of that company's `pack_ready` emails go to zero
recipients, silently (`send_pack_ready_email()` returns cleanly with no `system_alerts` row, since
an empty recipient list reads as "nothing to do," not a failure - itself the dominant bug-class
shape, just one step upstream: the ambiguity here is "opted out of X" being silently treated as
"opted out of this unrelated Y" rather than a discarded error, but the end state is the same
silent, unrecoverable loss this whole review tracks).

**Fix.** Removed the `daily_digest_opt_in` filter from the recipients list in
`send_pack_ready_email()` - now keeps every `company_notification_recipients()` row with a usable
email, same unfiltered shape as `criticalBidRecipients()`. Added a header comment on the function
and a module-docstring line naming the reasoning and precedent explicitly, so this doesn't
regress back to the wrong pattern later.

**Verified genuinely, red then green.** `engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` had an
existing test, `test_skips_cleanly_with_no_opted_in_recipients`, that asserted the *old, wrong*
behaviour (a recipient with `daily_digest_opt_in: False` gets no email) - ran the full suite
against the fix with that test still in place first: 1 failure, exactly that test, exactly as
predicted (`FAIL no send was logged when nobody is opted in`). Replaced it with
`test_skips_cleanly_with_no_valid_email_recipients` (a genuine empty-email case, still correctly
skipped) and added `test_sends_regardless_of_daily_digest_opt_in`, asserting a recipient with
`daily_digest_opt_in: False` now receives the email - reran: 0 failures. Full `engine/` sweep
(real exit codes, not grep) - 86 files, 0 failures, unchanged. `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors.
`npx eslint .` - 0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx vitest run` - 487/487, 62 files,
unchanged (this fix touched no TypeScript). Per-file `*.test.ts` node loop (no `--test` flag) -
28 files, 0 failures, unchanged.

**Regression:** `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py` (recipient filter + header comment,
~10 lines). `engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` (one test replaced, one added).

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a one-line behavioural change plus its test, confined to a single
already-isolated sender function, does not touch RLS/money paths/hard-stop gates, and does not
change what the production worker image installs/copies.

To verify independently: run `python3 engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` and confirm
`0 failure(s)`. Read `send_pack_ready_email()`'s recipient filter and confirm it checks only
`r.get("email")`/`"@" in r["email"]`, with no `daily_digest_opt_in` condition.

### Finding 162 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts`'s own
`lifecycleRecipients()` and `unsubscribeUrlFor()` both discarded a real RPC error with no logging
at all, silently indistinguishable from a genuine "nothing to do")

**Area:** `app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts` (`lifecycleRecipients()`, `unsubscribeUrlFor()`).

**How this was found.** Continuing the notification-engine sweep that found Findings 160/161 in a
row, checked every other Tier 0-3 sender script in `app/scripts/send-*.ts` and its Python siblings
in `engine/notify/` for the same two bug shapes named in this pass's own brief (a discarded read
error treated as "nothing to do"; a recipient/gating flag borrowed from the wrong feature).
`send-corrigendum-alerts.ts`, `send-returnables-digest.ts`, and `send-test-samples.ts` (all 3
previously unmentioned anywhere in this doc, confirmed by grep before reading) turned out clean:
all read errors are either loud (`console.error` + `process.exit(1)` on a total-fetch failure) or
correctly skip just the one bad item (`continue`), and all three already resolve recipients via
`lib/notificationRecipients.ts`'s `criticalBidRecipients()` - the already-fixed, correct,
unfiltered pattern Findings 160/161 reference. `send-onboarding-nudges.ts` (also previously
unmentioned) was different: its own `lifecycleRecipients()` -

```ts
async function lifecycleRecipients(supabase, companyId) {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc("company_notification_recipients", { p_company_id: companyId });
  if (error || !data) return [];
  ...
}
```

- discards `error` completely, with no `console.error` call, unlike every sibling resolver in the
codebase that calls this exact same RPC: `lib/notificationRecipients.ts`'s own
`operationalRecipients()` and `criticalBidRecipients()` both log
`` `company_notification_recipients rpc failed for company ${companyId}` `` on this identical
error branch. The sibling helper `unsubscribeUrlFor()` two lines below it has the identical shape
against `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for()`. Confirmed by grep that neither function appears in any
`.spec.ts` file before this pass - `send-onboarding-nudges.ts` had zero test coverage of its own
sender-script logic (only the pure candidate-selection functions in `lib/onboardingNudges.ts`/
`lib/trialLifecycle.ts` were tested), the same "real bug living in the untested half of a sender
script" shape as Findings 153/160.

**Consequence.** A transient `company_notification_recipients()` RPC failure (network blip,
timeout, a bad deploy of the function itself) for one company on one run is indistinguishable, in
the logs, from that company's own members having genuinely all opted out of Tier 0 lifecycle mail
- `lifecycleRecipients()` returns `[]` either way, and nothing anywhere records which case
happened. This is worse here than in most senders this review has fixed, because 3 of this
script's 5 stages are one-shot, non-retried windows, not an ongoing condition that self-heals on
the next run: `trialDay7Candidates()` (`lib/trialLifecycle.ts`) matches on
`daysUntil(trial_ends_at) === 7` exactly - a company that hits this failure on its one qualifying
day gets the `trial_day_7_milestone` nudge silently dropped forever, since the very next day's run
no longer matches (`daysUntil` is `6`, not `7`). `trial_expiring_48h` and `trial_expired` are
window/threshold-based and would self-heal on tomorrow's run if the company is still eligible, but
still with the same missing diagnostic trace of why a given run sent nothing. `unsubscribeUrlFor()`
failing the same way silently sends a Tier 0 lifecycle email with no one-click unsubscribe link at
all (a POPIA/CAN-SPAM one-click-unsubscribe gap, not just a missing header) rather than skipping or
logging - lower severity than the recipients gap, but the identical discarded-error shape, fixed
alongside it for consistency and because it shares the same function file and review pass.

**Fix.** Added the missing `console.error` call on the real-error branch of both
`lifecycleRecipients()` (`` `company_notification_recipients rpc failed for company ${companyId}` ``,
matching the exact wording `lib/notificationRecipients.ts`'s siblings already use for this RPC)
and `unsubscribeUrlFor()` (`` `lifecycle_unsubscribe_token_for rpc failed for user ${userId}` ``).
Behaviour on a genuine zero/opted-out/no-token result is unchanged - this is a logging-only fix,
not a behavioural change to who gets nudged. Exported both functions (previously unexported,
module-private) so they can be tested directly, same precedent `send-founder-digest.ts` already
set for its own `count*()` functions.

**Verified genuinely, red then green.** Neither function had any test coverage before this pass.
Added `app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts` (5 tests: each function's own real-error path
logs with the right message, each function's own genuine-empty/opted-out path logs nothing, and
each function's own success path still works). Ran against the pre-fix source first (`git stash`
on just the one source file, the new spec kept): **5 of 5 failed** - `TypeError: lifecycleRecipients
is not a function` / `unsubscribeUrlFor is not a function`, since neither was exported pre-fix,
confirming the test genuinely exercises the fixed file and not some stale import. Restored the fix
(`git stash pop`): **5/5 pass**. Full regression suite re-run after: `npm run typecheck` - 0
errors. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings, unchanged. `npx vitest run` -
**492/492, 63 files** (487 baseline + 5 new tests, 62 + 1 new file). The `*.test.ts` node loop (no
`--test` flag, real exit codes) - **28 files, 0 failures**, matching the standing baseline exactly.
Full `engine/` sweep (real exit codes) - **86 files, 0 failures**, unchanged (this fix touches no
Python).

**Regression:** `app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts` (2 functions: added error logging +
`export`, ~12 lines, no behavioural change to recipient selection itself).
`app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts` (new file, 5 tests).

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a logging-only fix (plus making two already-private functions
testable) confined to one already-isolated sender script, does not touch RLS/money paths/hard-stop
gates, and does not change what the production worker image installs or copies (this script runs
only via its own GitHub Actions schedule, same as every other Tier 0-3 sender).

To verify independently: run `npx vitest run app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.spec.ts` and
confirm 5/5 pass. Read `lifecycleRecipients()`/`unsubscribeUrlFor()` in
`app/scripts/send-onboarding-nudges.ts` and confirm each now calls `console.error` on its own real
`error` branch before returning its empty/undefined fallback.

### Finding 163 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts` gated the SARS Tax PIN/COID/B-BBEE/CIDB/ECSA/SACPCMP expiry digest on the unrelated "new tenders discovered" opt-in, the same bug shape as Finding 161, for a category that can disqualify an active bid outright)

**Area:** `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts` (`processComplianceDigestForCompany()`'s recipient
lookup).

**How this was found.** Continuing this chain's own notification-engine sweep, per this pass's
brief: checked each of `send-compliance-digest.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/
`send-deadline-reminders.ts`/`send-operational-alerts.ts` (the 4 remaining Tier 0-3 TypeScript
senders named explicitly) against its own prior-mention history in this doc first. `send-deadline-
reminders.ts` and `send-discovered-tenders.ts` read clean (both already resolve recipients via the
correct function for what they are - `criticalBidRecipients()` and `operationalRecipients()`
respectively, both deliberately set that way by commit `8623d38`, 2026-10-31). `send-operational-
alerts.ts` (0 mentions, genuinely unexamined before this pass) also reads clean: its one inline,
unchecked read (`runClarificationWindow()`'s per-task `tender_packs.pipeline_stage` lookup) fails
*open*, not closed - a discarded error there defaults `pipelineStageFor()` to `null`, and
`isClarificationCandidate(null)` is explicitly true (same "don't exclude by accident" rule as a
genuinely-missing pack row), so a real read failure there still sends the reminder rather than
silently suppressing it. And `8623d38`'s own commit message explicitly, by name, documents
`send-operational-alerts.ts` as "unchanged, still opt-in gated" - a deliberate, Sarel-attributed
product decision from the same commit that split the other 3 scripts onto the unconditional
resolver, not an oversight; left exactly as-is, not re-litigated.

`send-compliance-digest.ts` was different. It calls `operationalRecipients(supabase, company.id)` -
the `daily_digest_opt_in`-filtered resolver, migration 0073, default OFF for every member - for the
exact same reason Finding 161 flagged `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`: this is identical in
shape to the pattern `lib/notificationRecipients.ts`'s own header comment and `app/company/
Notifications.tsx`'s 2026-10-30 fix already named and fixed for 3 other scripts.
`send-compliance-digest.ts` was never one of them. Checked `8623d38`'s own commit message (the PR
that created `criticalBidRecipients()` and explicitly enumerated every sender it did and didn't
switch) line by line: it names exactly 5 scripts total - "switched: send-corrigendum-alerts.ts,
send-returnables-digest.ts, send-deadline-reminders.ts. Unchanged, still opt-in gated: send-
discovered-tenders.ts, send-operational-alerts.ts." `send-compliance-digest.ts` appears in neither
list, even though it already existed 4 days earlier (`dc9eb06`, 2026-10-27) - genuinely missed by
that review, not a third deliberate "leave gated" decision the commit forgot to mention (unlike
`send-operational-alerts.ts`, which IS named). Confirmed this isn't a case of "digest-style, so
opt-in is the right call anyway" by reading `app/company/Notifications.tsx`'s own current UI copy,
which the 2026-10-30 fix rewrote specifically to describe what IS and ISN'T gated: "Active bid
alerts (addenda/corrigenda, returnable checklists, and closing deadline reminders for tenders you
are actively bidding on) are always delivered **to keep your submissions compliant**." That promise
- "compliant" - is the word, and `send-compliance-digest.ts` is the one sender whose entire purpose
is submission compliance, yet it was the one left silently contradicting that exact sentence.
Multiple prior passes read this file closely for other angles (claim-before-recipients ordering,
`fdeab92`/`f661d26`; pagination, `3007`-`3023`; the creation-date lookback residual, `8119`-`8194`)
without ever checking this one - each was looking at a different shape of bug, not this one.

**Consequence.** `operationalRecipients()`'s own header comment states the real production number
this flag starts from: "33 company_members rows ... exactly 1 had ever opted in." For the other 32,
every SARS Tax Compliance PIN, COID Letter of Good Standing, B-BBEE proof, CIDB registration, and
per-person ECSA/SACPCMP credential nearing its 30/14/7-day expiry threshold produced zero email,
silently - no error, no log line distinguishing "nobody opted in" from "nothing is expiring" (the
`skippedNoRecipients` counter in `main()`'s own summary line folds both into one number either way).
Unlike a missed corrigendum or a missed deadline reminder (which the bidder would likely also notice
from the tender detail page itself), a lapsed B-BBEE certificate or CIDB registration is exactly the
kind of fact a bidding team has no other prompt to re-check until a buyer's own evaluation rejects
the submission on it - the compliance digest existing at all was meant to be that prompt. Rated
severe, not moderate (Finding 161's own rating for the same shape), because the consequence here is
disqualification of a live bid on a technicality, not merely a late pack-ready notification.

**Fix.** Switched `processComplianceDigestForCompany()`'s recipient lookup from
`operationalRecipients()` to `criticalBidRecipients()` - same unconditional, already-exported
resolver `send-corrigendum-alerts.ts`/`send-returnables-digest.ts`/`send-deadline-reminders.ts`
already use, no new migration or RPC needed (both go through the same
`company_notification_recipients()` call per that resolver's own header comment). Updated the
file's header comment, the recipients-before-claim inline comment, and every "Skipped (no opted-in
recipients)"/`"... skipped (no opted-in recipients)."` string (dry-run status + the final `main()`
summary line) to the already-established "Skipped (no recipients)" / "skipped (no recipients)"
wording `lib/senderCliArgs.ts`'s own `DryRunRow.status` type and `send-corrigendum-alerts.ts` already
use for this exact unconditional-resolver case, so the wording itself doesn't keep implying an
opt-in gate that no longer exists.

**Verified genuinely, red then green.** `scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` had 4 existing
tests (the `fdeab92`-era claim-ordering regression suite); none of them exercised the opt-in filter
itself - 2 even stubbed `daily_digest_opt_in: true` on their one mock recipient, which would have
masked this exact bug had it been present at the time. Added a 5th test,
`"sends regardless of daily_digest_opt_in"`, mocking a recipient with `daily_digest_opt_in: false`
(the real-world default for 32/33 companies) and asserting `skippedNoRecipients: 0`/`claimedCount:
1` - the opposite of what the pre-fix `operationalRecipients()` filter would produce for that exact
row. Updated the existing dry-run test's own expected status string to match the wording change.
Reverted ONLY the 2 functional lines (`operationalRecipients` import + call site) via a scripted
`python3` string-replace, keeping every test file change in place, and reran:
**exactly 1 of 5 failed** - the new test, `expected 1 to be +0` on `skippedNoRecipients` - exactly
the predicted failure, nothing else moved. Restored the fix the same way: **5/5 pass**. Full
regression after: `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, the same 3
pre-existing warnings. `npx vitest run` - **493/493, 63 files** (492 baseline + 1 new test, same 63
files). The `*.test.ts` node loop (no `--test` flag, real exit codes) - **28 files, 0 failures**,
unchanged. Full `engine/` sweep (real exit codes, not grep) - **86 files, 0 failures**, unchanged
(this fix touches no Python).

**Regression:** `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.ts` (1 import + 1 call site switched to
`criticalBidRecipients()`; header/inline comments updated; 2 dry-run/log status strings reworded
from "no opted-in recipients" to "no recipients"). `app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` (1
existing test's expected string updated, 1 new test added - 4 -> 5 tests). No other file touched -
`lib/notificationRecipients.ts` itself needed no change (`criticalBidRecipients()` already existed,
exported, used elsewhere).

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a one-import, one-call-site behavioural switch to an already-
existing, already-used, already-tested shared resolver, confined to a single already-isolated
sender script, plus its own test and wording updates. Does not touch RLS, the PayFast/money path,
any hard-stop gate, or what the production worker image installs/copies (`send-compliance-digest.ts`
runs only via `.github/workflows/compliance-alerts.yml`, GitHub Actions, not the worker image).

To verify independently: run `npx vitest run app/scripts/send-compliance-digest.spec.ts` and confirm

### Finding 164 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-but-same-shape - `app/billing/page.tsx`'s own team-count and bid-pack-quota reads discarded their Supabase/RPC `error`, rendering a real failure as a false "0 of X" right next to a sibling row that was already correctly guarded)

**Area:** Billing (`app/app/billing/page.tsx`), the "Current plan" card's "Team: N of X" and "Bid
packs this period: N of X" rows.

**Scenario:** broadened the search past the now-substantially-exhausted notification-engine sweep,
per this pass's own brief, into a fresh area (money/billing read paths - read-only, no change to
`start_payfast_checkout()` or any PayFast code, per the standing guardrail). `fetchCompanySubscription()`
(`lib/companySubscription.ts`) already distinguishes a genuine "no subscription row" from a real
read failure via its own `error` flag - a fix from the immediately-preceding 2026-11-06 standing
review pass, confirmed still in place and still correctly wired through to this page's own
`subscriptionError` banner. Reading the rest of the same page for the identical shape (not assumed
clean just because the headline case was already fixed) found two siblings that weren't: the
`Promise.all` fetching `memberCount` (`company_members` exact count) and `packsThisPeriod`
(`company_packs_this_period()` RPC, gated to `status === "active"`) destructured only `count`/`data`
- never `error` - from both calls. The page's own existing comment on the adjacent "Team" row
explains exactly this bug shape for a DIFFERENT failure point ("`membershipError`: `companyId`
never resolves, so `memberCount` would otherwise show a false '0 of X'... rather than genuinely
zero") but that comment, and the `membershipError` flag it reasons about, only covers the earlier,
separate `company_members.select("company_id")` lookup that resolves `companyId` itself - not
either of these two later queries' *own* failure. If `companyId` resolved fine but the count query
or the RPC itself then failed (a transient Supabase error, a timeout, an RPC-level exception), the
page rendered "couldn't load" nowhere and instead showed "0 of X" for the one it was really hiding
- a team with real members reads as having none, and (`status === "active"` only) a company that
has already used some of its monthly bid-pack quota reads as having used none of it. Traced the
real consequence rather than stopping at "returns a wrong display number": this page is read-only
display, not the gate - `request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()`
(migrations 0083/0084/0109/0115, independently re-verified by Findings 53/84 and PR #176's own
sweep) compute and enforce the real quota server-side on every actual request, so a false "0 used"
here cannot itself let a company over-consume its quota or bypass billing - but it is the exact
same "discarded read error rendered as a false-safe zero" shape this review's last four passes kept
finding in the notification engine (Findings 160-163), here on the one other customer-facing page
that shows a live usage number at all, and it directly misinforms a paying customer about their own
account state on the one page built specifically to show it to them.

**Fix:** captured `error` from both reads (`memberCountError`, `packsThisPeriodError`), added a
`console.error` for each (matching the existing `membershipError`/`companyError`/`subscriptionError`
convention elsewhere on this exact page), and widened both rows' existing "couldn't load" branch to
also fire on its own query's error, not only on the unrelated, earlier `membershipError`. Updated
the "Team" row's own comment to name both failure points it now actually covers, and added the same
style of comment to the "Bid packs this period" row, which had no explanatory comment at all before
this fix. No change to any Server Action, to the real quota-enforcement RPCs, or to the non-error
rendering path - only the previously-silent failure is now visible, same scope as Finding 144's
`document-scan/page.tsx` fix (`bc1e7b5`-era convention) this fix explicitly follows.

**Verification run myself, real exit codes - no red/green test, honest limitation, same as Finding
144.** This is a React Server Component page with no extracted testable logic and no existing test
file (`app/billing` has no `*.spec.ts`/`*.test.ts` anywhere - confirmed by `find` before concluding
this). Correctness rests on `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npx eslint .` (0 errors, the same 3

### Finding 167 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, near-zero live severity - `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s own AI-suggestion override detection could never actually fire, in the live pipeline only)

**Area:** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `gather()` (the SANRAL pack bridge's own
`pack_selections.yaml` construction, immediately before it calls
`engine/pack_generator/confirm_pack.py`'s `confirm()` to produce `pack.yaml`).

**This pass's angle:** findings 160-166's "discarded read error" sweep is exhausted (confirmed
again at the top of this pass, not re-litigated). Per the brief's option (a), read through the
actual pack-assembly pipeline (`engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`, `pdf_merge.py`,
`process_pack_jobs.py`, `engine/general/build_general_pack.py`, `fill_sbd_docx.py`,
`sanral_fill.py`, `make_envelope_covers.py`) for a correctness gap in the DELIVERABLE itself - a
wrong page, a missing attachment, a silently-wrong "ready" pack - rather than another notification-
plumbing instance. That specific shape came back clean: `pdf_merge.merge_with_contents()`'s own
`verify_pack()` read-back check is unconditionally called and unconditionally enforced before a job
is marked `ready` on BOTH pipelines (`process_pack_jobs.py` lines ~706-712 for SANRAL,
`process_general_jobs.py` lines ~751-752 for the general pack - both `raise RuntimeError` on any
problem, neither pipeline can reach "ready" with a page-count/contents-page/bookmark mismatch). The
SANRAL `front_count` edge case (an outer-envelope cover that itself failed to render) is already
guarded at the call site (`front_count=1 if sections[0]["pdf"] else 0`, confirmed by reading
`assemble_pack.py`'s own two call sites). Migration angle (option c) also came back clean: no
migration has landed after `0120` (confirmed, `ls app/supabase/migrations` - `0120` is still the
newest), and `0119`/`0120` are both anon-grant-revoke-only (no new table, RPC, or index - read both
in full), so there is no post-`0120` gap for `is_employee_in_company()` to close.

**What was actually found, while reading `gather()`'s own `pack_selections.yaml` construction
(line ~613-617 before this fix):**
```python
"suggested_person": (f"person_{index_of[by_code[p['code']]['suggested_person_id']]}"
                     if by_code[p["code"]].get("suggested_person_id") in index_of else None),
```
`index_of` (built a few lines above from `person_ids = [signatory["id"]] + [confirmed_person_id for
each required position]`) holds an index ONLY for the signatory and each position's own CONFIRMED
person - never for a person the AI suggested but the human did NOT pick. So the one case this field
exists to flag - `suggested_person_id != confirmed_person_id`, a real override - is exactly the case
where `suggested_person_id in index_of` is false (that person's row was never fetched into this
job's own reduced `people`/`index_of` set), so `suggested_person` silently becomes `None`.
`confirm_pack.confirm()`'s own override detection (`if sel.get("suggested_person") and person_id !=
sel["suggested_person"]:`) then never fires, because `sel.get("suggested_person")` is falsy -
`pack.yaml`'s own `_provenance.overrides` note always reads "none - every position was assigned its
top-suggested candidate", **even on a tender where a human genuinely overrode the AI's
suggestion for a position.** Confirmed this is a real, reproducible logic gap, not a guess: traced
`index_of`'s own construction (`person_ids`), confirmed `suggested_person_id` is a real, separately-
written DB column (`app/app/tenders/[id]/pack-inputs-actions.ts` writes it distinct from
`confirmed_person_id` when a position is first scored) that a human can and does diverge from when
confirming a position on the Tender Workspace.

**Why this is a real but near-zero-severity finding, not force-fit as a 160-166-shaped bug:** traced
every consumer of `pack.yaml`'s own `_provenance` block (`grep -rn "_provenance" engine/`) - only
`engine/fill_financial_hours.py` reads `_provenance.contract`, and NOTHING reads
`_provenance.overrides` anywhere in this codebase (confirmed: `grep -rn "\"overrides\"" engine/`
returns only this file's own writer and the unrelated `pack["tender"].get("overrides")` guard in
`fill_tender.py`/`fill_conventional.py`, which is a different field entirely - a defence against a
LEGACY hand-written pack.yaml overriding SANRAL's own pre-filled SETUP cells, not this one). The
actual submitted pack is unaffected either way: `confirm_pack.py` builds `pack_people`/`key_persons`
from `confirmed_person` alone, never from `suggested_person` - the right person's CV/project data
was always going into the right form regardless of this bug. `pack.yaml` itself is a transient
working file (`work = tempfile.mkdtemp(...)`, `shutil.rmtree(work, ...)` unless `--keep` debugging
is passed) - never uploaded, never stored, never read back by anything after the job finishes. And
the one place a human would actually want to see "AI suggested X, you picked Y" - the Tender
Workspace itself - already shows it correctly, straight from the same `tender_pack_assignments.
suggested_person_id`/`confirmed_person_id` columns (`app/app/tenders/[id]/compliance-data.ts`,
`page.tsx`), entirely independent of `pack.yaml`. So this bug's full blast radius is: one internal,
ephemeral, nothing-else-reads-it string inside a file that gets deleted. Reported and fixed anyway
(cheap, safe, genuinely wrong), but explicitly NOT claimed as a customer-facing defect.

**Fix:** added `_suggested_person_label(assignment, index_of)` - when `suggested_person_id` resolves
to an index in `index_of` (always true when it equals `confirmed_person_id`, i.e. no override),
returns the same `"person_N"` label `confirmed_person` would get; when it does NOT resolve (a real
override - the person's row was never fetched), returns the raw `suggested_person_id` UUID instead
of `None`. `confirm_pack.py`'s own override check only ever compares this string for equality and
then prints/stores both raw strings in the override note - it never looks `suggested_person` up in
its own `people` map - so a label that doesn't resolve to a `"person_N"` index still correctly flags
the override (just a less pretty string in an already-internal, already-ephemeral note). Zero
changes to `pack_people`, `key_persons`, `profile`, or anything the real forms are filled from.

**Verification, real exit codes, red-then-green (not the honest-limitation precedent used for
untestable RSC pages - this is a plain Python function, fully unit-testable).** Added
`test_suggested_person_label_flags_a_real_override_even_when_unresolved()` to
`engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (3 cases: no override resolves to the same `person_N` as
confirmed; a real override still returns a non-`None`, non-matching label; no suggestion on file at
all stays `None`). RED: reverted `_suggested_person_label()`'s own `else sid` to the old `else None`
(`Edit` in place) and ran `python3 engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` - **1 failure**, the
predicted one and only one (`FAIL real override: still returns a label...`), real exit code **1**.
Restored the fix, re-ran - **0 failures**, real exit code **0**. Then the full standard: full
`engine/` sweep (every `test_*.py`, real exit codes, not grepped) - **86 files, 0 failures**. `npm
run typecheck` - **0 errors**. `npx eslint .` - **0 errors**, same 3 pre-existing warnings. `npx
vitest run` - **493/493, 63 files**, unchanged (this fix touches no TypeScript). The `*.test.ts`
node loop (`node --experimental-strip-types <file>` per file, real exit codes) - **28 files, 0
failures**, unchanged. `npx next build` - compiled successfully, same route table, `Proxy
(Middleware)` present (unaffected by this Python-only change, run anyway as a final sanity check).
`git fetch origin main` both before starting this pass and immediately before pushing: HEAD matched
`origin/main` exactly both times (`d925926`), no sibling commits landed during this pass.

**Regression:** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` (one new ~25-line helper function,
`_suggested_person_label()`, plus its one call site changed from an inline conditional to a call to
it - no other line touched) and `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (one new test function). No
other file touched.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a small, fully-unit-tested, well-isolated Python logic fix with zero
effect on the real pack's filled content and zero RLS/money/hard-stop/worker-image-install surface.

To verify independently: read `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `_suggested_person_label()` and

### Finding 168 (CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED - reported for Sarel's own judgment, same treatment as the
`start_payfast_checkout()` revenue-integrity item - a yearly-billing company's bid-pack quota
resets only once a YEAR, even though every plan's `max_packs_per_month` is an explicitly MONTHLY
allowance)

**Area:** `company_packs_this_period(p_company_id uuid)` (`app/supabase/migrations/0115_pack_quota_
regression_and_request_race.sql`, lines 69-85, the live, current definition - re-merged 2026-11-04
after 0109 regressed it, unchanged by 0116-0120, confirmed by `grep -rn "company_packs_this_period"
app/supabase/migrations/` showing only 0083/0084/0096/0101(reference only)/0109/0115/0120(grant-
revoke only) ever touch it). The one quota-counting RPC `company_can_request_pack()` and both real
insert gates (`request_submission_pack_checked()`, `request_general_job_checked()`, same file) call
before letting a company request a new bid pack; also the one number `app/app/billing/page.tsx`
shows as "Bid packs this period: X of {max_packs_per_month}".

**This pass's angle:** per the brief's option (c), a read-only investigation of the quota-counting
RPC's own SQL in the migrations for an off-by-one/timezone/billing-period-boundary bug. `engine/cv/`
(64 mentions in this file) and `engine/general/` (103 mentions) were both checked first via `grep -c`
per the brief's own "heavily mined, skip" instruction and both came back far above a reasonable
threshold for the "wrong not missing field" shape without a clear untouched angle, so this pass
moved to (c) rather than force a CV/general re-sweep. `grep -i "yearly"` across both spec files first,
to make sure this exact shape wasn't already found and deliberately deferred - the only yearly-
billing hits are an unrelated privilege-escalation bug (`start_payfast_checkout()` lacking a role
check, fixed by 0117) and the already-documented `start_payfast_checkout()` grants-before-ITN timing
item (2026-11-07e) - neither is this bug.

**What was found, reading `company_packs_this_period()`'s own body:**
```sql
select count(*)::integer
from pack_generation_jobs
where company_id = p_company_id
  and status in ('requested', 'generating', 'ready')
  and requested_at >= (
    select coalesce(current_period_start, created_at) from company_subscriptions where company_id = p_company_id
  )
```
This counts every in-flight-or-finished pack since `current_period_start` - no upper bound, and no
re-derivation of a monthly window at all. `current_period_start` is set to `now()` in exactly one
place in the whole codebase outside this function's own migration history - `apply_payfast_itn()`
(`0112_payfast_itn_amount_verification.sql` line 100 and line 125) - and ONLY on a successful
('COMPLETE') PayFast ITN, i.e. once per real recurring charge (confirmed: `grep -rln
"current_period_start"` across `engine/`, `app/`, migrations other than the RPC's own hits only
the two `apply_payfast_itn()` branches and the column's own `0083` migration comment - no monthly
cron, no other write path anywhere). `lib/payfast.ts`'s own `PAYFAST_FREQUENCY` confirms PayFast is
told to bill `monthly` interval subscriptions every month (code 3) and `yearly` interval
subscriptions every 12 months (code 6, `developers.payfast.co.za`'s own documented codes) - so for a
`billing_interval = 'yearly'` company, the ITN that resets `current_period_start` fires roughly once
a YEAR, not once a month. Meanwhile `max_packs_per_month` is explicitly, by name and by
`lib/billing.ts`'s own header comment ("plans differing only by seat count and monthly bid-pack
volume"), a MONTHLY allowance - identical for a Professional company whether they pay monthly or
pay for the whole year up front (`yearlyPriceZar()` just discounts the same monthly rate ×10, it
does not scale the pack allowance). `company_packs_this_period()` has no logic anywhere to re-derive
a rolling monthly window inside a yearly billing period - "this period" for a yearly biller really
does mean the whole 12-month span between ITNs, not a month.

**Net effect:** a yearly-billing company that uses its full monthly allotment once, early in its
12-month billing cycle, stays capped at that same count - and blocked from requesting any more bid
packs at all - for the remaining ~11 months, instead of getting a fresh `max_packs_per_month` every
single month the way a monthly-billing company on the identical plan does. This is the opposite of
"might let a company exceed its quota" - it is a real, severe UNDER-grant: a paying yearly customer
on Professional (R2,990/mo equivalent, paid annually) gets roughly 1/12th of the bid-pack volume a
monthly-billing Professional customer gets across the same year, for the same money, purely because
of how `current_period_start` happens to be re-stamped.

**Live-reproduced in a disposable scratch Postgres** (`service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c
"psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE scratch_quota168'"`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d
scratch_quota168`, all 110 migrations applied clean; dropped and `service postgresql stop`
afterward - nothing left running). Seeded one company, `billing_interval = 'yearly'`,
`plan_tier = 'professional'`, `status = 'active'`, `max_packs_per_month = 15` (the real Professional
number), `current_period_start = now() - 11 months`, `current_period_end = now() + 1 month` (i.e. an
ITN-driven annual renewal 11 months ago, due again in 1 month - the ordinary middle of a yearly
cycle). Inserted exactly 15 `pack_generation_jobs` rows (`status = 'ready'`), all `requested_at`
dated to 11 months ago (month 1 of this billing year) - the company's real, full, legitimately-used
monthly allotment, used once, 11 months in the past, with ZERO packs requested since. As that
company's own `owner` (`set role authenticated; select set_config('test.uid', ...)`, this repo's own
stub convention): `select company_packs_this_period(...)` returned **15** (should be 0 - nothing
requested in the current, 11-months-later, calendar month), `select company_can_request_pack(...)`
returned **false** (should be true - 0 of 15 used so far this month). Called the real, live gate a
genuine pack request goes through, `select request_general_job_checked(..., 'generate_pack')`, with
no other state changed: it **raised** `"You've reached your plan's bid pack limit for this period -
upgrade on the Billing page to generate more."` - the exact user-facing error a real customer would
hit, 11 months into a 12-month cycle, having requested nothing in 11 months.

**Why this is reported, not fixed, this pass - deliberately, not left for lack of time.** The
correct SQL fix is not mechanical: it requires deciding what "this period" should mean for a yearly
biller specifically a product-policy call, not a QA one. Candidate semantics differ in real,
customer-visible ways Sarel would need to pick between, e.g.: (a) a rolling monthly window anchored
to the billing anniversary day-of-month (needs the same day-of-month-overflow care `lib/payfast.ts`'s
own `nextPeriodEnd()` already documents fixing once, for `addMonths()` vs bare `setMonth()`, so as
not to introduce a sibling leap/short-month bug while fixing this one); (b) a plain calendar-month
window (`date_trunc('month', now())`), simpler but not anniversary-aligned; or (c) treating a yearly
plan's allowance as `max_packs_per_month * 12` available for the whole year up front, if that is
actually the intended trade-off for paying annually (nothing in `lib/billing.ts`'s pricing comments
says so, but it's a legitimate alternative design). This is the same shape of call the standing
guardrail already reserves for `start_payfast_checkout()`'s revenue-integrity gap (2026-11-07e) -
adjacent to real money and quota-enforcement, not a display bug - so, per this pass's own brief,
reported for Sarel's judgment rather than guessed at and pushed to `main` or opened as a PR on a
semantics nobody has confirmed.

To verify independently: replay all 110 migrations onto a scratch Postgres
(`engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d <db>`), seed a company exactly as above (yearly
Professional, `current_period_start` 11 months ago, 15 `ready` jobs dated to month 1 of that period,
nothing since), and confirm `company_packs_this_period()` returns 15 and `company_can_request_pack()`
returns false as that company's own member. Read `app/supabase/migrations/0115_pack_quota_
regression_and_request_race.sql` lines 69-85 and confirm there is no month-window re-derivation in
the function body. Read `app/lib/payfast.ts`'s `PAYFAST_FREQUENCY` (monthly=3, yearly=6) and
`app/supabase/migrations/0112_payfast_itn_amount_verification.sql` lines 96-101/121-131 and confirm
`current_period_start` is set to `now()` only on a successful ITN, which for `yearly` fires roughly
once a year, not once a month.

### Finding 169 (CONFIRMED, FIXED - open as **PR #182**, not merged this pass -
`company_packs_this_period()`/`company_can_request_pack()` bypassed PR #176/0117's own "employee
has no billing access" RESTRICTIVE policy entirely)

**Area:** `company_packs_this_period(p_company_id uuid)` and `company_can_request_pack(p_company_id
uuid)` (`app/supabase/migrations/0115_pack_quota_regression_and_request_race.sql`, lines 69-120, the
live definitions prior to this pass's own fix below) - both `SECURITY DEFINER`, both `grant execute
... to authenticated`, both directly `supabase.rpc()`-callable by any signed-in user, not only
through `app/app/billing/page.tsx` (the one app page that calls the first of the two).

**This pass's angle:** per the brief's option (c) - a fresh RLS angle, specifically whether any
SECURITY DEFINER RPC touched by migrations 0093-0120 has an employee-visibility gap the still-open
PR #176 (its own 0119, "12 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs bypassed employee RLS entirely") didn't catch. Read
PR #176's own diff in full first (`mcp__github__pull_request_read`, `get_files`) to get its exact
12-function list and its own explicitly-excluded list (`create_company_invite_checked`,
`remove_member_checked`, `set_member_role_checked`, `set_my_daily_digest_opt_in`,
`create_company_and_join`, every `platform_admin_*` function, the `tt_*_check` trigger helpers) -
then cross-checked that list against every `supabase.rpc("...")` name actually called anywhere in
`app/` (`grep -rohE 'rpc\("[a-z_0-9]+"' app`). Two names - `company_packs_this_period` and
`company_can_request_pack` - are client-callable, SECURITY DEFINER, read company-scoped billing data
company_subscriptions holds, and appear in NEITHER PR #176's fixed-12 list NOR its explicitly-
excluded list - a genuine gap in an otherwise very thorough sweep, not something PR #176 considered
and dismissed.

**What was found, reading both functions' own bodies (0115, the live definition before this fix):**
```sql
-- company_packs_this_period:
select case when is_company_member(p_company_id) then (...) else null end;
-- company_can_request_pack:
if not is_company_member(p_company_id) then return null; end if;
```
Neither checks `is_employee_in_company()` - only `is_company_member()`, which is true for an
employee too. Migration 0117 (2026-11-06, "billing employee role gap") added a RESTRICTIVE
`"company_subscriptions: employee has no access" ... for all ... using (not
is_employee_in_company(company_id))` policy specifically so an employee-role member can never read
or act on `company_subscriptions`. Both of these functions are SECURITY DEFINER and read
`company_subscriptions`/`pack_generation_jobs` directly inside their own function body - which runs
as the function owner and bypasses ALL table RLS, RESTRICTIVE policies included, the exact "a
RESTRICTIVE select policy on `company_subscriptions` does not, by itself, stop a SECURITY DEFINER
function ... from [reading] a different table's row by company_id" risk 0117's own header already
named for `start_payfast_checkout()` - just never swept for these two.

**Live-reproduced in a disposable scratch Postgres** (`service postgresql start` as `postgres`;
`CREATE DATABASE scratch_billing170`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d
scratch_billing170`, all 110 migrations applied clean). Seeded one company (`professional`/
`monthly`/`active`, `max_packs_per_month = 15`, one `ready` pack job), one `owner` member, one
`employee` member. As the employee (`set role authenticated; select set_config('test.uid', ...)`):
`select count(*) from company_subscriptions where company_id = ...` correctly returned **0** (0117's
own RESTRICTIVE policy doing its job) - but `select company_packs_this_period(...)` returned **1**
(the real count, not null) and `select company_can_request_pack(...)` returned **true** (the real
answer, not null). Both SECURITY DEFINER functions handed the employee the company's real billing-
quota state despite the underlying table itself being correctly locked down. As the owner, both
returned the same real values unaffected - confirming the gap was role-specific, not a general
breakage.

**Live app-layer impact is limited but the RPC-level gap is real:** `/billing`'s own page derives its
`status` from a direct `company_subscriptions` read (`fetchCompanySubscription()`), which 0117
already blocks for an employee - so the page's own call to `company_packs_this_period` (gated on
`status === "active"`) never actually fires for that role in practice. The exposure is a direct
`supabase.rpc()` call bypassing the page entirely - same shape and same severity class as the 12 PR
#176 already fixed, which is why this is fixed the same way, not left as display-layer-only.

**Fixed; opened as PR #182 (`fix/employee-billing-quota-rpc-gap`), not pushed directly to `main`** -
this is RLS/money-adjacent surface (a `SECURITY DEFINER` function gaining a role check, on the
billing-quota path), the same guardrail category PR #176 itself went through rather than a direct
commit, so this pass followed the same path rather than treat its own read of "this one's small and
additive" as license to bypass that guardrail. Not merged by this pass, per the standing instruction
never to merge a PR without Sarel's own explicit go-ahead.

Migration `0121_pack_quota_rpcs_employee_gap.sql` (on the PR branch): both functions now also
return `null` for an employee, extending the EXISTING "null means no answer for this caller"
contract 0109 already established for a non-member, rather than inventing a new raise/error shape
neither function had before. For owner/admin/member, `is_employee_in_company()` is false, so
behaviour for every other role is completely unchanged - re-verified, not assumed: re-ran the same
scratch-DB repro post-fix (employee now gets `null`/`null`; owner, and a plain `member` role added
for completeness, both still get the real `1`/`true`; a non-existent/non-member company still
correctly returns `null`). Added a permanent regression test to
`engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s existing `part2_employee_role()` (section `[18]`, two
new checks alongside the sibling `company_tender_preferences` check 0118 already added there) rather
than a new section, since this is the same employee-role fixture already in place. Full suite
(`TENANT_PSQL=... python3 engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`) - **ALL PASSED**, 250 checks, 0
failures, real exit code 0 (captured directly, not through a swallowing pipe); part1-only (no
`TENANT_PSQL`) also exits 0. Full `engine/` sweep (86 `test_*.py` files run individually, real exit
codes) - 0 failures, matching baseline exactly, confirming this SQL-only change touched nothing else.
Scratch databases dropped and `postgresql` service stopped afterward.

To verify independently: check out PR #182's branch (`fix/employee-billing-quota-rpc-gap`), replay
all 111 migrations (110 plus its own 0121) onto a scratch Postgres, seed a company/owner/employee as
above, and confirm `company_packs_this_period()` and `company_can_request_pack()` both return `null`
for the employee and their real values for the owner. Run `TENANT_PSQL="psql -U postgres -d <db>"
python3 engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` and confirm `ALL PASSED` including the two new
`[18]` checks naming these functions by name.

### Finding 170 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `classify_tender.py`'s own `CLOSING_TIME_RE` and `find_delivery_address()` both returned `None` on a real, current, open-for-bidding SANRAL Book 1, silently losing the real closing time and tender-box address a general-family pack build would otherwise have recorded automatically)

**Area:** Intake (`engine/intake/classify_tender.py` - `CLOSING_TIME_RE`/`find_closing_time()` and
`_address_lines_after()`/`find_delivery_address()`, both called from `process_general_jobs.py`'s own
SANRAL-route branch when a tender's closing date/delivery address aren't already recorded).

**Scenario:** fetched a REAL, live, currently-open SANRAL tender document (N.003-010-2027/3R, "THE
UPGRADE OF NATIONAL ROUTE 3 SECTION 1", found via web search, downloaded directly from its own public
tender-documents host) and ran this module's own functions against its real extracted text, rather
than only the fixtures already committed. `find_closing_time()` and `find_delivery_address()` BOTH
returned `None` on this real document, even though both values are clearly, explicitly stated in it.
`find_nra_reference()` worked correctly (confirmed against the real text too).

**Two distinct gaps in `CLOSING_TIME_RE`, both on the SAME real sentence** (clause C.2.15, SANRAL's
own numbered Tender Data clause: *"The closing time for submission of tender offers is Friday, 12H00
on the 24 July 2026"*):
1. A day-of-week name ("Friday,") sits between "is" and the time - the regex required the time
   immediately after "is", with no allowance for this.
2. "for submission of tender offers" - the regex's optional infix only ever accepted "for (the)
   receipt of tenders", the ONE phrasing this module's own docstring had confirmed (from R.396 Book
   1 T-6) - this is a second, equally real SANRAL phrasing for the identical clause, on a different
   real contract.

Without either fix, `process_general_jobs.py`'s own documented fallback silently substituted the
11:00 placeholder for this real tender's own stated 12:00 closing time - a currently-open tender a
real company could be building a pack for today.

**One gap in `_address_lines_after()`**: `DELIVERY_RE`'s own match on "tender box at:\n" is
immediately followed, on this real document, by a short sub-heading restating the anchor itself
("Location of tender box:") before the real address lines start. That heading isn't an address line,
but it isn't a disqualifying SENTENCE either - it was only ever caught by the function's own
"tender/must/shall" stop-word guard because it happens to repeat "tender box", the anchor's own
words, not because it signals real prose. `find_delivery_address()` returned `None` on this real
document even though the real address was right there, one line further down.

**Fixed:** `CLOSING_TIME_RE` widened with an optional day-of-week-name alternation before the time,
and the "for ... of ..." infix widened to accept "submission of tender offers" alongside "receipt of
tenders". `_address_lines_after()` now skips (not collects, not a stop) a short (≤40 char),
colon-ending heading line, but only before any real address line has been seen - a heading
appearing mid-address still correctly ends collection, unchanged.

**Verified red-then-green, against both the real document AND new fixtures.** Confirmed all three
functions return the real, correct values when run directly against the downloaded document's own
extracted text (`closing_time: 12:00`, the real 4-line Provincial Office address, `nra: NRA
2026/0631`) - before the fix, the first two returned `None`. New checks in
`test_classify_tender.py` using the real phrasings as fixtures. Reverted `classify_tender.py` via
`git apply -R`, re-ran - exactly the 3 new checks failed as predicted, nothing else; reapplied -
`0 failure(s)`. `py_compile` clean. Regression: `test_process_general_jobs.py`,
`engine/discovery/test_assess_tender.py`, `test_make_envelope_covers.py`, `test_form_field_audit.py`
- all `0 failure(s)`.

**Regression:** `engine/intake/classify_tender.py` (`CLOSING_TIME_RE`, `_address_lines_after()`, ~25
lines including comments); `engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` (3 new checks appended to the
existing closing-time/delivery-address test functions). No change to `find_nra_reference()`,
`discrepancies()`, or any other function in this file.

tenders state the clause as "closing DATE AND TIME ... is", and in every one of those 4 the real
sentence states the DATE first and the TIME second - the exact mirror of the already-handled

- CONTRACT SANRAL - N.003-010-2020/2R: *"The closing date and time for receipt of tenders is

- CONTRACT SANRAL - N.002-267-2024/2R: *"The closing date and time for receipt of tenders is 04

- CONTRACT SANRAL: C.003-081-2023/1: *"The closing date and time for receipt of tenders is 26
  November 2026 @ 11:00 AM (South African Time)."*

(The other 4 fetched - CONTRACT SANRAL N.002-160-2027/1F, C.004-086-2022/1F, NRA 2026/0759 (E), and

schedule or an addendum), e.g. (cidb 004 2627, Awarded):

> Appointment of a service provider for electrical infrastructure upgrade project: supply and
> install a 1250 KVA transformer...&lt;a href="https://www.cidb.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/
> Annexure-B-Transformer-and-Electrical-Installations-Unpriced-BOQ.xlsx" target="_blank"
> style="color:#b62836;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Click here&lt;/a&gt; to download the Pricing Schedule.

`normalize()` only ever built `documents` from `tender_advert_file`/`tender_briefing_file` - this
second, real document (a pricing schedule or addendum PDF/XLSX, 8 of 25 rows: cidb 002/004/005/012/
017(x2)/018/019/020-2526/2627) was never added to `documents` at all, and since `sh.clean()` only
normalizes whitespace (never strips tags), the literal `<a href=...>Click here</a>` HTML stayed in
`title`/`description` verbatim - both a silently-dropped real document (the same "silently lost
real data" impact the `classify_tender.py` findings above all share) and literal markup leaking
into whatever shows or reads that text (the app's own tender description display, and this
description string is also what feeds a fit-assessment LLM call downstream if this source is ever
scored the way `assess_tender.py` scores others - noise in that input either way).

One row (cidb 005 2526) has a genuinely malformed tag on the live site's own markup - `href=https:/
/www.cidb.org.za/.../annexure-a....xlsx"` (closing quote present, opening quote missing) - confirmed
real, not a hypothetical edge case invented for the fix.

Only 1 of the 34 rows is currently `realstatus: "Open"` (`fetch_releases()` filters to `Open` only,
so only Open rows actually reach `normalize()` in the real pipeline today), and that one row's own
description happens to be plain text - so this gap has zero live impact on `main` *today*, but the
32% base rate on this exact feed (8 of 25 Awarded/Closed rows checked) makes it a near-certainty on
a future Open row, not a one-off. Reported as a real, evidence-backed gap on exactly that basis, the
same "not live yet but real and reachable" framing the 2026-11-07hh pass used for the CI path-filter
gap on PR #181.

**Fixed:** added `_extract_description_links()` to `cidb_tenders.py` - finds any `<a href=...>...
</a>` embedded in the raw `description` (tolerating the missing-opening-quote shape above), pulls
each one out as a `{"title", "url"}` document (titled from the trailing "to download &lt;X&gt;"
text when present, else the anchor's own text), and returns the description with all such tags
stripped so the plain English sentence remains readable without the markup. `normalize()` merges
these into `documents` alongside the existing `tender_advert_file`/`tender_briefing_file` entries
(de-duplicated by URL) and uses the stripped text for both `title` and `description`. No change to
any other reader, `source_http.clean()` itself (left alone - no evidence any other reader's feed
embeds raw HTML in a text field the way cidb's does), or `fetch_releases()`'s Open-only filter.

**Verified red-then-green against the real row and a new fixture, plus the real malformed-quote
row.** Confirmed directly in Python against the real live feed (`https://www.cidb.org.za/
tenders.json`) that `_extract_description_links()` recovers the real `.xlsx` document URL and titles

### Finding 174 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `general-workspace.tsx`'s and `intake-card.tsx`'s own primary `tenders` select each discarded its read error, so a transient failure there was indistinguishable from "no such tender"/"nothing to show" and silently blanked real sections with no indication anything went wrong)

**Area:** Tender Workspace `.tsx` components, the one surface this chain's own earlier Server
Actions sweep (`a3ffb9e`, `2026-11-07vii`) explicitly never touched - every `.tsx` file under
`app/app/tenders/[id]/` and the remaining ~215 lines of `actions.ts` beyond line ~440, per this
pass's own handoff.

**Scenario:** read every `.tsx` file under `app/app/tenders/[id]/` in full (39 files) and finished
`actions.ts` to its end (line 656) - the fresh surface this chain had never opened. Two files repeat
this chain's dominant bug class (discarded Supabase/fetch errors treated as empty state, Findings
144/147/164-166) on their own gating read, each with real, non-cosmetic consequences:

- `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-workspace.tsx`'s `GeneralTenderWorkspace()` (the whole non-SANRAL
  tender-preparation component) opens with `const { data: tender } = await supabase.from("tenders")
  .select(...).eq("id", tenderId).maybeSingle(); if (!tender) return null;` - no `error` captured.
  `page.tsx` renders every one of this function's 5 returned sections
  (`overview`/`documents`/`questions`/`people`/`pack`) via optional chaining
  (`generalSections?.overview`, etc. - confirmed by reading every one of those 6 call sites in
  `page.tsx`), so a `null` return (whether from a genuine missing tender or a transient read
  failure) renders every one of those slots as nothing at all, across every tab, with zero banner
  anywhere on the page. `page.tsx`'s own header comment on its `try/catch` around this exact call
  (lines ~508-517) explicitly documents the intended design - "one bad read degrades to a friendly
  ErrorBanner... instead of throwing and 500-ing the whole tender workspace" - but that `try/catch`
  only ever catches a *thrown* exception; a Supabase client never throws on a query error, it
  returns `{data: null, error}`, so the already-wired `complianceError` banner (shown once, in the
  Overview tab, right where `generalSections?.overview` sits) was never actually reachable for this
  read's own failures - the one case that comment's own reasoning was written for.
- `app/app/tenders/[id]/intake-card.tsx`'s `IntakeCard()` ("How this tender was read") has the
  identical shape on its own first `tenders` select - `if (!tender) return null;`, no `error`
  captured - silently hiding that whole card (intake routing, fingerprint check, SANRAL templates
  found, fit-for-company verdict) on a transient failure, with nothing to say so. Unlike
  `general-workspace.tsx`, `IntakeCard` is mounted via plain JSX (`<IntakeCard tenderId={id} />`,
  `page.tsx` line 1214) rather than one of `page.tsx`'s own `try/catch`-wrapped direct calls, so
  rethrowing here would genuinely 500 the whole page instead of degrading - confirmed by reading
  `page.tsx`'s own header comment distinguishing the two calling conventions before picking a fix.

Both read `tenders` a SECOND time (the outer `page.tsx` has already read the same table
successfully to get this far) purely for their own component-local fields, so a transient failure
specific to this second, redundant query is a real, reachable case - RLS/connection-pool hiccups
affect one query at a time, not the whole request.

**Fixed:** `general-workspace.tsx` now captures `error: tenderError` on that select and rethrows it
(`if (tenderError) throw tenderError;`) before the existing `if (!tender) return null;` - this is
exactly the case `page.tsx`'s own `try/catch` around this call was written to catch, so a real read
failure now surfaces as the same `complianceError` `ErrorBanner` ("Couldn't load the compliance
check...") in the Overview tab that `ComplianceReport`'s own read failures already use, instead of
silently bypassing that machinery. `intake-card.tsx` now captures the same error and, since
rethrowing there would 500 the page instead of degrading (see above), returns an inline destructive
banner ("Couldn't load how this tender was read - try refreshing.") instead - the same safe,
component-local pattern `activity-log.tsx`'s own `membershipError` branch already uses elsewhere on
this exact page. Neither file's "no such tender"/"nothing to show yet" branch changed at all - only
the previously-undistinguished failure case.

**Verification run myself, real exit codes - no red/green test, honest limitation, same as Findings
144/164/165/166.** Neither component has extracted testable logic or its own test file (`find
. -iname "*.test.ts*"` under `app/app/tenders/[id]/` turns up only pure-logic files -
`general-pack-review-logic.test.ts`, `won-project-sync-logic.test.ts`, `signatory-logic.test.ts`,
`tender-readiness.test.ts`, `pack-review-logic.test.ts` - none touching either component's own
Supabase read). Correctness rests on `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npx eslint .` (0 errors, the
same 3 pre-existing warnings), `npx next build` (compiled successfully in the same route table,
`/tenders/[id]` still a Partial Prerender route), and a plain reading of the diff (each file's
"tender not found" branch is byte-for-byte unchanged; only a new `tenderError` branch was added
before it). `npx vitest run` - **493/493, 63 files**, unchanged. The `*.test.ts` node loop (no
`--test` flag, real exit codes) - **28 files, 0 failures**, unchanged. Full `engine/` sweep not
re-run - this fix touches no Python.

**Regression:** `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-workspace.tsx` (+7 lines) and
`app/app/tenders/[id]/intake-card.tsx` (+16 lines) only. No other file touched.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a read-only display-component fix on a newly-captured, newly-logged
error flag, no RLS/money/hard-stop/worker-image-install surface touched, same category and
direct-push precedent Findings 164-166/170-173 all used.
