### Finding 175 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - the Pipeline board's and Pricing history's shared "Credit for the submission" `<select>` silently wiped a real credit/commission attribution on ANY unrelated save, whenever its own `people` read came back empty)

**Area:** `app/app/pipeline/economics-form.tsx` (`EconomicsForm`, shared by `/pipeline` and
`/pipeline/pricing`), fed by `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` and `app/app/pipeline/pricing/page.tsx`'s
own discarded `people`-select errors.

**How this was found.** Finding 174 closed out `app/app/tenders/[id]/` after 6 consecutive
negatives there; this pass's own brief named `app/app/pipeline/pricing/` as a genuinely fresh
surface (touched once by PR #180, but the `pricing` subpage itself never swept). Read
`app/app/pipeline/pricing/page.tsx` in full: its `Promise.all` destructures `tender_packs`' own
`error` and renders a banner on it, but discards the sibling `people` select's `error` entirely
(`const [{ data: packs, error }, { data: peopleRows }, { data: opportunities }] = await
Promise.all([...])`) - the exact dominant bug class this review tracks. Tracing the consequence
turned up something this review's own prior pass on `/pipeline` (Finding 165's "genuinely clean"
writeup) had judged too quickly: Finding 165 checked `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s own `peopleRows`
and found it fed only "a verdict badge per card, an assignee-name map... a real failure there means
a missing badge or blank assignee name, not a false '0 of X' fact; thin, but not this bug shape" -
true for that page's own direct uses, but it never followed `peopleRows` into the shared
`EconomicsForm` component both pages hand it to as their `people` prop, which is where the real,
severe consequence actually lives.

`EconomicsForm`'s "Credit for the submission" `<select>` is built as `defaultValue={economics
?.submitted_by_person_id ?? ""}` with one `<option>` per entry in `people`, plus a hardcoded `""`
("Nobody yet") - no fallback option for an id not in `people`. When the `people` read fails (or,
less commonly, the credited person is since removed), `people` is `[]`/missing that id, so the
`<select>`'s `defaultValue` matches NO `<option>` - the browser silently renders its first option
("Nobody yet", value `""`) as selected instead, with nothing on screen to say the real pick is
anything other than "nobody". This is already a false-display instance of the dominant bug class -
but this form's own save path (`saveTenderEconomics`, `app/app/pipeline/actions.ts` line 107:
`submitted_by_person_id: typeof personId === "string" && personId ? personId : null`) always
writes `person_id` fresh from EVERY submit of this form, together with price/VAT/commission/sector/
note in one `.update()`. So the very next time anyone saves ANY other field on this form - correcting
the price, say - while the `people` read happened to have failed for that render, the browser
resubmits `person_id=""`, and `saveTenderEconomics` writes `submitted_by_person_id: null`,
**silently and permanently erasing a real, previously-recorded credit/commission attribution**,
with zero error anywhere, triggered by someone doing something that has nothing to do with the
credited person at all. This is the same root cause (a discarded `people`-select error) as the
dominant bug class, but a more severe variant than this review has flagged before: not a false
*read*, a silent, persisted *write* that destroys real data.

On `/pipeline/pricing/page.tsx` specifically, the same discarded `peopleRows` error additionally
makes the page's own name column (`person: p.submitted_by_person_id ? nameById.get(p
.submitted_by_person_id) ?? "(removed person)" : null`) falsely claim every single credited person
was "(removed person)" on a transient failure - the familiar false-display shape Findings 164/165
already fixed elsewhere, compounding the write-path bug above on the exact same page.

**Fixed, in three parts:**
1. **`app/lib/dealEconomics.ts`:** added a tiny pure helper, `needsCreditFallbackOption
(assignedPersonId, people)`, returning whether the currently-credited person is missing from the
loaded `people` list (true whether that's a discarded read error upstream or a genuine removal).
2. **`app/app/pipeline/economics-form.tsx`:** the `<select>` now renders a synthetic `<option
value={assignedPersonId}>(unavailable right now - keeping this pick)</option>` whenever
`needsCreditFallbackOption` is true, so `defaultValue` always matches a real `<option>` and an
unrelated save can never again silently null out a real attribution. The happy path (person
resolved normally) renders byte-for-byte as before - the new option only ever appears when it is
needed.
3. **`app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` and `app/app/pipeline/pricing/page.tsx`:** both now capture `error:
peopleError` on their own `people` select and `console.error` it (logged, not gated - the
`EconomicsForm` fix above already makes the credited value safe regardless, so these are
visibility-only). `pricing/page.tsx`'s own name column additionally now says "(couldn't load name)"
instead of the false "(removed person)" specifically when `peopleError` is set, leaving the genuine-
removal case worded exactly as before.

**Verified red-then-green, real exit codes.** Added `app/lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` (4 tests) for
the new pure helper - the one piece of this fix with extractable, testable logic (the `<select>`
JSX itself has none, same honest-limitation shape as Findings 144/164/165/166/174 for the rest of
the diff). Green: `npx vitest run lib/dealEconomics.spec.ts` - **4/4 passed**, exit 0. Red: reverted
only `needsCreditFallbackOption`'s own body to `return false;` (the pre-fix behavior - never adds
the fallback option), kept the test file as-is, re-ran - **exit 1, 2 of 4 failed**, exactly the two
predicted "needs fallback" cases (`AssertionError: expected false to be true`), with both negative-
control cases ("nobody credited", "person already in the list") still passing. Restored the real
fix from backup, re-ran - **4/4 passed, exit 0** again, confirmed by `grep`-reading the restored
file's own body back out.

Full suite after restoring the real fix: `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors, exit 0. `npx eslint .` - 0
errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings, exit 0. `npx next build` - compiled successfully, exit 0,
same route table (`/pipeline` and `/pipeline/pricing` both still Partial Prerender routes). `npx
vitest run` - **497/497, 64 files** (the baseline 493/63 plus this fix's own new 4/1) - exit 0. The
`*.test.ts` node loop (plain `node <file>`, no `--import tsx`, no `--test` flag, real exit codes) -
**28 files, 0 failures**, unchanged, exit 0 on every file. `engine/` sweep not re-run - this fix
touches no Python.

**Regression:** `app/lib/dealEconomics.ts` (+16 lines, one new pure function), `app/lib
/dealEconomics.spec.ts` (new file, 4 tests), `app/app/pipeline/economics-form.tsx` (~12 lines: one
renamed local, one new conditional `<option>`, one new import), `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx` (~6
lines: one destructured `error`, one `console.error`), `app/app/pipeline/pricing/page.tsx` (~10
lines: one destructured `error`, one `console.error`, the name-fallback wording split). No other
file touched.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a read-path logging addition plus a write-path correctness fix that
only ever changes behavior on an already-broken-upstream render (the happy path's rendered HTML and
written data are unchanged), with a genuine red/green unit test added; no RLS, no money-processing
path (this only affects which person a company credits internally, not Payfast/billing), no
worker-image-install surface touched - same category and direct-push precedent Findings 164-166/
170-174 all used.

**Backlog status.** Finding 168 and the `start_payfast_checkout()` revenue-integrity gap both
remain exactly as left, untouched, per the standing guardrail. All 9 PRs remain open and unmerged
(re-checked this pass via `mcp__github__list_pull_requests`: `#176`/`#177`(draft)/`#178`/`#179`/
`#180`/`#181`/`#182` and the two stale drafts `#164`/`#165`, same `updated_at` timestamps every
preceding pass has recorded) - none touched, amended, or merged by this pass. This finding is also
a correction to Finding 165's own "genuinely clean" judgment on `app/app/pipeline/page.tsx`'s
`peopleRows` - that judgment was right about the page's own direct display uses, but incomplete
about the shared `EconomicsForm` component it also feeds; worth flagging explicitly so a future pass
doesn't treat a "feeds only a cosmetic lookup" finding as closing out every consumer of a given
read without tracing each one, this file included. `app/app/pipeline/pricing/market-comparison.tsx`
was re-confirmed clean in passing (already correctly captures and renders its own `loadOutcomesFor
Tenders` error, per Finding 158's own writeup on this exact call site - not re-litigated).
`engine/discovery/`'s still-not-re-swept direct-buyer readers (`dbsa_procurement.py`/`vaal_central_water.py`/`kouga.py`/
`lephalale.py`/`sars_procurement.py`) and `randwater.py`'s own TLS-blocked live-fetch limitation
remain live angles for a future pass, as does the rest of `app/app/people/` and `app/app/company/`

read (`roleErr`) all already capture and surface their own errors. But the SECOND half of that same
`Promise.all` - the `person_role_eligibility` select that produces `tagRows` (the person's own
currently-held role tags, used only to compute `taggedRoles` for the checkbox list below) -
discarded its `error` entirely (`const [{ data: roleRows, error: roleErr }, { data: tagRows }] =
await Promise.all([...])`, line ~306, pre-fix).

**Why this isn't just a cosmetic display bug, following this chain's own standing methodology of
tracing a discarded read into every shared/downstream consumer rather than stopping at "its direct
display use looks fine":** `taggedRoles` feeds two things - the "Tagged for: ..." summary text
(cosmetic) and, more importantly, every checkbox's `defaultChecked={taggedRoles.has(r.code)}` in
the `saveRoleEligibility` form (lines ~761-792). On a transient `person_role_eligibility` read
failure, `taggedRoles` becomes an empty `Set` while the person's real tags are still in the
database - every checkbox renders **unchecked**, with the existing `rolesError` gate (which checked
only `roleErr`, the *catalog* read, not this one) never firing, so the form still renders as
normal, giving no indication anything is wrong. `saveRoleEligibility` itself
(`app/app/people/actions.ts` lines 874-914) does NOT trust the page's own `taggedRoles` for
correctness - it re-reads `person_role_eligibility` fresh at submit time (`current`), builds `have`
from that fresh read, diffs it against `wanted` (the checkboxes actually submitted), and then
`DELETE`s every `role_code` that's in `have` but not in `wanted` (`toRemove`). So: the page's read
fails transiently -> every checkbox shows unchecked -> a user who simply clicks "Save role tags"
without touching anything (or who adds one new, unrelated tag without noticing the existing ones
look wrong) submits `wanted = {}` or `wanted = {the one new tag}` -> the action's own fresh read
(usually succeeding, since the page's failure was transient) returns the real, full `have` set ->
`toRemove` becomes every real tag the person has -> they are silently, permanently deleted, with
zero error anywhere since the delete itself succeeds. This is the identical shape to Finding 175 (a
discarded secondary-read error feeding a save path that destroys real, previously-recorded data on
an unrelated/no-op-looking submit) - this time via a `DELETE ... WHERE role_code IN (toRemove)`
diff instead of a whole-row `null`-out, and on role eligibility tags (which gate which CVs/key-
position matches a tender's compliance check trusts) rather than credit/commission attribution.

**Fixed:** `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx` now captures `error: tagErr` on the
`person_role_eligibility` select alongside the existing `roleErr`, logs it
(`console.error("person_role_eligibility select failed for person detail", tagErr.message)`), and -
the actual fix - folds it into `rolesError` (`rolesError = roleErr?.message ?? tagErr?.message ??
null`) instead of `rolesError` depending on `roleErr` alone. `rolesError` already gates the whole
`saveRoleEligibility` form behind the existing "Couldn't load role options — try again shortly."
warning banner (this exact mechanism `roleErr` already used) - so a failed `tagRows` read now hides
the save form entirely instead of rendering it with silently-wrong (empty) checkbox state, the same
"surface the failure instead of letting it look like real data" fix shape as the rest of this page's
already-correct reads. The catalog-failure path (`roleErr`) is completely unchanged; only the
previously-undistinguished `tagErr` case is newly folded in.

**Verification run myself, real exit codes - no red/green test, honest limitation, same as Findings
144/164/165/166/174.** `page.tsx` has no extracted pure logic for this specific diff (the fix is a
destructuring addition plus a `??` fallback, not a function); `find app/app/people -iname
"*.test.ts*"` turns up only `app/app/people/actions.spec.ts`, which does not touch this read.
Correctness rests on: `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors, exit 0. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, the same 3
pre-existing warnings, exit 0. `npx next build` - compiled successfully, exit 0, same route table
(`/people/[id]` still a Partial Prerender route). `npx vitest run` - **497/497, 64 files**,
unchanged (this fix adds no test). The `*.test.ts` node loop (plain `node <file>`, no `--import
tsx`, no `--test` flag, real exit codes, run as a loop over all 28 files individually) - **28
files, 0 failures**, unchanged. A plain reading of the diff confirms every other branch (the
catalog-failure banner, the "not tagged for any role yet" empty state, the checkbox list itself,
`saveRoleEligibility`'s own diff/delete logic) is byte-for-byte unchanged - only the new `tagErr`
capture and its fold into `rolesError`. `engine/` sweep not re-run - this fix touches no Python.

**Regression:** `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx` only (+13 lines: one destructured `error`, one
`console.error`, one comment block, one changed assignment). No other file touched.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a read-failure-surfacing fix that only changes behavior on an

for the sibling read), no RLS, no money-processing path, no worker-image-install surface touched -

**Area:** `app/app/company/principals/page.tsx` (`PrincipalForm`'s "Also one of your people
(CV)?" `<select>`), `app/app/company/registrations/page.tsx` (`HeldForm`'s "Held by" `<select>`),
`app/app/company/bank-accounts/page.tsx` (`AccountForm`'s "Whose account" `<select>`) - three
independent instances of the identical shape, found in one pass's own full sweep of
`app/app/company/` (named as a candidate by three prior passes and finally reached this pass).

**How this was found.** Per the directive's own standing methodology ("trace every value a read
produces into every component or Server Action it feeds, not just its own display use"), read
every file under `app/app/company/` (`page.tsx` and its 7 subpages' `page.tsx`/`actions.ts`, plus
every `_components/*.tsx`). Most of the surface was already careful about this review's dominant
bug class - `page.tsx` itself captures and banners every one of its own reads, and the
`_components/` files do no reads of their own at all. But `principals/page.tsx`'s own `people`
select (`const [..., { data: people }, ...] = await Promise.all([...])`) discarded its error
entirely - and tracing it past its own "No" default into `PrincipalForm`'s `person_id` `<select>`
(options built as `[{value:"",label:"No"}, ...people.map(...)]`, `defaultValue={p?.person_id ??
""}`) found the same severe shape Findings 175/176 already established: when `people` fails (or
the linked person is since removed), the `<select>`'s `defaultValue` matches no `<option>`, so the
browser silently selects "No" instead - and `savePrincipal()` (`app/app/company/principals

EVERY submit of this whole-row form, so saving ANY other field on an existing director/shareholder
(position, ownership %, appointed-on date...) silently and permanently nulls out a real

line ~342) reads `company_principals.person_id` to pull a director's ECSA/SACPCMP registration
number onto a real generated SANRAL Form C.1.2.3 ("Name of Partners, Members or Directors") - so

Having established the shape, grepped every other `<select>` in `app/app/company/**/page.tsx`
whose `options` are built from a variable (DB-sourced) array rather than a module-level constant

### Finding 178 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `set_opportunity_tag()`'s own read-then-write window let two concurrent "add tag" calls on the SAME Discovery row silently lose one tag to the other's stale-snapshot overwrite, with no error on either side)

**Area:** `set_opportunity_tag(uuid, text, text)` (`app/supabase/migrations/0089_opportunity_tags_interest.sql`), the SECURITY DEFINER write path behind `app/app/discovery/actions.ts`'s `setOpportunityTag()`, called from `OpportunityQuickActions.tsx` on `/discovery`. First fresh surface opened this pass per the task's own candidate list (`app/app/discovery/` - untouched by this chain so far).

**How this was found.** Read the whole `app/app/discovery/` surface in full (`page.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `preferencesActions.ts`, `OpportunityPreferencesPanel.tsx`, `OpportunityQuickActions.tsx`, `downgrade-flag.tsx`, `loading.tsx`) looking for this review's dominant shape (a discarded Supabase read's error treated as false-safe, then traced into a write path). That shape is NOT present here - every write on this surface (`setOpportunityTag`, `setOpportunityInterest`, `acknowledgeDowngrade`, `pursueOpportunity`) goes through a SECURITY DEFINER Postgres RPC rather than a client-side diff-and-update, so there is no discarded-read-feeds-a-`<select>` instance to find (unlike Findings 175-177). But reading each RPC's own SQL body (0089/0051/0055/0018/0024, `app/supabase/migrations/`) for the SAME underlying hazard those findings keep naming - "a stale value feeding an overwrite on save" - turned up a different root cause with the identical silent-data-loss symptom: `set_opportunity_tag()` does `select * into opp from discovered_opportunities where id = p_opportunity_id` ONCE, with no lock, then on `'add'`/`'remove'` computes the new `company_tags` array via `array_append(opp.company_tags, tag)` / `array_remove(opp.company_tags, tag)` against that in-memory SNAPSHOT and writes it back unconditionally. Two concurrent calls for the SAME opportunity row - two team members tagging it at once, a double-click before `OpportunityQuickActions.tsx`'s own optimistic UI settles (the file's own header comment already documents a related double-click bug Sarel reported for the interest button, fixed 2026-10-29, but that fix only addressed the CLIENT-side symptom, not this SERVER-side race), or two open browser tabs - each take their own snapshot before either commits, so the SECOND call's `UPDATE` silently overwrites the FIRST call's tag. `set_opportunity_interest()` (same migration) was checked for the same shape and is safe: it sets `interest_marker` purely from its own parameter, never from the `opp` snapshot, so there is nothing stale to lose.

**Reproduced directly in a disposable scratch database** (never this app's live DB - `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` against a fresh local Postgres 16, dropped afterward per the standing guardrail): replayed all 110 pre-fix migrations, seeded one `companies`/`company_members`/`discovered_opportunities` row (`company_tags = '{}'`), then ran two concurrent `psql` sessions calling a copy of the real function body with a `pg_sleep(3)` inserted right after the read (widening the real race window for a deterministic demo - no logic changed) - session A: add `'foo'`, session B: add `'bar'`. Both calls returned successfully, no error either side. Final `company_tags`: `{foo}` only - `'bar'` vanished with zero trace in either caller's response. Repeated the same two-session reproduction directly against the REAL `set_opportunity_tag` function name itself (not just a copy) after temporarily widening its live window the same way on the scratch DB only: same result, `{bar}` only (the tag that survived varies run to run with OS scheduling - confirmed losing `'foo'` or `'bar'` on different runs, always exactly one of the two).

**Fixed**, same pattern this codebase already uses for this exact class of bug (0107's `redeem_company_invite()`, 0113's `create_company_invite_checked()`, both cited in their own migration files): added `for update` to the function's initial `select * into opp ...`, so a second concurrent call for the SAME opportunity blocks on that row lock until the first commits, then its own read sees the first call's already-applied change rather than a pre-commit snapshot - no second overwrite, no lost tag. New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0121_opportunity_tag_add_remove_race.sql` (`create or replace function set_opportunity_tag(...)`, same body otherwise, plus a `comment on function` documenting the fix). `set_opportunity_interest()` was not touched - confirmed above it has no equivalent race.

**Verified red-then-green, real exit codes, against the scratch DB (not the real schema's live data).** RED (pre-fix body, widened window, two concurrent adds): `company_tags` ended as a single-tag array both times tried - run 1: `{foo}` (lost `'bar'`), run 2 (after restoring the pre-fix body a second time to re-confirm): `{bar}` (lost `'foo'`) - exit 0 on both `psql` calls either time, no error surfaced anywhere, matching the predicted failure exactly (silent loss, not a crash). GREEN (0121's `for update` body, same widened window, same two concurrent adds, run twice): `company_tags` ended as `{foo,bar}` both times - exit 0, both tags present. ### Finding 179 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - the registrations catalog (0050) never got the "lapses before closing" check Finding 132/139 built for company-wide vault documents and key-person professional registrations, so a PSIRA/SETA/other held registration fine today but lapsing before an open tender's closing date was never proactively flagged for the company-held case)

**Area:** Compliance / reminders (`engine/compliance/registration_reminders.py`, wired into
`watch_deadlines.py`'s `main()` and `daily_digest.py`'s live mode).

**Scenario:** `registration_reminders.py`'s own docstring frames itself as the generalised
replacement for the fixed per-column tracking (`TRACKED_EXPIRY_FIELDS`/`TRACKED_PERSON_EXPIRY_FIELDS`)
- "one held_registrations row = one tracked expiry, whatever body it is (PSIRA, SETA accreditation,
a waste permit ...), so a new registration type needs no code change." But the "lapses before
closing" framing Finding 132 built for `TRACKED_EXPIRY_FIELDS` (`find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`)
and Finding 139 extended to `TRACKED_PERSON_EXPIRY_FIELDS` (`find_person_credentials_lapsing_before_closing()`)
was never extended to this catalog at all - confirmed by grep: zero references to
"lapsing_before_closing"/"lapses_before_closing" anywhere in `registration_reminders.py` before this
fix. A held registration fine today under the normal 60-day window, but due to lapse before an open
tender's closing date, was never proactively flagged - only reactively, same gap shape as the
original Finding 132.

**Scoped deliberately, not forced to cover every holder type in one pass**: `held_registrations` rows
can be held by a company, a person, or a company principal (director). This fix covers COMPANY-held
rows only, mirroring `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`'s own company-wide scope - the exact
scope Finding 132 itself started with before Finding 139 extended it to persons in a later, dedicated
pass. A PERSON-held row (e.g. a key person's own PSIRA) would need the identical
`tender_pack_assignments.confirmed_person_id` scoping `find_person_credentials_lapsing_before_closing()`
uses - a real, matching gap, deliberately left open rather than guessed at. A PRINCIPAL-held row
(a director's own PSIRA) has no "confirmed onto a tender" concept at all - principals aren't assigned
to tender positions the way key people are - so it stays on this module's own reactive coverage
(`app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`) only. `property_documents`' own equivalent gap is also left open,
named as a follow-up, not attempted in this same pass.

**Fix:** new function `find_held_registrations_lapsing_before_closing(url, key, seen, today,
lead_days)` in `registration_reminders.py`, mirroring `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`'s
exact SAST closing-day math and "already inside normal window"/"already expired" guards, scoped to
rows with no `person_id`/`principal_id` set, crossed against the company's own open `tender_packs`.
Wired into `watch_deadlines.main()`'s `--out` report AND `daily_digest.py`'s live mode in the SAME
pass that built it (unlike Finding 132's own `documents_before_closing`, which went 2 days without the
live-digest wiring the first time around - the exact mistake this fix was careful not to repeat).

**Verified with a real adversarial scenario.** New checks in `test_principals_registrations.py`'s
`part1()`: a company-held SETA accreditation at 90 days (outside the 60-day window) against a company
tender_pack closing at 100 days - reported, naming the real tender; two SIBLING rows with the
IDENTICAL expiring shape but person-held/director-held - confirmed NOT reported by this company-only
check, proving the scope boundary is real, not accidental; a second same-day run reports nothing new
(seen-store de-dup). Needed one small, additive fixture-infrastructure fix along the way: the shared
`test_watch_deadlines_urgency.fake_request()` helper (reused by `test_principals_registrations.py`)
had no `is.null` filter support at all (only `not.is.null`) - added, since the new function's own
`person_id=is.null&principal_id=is.null` query needed it; purely additive, no existing test's
behaviour changed.

**Verified red-then-green.** Reverted all three touched production files via `git apply -R`, re-ran -
failed exactly as predicted, `AttributeError: module 'registration_reminders' has no attribute
'find_held_registrations_lapsing_before_closing'`; reapplied - `0 failure(s)`. `py_compile` clean on
all five touched files. Regression: `test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py`, `test_watch_conditional_registrations.py`,
`engine/notify/test_digest_live.py`, `test_send_digest_emails.py`, `test_send_pack_ready_email.py` -
all `0 failure(s)`.

**Regression:** `engine/compliance/registration_reminders.py` (1 new function, ~100 lines including
docstring/comments, `import datetime` added); `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py` (`main()`, 1 new
call + print block + report key); `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (`document_expiry_signals()`, 1 new
OR-term); `engine/compliance/test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` (1 new `is.null` filter branch in the

### Finding 180 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `redeem_company_invite()`'s own unlocked `linked_person_id` read let two concurrent redemptions of TWO DIFFERENT invite tokens naming the SAME roster person silently race for ownership of that person's `linked_user_id`, with no error on either side)

**Area:** `redeem_company_invite(text)` (originally `app/supabase/migrations/0077_company_invites_and_employee_role.sql`, invite-row lock added by `0107`, one-company-per-user guard added by `0116` - `0116` is the version that shipped going into this pass), the SECURITY DEFINER RPC behind `app/app/invite/actions.ts`'s `acceptInvite()` on `/invite/<token>`.

**How this was found.** This pass's angle, per the task brief's own fresh-angle suggestion (named by the immediately preceding pass, `14a591d`, as untried by this chain): re-trace every OTHER currently-shipping SECURITY DEFINER function for the exact TOCTOU shape `record_tender_document()` (0043) once had before `0045` closed it - a scalar/count `select ... into`, a conditional `raise exception` gate based on it, then a SEPARATE, unconditional `insert`/`update` that never re-verifies the gate's condition still holds. Grepped every `select ... into` across `app/supabase/migrations/*.sql` that is not a `%rowtype` read (the already-swept Finding-178-class shape) and cross-referenced against `raise exception` gates in the same function body. Most hits are already-fixed instances of the OUTER race (0107/0113/0114/0116's own invite-row/subscription-row/membership locks) or pure quota-style reads with no write-back. One function's OWN comment flagged exactly the hazard this pass was looking for, as something it claims to already be safe against: `redeem_company_invite()`'s `linked_person_id` branch reads `select linked_user_id into v_person_owner from people where id = v_invite.linked_person_id` with **no lock**, gates a `raise exception 'That roster entry is already linked to a different account.'` on it, then does a SEPARATE unconditional `update people set linked_user_id = v_uid ...` - the function's own comment says this "would only happen if the same person row were pointed at by two accepted invites, which createInvite's own form doesn't offer, but the function stays safe against it regardless." The claim is true only for the SEQUENTIAL case (one invite already accepted before a second is opened) - not for two invites redeemed concurrently. And nothing actually stops the precondition: `create_company_invite_checked()` (0113) checks only the plan's seat cap before inserting a new `company_invites` row, never whether `linked_person_id` already has a pending invite, so a double-submit on "Send invite" (the SAME double-click scenario 0113's and 0114's own header comments already name for the sibling races those fixed) or a deliberate re-invite of the same roster entry both leave two live, independently-valid tokens pointing at the same person - no DB constraint, no UI check, blocks it either.

**Reproduced directly in a disposable scratch database** (never this app's live DB - `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` against a fresh local Postgres 16, dropped and the service stopped afterward per the standing guardrail): replayed all 111 pre-fix migrations, seeded one company, one `people` row with `linked_user_id` null, and TWO `company_invites` rows (different tokens, same `linked_person_id`, same company). Ran two concurrent `psql` sessions, each `set_config('test.uid', ...)` as a different real `auth.users` account under `set role authenticated`, each redeeming its own token - against a scratch-only copy of the real (0116) function body widened with a `pg_sleep(2)` right after the unlocked `people` read (the same widening technique this review's own Finding 178 used, cited in `0121`'s header), run TWICE over:
- RED (pre-fix body, both runs): neither call raised an error - both invites ended up with `accepted_at`/`accepted_by` correctly set to their OWN real, distinct user, and both got a real `company_members` row, but `people.linked_user_id` silently ended up pointing at only ONE of the two accounts (run 1: the first caller's write survived; run 2: the second's did, confirming genuine non-deterministic MVCC racing, not a scripting artifact). The LOSING side's own invite record ends up self-contradictory - its `accepted_by` names one real account, while the roster row it claims to have linked now names the OTHER - with zero error raised to either caller.
- GREEN (after adding `for update` to the `people` select, both runs): exactly one call succeeded in full (invite accepted, person linked, `company_members` row inserted); the other blocked on the row lock until the first committed, then correctly re-read the now-current `linked_user_id` and raised `'That roster entry is already linked to a different account.'` - its WHOLE transaction, including its own earlier `company_members` insert, rolled back atomically (confirmed: the losing side's invite stayed unaccepted and got no membership row at all), leaving no half-joined, inconsistent state. Which side won varied between the two GREEN runs (same as the two REDs), confirming the fix removes the race rather than just reordering who wins it.
Also confirmed the real, as-shipped `0122` migration file (no `pg_sleep`, verbatim fix) replays cleanly on top of all 112 migrations via the same `replay_schema.sh` harness, and re-seeded/re-ran the full two-session scenario against it with no widening at all - same outcome shape as the widened GREEN runs (one winner, one clean rejection), confirming the fix holds on the real function, not only the widened scratch copy.

**Fixed**, same pattern this exact function (and this review generally - 0107/0113/0114/0116) already uses: added `for update` to the `people` select feeding the gate. New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0122_redeem_invite_linked_person_race.sql` (`create or replace function redeem_company_invite(text)`, full body carried over verbatim from `0116` with the one line changed, plus an updated `comment on function`). No other behavior changed - the invite-row lock (0107), the one-company-per-user guard (0116), and the re-join-with-updated-role path are all unchanged.

**Verified red-then-green, real exit codes, against the scratch DB (never the live data).** Two independent RED runs (widened pre-fix body): both `psql` calls exited `0` on both runs, no error surfaced on either side, `people.linked_user_id` ended up naming only one of the two real accounts both times (non-deterministic which) - exactly the predicted silent-loss failure, not a crash. Two independent GREEN runs (widened post-fix body): exactly one `psql` call exited `0` (full success) and the other exited non-zero with `ERROR: That roster entry is already linked to a different account.` on both runs; final state both times showed exactly one invite accepted, one `company_members` row, and `people.linked_user_id` matching that same account - fully consistent. `bash engine/security/replay_schema.sh -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U postgres -d <scratch>` with the real (un-widened) `0122` file included - exit `0`, "Schema replay complete (112 migrations)".

Full TS/JS suite re-run after the fix (this migration touches no TypeScript, but the standing standard calls for a full re-run regardless of which layer changed): `npm run typecheck` - 0 errors, exit 0. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors, the same 3 pre-existing warnings, exit 0. `npx vitest run` - **505/505 passed, 66 files**, exit 0. The `*.test.ts` node loop (plain `node <file>`, no `--import tsx`, no `--test`) - **28 files, 0 failures**, exit 0 on every file (looped by hand; real exit codes captured with no pipe in between, per the standing bash pitfall). `next build` not run - no RSC/page/TS file touched, per the standing rule's own scope.

**Regression:** `app/supabase/migrations/0122_redeem_invite_linked_person_race.sql` (new file, one `create or replace function`). No TypeScript/JS file touched - `app/app/invite/actions.ts`'s `acceptInvite()` calls the same RPC name/signature, unchanged. No new automated regression test was added to this repo's own TS/Python suites: the hazard only manifests under real Postgres MVCC concurrency across two genuinely overlapping transactions, which neither `vitest` (no DB) nor the plain-`node` `*.test.ts` loop can exercise - the scratch-DB reproduction above (against both the widened copy AND the real, un-widened `0122` file) is the real verification for this fix, same precedent Finding 178 set. Documented here, and in the migration file's own header comment, so a future pass can re-run the identical scratch-DB reproduction without re-deriving it.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - a narrow, single-function SQL fix (one `for update` added to an existing unlocked read) that only changes behavior under concurrent writes to the same `people` row (the single-redemption happy path is byte-for-byte unchanged: same inputs, same outputs, same error conditions for every existing check), verified end-to-end against a real Postgres instance with a genuine two-round red-then-green cycle on both a widened scratch copy and the real shipped file; touches no RLS policy (grants/revokes carried over verbatim - `create or replace function` does not reset existing privilege grants), no money/Payfast path, and no production worker-image install/copy surface - same category and direct-push precedent Finding 178 (and 164-166/170-177) used for "small, safe, well-verified fix."

**Backlog status.** Finding 168 and the `start_payfast_checkout()` revenue-integrity gap both remain exactly as left, untouched, per the standing guardrail. None touched, amended, or merged by this pass. The task brief's own suggested fresh angle (every OTHER security-definer function with the scalar-read/conditional-raise/unconditional-write shape) is now genuinely swept - this was the one live instance found; everything else matching the initial grep was either already-fixed (0107/0113/0114/0116's own locks), a pure read-only quota gate with no write-back, or (per the immediately preceding pass's own writeup) the now-superseded, never-shipped `record_tender_document()` shape itself. ### Finding 181 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate-but-proactive - `sars_procurement.py`'s own in-page de-duplication silently DROPPED a genuine re-advertisement that reuses the same Ref No. under a new detail-page URL, before it even reached its own `ocid`; its `ocid` construction also had the same raw-ref-with-no-disambiguator shape `kouga.py` and `dbsa_procurement.py` were already fixed for - no live collision reproduced, closed proactively with a synthetic-fixture regression test per the standing backlog's own named, lower-priority candidate)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/sars_procurement.py`'s `fetch_releases()` and `normalize()` (South African Revenue Service's own Published Tenders page reader), plus its offline test coverage in `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py`.

**How this was found.** Per this pass's own task brief, item 3: the standing backlog had named `sars_procurement.py`'s "listing-drop on ref reuse" risk as a candidate for three prior passes running (System-Status.md), explicitly flagged as lower priority than the `app/app/` surface sweep and explicitly offered for a synthetic-fixture regression test "even without a live reproduction." `app/app/dashboard/` (this pass's own first-priority candidate) was checked first and came back genuinely clean (see this pass's own `System-Status.md` entry) - no write path of any kind exists on that surface at all, so this pass fell through to item 3 rather than forcing a finding on item 1.

Read `sars_procurement.py` in full. `normalize()` builds `ocid=f"sars-procurement:{entry['ref'] or sh.norm_ref(entry['url'])}"` - the identical raw-ref-alone shape `kouga.py`'s and `dbsa_procurement.py`'s own `_disambiguate_reused_refs()` fixes (2026-11-06/07, cited by name in this file's own backlog note) already closed for their sibling readers, confirming SARS genuinely belongs to that same named bug class, not just a superficial pattern match. But reading `fetch_releases()` itself surfaced something the backlog note hadn't named: its own in-page "same tender can appear once per section re-listing" de-duplication (`key = e["ref"] or e["url"]`) runs BEFORE `normalize()` is ever called - so a genuine re-advertisement reusing the same ref under a DIFFERENT detail-page URL doesn't just collide at the `ocid`/upsert stage the way Kouga's and DBSA's did; it is silently DROPPED from the output entirely, before it is ever normalized, scored, or written anywhere. That is strictly worse than the two already-fixed siblings' own failure mode (a merged/overwritten row, not a vanished one).

**Checked live, not left as a theoretical pattern-match, per the standing real-document verification standard.** Fetched the real, current `https://www.sars.gov.za/procurement/published-tenders/` page directly (`curl`, HTTP 200) and ran the actual unmodified `parse_listing()`/`fetch_releases()` against the real bytes: **2 open tenders today, 2 distinct refs** (`RFP14/2026`, `RFP18/2026`) - no live collision exists right now, the same "sample too small to clear the risk, not proof the code is any safer" conclusion the immediately preceding pass's own backlog note already recorded for this file. Confirmed with the real live page's own HTML that SARS's page separately carries THREE "addendum"-style `<strong>` announcements for `RFP18/2026` (28 Oct, 3 Nov, 5 Nov - on top of its own original "9 October - New Tender" dated entry, which is the one actually captured today) sitting outside the `<ul>`-wrapped dated-list section `DATE_BLOCK`/`TENDER_LINK` actually parse, plus a similar standalone announcement naming a fourth ref, `RFP01/2026` (29 Oct), that has no currently-open "New Tender" dated entry of its own at all. Today those bare addendum announcements simply aren't captured by this reader (a separate, narrower gap: this reader has never read that section at all, live or otherwise), so they don't yet trigger the ref-reuse path live - but they are concrete, real evidence that SARS's own site DOES re-announce the same ref under a new heading in practice, exactly the shape this fix guards against the moment a future re-advertisement lands inside the `<ul>`-wrapped section instead.

**Reproduced the real bug on a synthetic fixture, red-then-green, before fixing anything (not fixed speculatively on faith alone).** Built a minimal fixture mirroring Kouga's and DBSA's own real reused-ref cases: an original "16 October 2026 - New Tender" dated entry and a later "5 November 2026 - New Tender" re-advertisement, same Ref No. (`RFP99/2026`), two different detail-page URLs. Ran the real, pre-fix `parse_listing()`/`fetch_releases()` against it directly (ad hoc, not yet the committed test):
```
parsed entries: 2   (both RFP99/2026, different urls)
kept after fetch_releases-style dedup: 1   -- DROPPED: the re-advertisement, silently
```
Confirmed RED exactly as predicted: the pre-fix `key = e["ref"] or e["url"]` dedup kept only the first-seen entry and threw the second away with no warning, no log line, no error - a real open tender that would never reach a company's discovery feed at all.

**Fix.** Two changes, both additive, in `sars_procurement.py`:
1. `fetch_releases()`'s own in-page dedup key changed from `e["ref"] or e["url"]` to `e["url"]` alone. This still correctly collapses the SAME tender mentioned twice in different page sections (the dedup's own original, still-valid purpose - two mentions of one real tender always share the identical detail-page URL), while no longer conflating that with two DIFFERENT tenders that merely happen to reuse the same Ref No. (different URLs, now both kept).
2. A new `_disambiguate_reused_refs(rels)`, the identical shape as `kouga.py`'s and `dbsa_procurement.py`'s own versions: groups the normalized output by `contract_number` (the ref), and for any group of 2+, suffixes each one's `ocid` with its own URL slug (`rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]`) - SARS always gives each tender its own stable, distinct detail-page URL (unlike DBSA, which shares one list-page URL for every row and needed a `published_date`/hash fallback), so no fallback chain is needed here. Only a colliding ref's `ocid` is touched; every non-colliding tender keeps exactly the plain `ocid` it always had, so this does not re-trigger a "new tender" alert for any SARS tender that was never ambiguous. Called at the end of `fetch_releases()`.

### Finding 183 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, significant - `sars_procurement.py`'s own `fetch_documents()` matched ZERO real documents on the real live site, for ANY tender, ever - not just an "addendum" gap, but its own primary tender pack too - because SARS's site links every document through an extension-less WordPress pretty permalink, which `DOC_LINK`'s own regex, requiring the href to literally end in a file extension, could never match)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/sars_procurement.py`'s `fetch_documents()`/`DOC_LINK` (new `_DOC_SECTION`/`_SECTION_LINK` added), wired into every `with_documents=True` call (the default throughout `gov_sources.read_source()`/`fetch_all()`/`releases_for_watch()`, and in turn `watch_new_tenders.py` → `download_discovered_documents.py`'s permanent per-tender document store). Also checked, found NOT the real gap: the "What's New" bare-list section outside the `<ul>` block `DATE_BLOCK`/`TENDER_LINK` already parse.

**How this was found.** Per this pass's own task brief (angle 1): the immediately preceding two passes (Findings 181/182) both named, but never opened, `sars_procurement.py`'s own live page carrying bare "addendum"-style announcement blocks ("RFP18/2026"/"RFP01/2026" cited) OUTSIDE the `<ul>`-wrapped section `DATE_BLOCK` reads, asking whether that section ever carries real information (a closing-date change, a genuinely new ref, a cancellation) not otherwise captured.

Fetched the real live `https://www.sars.gov.za/procurement/published-tenders/` page (`curl`, HTTP 200, 274,730 bytes) and read its real HTML directly (not WebFetch's markdown conversion, to see the exact tag structure the regexes need). The page's own `<h2>What's New</h2><ul>...` section does carry several `<li><strong>DATE – REF: title</strong><ul><li><a href=...>label</a></li></ul></li>` entries for RFP18/2026 ("Price template", "Questions and answers", "Briefing session presentation") and one for RFP01/2026 ("Extension of validity period") - none of which `DATE_BLOCK` matches, because that regex requires the text between the date and `</strong>` to be empty or the literal string `"New Tender"`, and these entries are neither (they're update/addendum postings for an EXISTING tender, not a new-tender announcement) - confirmed by direct regex testing against the real captured bytes.

Fetched the linked PDF behind "Extension of validity period" (`https://www.sars.gov.za/tender-validity-extention-rfp-01_2026/`, a 301-redirecting pretty permalink, real `curl -L` landed on a 323,442-byte `application/pdf`) and extracted its real text (`pypdf`): a formal SARS letter extending the VALIDITY of bids already submitted for RFP01/2026 to 30 December 2026, because evaluation is still in progress - not a closing-date change, not a new ref, not a cancellation. RFP01/2026 itself no longer appears anywhere else on the live page at all (no `/tender/` link, no entry in the separate "Published Tenders" Closing-Date detail section either) - it has already fallen out of both sections this reader parses, since it's long past its own closing date. **Conclusion on the originally-posed question: the "What's New" bare-list entries for RFP18/2026 turned out to be pure DUPLICATES of documents already linked on that tender's own detail page (see below) - not new information. The one genuinely non-duplicated item (RFP01/2026's bid-validity extension) is real status information with no home in this reader's current output, but it concerns an already-closed tender under evaluation, not an open-tender field (closing date/ref/cancellation) this reader tracks at all - a narrow, low-value gap, deliberately NOT fixed this pass (same "don't force a fix against an out-of-scope, low-value gap" discipline `vaal_central_water.py`'s own write-up above used), left as a named-but-declined candidate below.**

**The real finding came from following that duplication one level deeper.** Both of RFP18/2026's "What's New" document links (`briefing-session-presentation-rfp-18-2026-hygiene-services-v2`, `rfp-18-2026-qa`, `rfp18-2026_hygiene-pricing-template-final`) are ALSO linked directly from RFP18/2026's own detail page (`https://www.sars.gov.za/tender/rfp18-2026-...-36-months/`, the same page `fetch_documents()` already fetches for every discovered SARS tender) - so if `fetch_documents()` worked correctly, the "What's New" section would be fully redundant for this tender, by design. It doesn't. Running the real, unmodified `fetch_documents()` against the real live detail-page HTML (fetched directly, `curl`, HTTP 200) for BOTH of SARS's 2 currently open tenders returned **`[]` for both** - zero documents, for the tender's own advert/specification/"Main" tender pack AND every "Supporting" addendum alike.

**Root cause, read directly off the real HTML.** SARS's WordPress site exclusively links tender documents through a pretty permalink with no file extension at all in the URL (`/rfp18-2026-tender-pack/`, `/rfp-18-2026-qa/`, `/rfp18-2026_hygiene-pricing-template-final/` - each a real, confirmed 301 redirect server-side to the actual `.pdf`, verified with `curl -L -v`). `DOC_LINK = re.compile(r'<a[^>]+href="([^"]+\.(?:pdf|docx?|xlsx?|zip))"...')` requires the href to literally END in one of those extensions - it matched zero `<a>` tags anywhere on either real detail page, confirmed by running the regex directly against the real bytes. This is NOT a theoretical pattern-match: it means every SARS tender ever discovered by this reader, since its first commit (`cace3f7`), has had its OWN advert/specification document - the one thing a bidder actually needs, not just a later addendum - silently recorded as having 0 documents, with `download_discovered_documents.py`'s own module docstring wrongly asserting this source "gives a direct, unauthenticated link" the same way the other 7 sources genuinely do. The only existing test coverage for `fetch_documents()` (`test_gov_sources.py`, pre-this-pass) used a synthetic fixture with hrefs already ending in `.pdf` ("/files/tender/spec.pdf") - a fixture never checked against the real site's actual URL shape, so this gap went undetected through every prior pass that touched this file (Findings 181 and the file's own earlier fixes included).

A second, compounding issue found the same way: even an extension-agnostic fix would still miss RFP18/2026's own real "Main" tender-pack link, because its link text re-uses the FULL tender title (168 characters, confirmed by direct measurement) - longer than `DOC_LINK`'s own `{1,150}` title cap.

**Fix**, in `sars_procurement.py` only. Read the real detail-page HTML directly (`curl`) for both RFP14/2026 and RFP18/2026 to find the real, consistent structure: every document link sits inside the post's own single `elementor-widget-theme-post-content` widget, under a `<p><strong>Main</strong></p>` marker (the tender pack) optionally followed by a `<p><strong>Supporting</strong></p>` marker and more links (briefing presentations, Q&A, pricing templates - RFP18/2026's real case), each `<a>` sometimes wrapped in a `<span>` but never nested inside another `<a>`. New `_DOC_SECTION` regex scopes to exactly that one widget (`<p><strong>Main</strong></p>(.*?)</div>`, non-greedy to the container's own first closing `</div>`) - deliberately NOT a page-wide extension-agnostic match, because the detail page's shared nav/footer chrome (`Home`/`About SARS`/`Careers`/`Media`/`Site Map`/...) is ALSO a plain extension-less `https://www.sars.gov.za/...` link; matching page-wide would have swept all of that in as bogus "documents" instead of fixing the real gap. New `_SECTION_LINK` regex (no title-length cap, safe because it only ever runs against this small, already-scoped section) extracts every `<a href=...>` inside it. `fetch_documents()` now runs both `DOC_LINK` (unchanged, kept in case SARS's CMS ever links a raw file directly again) and the new section match, merged and de-duplicated by resolved URL exactly as before.

### Finding 184 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `applyCvExtraction()` (`app/app/people/actions.ts`) and `applyMyCvExtraction()` (`app/app/my-cv/actions.ts`) each read-gated on `cv_extraction_results.review_status = 'pending_review'` then wrote through THREE/TWO separate, unlocked REST calls with no re-check of that gate on the final write, so two concurrent "Apply" submissions for the SAME extraction silently duplicated real `projects` rows with no error to either caller - the TypeScript analog of the Finding-178/180 Postgres read-then-write race, found by this pass's own new systematic angle applying that lesson to Next.js Server Actions)

**Area:** `app/app/people/actions.ts` `applyCvExtraction()` (and the `queueStandardCvs()` helper it calls), `app/app/my-cv/actions.ts` `applyMyCvExtraction()`. New migration `supabase/migrations/0123_cv_extraction_apply_race.sql` (`apply_cv_extraction_checked()`, `apply_my_cv_extraction_checked()`, private helper `_apply_cv_person_fields()`).

**How this was found.** This pass's own task brief introduced a new, seventh systematic angle: apply the lesson Findings 178 (`set_opportunity_tag()`'s lost-update race) and 180 (`redeem_company_invite()`'s TOCTOU race) already established for Postgres functions - an unlocked read-then-write window, or a gate-check read followed by a write that never re-checks the gate - to Next.js Server Actions instead, which have the exact same shapes available minus a database row lock to reach for. Read every `actions.ts` under `app/app/` (22 files), tracing each write-after-read sequence into its real backing Postgres call rather than reading the TypeScript in isolation, to tell which already inherit atomicity from a locked RPC or DB constraint (`app/company/team/actions.ts`'s `createInvite()`/`setMemberRole()`/`removeMember()`, `app/tenders/[id]/actions.ts`'s `requestTenderCv()` via migration 0075's partial unique index, `app/discovery/actions.ts` via migration 0121, `app/invite/actions.ts` via migration 0107/0122) and which have no read-then-write window to race in the first place (every write in `app/pipeline/actions.ts`, `app/experience/actions.ts`, `app/company/principals|properties|registrations|bank-accounts/actions.ts`, `app/onboarding/actions.ts`, `app/tenders/new/actions.ts`, `app/admin/*/actions.ts` is a plain `.update()`/`.insert()`/`.delete()` keyed directly by a caller-supplied or freshly-generated id, never by a value read-then-recomputed from an earlier SELECT in the same request).

`app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `applyCvExtraction()` and `app/app/my-cv/actions.ts`'s `applyMyCvExtraction()` stood out: both read `cv_extraction_results` once, check `review_status === 'pending_review'`, then write through three (full version: people update, projects insert, cv_extraction_results mark-applied) or two (self-service version: people update, mark-applied) separate, unlocked REST calls - and the LAST of those writes never repeated the `review_status = 'pending_review'` check in its own `.eq()` chain. Their own sibling in the SAME file, `discardCvExtraction()`/`discardMyCvExtraction()`, already had exactly that guard (`.eq("review_status", "pending_review")` on its own update, standing review, 2026-11-06, with a comment literally naming "the row having moved on from 'pending_review' already" as the risk it closes) - the "apply" twin right next to it never got the same fix. Not the same bug class as Findings 175-177 (a discarded Supabase read error feeding a stale value into an unrelated save): this is two genuinely concurrent invocations of the SAME action racing each other, with no error on either side, the TypeScript shape of Finding 178/180's own SQL-side lesson.

**Real, reachable race, not contrived.** Two concurrent "Apply"/"Save selected fields" submissions for the SAME extraction - a double-click before the page navigates away, or the same pending-review card left open in two browser tabs - both pass the initial read's `review_status` check before either commits. For `applyCvExtraction()` specifically this duplicates real rows in `projects` (NOT idempotent - every ticked project gets inserted twice, silently, with no error to either caller) and queues a second full set of standard-CV-generation jobs (`queueStandardCvs()`, called right after - itself already flagged by its own comment as having no database-level backstop of its own, unlike `requestTenderCv()`'s migration-0075-backed dedupe). `cv_extraction_results.applied` is simply overwritten a second time and both redirects report success.

**Fix**, same pattern as 0121/0113/0107/0114: move the whole read-gate-write sequence into one locked SQL transaction per caller, instead of three/two separate client queries. `apply_cv_extraction_checked()` and `apply_my_cv_extraction_checked()` (both `security definer`, new migration 0123) lock the `cv_extraction_results` row (`for update`), re-check company membership (`is_company_member()`), that `person_id` matches, and that `review_status` is still `'pending_review'`, all under that lock, then perform the people update (`_apply_cv_person_fields()` - a private, never-granted helper, same convention as 0024's `_manual_tender_documents()`, updating only the people columns whose key is present in the jsonb object, mirroring the TypeScript `personUpdate` object's own "only ticked keys present" shape exactly), the projects insert (full version only, from a `jsonb_array_elements()` pass over the ticked project rows), and the mark-applied write - all before releasing the lock. A second concurrent call for the SAME extraction blocks on the row lock until the first commits, then raises "These extracted fields were already saved or discarded." instead of silently re-applying. All validation (date format, select options, required fields, the SAST-anchored `source_note`) stays exactly where it was, in TypeScript; only the write itself moved into the database. Both Server Actions now make one `supabase.rpc()` call in place of their old three/two-separate-write sequence.

**Verified with a real two-session Postgres reproduction, not just unit tests.** Built a disposable scratch database (local Postgres 16, started and dropped for this pass only - never this app's live DB) with a minimal schema matching `companies`/`company_members`/`is_company_member()`/`people`/`projects`/`cv_uploads`/`cv_extraction_results` verbatim from `0001_init_schema.sql`/`0008_cv_uploads.sql`/`0023_cv_extraction_results.sql`. RED: a copy of the OLD three-separate-query shape (no lock, `pg_sleep(1)` right after the read to widen the window deterministically, same technique 0121's own repro used) run as two genuinely concurrent `psql` sessions against the SAME extraction - both calls returned successfully, final `projects` row count: **2** (the same project duplicated), `cv_extraction_results.applied` overwritten twice, no error either side. GREEN: the identical two concurrent calls against a `pg_sleep(1)`-widened copy of `apply_cv_extraction_checked()` (to prove the second caller genuinely BLOCKS on the lock rather than winning a fast race, confirmed by wall-clock timing - the second call's total time ~1.8s, consistent with waiting on the lock before its own 1s sleep): the first call committed normally (1 project row); the second call's `for update` blocked until the first committed, then raised the clear error - final `projects` row count: **1**, exactly one extraction applied. Direct functional checks against the real (non-sleep) functions confirmed: ticked person fields including a date field write correctly, a ticked project inserts correctly, `applied` metadata is stored correctly, a second synchronous call on an already-applied row raises cleanly, and `apply_my_cv_extraction_checked()` (no-projects variant) updates its one ticked field correctly. Scratch DB dropped and the Postgres service stopped at the end.

**Full TS/JS verification, all green.** `npm run typecheck` - exit `0`. `npx eslint .` - exit `0`, 0 errors, 3 pre-existing warnings (unchanged). `npx vitest run` - exit `0`, **503/503 passed, 66 files** (505 baseline minus 2: the now-obsolete TS-level "zero-rows-matched" race tests per apply function were consolidated into rpc-level success/failure pairs, since that race-detection logic moved into the new locked SQL function and is no longer separately observable at the TS mock layer; `app/app/people/actions.spec.ts` and `app/app/my-cv/actions.spec.ts` both updated to mock `supabase.rpc()` the same way they already mocked `.from()`, asserting on the real parameters passed to the rpc call). The node `*.test.ts` loop (plain `node <file>`, no flags) - **28 files, 0 failures**, unchanged. `npx next build` - clean, no errors. Full `engine/` Python sweep re-run as a regression check even though no Python changed - **86 files, 0 failures**, unchanged.

**Declined, named for the record, not fixed this pass:** `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts` (483 lines, the onboarding AI-document-review screen, 0063) has the identical angle-(b) shape repeated across five separate "confirm" paths sharing one gate (`loadPendingResult()`) and one shared "mark applied" write (`markApplied()`, no re-check of `review_status` in its own `.eq()` chain). The clearest instance: `confirmExperienceItem()`'s `experience_items.insert()` - two concurrent confirms of the same onboarding document would both pass the gate and both insert, the identical `projects`-duplication shape this finding just closed, just in a different table. `confirmCvHandoff()`'s `cv_uploads.insert()` has the same risk; `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmIdDocument()`'s column updates are lower severity (closer to idempotent, though each also orphans a freshly-`randomUUID()`-named storage copy on the losing side); `skipOnboardingDocument()`/`discardOnboardingDocument()` already guard against the RLS-revocation race (2026-11-06) but not this one. NOT fixed this pass because a correct fix needs a SEPARATE locked RPC per confirm path (five different target tables, each with its own storage-copy side effect) with the lock acquired before the FIRST dependent write, not just the last one (guarding only `markApplied()`'s own final write would not close the race, for the same reason it wouldn't have here) - a properly-scoped pass of its own, named here with exact function/line evidence so a future pass can open it directly.

**Backlog status.** Finding 168 and the `start_payfast_checkout()` revenue-integrity gap both remain exactly as left, untouched, per the standing guardrail. All 9 PRs remain open and unmerged (re-checked via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open`): `#176`/`#177`(draft)/`#178`/`#179`/`#180`/`#181`/`#182` and the two stale drafts `#164`/`#165`(both draft), same set every preceding pass has recorded - none touched, amended, or merged this pass. This pass's own new angle (TypeScript Server Action read-then-write/TOCTOU-gate races) is not fully exhausted - `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s own five-path version of the identical bug (named above) is the clear next candidate, using migration 0123 as the fix template. A second, lower-priority residual: `queueStandardCvs()`'s own pre-existing "no database-level backstop" gap no longer reachable via its one current call site (this fix stops the race before it ever gets there), but would need its own fix if a second trigger is ever added.

To verify independently: re-run this finding's own scratch-DB red/green reproduction (steps above) in a fresh disposable Postgres. Read `supabase/migrations/0123_cv_extraction_apply_race.sql` and confirm `apply_cv_extraction_checked()`/`apply_my_cv_extraction_checked()` both lock the `cv_extraction_results` row (`for update`) before any dependent write, and re-check `review_status = 'pending_review'` under that lock. Run `npm run typecheck`/`npx eslint .`/`npx vitest run`/the node `*.test.ts` loop/`npx next build` and confirm the exit codes and counts above. Confirm via `gh api repos/sareljvr2024/tender-tool/pulls?state=open` that all 9 PRs are still open/unmerged, and that `git log --oneline -1 origin/main` is this finding's own new commit, with no further sibling commits having landed in between.

### Finding 185 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-but-real - `confirmIdDocument()` (`app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts`) hardcoded a literal `null` for `reviewed_by` on every certified ID document ever filed through the onboarding document-scan screen, never threading through the real signed-in user's id that was already sitting free in its own `requireCompanyId()` return value - a deterministic, 100%-of-the-time audit-trail gap on this screen's single most compliance-sensitive document type, not a race)

**Note on numbering:** this is the next number actually landed in this file (184 was the highest recorded at the start of this pass, confirmed by grepping `### Finding [0-9]+` here before picking 185). **PR #183 (still open, not merged) self-labels its own fix as "Finding 185" in its own PR description** - that number has never actually landed in this file since #183 hasn't merged. Whoever merges #183 needs to renumber its own internal "Finding 185" references to the next free number at merge time (186 or higher, depending on what else has landed by then), since this entry has now taken 185 for real. Flagged here explicitly so that renumbering isn't missed.

**Area:** `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts` `confirmIdDocument()` (migration 0063's `id_document -> company_principals.certified_id_path` confirm path). Test coverage added in `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.spec.ts`.

**How this was found.** This pass's primary task was a GitHub-Actions-dispatched live check of `randwater.py` (see `System-Status.md` for that result, a repeatable real negative, not a bug fix). The task's own secondary fallback named `confirmIdDocument()`'s preserved `reviewed_by = null` quirk - flagged by Finding 184's own writeup as "worth a future pass's own look" (not that finding's bug) - for this pass to determine, on its own merits, whether it's deliberate or a genuine oversight.

Reading `confirmIdDocument()` end to end: it is the ONLY one of this file's four `markApplied()`-calling confirm paths whose `requireCompanyId()` destructuring drops `userId` entirely (`const { supabase, companyId } = await requireCompanyId()`, vs. `confirmVaultDocument()`/`confirmExperienceReferenceLetter()`/`confirmCvHandoff()`, which all destructure `userId` too) and passes a literal `null` into `markApplied(supabase, resultId!, null, ...)` where every sibling passes the real `userId`. `requireCompanyId()` itself (line 30) always returns `userId: user.id` - a non-null, already-authenticated value, at zero extra query cost; nothing stops `confirmIdDocument()` from using it.

**Why this is a genuine oversight, not a design choice - checked, not assumed.** (1) `git log --follow -p` on this file shows the literal `null` has been there since the function's very first commit (`eb5a846f`, 2026-10-18, migration 0063's own introduction) - never a later regression, but also never a documented choice. (2) No comment anywhere in the file explains it, unlike this file's own firm, demonstrated convention of commenting every deliberate quirk (e.g. `confirmExperienceReferenceLetter()`'s "left untagged on purpose" note, `confirmIdDocument()`'s own neighboring `certified_id_on`/SAST-anchoring comment two lines below the one that was wrong). (3) `reviewed_by` on `onboarding_document_results` is a real audit-trail column (migration 0063 line 137, `reviewed_by uuid references auth.users(id)`) that every other `document_kind`'s confirm path correctly fills with the real reviewer - `id_document` was the one silent exception. (4) The column is never displayed anywhere in this screen's own UI (`page.tsx`/`review.tsx` select neither `reviewed_by` nor `reviewed_at`), which is exactly why this has gone unnoticed through several subsequent patches to this same file (including two later race-condition fixes on lines immediately around it) - nobody looking at the UI would ever see the gap, only a raw-row audit/compliance query would.

**Real, reachable, deterministic consequence (not a race, not contrived) - checked against the only document type this matters most for.** Of this file's four confirm paths, `confirmIdDocument()` is the one filing a director/shareholder's own identity document (`company_principals.certified_id_path`) - the most KYC/compliance-sensitive document kind on this screen. Every single time any user has ever confirmed an ID document through this screen, `onboarding_document_results.reviewed_by` was stamped `NULL` instead of that user's own id - a 100% reproducible, always-wrong value (not a race window), genuinely load-bearing if a compliance review or dispute ever needs to know who actually reviewed and filed a specific principal's certified ID.

**Fix.** Thread the already-available `userId` through, exactly matching this file's three other confirm paths: `const { supabase, companyId, userId } = await requireCompanyId();` and `await markApplied(supabase, resultId!, userId, { table: "company_principals", id: principalId, column: "certified_id_path" });`. A comment was added at the function's own header explaining the gap and the fix, matching this file's own convention.

**Verification - red then green, no live/network dependency since this is a deterministic code bug, not a race.** Added a new test, `confirmIdDocument - reviewed_by on the mark-applied write is the real signed-in user, not null`, asserting the `markApplied()` call's own update payload has `reviewed_by: "user-1"` (the spec file's mocked signed-in user). **Red:** run against the unfixed code - real exit code `1`, `AssertionError: expected null to be 'user-1'` (`expected null to be 'user-1' // Object.is equality`), exactly the predicted failure. **Green:** restored the fix, re-ran - real exit code `0`, all 10 tests in the file pass (the 9 pre-existing plus this new one).

**Full verification suite, all green.** `npm run typecheck` - exit `0`. `npx eslint .` - exit `0`, 0 errors, 3 pre-existing warnings (`Logo.tsx` x2 `no-img-element`, `analytics/page.tsx` 1 unused-var), unchanged. `npx vitest run` - exit `0`, **504/504 passed, 66 files** (503 standing baseline + this pass's 1 new test). The node `*.test.ts` loop (plain `node <file>`, no flags) - **28 files, 0 failures**, unchanged. `npx next build` - clean, no errors. Full `engine/` Python sweep re-run as a regression check even though no Python changed - `find engine -name "test_*.py" | wc -l` = `86`, looped with plain `python3 <file>` - **86/86, 0 failures**, unchanged.

**Backlog status.** Finding 168 and the `start_payfast_checkout()` revenue-integrity gap both remain exactly as left, untouched, per the standing guardrail. ### Finding 186 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor - `extract_cv_fields.py`'s `fail_stale_uploads()` was the one `cv_extract` alert source in this file whose `system_alerts.record()` context never carried `company_id`, because its own GET query never selected the column, so the admin System Alerts page's "tenant: &lt;company&gt;" badge silently never appeared for any alert this function raised)

**Area:** `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py` `fail_stale_uploads()`. Test coverage added in `engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py`.

**How this was found.** This pass's task was a genuinely new angle on the engine layer: extending Finding 185's own method (reading a file's sibling functions/call-sites side by side for an unexplained, undocumented field-dropping inconsistency - not a race) to `engine/pack/`, `engine/notify/`, `engine/compliance/` and `engine/cv/`. Most of the obvious sibling families in these four directories turned out, on close reading, to already be correctly consistent or to have their difference already explained by an earlier pass (see "Also checked and ruled out" below) - this was the one that wasn't.

**The sibling family.** Every `system_alerts.record("cv_extract", ...)` call site in `extract_cv_fields.py` that has a `cv_uploads` row in hand puts that row's own `company_id` into `context` - `process_upload()`'s own 3 alerts (`context={"cv_upload_id": upload["id"], "company_id": upload.get("company_id"), ...}`, lines 903/910/915) and `poll_once()`'s own per-item alert (`context={"cv_upload_id": up.get("id"), "company_id": up.get("company_id")}`, line 972). `fail_stale_uploads()`'s own 3 alerts (lines 822, 851, 861 before this fix) were the one exception: `context={"cv_upload_id": up["id"], ...}` with no `company_id` at all, in the same file, same alert source, same general shape of row. The two true cross-file siblings this bug class was explicitly modelled on elsewhere - `process_pack_jobs.fail_stale_jobs()` (`context={..., "company_id": job.get("company_id"), "tender_id": ...}`) and `process_cv_jobs.py`'s own stale sweep (`context={..., "company_id": job.get("company_id"), "person_id": ...}`) - both already include `company_id` too; `fail_stale_uploads()` was the only one of the three that didn't.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `fail_stale_uploads()`'s own `GET` deliberately narrows its select to just what its own logic reads: `"cv_uploads?status=eq.extracting&select=id,extraction_claimed_at"`. That's a reasonable minimal-select instinct on its own - but as a side effect, `up` never carries `company_id` at all inside this one function, so none of its 3 `system_alerts.record()` calls could include it even if someone had thought to try. No comment anywhere explains the omission (unlike this file's own demonstrated habit of calling out every deliberate difference, e.g. the self-heal branch's own multi-line comment two lines above the alert it then under-informs).

**Real downstream consequence, confirmed by reading the actual consumer, not assumed.** `app/app/admin/page.tsx` (line 185) resolves `a.context?.company_id` through `platform_admin_companies()` into `resolvedCompanyName`, and `SystemAlertRow.tsx` renders that as a `tenant: <company>` badge on the alert row in the admin System Alerts panel - the one piece of UI a platform admin uses to see, at a glance, which company's background job broke. For every other stale-job alert in this codebase (SANRAL pack jobs, CV generation jobs) that badge renders. For a CV extraction stuck `extracting` long enough to be reclaimed - or one whose `extraction_claimed_at` was malformed, or one that self-healed after a worker died mid-write - the admin System Alerts page showed the alert with no tenant badge at all, every single time, with nothing to suggest which company's upload it was without opening a database console.

**Fix.** Widened `fail_stale_uploads()`'s own `GET` to `select=id,company_id,extraction_claimed_at` (one extra column, no new query), and added `"company_id": up.get("company_id")` to each of its 3 `system_alerts.record()` calls - matching this file's own `process_upload()`/`poll_once()` convention exactly. A comment was added at the new `select=` explaining why `company_id` is fetched even though this function's own logic never reads it.

### Finding 187 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `daily_digest.py`'s own finance/cv_admin role filters for the `document_expiry` section checked ONLY the literal string `"person_credential"`, so Finding 139's new `person_credential_before_closing` item type was silently dropped from cv_admin's digest - the ONE role whose entire job is to act on it - and silently shown to finance, whose own matrix rule explicitly says they should never see a person's credential renewal)

**Area:** Notify (`engine/notify/daily_digest.py`'s `build_digest_for_person()` - the role-based section
filtering that decides what each recipient's own daily digest email actually contains).

**Scenario:** found while reading `build_digest_for_person()`'s `document_expiry` section routing end
to end, specifically checking whether every item TYPE this section can ever carry is correctly
recognised by its own role filters - not assumed from the surrounding comments, which describe the
INTENT ("exactly the person_credential items") rather than the literal code
(`i.get("type") == "person_credential"`). Finding 139 (2026-11-06, this same standing QA track)
introduced a SECOND item type for the identical underlying fact - a specific person's own
professional registration, just scoped to a tender's closing date instead of the plain reminder
window - `"person_credential_before_closing"`. The finance-exclusion filter
(`item.get("type") != "person_credential"`) and the cv_admin-inclusion filter
(`item.get("type") == "person_credential"`) were never updated for it, since both check the one
literal string, not the underlying category.

**Confirmed live, not just reasoned about:** called `build_digest_for_person()` directly with a
`person_credential_before_closing` item and both roles. cv_admin's own digest came back with
`document_expiry: []` - the item was silently dropped, even though cv_admin's own matrix rule
("only if the expiring item would block a specific person's own registration being usable on a
pack") describes EXACTLY this item. finance's own digest came back WITH the item - even though
finance's own matrix rule ("not a person's ECSA/SACPCMP renewal, not theirs to act on") explicitly
excludes this exact case. Both role filters were doing the opposite of their own documented intent,
for every `person_credential_before_closing` item, ever since Finding 139 shipped the day before.

**Fix:** added `PERSON_CREDENTIAL_TYPES = ("person_credential", "person_credential_before_closing")`
and changed both filters from exact-equality checks to membership checks against this tuple. The
company-item types (`"document"`, `"document_before_closing"`, and Finding 179's new
`"held_registration_before_closing"`) were already correctly handled by both filters (they're simply
never equal to `"person_credential"`), so this fix touches only the person-credential branch.

**Verified red-then-green, against all three "before closing" item types at once.** New checks in
`test_watch_person_credentials.py`'s existing digest-routing section: a mixed batch of
`person_credential_before_closing`/`document_before_closing`/`held_registration_before_closing`
items - cv_admin must see exactly the person item, finance must see exactly the two company items.
Reverted `daily_digest.py` via `git apply -R`, re-ran - both new checks failed exactly as predicted
(cv_admin got nothing, finance got all three including the person item); reapplied - `0 failure(s)`.
`py_compile` clean. Regression: `test_digest_live.py`, `test_send_digest_emails.py`,
`test_digest_opt_in.py`, `test_watch_conditional_registrations.py`, `test_principals_registrations.py`
- all `0 failure(s)`.

**Regression:** `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (1 new module-level constant, 2 filter conditions
changed from `==`/`!=` to `in`/`not in`, ~15 lines including comments);
`engine/compliance/test_watch_person_credentials.py` (2 new checks appended to the existing
digest-routing test). No change to any other section's role filtering, `SECTION_VISIBILITY`, or the
`own()` company-scoping function.
