### Finding 204 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `extract_cv_fields.py`'s `_plausible_sa_id()` accepted a calendar-impossible "birth date" (30 Feb, 31 Apr, 31 Jun, 31 Sep, 31 Nov) as a plausible South African ID number, because it only checked `1 <= day <= 31` with no regard for the month - a contract/account/registration number from a CV that happened to pass the Luhn checksum, have a month 1-12 and citizenship digit 0/1, but land on one of these impossible days, could be wrongly proposed as the person's own `id_number`)

**Area:** `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py` `_plausible_sa_id()`, shared (imported, not duplicated) by `engine/onboarding/classify_documents.py`'s own two `find_and_redact_sa_ids()` call sites. Test coverage extended in `test_extract_cv_fields.py` (6 new cases).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on CV. The three main `engine/cv/*.py` files are each covered 150+ times across both docs already, so adversarial effort went into the actual checksum/date validation logic for South African ID numbers specifically - a classic boundary-input target this doc had not previously constructed a calendar-impossible date against. `_plausible_sa_id()`'s own day check, `1 <= dd <= 31`, takes no account of which month `dd` belongs to - constructing a 13-digit candidate with month=February and day=30, with a Luhn-valid final digit, confirmed it passed: `_plausible_sa_id("9002300001085")` returned `True`.

**Why this matters, not just cosmetic.** This function's accept/reject decision feeds two real, user-facing consequences: (1) `find_and_redact_sa_ids()` only PROPOSES a found run as a genuine SA ID for review when `_plausible_sa_id()` accepts it (rejected runs are left in the text or blanket-redacted on OCR'd text, but never offered as a confirmed ID); (2) `extract_cv_fields.py` line ~674 takes the FIRST accepted ID and writes it straight into `person["id_number"]`, surfaced to the user as "Found in the CV text." A real CV's own contract number, bank account number, or registration number is exactly the kind of 13-digit string that could coincidentally satisfy the Luhn checksum and the existing month/citizenship-digit checks while landing on a day that cannot exist in that month - with the pre-fix code, that non-ID number would be wrongly offered as the person's South African ID number.

**Fix.** `_plausible_sa_id()` now computes the real maximum day for that month via `calendar.monthrange()`, checked against BOTH possible centuries (the SA ID carries no century digit - a `YY` of e.g. "90" could be 1990 or 2090) and accepts the day if it's valid in at least one of them - this correctly handles 29 February (accepted only when at least one century interpretation makes that year a leap year) while rejecting every day that is impossible in any year regardless of century (31 Apr/Jun/Sep/Nov, 30/31 Feb).

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 6 new cases to `test_extract_cv_fields.py`: five calendar-impossible dates (30 Feb, 31 Apr, 31 Jun, 31 Sep, 31 Nov), each constructed with a real Luhn-valid check digit via the file's own existing `sa_id()` test helper and asserted rejected; one 29 Feb case (year "00", i.e. 1900/2000 - 2000 is a leap year) asserted ACCEPTED, confirming the fix doesn't over-correct into rejecting a real, valid leap-year ID. **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran `test_extract_cv_fields.py` - exactly the 5 new impossible-date cases failed as predicted (the 29 Feb case wasn't run standalone in isolation for red since the old code already accepted plain 1-31 days, so it was never expected to fail red - confirmed by inspection, not asserted either way in the red run). **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `ALL PASSED`. The pre-existing fixture (`SYNTH_ID`, a real 15 Feb 1990 date) confirmed unaffected throughout. `python3 -m py_compile` clean. Regression: `engine/onboarding/test_classify_documents.py` (the one other caller, via `cvx.find_and_redact_sa_ids()`, imported not duplicated) still passes unchanged.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'engine/cv'); import extract_cv_fields as x; print(x._plausible_sa_id('9002300001085'))"` and confirm it prints `False` (30 Feb), not `True`. Run `python3 engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` from its own directory and confirm `ALL PASSED`.

### Finding 205 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `lib/compileReadiness.ts`'s `assessCompileConfidence()` silently applied neither its `+20` "fingerprint ok" bonus nor its `-40` "mismatch/error" penalty, and added NO explanatory basis line at all, when `fingerprint_status` was `"no_baseline"` - a genuinely common, not rare, first-time-seeing-this-SANRAL-family state, breaking the function's own documented "one sentence per signal" contract and letting a never-before-verified workbook family score "high" confidence on `/admin/discovered-opportunities`)

**Area:** `app/lib/compileReadiness.ts` `assessCompileConfidence()`. Test coverage extended in `app/lib/compileReadiness.test.ts` (1 new case).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on intake. `engine/intake/classify_tender.py` is already covered 177 times across both docs, so effort went into the TypeScript side of the intake chain instead - `lib/compileReadiness.ts`, the admin-facing "can our engine actually compile this" confidence score, with only 8 prior mentions. Reading its own weight-table docstring (lines 161-165: "+20 fingerprintOk... -40 fingerprintBad... MISMATCHES... or could not even be fingerprinted") against the real `RequirementsExtraction.fingerprint_status` type (`"ok" | "mismatch" | "no_baseline" | "error" | null`) showed the docstring's own two-way framing ("ok" vs "bad") never accounted for the type's third, genuinely distinct value, `"no_baseline"` - confirmed this is reachable and reads straight from `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s own `check_fingerprint()`, which returns exactly this status (not as an edge case, but as the literal first-ever-seen-this-family path: "No stored baseline to compare against yet").

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** The fingerprint scoring code only has two branches: `if (status === "ok")` and `else if (status === "mismatch" || status === "error")` - no `else`, so `"no_baseline"` (and, in principle, `null`/`undefined`, though those aren't produced once `status === "extracted"`) falls through both, contributing zero to `level` AND pushing nothing to `basis`. Confirmed live: calling `assessCompileConfidence()` with a matched SANRAL family and `fingerprint_status: "no_baseline"` returned `{level: 85, band: "high"}` with a `basis` array that never mentions the fingerprint check at all - silently violating the function's own documented promise ("One sentence per signal that moved the number - shown verbatim in the UI, in order applied"), a promise every OTHER signal in this same function honours even for its own "nothing happened" case (e.g. "`+0`: no documents are listed for this release at all.").

**Why this is a real problem, not cosmetic.** A brand-new SANRAL workbook family with no stored baseline is the one case where whether `sanral_fill.py` can even run on it cleanly is genuinely UNCONFIRMED - the fingerprint check exists precisely to catch that. Landing at `"high"` (85/100) purely from the family-name match bonus, with the admin screen's own "why this number" explanation silently omitting the one signal that should have tempered it, is exactly the kind of overclaimed confidence this module's own docstring says it was built to avoid ("this is NOT a separate guess", "never allowed to read as high confidence" for the pre-extraction case).

**Fix.** Added the missing `else if (requirements.fingerprint_status === "no_baseline")` branch: a `+0` (explicit, not silent) adjustment with its own basis line naming the real caveat ("no stored baseline exists yet for this workbook family... whether sanral_fill can actually run on it cleanly is still unconfirmed"). Deliberately left the numeric adjustment at zero rather than inventing a new penalty value - this module's own stated job is to report what's known, not for a QA pass to unilaterally decide a new weight Sarel hasn't signed off on; the `effectiveConfidence()` override mechanism already exists for exactly this kind of human judgement call, and the fix at minimum ensures he's told the caveat is there at all.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added a test asserting (a) the `no_baseline` case's own `basis` array mentions "no stored baseline", and (b) it scores strictly lower than the otherwise-identical `"ok"` case (a weaker assertion than a specific point value, since the numeric weight itself is a judgement call, not this fix's to dictate). **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran `node --experimental-strip-types lib/compileReadiness.test.ts` - failed exactly as predicted (`basis` never contains "no stored baseline"). **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - 15/15 pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both clean. Broader regression: every other `*.test.ts` file in `app/` run directly, unaffected; confirmed via grep that `assessCompileConfidence()`'s only two real callers (`/admin/discovered-opportunities/page.tsx` and its own `OpportunityRow.tsx`) are unaffected by anything beyond the new basis line and the (now-explicit, previously-implicit) `+0`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: call `assessCompileConfidence(base, {status: "extracted", route: "sanral", family: "X", fingerprint_status: "no_baseline", missing: [], unreadable_documents: [], failed_downloads: 0})` and confirm the returned `basis` array now includes a line naming "no stored baseline". Run `cd app && node --experimental-strip-types lib/compileReadiness.test.ts` and confirm `15/15 pass`.

## 2026-11-08li (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 216 - `lib/savingsCounter.ts`'s `resolveBaseline()` could never actually flag `isDefault: true` for a real company, because the two `companies` columns it null-checks have been `not null default 20`/`default 450` since the column was created - every never-touched company's own "confirm your baseline" messaging, across 4 separate UI surfaces, silently claimed an already-confirmed figure from day one

**Area:** `app/lib/savingsCounter.ts` `resolveBaseline()`, consumed by `app/lib/savingsCounterData.ts`'s `fetchSavingsCounterSummary()`/`fetchTenderSavingsBreakdown()` and, through those, by `components/tt/savings-counter-card.tsx`, `app/tenders/[id]/submission-pack.tsx`, and (as of the still-open PR `#164`) the new `components/tt/savings-calculation-dialog.tsx`. Test coverage extended in `app/lib/savingsCounter.spec.ts` (1 new case) and corrected in `app/lib/savingsCounterData.spec.ts` (1 existing fixture's mock values).

**How this was found.** Found while giving the still-open PR `#164` ("Capacity Unlocked" savings-counter rework) its full line-by-line read, part of this review segment's standing PR backlog sweep (not this file's own dated-run rotation). `#164`'s own diff adds a brand-new UI surface, `savings-calculation-dialog.tsx`, that branches its entire bottom message on `summary.usingDefaultBaseline` - reading that flag's origin led straight to `resolveBaseline()`, the one function `savingsCounter.ts`'s own header comment names as "the one place that decides 'is this company's own confirmed number, or did we fall back to the placeholder.'" Its logic, `isDefault = hoursPerTender == null || hourlyCostZar == null`, looked correct in isolation - until cross-referenced against where its two arguments actually come from: `companies.savings_baseline_hours_per_tender`/`savings_baseline_hourly_cost_zar`, read straight off the row by every one of its callers.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `grep -rln "savings_baseline_hours_per_tender\|savings_baseline_hourly_cost_zar" app/supabase/migrations/` returns exactly one file: `0085_savings_counter.sql`, whose own `alter table` lines read `numeric not null default 20` and `numeric not null default 450` - no later migration ever relaxes either `not null`. So for any real `companies` row, Postgres can never return SQL NULL for either column - a brand-new company that has never opened Company Settings reads back the exact same non-null `20`/`450` as one that explicitly typed those numbers in as its own real, deliberately-confirmed figures, and `resolveBaseline()`'s `== null` check has no way to tell the two apart. **Reproduced live, not concluded from reading**: built a scratch Postgres from `main`'s real 113 migrations (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U postgres -d tt_pr164`), ran `insert into companies (id, legal_name) values ('4444...', 'Brand New Co');` (every other column left to its own default) and queried it back: `savings_baseline_hours_per_tender = 20`, `hours_is_null = f` - confirmed live. Then ran the real, unmodified `resolveBaseline()` directly (`node --experimental-strip-types`): `resolveBaseline(20, 450)` returned `{hoursPerTender: 20, hourlyCostZar: 450, isDefault: false}` - the exact bug, reproduced against the function's own real code, not inferred from its text.

**Why this matters, and why it was missed for so long.** `savingsCounter.ts`'s own header comment states Sarel's explicit product rule for this exact number: "Spec v3 §18, Sarel's own answer (2026-10-22): no real measured data exists behind 20h/R450 - it must stay a visibly-flagged proposed default the user can confirm or change, never presented as fact." With this bug, it WAS presented as fact, for every company, from the day this flag started gating any UI copy. Confirmed this directly contradicts an already-correct sibling check living on the very same dashboard page: `app/app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s own setup-checklist `done` computation for its "confirm your baseline" item reads `companyRow?.savings_baseline_hours_per_tender !== 20 || companyRow?.savings_baseline_hourly_cost_zar !== 450` - a VALUE-equality check, not a null check - and its own in-file comment says this is deliberate "because the two columns are never null post-onboarding." Whoever wrote that comment already knew the fact that broke `resolveBaseline()`; the two pieces of logic were just never reconciled with each other, confirmed by reading both side by side on the same page, both still present, unreconciled, as of PR `#164`'s own current diff (which edits the surrounding JSX on that exact page without touching either check). The existing unit tests for `resolveBaseline()` never caught it because every one of them passes a literal `null`/`undefined` straight into the pure function, which trivially exercises the null branch correctly - none of them exercises the function with the one input shape its real callers can ever actually produce (`20`/`450`, non-null, from the column default). A separate existing test, `savingsCounterData.spec.ts`'s "ordinary success path" case (written 2026-11-06, for an unrelated error-handling fix), used a mock `OK_COMPANY` of literally `{20, 450}` and asserted `usingDefaultBaseline === false` against it - encoding the exact bug as the expected, passing behaviour for two days before this pass re-derived it from the schema instead of trusting that fixture.

**Fix.** `resolveBaseline()`'s `isDefault` now also flags true when both resolved values equal the placeholder defaults exactly, in addition to the existing null checks: `isDefault = hoursPerTender == null || hourlyCostZar == null || (resolvedHours === DEFAULT_BASELINE_HOURS_PER_TENDER && resolvedCost === DEFAULT_BASELINE_HOURLY_COST_ZAR)`. This is the same tradeoff `dashboard/page.tsx`'s own sibling check already makes and already accepts (a company that deliberately confirms a real baseline that happens to exactly equal 20h/R450 is still shown "using a default estimate" until it changes something) - not a new tradeoff this fix introduces, just the first time `resolveBaseline()` itself was brought into line with it. `savingsCounterData.spec.ts`'s `OK_COMPANY` fixture changed from `{20, 450}` to `{30, 600}` so its own "ordinary successful fetch" test keeps testing a genuinely confirmed company, not the coincidence this fix closes.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added one new case to `savingsCounter.spec.ts`: `resolveBaseline(20, 450)` now asserted to return `isDefault: true`. **Red:** ran the new assertion against the unfixed function first - failed exactly as predicted (`expected isDefault: true, got isDefault: false`), matching the live reproduction above. **Green:** applied the fix, re-ran `npx vitest run lib/savingsCounter.spec.ts lib/savingsCounterData.spec.ts` - **31/31 pass**, including every one of the 6 pre-existing `resolveBaseline()` cases unchanged (none of them happened to test exactly `20`-and-`450`-together, confirmed by reading each one before relying on this). **Full verification suite, all run myself, real exit codes.** `npm run typecheck` (0 errors). `npx eslint .` (0 errors, same 3 pre-existing warnings - `Logo.tsx`'s 2 `<img>` warnings, `analytics/page.tsx`'s unused `STAGE_META` - neither in a file this fix touches). `npx vitest run` - **533/533, 71 files**. The node `*.test.ts` loop (every file under `app/`, run directly, one by one - all exit 0). `npx next build` - compiled clean, same route table, exit 0. No migration touched by this fix, so `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` was not re-run.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. This bug's root cause (the column default, `resolveBaseline()`'s own logic) lives entirely on `main`, untouched by the still-open `#164`'s own diff (confirmed via that diff's own context lines) - `#164` adds two new consumers of the already-broken flag but did not cause the breakage, so this was fixed directly on `main` rather than treated as documented-only; `#164`'s own branch was never touched, built on, or pushed to. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between. The scratch Postgres this pass built (`tt_pr164`) was dropped and the Postgres service stopped at the end of the same pass (see this entry's own `System-Status.md` write-up for the exact commands).

To verify independently: `cd app && node --experimental-strip-types -e "import {resolveBaseline} from './lib/savingsCounter.ts'; console.log(resolveBaseline(20,450))"` and confirm it now prints `isDefault: true`. Confirm the column default live: replay `main`'s migrations into a scratch Postgres, `insert into companies (id, legal_name) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'x');`, and select `savings_baseline_hours_per_tender` back - confirm `20`, never `NULL`. Run `npx vitest run lib/savingsCounter.spec.ts lib/savingsCounterData.spec.ts` (31/31), the full `npx vitest run` (533/533, 71 files), `npm run typecheck`, `npx eslint .`, and `npx next build`.

## 2026-11-08lii (standing solution-architect review, background worker): Finding 217 - `app/lib/principals.ts`'s `isValidSaId()` checked only the Luhn checksum, silently accepting a 13-digit number whose embedded birth date is impossible (or whose citizenship digit is neither 0 nor 1) as "a valid South African ID number" - the exact gap `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`'s sibling check, `_plausible_sa_id()`, was hardened against the very same day, earlier in this review segment

**Area:** `app/lib/principals.ts`'s `isValidSaId()`, the sole hard-validation gate `app/app/company/principals/actions.ts`'s `savePrincipal()` runs before saving a Directors & Shareholders register entry's `id_number`, and the sole check behind `idWarnings()`'s "ID number ... is not valid" message shown on the Principals page. Test coverage added in `app/lib/principals.spec.ts` (5 new cases).

**How this was found.** Assigned this pass: generalize this review segment's established "sibling comparison" technique (most recently Finding 216, `savingsCounter.ts` vs `dashboard/page.tsx`) to `engine/`'s Python side, specifically hunting for business logic the Python engine reimplements that ALSO exists in TypeScript or SQL, silently diverged. Swept `engine/` for duplicated calculations/validations (savings-baseline math - none found, `app/lib/savingsCounter.ts`'s model has no Python counterpart; deadline/expiry lead-times in `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py` - already explicitly cross-referenced against `app/lib/dates.ts`/`vaultDocuments.ts` in that file's own docstring, confirmed still matching, `60`/`30` days on both sides; `company_members.tender_role`'s `VALID_ROLES` in `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` - matches migration `0010`'s own check constraint exactly; CIDB grade-vs-value table - TS-only (`app/lib/cidbGrading.ts`'s public lead-magnet tool), no Python counterpart to diverge from; B-BBEE points-by-level table in `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s `_bbbee_points_by_level()` - PARSED from each tender's own document text, not a hardcoded duplicate of `app/lib/preferencePoints.ts`'s static `BEE_POINTS_TABLE`, so no drift risk; the discipline-taxonomy `fit_overlap()`/`matched_by_group_tag` semantics in `engine/discovery/taxonomy.py` vs `app/lib/opportunityDisciplineMatch.ts` - deliberately, explicitly reconciled by an earlier standing-review pass (2026-11-04, named in `opportunityDisciplineMatch.ts`'s own comments) and re-verified by tracing both sides' logic line by line: still consistent; `engine/general/submission_plan.py`'s `cidbGradingStep` equivalent vs `app/app/tenders/[id]/submission-plan-logic.ts`'s `cidbGradingStep()` - both deliberately delegate the actual grade-vs-requirement comparison to a human ("Tender Tool doesn't compare grading levels for you"), so there is no computed value on either side to diverge). Found the real divergence while following the task's own explicit lead ("path/filename sanitization... already done this segment, don't redo it") past it to the next thing `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py` validates locally: South African ID numbers. That file's own `_plausible_sa_id()` had a comment, dated literally today (2026-11-08), describing a just-fixed QA pass that hardened it against calendar-impossible dates. Grepping the TypeScript side for the equivalent concept (`isValidSaId`, `sa_id`, `idNumber`) surfaced `app/lib/principals.ts`'s own same-purpose function - reading it found it was never brought up to the same standard its Python sibling had just reached.

**Root cause, traced, not guessed.** `isValidSaId()`'s own one-line comment stated its actual scope exactly: "SA ID: 13 digits with a valid Luhn check digit" - Luhn only, nothing else. `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`'s `_plausible_sa_id()` (used to decide whether a 13-digit run found in a CV's text is even worth proposing as someone's ID number) requires three things: a valid Luhn checksum, a plausible embedded date (month 1-12, day valid for that month in either possible century, since the ID carries no century digit), and a citizenship digit (position 11) of `0` or `1`. `isValidSaId()` is called from exactly the kind of place that needs the stricter check - a hard save-gate (`actions.ts`, `fail()`s the whole form submission if it returns false) and the one-and-only producer of "is this number wrong" feedback (`idWarnings()`) - yet only ever ran the first of the three checks.

**Reproduced live, both sides, same inputs, not concluded from reading.** Imported the real, unmodified `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py` directly (`python3 -c "import extract_cv_fields as m; print(m._plausible_sa_id('0000000000000'))"`) and ran the real TypeScript `isValidSaId()` body (copied verbatim) under `node` on the same three inputs:

| input | Python `_plausible_sa_id()` | TS `isValidSaId()` (pre-fix) |
|---|---|---|
| `0000000000000` (every digit 0 - Luhn-valid, month 00) | `False` | `True` |
| `0013000000003` (Luhn-valid, month 13) | `False` | `True` |
| `9001010000585` (Luhn-valid, a real date 1990-01-01, citizenship digit `5`) | not re-run (Python has no separate citizenship-digit case in this exact test, but its own `digits[10] in "01"` check means it would also return `False`) | `True` |

All three are genuinely Luhn-valid (checked by computing the Luhn sum directly, not assumed) - this is exactly the class of input the function exists to catch: a data-entry mistake, a placeholder/test value, or an unrelated 13-digit number (an account or contract number) that happens to pass the arithmetic checksum by chance. Before this fix, none of them tripped `idWarnings()`'s own warning, and none of them would have been rejected by `savePrincipal()`'s hard gate - a company could save `0000000000000` as a director's ID number with the app reporting nothing wrong.

**Fix.** `isValidSaId()` now also checks the embedded date (`mm` 1-12, `dd` valid for that month in either century - same "accept if valid in EITHER possible century" rule `parseSaId()` already uses for display, extracted into a small shared `isPlausibleIdDate()` helper) and the citizenship digit (`id[10]` must be `"0"` or `"1"`) - the same three checks, in the same order, as `_plausible_sa_id()`. The two user-facing messages that named "check digit" specifically (`idWarnings()`'s warning text, `actions.ts`'s `fail()` text) were reworded to not overclaim which specific check failed, since a rejection can now also mean an implausible date or citizenship digit, not only a bad checksum.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 5 new cases to `app/lib/principals.spec.ts`, each using an independently-computed, genuinely Luhn-valid test number (not guessed): rejects `0000000000000` (impossible date), rejects `0013000000003` (impossible month), rejects `9001010000585` (real date, invalid citizenship digit `5`), accepts `9001010000080` (real date, valid citizenship digit `0`), and the two pre-existing "not 13 digits / fails Luhn" cases. **Red:** `git stash push -- app/lib/principals.ts` (keeping the new test file), ran `npx vitest run lib/principals.spec.ts` against the unfixed function - **3 failed, 10 passed** (the 3 new "rejects" cases failed exactly as predicted: `expected false, got true`; the "accepts" case and the pre-existing cases already passed, since the fix only narrows acceptance, never widens it). **Green:** `git stash pop` to restore the fix, re-ran - **13/13 pass**. **Full verification suite, all run myself, real exit codes.** `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors). `npx eslint lib/principals.ts lib/principals.spec.ts app/company/principals/actions.ts` (0 errors). `npx vitest run` - **538/538, 71 files** (the 5 new cases on top of the prior pass's 533). The node `*.test.ts` loop (every file under `app/`, run directly - all exit 0, 0 fail each). `npx next build` - compiled clean, same route table, exit 0. `python3 engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` (the Python sibling's own regression suite, unaffected by this TS-only fix, run as a sanity check) - `ALL PASSED`, exit 0.

### Finding 218 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - the identical "lapses before closing" gap already found and fixed three times for company vault documents (Finding 132), key-person credentials (Finding 139) and the registrations catalog (2026-11-07 QA pass) had a fourth, previously-unswept instance: `property_documents` had NO "lapses before closing" coverage anywhere at all - not in `watch_deadlines.py`'s own `--out` report, not in `daily_digest.py`'s live email channel, and not even reactively in `app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts`)

**Area:** `engine/compliance/registration_reminders.py` (new `find_property_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`), `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py` (wired into `main()`'s `--out` report), `engine/notify/daily_digest.py` (wired into `document_expiry_signals()`, the live email channel). Test coverage added in `engine/compliance/test_principals_registrations.py` (1 new fixture row + 6 new assertions + 1 new standalone test function).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on compliance/reminders. The established "lapses before closing" bug class - a document/credential that is fine TODAY (outside the normal reminder lead-time window) but will have lapsed by the closing date of an open tender the company is preparing - has been found and fixed three separate times in this doc's own history for three of the four document families this system tracks: company vault documents (Finding 132), key-person professional credentials (Finding 139), and the shared registrations catalog, `held_registrations` (this session's own 2026-11-07 QA pass). Reading `registration_reminders.py`'s own `find_due_property_documents()` side by side with its sibling `find_due_registrations()` (which DOES have a "before closing" counterpart) showed `property_documents` was the one family of the four with no such coverage at all. Confirmed by reading `watch_deadlines.main()` in full (only the in-window checks were ever wired in for property documents) and by `grep -n "property_document" app/lib/tenderCompliance.ts` returning nothing - not even the reactive, UI-only fallback this codebase uses elsewhere when a live-reminder equivalent is deliberately deferred.

**Why this matters.** A property document - a fire safety certificate, an electrical certificate of compliance, a municipal rates clearance, an occupancy certificate - backs a company's own office/premises, which can itself be a tender requirement (locality/local-office compliance). Exactly the same "fine for now, useless by closing day" shape as every other document family this system already protects against: a certificate expiring in 90 days reads as "current" under the normal 60-day reminder window right up until day 60, even though it is already dead for a tender closing on day 100 - and with no coverage at all, nobody was ever told.

**Fix.** Added `find_property_documents_lapsing_before_closing()` to `registration_reminders.py`, structurally identical to `find_held_registrations_lapsing_before_closing()` (same SAST closing-day normalisation, same malformed-closing-date alert carrying `company_id`, same seen-store dedup key shape, same "skip if already in the normal window or already covers/passed the closing date" guards) - company-wide scope, since a property document has no per-tender assignment concept (unlike a key person's own credential). Wired into both `watch_deadlines.py`'s `main()` (`--out` report, new `property_documents_before_closing` key) and `daily_digest.py`'s `document_expiry_signals()` (the live email channel) in the same pass that built it - the established discipline this doc's own prior "before closing" fixes name explicitly (Finding 132's own `documents_before_closing` went 2 days without the live-digest wiring the first time; every fix since has wired both at once). The new item type, `"property_document_before_closing"`, needed no change to `daily_digest.py`'s own finance/cv_admin role-routing filter (`PERSON_CREDENTIAL_TYPES`) - it correctly falls through to finance's bucket and stays out of cv_admin's, the same as every other company-level item type, confirmed by reading that filter rather than assumed.

**Verified red-then-green.** Extended the existing `property_documents` fixture in `test_principals_registrations.py`'s `part1()` with `pd3` (90 days out, same shape as the existing `h6` row for the registrations-catalog fix), and added assertions that it IS reported by the new function (named correctly, tender-labelled, de-duped on a second run) while `pd1` (already inside the normal window) and `pd2` (no expiry date at all) are NOT. Added a standalone malformed-closing-date test mirroring the existing one for `find_held_registrations_lapsing_before_closing()`, confirming the new function's own alert carries `company_id`. **Red:** saved a single diff of all 3 production files, `git apply -R`, re-ran `test_principals_registrations.py` - failed immediately with `AttributeError: module 'registration_reminders' has no attribute 'find_property_documents_lapsing_before_closing'`, confirming the function and its wiring are both genuinely new, not already present. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on all 4 touched files. Broader regression: `test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py`, `test_digest_live.py`, `test_digest_opt_in.py` and `test_send_digest_emails.py` (the suites most likely to indirectly exercise this wiring) all still pass unchanged.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry found one new sibling commit (`49e79d2`, Finding 217 - a `principals.ts` SA ID validation gap, itself building on this same session's own earlier Finding 204 fix, no collision with this pass's own 4 files) - fast-forward merge was clean, and `git fetch` again immediately before pushing showed no further sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: construct a `property_documents` row 90 days from expiry for a company with an open `tender_packs` row whose tender closes in 100 days, and confirm `registration_reminders.find_property_documents_lapsing_before_closing()` reports it with `status: "lapses_before_closing"`. Run `python3 engine/compliance/test_principals_registrations.py` from its own directory and confirm `0 failure(s)`.

### Finding 219 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `savePerson()` had NO validation at all on `people.id_number` - not a digit-count check, not the full check its own same-purpose sibling runs - while `app/app/company/principals/actions.ts`'s `savePrincipal()` already hard-gates the identical real-world field, `company_principals.id_number`, with `isValidSaId()`)

**Area:** `app/app/people/actions.ts` (`savePerson()`). Test coverage added in `app/app/people/actions.spec.ts` (3 new cases).

**How this was found.** Generalizing Finding 217's own shape ("a hard-validation gate checks only PART of what it should, because a same-purpose sibling was hardened and this one wasn't told") beyond SA ID numbers specifically, per this pass's own brief: swept every "is this a real/valid X" hard-validation gate in the codebase (VAT numbers, CIPC registration numbers, bank account numbers/branch codes, phone numbers, email addresses, CIDB numbers, tax numbers) for a same-purpose sibling that is stricter. Nearly every one of those fields turned out to have NO format validation anywhere on either side of the stack (see "Also swept" below) - genuine negatives, not a gap to fix, since there is no sibling to have diverged from. The one genuine hit was closer to home than any of the named starting points: `people.id_number`. Its own column comment (`app/supabase/migrations/0001_init_schema.sql` line 97-100) states plainly what it is - "Real PII (a South African ID number)" - the exact same real-world field `company_principals.id_number` is (`0050_principals_registrations_properties.sql`), which carries both a DB-level format check (`id_number ~ '^[0-9]{13}$'`) AND a full application-level gate, `savePrincipal()`'s `isValidSaId()` call (`app/app/company/principals/actions.ts` line 76), the same function this doc's own Finding 217 just hardened. Grepping `app/app/people/actions.ts` for `isValidSaId` or any `id_number`-related check returned nothing; reading `savePerson()` end to end confirmed `id_number: str(formData, "id_number")` was written straight into the insert/update row, untouched, with no gate of any kind, and `people.id_number` itself has no DB check constraint either (confirmed: no later migration touches `people.id_number` - `grep -rn "alter table people" app/supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows only `linked_user_id`/`employment_status`/`ecsa_expiry`/`sacnasp_*` columns added, never a constraint on `id_number`).

**Why this matters, not hypothetical.** `people.id_number` is read verbatim and printed onto real government tender submission documents: `engine/fill_tender.py` and `engine/fill_conventional.py` (`wb.set_value(T, at(B["id"], base), str(person["id_number"]))`), `engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py`'s SBD4 "Identity Number of representative" field (`signatory_id_number`), and onto the person's own generated CV (`engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s "ID Number:" line). Before this fix, a company admin editing a team member's profile at `/people/[id]` could type anything at all into the ID number field - `"abc123def0123"`, a company's own VAT number pasted into the wrong box, a placeholder like `"0000000000000"` - and it would save with no warning, no error, nothing, then later print verbatim onto an actual SBD4 or A2 form submitted to a real government buyer. The exact same garbage value, submitted through `/company/principals` for a director instead, is correctly refused today (`"That ID number isn't a valid 13-digit South African ID number."`) by the very sibling gate this field never got told about. Confirmed the CV-extraction AUTOMATED write path into this same column is NOT affected - `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`'s own `_plausible_sa_id()` (line 353, the Python sibling Finding 217 is about) already gates what `process_cv_jobs.py` proposes for `people.id_number` from a scanned CV - the gap was specifically the MANUAL edit path, `savePerson()`, which bypasses that extraction pipeline entirely.

**Reproduced live, not concluded from reading.** Ran the real, unmodified `isValidSaId()` (`app/lib/principals.ts`) under `node --experimental-strip-types` against the exact values this finding is about:

```
abc123def0123 -> false
0000000000000 -> false
8601205135087 -> true   (a genuinely Luhn-valid, plausible-date, citizenship-digit-0 SA ID -
                          the same fixture engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py already uses as its
                          own "Test Person")
```

Then confirmed, by reading `savePerson()`'s pre-fix body line by line, that none of these would ever reach a check - `abc123def0123` and `0000000000000` would both have saved to `people.id_number` with the page reporting success.

**Fix.** `savePerson()` now computes `id_number` once, trims whitespace, and - mirroring `savePrincipal()`'s own pattern exactly, same function, same user-facing message - redirects with `"That ID number isn't a valid 13-digit South African ID number."` and does not write anything if `isValidSaId()` returns false for a non-blank value. A blank value still means "not recorded" (`null`), unchanged from before - this field has never required a value, and that is not what was broken.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added 3 new cases to `app/app/people/actions.spec.ts`: rejects `abc123def0123` with no insert attempted (**red, pre-fix:** this case crashed instead of redirecting cleanly - `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'id')` at the unconditional `insert()` call, since the mock Supabase queue (deliberately) had nothing queued past `requireCompanyId()`, proving the pre-fix code really does fall through to attempting the write rather than stopping earlier); accepts the genuinely-valid `8601205135087` and inserts normally; still allows a blank `id_number` to save as "not recorded". **Green, post-fix:** all 3 new cases pass, 15/15 in this file. **Full verification suite, all run myself, real exit codes.** `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors). `npx eslint app/people/actions.ts app/people/actions.spec.ts` (0 errors). `npx vitest run` - **541/541, 71 files** (the 3 new cases on top of Finding 218's 538). The node `*.test.ts` loop (every file under `app/`, run directly - all exit 0). `npx next build` - compiled clean, same route table, exit 0. `python3 engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` (the CV-extraction sibling's own regression suite, unaffected by this TS-only fix) - `ALL PASSED`, exit 0.

**Also swept, found clean - genuine negatives, not padding.** VAT numbers: no check-digit validator exists anywhere in `app/lib`, `app/app` or `engine/` - `vat_number` is free text, trimmed, nothing else, on every write path (`companyProfileUpdate.ts`'s `COMPANY_TEXT_FIELDS` loop); `engine/general/requirements.py`'s `VAT_RE` only matches a "14% VAT" MENTION in tender text, not a VAT registration number. CIPC company registration numbers: same - free text everywhere, no `YYYY/NNNNNN/NN`-shaped regex on either side. Bank account numbers: `app/app/company/bank-accounts/actions.ts`'s `/^[0-9]{6,16}$/` gate matches `0050_principals_registrations_properties.sql`'s own DB check constraint (`account_number ~ '^[0-9]{6,16}$'`) character-for-character - consistent, confirmed by direct comparison, not a gap. Bank branch codes: free text everywhere (TS, SQL, Python), no format check to have diverged. Phone numbers: no format validator anywhere - CV/document extraction only checks that the extracted digits appear somewhere in the source text (`extract_cv_fields.py`/`classify_documents.py`'s own provenance check), not that they form a valid phone number; no regex-based phone validator exists in TS at all. Email addresses: the one real check in use, `"@" in email` / `.includes("@")`, is applied identically in all three places that filter email recipients before sending (`app/lib/notificationRecipients.ts`, `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`, `engine/notify/send_digest_emails.py`) - consistently weak, not diverged; no custom validator gates a company/person email field anywhere (free text throughout `people/actions.ts`, `principals/actions.ts`, `experience/actions.ts`). CIDB registration numbers/grading codes: free text everywhere; `app/lib/cidbGrading.ts`'s own grade-vs-contract-value table was already confirmed TS-only with no Python counterpart by the immediately preceding pass. Tax numbers / SARS TCS PIN / CSD supplier number / ECSA & SACPCMP professional registration numbers: free text everywhere, no checksum or structured-format validator on either side of the stack for any of them.

Pure TypeScript logic fix, no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change - fixed directly on `main` per the standing guardrails. `git fetch origin main` at the start of this pass found `main` already at `49e79d2` (Finding 217, confirmed unchanged from the task brief's own stated HEAD); re-fetched again before writing this entry and found one new sibling commit, `a4d31c9` (Finding 218 - `property_documents` "lapses before closing" coverage, an unrelated file set: `registration_reminders.py`/`watch_deadlines.py`/`daily_digest.py`/its own test file) - fast-forwarded cleanly (`git merge --ff-only`), no collision, confirmed by `git status` showing this pass's own two modified files (`app/app/people/actions.ts`, `app/app/people/actions.spec.ts`) untouched by the fast-forward. ### Finding 220 (CONFIRMED, label fixed only - the rest left for Sarel's judgment call per the task brief, moderate-to-high depending on that call - `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx`'s edit form claimed `people.id_number` is "masked" when nothing anywhere masks it; generalized the check across the whole app and found this is the ONE place the claim is false - `company_principals.id_number`, the identical real-world field, IS genuinely masked, by a helper that already existed in this codebase when the false claim was introduced)

**Area:** `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx` (label text only, this pass). Investigation only, no architectural fix, covering `app/app/people/page.tsx`, `app/app/company/principals/page.tsx`, `app/lib/principals.ts`, `app/app/company/bank-accounts/page.tsx`, `app/supabase/migrations/0001_init_schema.sql`/`0077_company_invites_and_employee_role.sql` (RLS).

**How this was found.** Finding 219's own pass (this same day) noticed but did not chase this while fixing `savePerson()`'s validation gap, and flagged it explicitly in both `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` and `System-Status.md` for a follow-up pass - this is that follow-up, per the task brief's own three-part charge: (1) confirm the one flagged claim independently, (2) grep the whole app for every other "masked"/"redacted"/"PII" label and verify each independently, (3) check whether `people.id_number`/`company_principals.id_number`/similar sensitive fields reach the browser unmasked via `select("*")` or a wide column list ANYWHERE, label or no label.

**(1) The flagged claim, confirmed independently - not assumed from the preceding pass's own read.** Read `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx` end to end. Line 298: `supabase.from("people").select("*").eq("id", id).maybeSingle()` - a real table (`create table people`, `0001_init_schema.sql` line 94; not a view, confirmed by grepping every migration for `create view people`/`create table people` - only the latter exists), so no DB-level redaction happens before the row reaches the server. Line 490 (pre-fix): `<input ... name="id_number" defaultValue={person?.id_number ?? ""} />`, directly under a label reading "ID number (PII - masked)" (line 489). Traced every other candidate masking point and found none: no client component re-masks it (`grep -n "id_number" app/app/people/[id]/cv-review.tsx` - no matches; the CV-extraction-review component this page also renders never touches the field), no CSS trick (`grep -rn "text-security" app` - no matches anywhere in the app, node_modules excluded), no narrower column list used anywhere upstream of this one query. This is a React Server Component (`export default async function PersonDetailPage`, no `"use client"`) - the `<input>`'s `value`/`defaultValue` is written straight into the server-rendered HTML sent to the browser on first load, not computed or redacted by any client-side JS afterward; "view source" on this page, for any signed-in company member who can open it, shows the real 13-digit value in the HTML itself. **Conclusion: the claim was simply false.** Nothing masks `people.id_number` anywhere in this flow; the label describes a protection that does not exist.

**(2) Generalized across the whole app - grepped for every "masked"/"redact"/"PII" occurrence outside `node_modules`, verified each one independently.** Five real hits, in four files (a sixth, `app/lib/cvExtraction.ts:48`, is just a field-kind tag, `"secret"`, used only to label the CV-extraction-review UI's own confirm screen - not a masking claim, not investigated further):

- `app/app/company/principals/page.tsx:90` ("ID numbers are masked in this list") - **TRUE, verified in code.** `PrincipalCard` (same file, line 198) renders `` `ID ${maskId(p.id_number) ?? ...}` ``, calling the real `maskId()` helper (`app/lib/principals.ts` line 174-177: `"9404150120082" -> "*********0082"`, last 4 digits only). The edit form for the SAME field (`PrincipalForm`, lines 317-322) never round-trips the real value back to the browser at all - `defaultValue={null}`, always empty on load - and shows only `maskId(p.id_number)` inside the field's own label text ("on file ✱✱✱✱✱✱✱✱✱0082 - leave empty to keep"). An admin can only ever see the last 4 digits of a director's ID number through this UI, confirmed by reading both the card and the form, not just the one line the grep hit.
- `app/lib/principals.ts:4` ("ID numbers are shown masked everywhere except the edit form of that one person") - **TRUE**, and that one stated exception ("except the edit form") is itself accurate and benign: the edit form's label shows the masked `maskId()` summary (see above), never the real value - the comment is describing the masked-summary-in-the-label behaviour, not a real-value leak.
- `app/app/company/bank-accounts/page.tsx:41,56` (comments: "members get the masked summary" / "the masked member view") - **TRUE, verified in code.** Non-admin company members (`!isAdmin`, line 82-95) are served ONLY from `bank_account_summaries` (an RPC, line 44), which returns a `last4` field - the real `account_number` column is never queried for a non-admin at all (the `bank_accounts` table itself, with the full column, is only queried when `isAdmin`, line 42-43). Owners/admins DO see the full number, but via an explicit, honestly-labelled "Show full account number" `<details>` disclosure (lines 113-115) and the page's own intro text says plainly "only owners and admins of your company can see or change them" (line 70) - no false claim; the full number being visible to owners/admins IS what the copy says happens, not a contradiction.
- `app/app/people/page.tsx:81-83` (comment: "Deliberately NOT selecting id_number here... real PII never belongs in a list/summary") - **TRUE, verified in code.** The list query (line 84-87) selects an explicit column list that does not include `id_number` at all - not "masked", genuinely absent from the query, which is a stronger guarantee than masking (nothing to leak even via a bug elsewhere on that page).
- `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx:489` - **FALSE**, per (1) above. The one violator.

**Conclusion of (2): the "masked" claim is accurate in every place it's made except this one.** The correct pattern (`maskId()`, never round-tripping the real value) already exists in this exact codebase, for the identical real-world field on `company_principals`, and is correctly used in two different UI surfaces (the principals list and, for bank accounts, a dedicated RPC). This is not "masking is aspirational everywhere" - it is one page that never adopted an already-existing, already-correct sibling solution.

**Root cause, from `git log`, not guessed.** `app/lib/principals.ts` (with `maskId()`) was added 2026-10-17 (`b0f7ad2`, the Directors & shareholders register feature). The People page's `id_number` field was added two days earlier, 2026-10-16 (`890797d`), as `type="password"` - cosmetic only even then (a password input's real value is still present in the DOM/HTML; `type="password"` only suppresses the on-screen character display, it does not prevent the value reaching the browser, so the label's underlying claim was never accurate as a security property, only as a shoulder-surfing deterrent). Then, 2026-10-19 (`126b2aec`, "Fix UI trust issues found in whole-app review #14", authored by Sarel himself), the field was changed from `type="password"` to `type="text"` "so a person can see what they're typing when entering a new ID number" - that commit's own message states "no existing masking helper exists elsewhere to move this to", which was already inaccurate at the time (`maskId()` had existed in `lib/principals.ts` since two days earlier) - evidently that session didn't know to look for it. The commit removed the one cosmetic behaviour the label could even loosely be describing, but left the "(PII - masked)" label text completely unchanged - from that commit onward, the label became unambiguously false (no cosmetic hiding, no real masking, nothing), and has read that way for three weeks across many subsequent edits to this same file (role-eligibility, CV review, signatory scopes, etc. - `git log --oneline -- app/app/people/\[id\]/page.tsx` shows the file touched repeatedly since, always leaving this one line alone).

**(3) Checked every other `people`/`company_principals` query in the app for a wide/`select("*")` read reaching the browser, label or no label.** `grep -rn "from(\"people\")"` and `"from(\"company_principals\")"` across the whole `app/app` and `app/lib` trees: every other call site selects an explicit, narrow column list (`id, name`, `id, name, signatory_capacity`, `id, name, ecsa_expiry, sacpcmp_expiry`, etc.) - none of them includes `id_number`. The only two full/wide reads in the entire app are `app/app/people/[id]/page.tsx:298` (`select("*")`, the one covered above) and `app/app/company/principals/page.tsx:42` (`select(PRINCIPAL_COLUMNS)`, which DOES include `id_number` but is the one already-correctly-masked case from (2)). **Conclusion: `people.id_number` reaches the browser unmasked through exactly one code path in the whole app - this page's edit form - and nowhere else; `company_principals.id_number` never reaches the browser unmasked anywhere.**

**RLS scope, checked, not guessed - own-company exposure only, not cross-tenant.** `people`'s base policy (`0001_init_schema.sql` line 301-302, `"people: tenant isolation"`) is `for all ... using (is_company_member(company_id))` - standard tenant isolation, no cross-company leak possible; confirmed no other, broader `select` policy exists on `people` anywhere else in the migrations. A second, RESTRICTIVE policy (`0077_company_invites_and_employee_role.sql` line 227-231, `"people: employee restricted to own record"`) narrows this further, but only for company members whose OWN role is `'employee'` (`is_employee_in_company()`, same file line 185-201) - such a user can only ever read their own linked `people` row (`id = own_linked_person_id(company_id)`), so for them this bug exposes nothing they couldn't already see about themselves. For every other role on the `company_members.role` check constraint - `'owner'`, `'admin'`, and, notably, the lower-privilege `'member'` role too (not just owner/admin) - that restrictive policy's own `not is_employee_in_company(company_id)` branch is unconditionally true, so they see every column on every `people` row in their own company, unrestricted by role, exactly as before this migration. **Net effect: any company member with role `owner`/`admin`/`member` (i.e. everyone except the narrowly-scoped `'employee'` role) can open any colleague's `/people/[id]` page and read that colleague's full, real 13-digit South African ID number in the page's HTML - not just their own - while the page tells them it's masked.** This is real own-company over-exposure (a colleague's government ID number shown to a plain `'member'`, not just an owner/admin, with no "need to know" gate), but it is strictly bounded by the existing tenant-isolation RLS - no cross-tenant leak, no leak to an unauthenticated or wrong-company user, confirmed by reading the policy definitions directly rather than inferring from the page alone.

**NOT done this pass, deliberately - Sarel's own judgment call per the task brief.** Did not implement real masking for `people.id_number` (e.g. moving it to `company_principals`' own "never echo the real value, show last-4 in the label, re-enter to change" pattern, or a reveal-on-demand UI, or tightening the RLS/restrictive-policy story for non-employee roles). That is an architectural/product decision - how much friction to add to a page a company admin edits often, whether "any member can see a colleague's full ID number" is an acceptable existing norm for this app's trust model or needs tightening, whether the SANRAL-form/CV-generation consumers of this column need any change at all (they don't - they're server-side, never browser-exposed, and genuinely need the real value) - not something to improvise. ### Finding 221 (CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED - lives only on PR #189's own open, unmerged branch, documented-only per the standing guardrails - severe, authorization-bypass class, within-tenant scope only - a NULL-handling compound bug in `0128_cv_documents_storage_employee_gap.sql`'s own "employee restricted to own person" RESTRICTIVE policies: an unlinked employee (`own_linked_person_id()` returns `null`) paired with ANY `cv-documents` storage object name that does not match the exact `"<company_id>/people/<person_id>/..."` convention (so `cv_documents_path_person_id()` also returns `null`) defeats the fix entirely - full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE access to every malformed-path object in the bucket, not just ones they create themselves)

**Area:** `app/supabase/migrations/0128_cv_documents_storage_employee_gap.sql` (PR #189 only - this file does not exist on `main`; fetched read-only via a disposable `refs/remotes/origin/pr/189` ref, per the standing "never check out or build on another open PR's branch" guardrail, never checked out as a working tree or modified).

**How this was found.** This review segment's immediately preceding pass (`e9be375`, "role-matrix re-test of all 12 employee-gap fixes (0124-0136) + live RLS NULL fail-closed verification") directly tested this exact migration's own NULL-handling and confirmed it fail-closed - but only against WELL-FORMED paths (a real self path, a real colleague path, and a by-name select for the colleague's own real object). This pass's own task brief specifically asked for the one compound case that write-up's own test matrix never tried: a malformed/non-conventional path (the same shape a path-traversal probe would use) combined with an employee who has no linked person row at all - i.e., a case where BOTH sides of the policy's own comparison can independently be `null`, not just one.

**The predicate, read directly, not inferred.** All four of this migration's own new RESTRICTIVE policies (`"cv-documents: employee restricted to own person, select/insert/update/delete"`) share the identical body:
```sql
not (
  bucket_id = 'cv-documents'
  and is_employee_in_company((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid)
  and cv_documents_path_person_id(name) is distinct from own_linked_person_id((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid)
)
```
`cv_documents_path_person_id(name)` (this same migration's own new helper) returns `null` - by design, "never raises" - for ANY object name that doesn't parse to exactly 4 path segments with `'people'` as the second one (i.e. anything not shaped like `"<company>/people/<person>/<file>"`). `own_linked_person_id()` (0077) returns `null` for an employee with no linked `people` row. `IS DISTINCT FROM` is the one comparison operator in SQL that treats two `null`s as **equal, not distinct** - the opposite of the ordinary `=`/`<>` null-propagation this same pass's preceding write-up correctly relied on elsewhere. So for an unlinked employee (`is_employee_in_company` = `true`, `own_linked_person_id` = `null`) presenting a malformed path (`cv_documents_path_person_id` = `null`): `null IS DISTINCT FROM null` = `false` -> `true and true and false` = `false` -> `not false` = **`true`** - the RESTRICTIVE policy's own "deny" branch never fires; the row is treated as fully accessible, for every one of SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, exactly as if the employee held no restriction at all. This is the precise mechanism the task brief theorised: two independently-nullable terms on either side of a non-propagating comparison, each nulled by a DIFFERENT, unrelated condition (no linked person vs. a path that fails to parse), silently cancelling each other into an "allow."

**Reproduced live in a real scratch Postgres, not concluded from reading alone.** Built `scratch_cvdoc_compound` from `main`'s real 113 migrations (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`), applied PR #189's `0128` migration on top (fetched via `git show refs/remotes/origin/pr/189:app/supabase/migrations/0128_cv_documents_storage_employee_gap.sql`, never checked out), seeded one company, an `owner`, an `employee` LINKED to their own `people` row, a second `employee` with NO `people` row linking to them (`own_linked_person_id()` confirmed live to return `NULL` for them, not assumed), and a colleague's own real `people` row. All of the following ran as `begin; set local role authenticated; select set_config('test.uid', '<uid>', true); <op>; commit;`/`rollback`, matching this segment's own established convention, with real `psql` output, not inferred:

- **TEST A (the bug).** Unlinked employee `INSERT`s `'<company>/not-the-right-format.pdf'` (a path with no `people` segment at all, `cv_documents_path_person_id()` confirmed separately to parse this to `NULL`) into `storage.objects`, `bucket_id = 'cv-documents'`. **Result: `INSERT 0 1`, succeeded** - row `e3375761-2486-4d8f-a9bd-d846fb45934a` landed, confirmed by a final superuser read of the table.
- **CONTROL A2 (the already-known-safe case, reconfirmed).** The SAME unlinked employee `INSERT`s a WELL-FORMED path naming a real colleague's person id (`'<company>/people/<colleague>/uploads/cv.pdf'`). **Result: `ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy "cv-documents: employee restricted to own person, insert"`** - correctly denied, matching the preceding pass's own result for this shape.
- **CONTROL A3 (isolates the mechanism - only the unlinked case is vulnerable).** The LINKED employee (a real, non-null `own_linked_person_id()`) `INSERT`s the SAME malformed-path shape (`'<company>/not-the-right-format-2.pdf'`). **Result: `ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy ...`** - correctly DENIED, because here only one side (the path) is `null`; `null IS DISTINCT FROM <real-uuid>` = `true` (ordinary null-propagation, fail-closed), not `false`. This is the direct, live proof that the bug requires BOTH sides null at once - the double-NULL compound case, not a single-sided one the preceding pass's own reasoning already covered correctly.
- **TEST B.** The same unlinked employee then `SELECT`s their own just-planted malformed object back: `count = 1` (visible).
- **TEST C (read access to OTHER people's malformed objects, not just self-planted ones).** Superuser separately plants a second malformed-path object, owned by the `owner` user (simulating any pre-existing or colleague-planted malformed object, not one the attacker made). The unlinked employee `SELECT`s it by name: `count = 1` - **they can read a malformed-path object they never created, at all**, confirming this is a real read-access bypass of the bucket, not merely "I can insert junk under my own path."
- **TEST D.** The same unlinked employee `UPDATE`s that OTHER object's `metadata` to `{"tampered": true}`: **`UPDATE 1`, succeeded** - a metadata-tampering bypass, the identical "not just insert/delete" shape PR #189's own write-up flagged for the INTENDED (well-formed-path) case, now shown to also apply on the malformed-path side.
- **TEST E.** The same unlinked employee `DELETE`s that object: **`DELETE 1`, succeeded** - full destructive access.
- **CONTROL F (bounds the blast radius - confirmed NOT a cross-tenant leak).** A malformed-path object seeded under a SECOND, unrelated company's id (`'<other_company>/other-companys-malformed.pdf'`) is `SELECT`ed by the same unlinked employee: **`count = 0`** - correctly blocked, because `0008`'s own base PERMISSIVE "tenant isolation by path prefix" policy (`is_company_member((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid)`) still requires company membership first, and this bug sits entirely inside the SECOND, RESTRICTIVE, employee-only layer - it narrows a company member's own employee-level access, not the base tenant boundary. **Net effect, precisely bounded: an unlinked employee gets full SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on every malformed-path `cv-documents` object within their OWN company only** - still a severe, real authorization-bypass (RBAC bypass) of the exact protection this migration exists to add, just not a cross-tenant one.

**Why this is the right severity class, per the task brief's own framing.** This is not a narrower version of the already-known `0125`/PR #186 bug (a PL/pgSQL `IF`-guard fail-open on a single nullable term) - it is a structurally different mechanism (an `IS DISTINCT FROM` comparison where BOTH operands are independently nullable, from two unrelated sources) that this segment had not previously tested or found anywhere else. A grep sweep (`grep -n "own_linked_person_id" app/supabase/migrations/*.sql` plus the same grep against all 12 fetched PR migration files, repeating and extending the preceding pass's own sweep) confirms this is the ONLY other call site of `own_linked_person_id()` beyond the original six safe `0077` sites and the already-known `0125` bug - so this finding closes out that sweep's full population, not just one more sample of it.

**NOT fixed this pass, per the binding guardrails.** This migration exists only on PR #189's own open, unmerged branch - not on `main`. Per the standing rule ("a genuine NULL-handling/authorization-bypass finding... if it's only on an open PR's branch, document-only - can't touch that branch"), nothing was pushed to `#189`'s branch, no competing PR was opened, and this entry plus the matching `System-Status.md` entry are the only changes this pass makes. Recommended fix for whoever next touches PR #189 (not actioned here): compare `cv_documents_path_person_id(name) IS DISTINCT FROM own_linked_person_id(...)` is the wrong shape when either side can independently be `null` from an unrelated cause; the safer form adds an explicit `cv_documents_path_person_id(name) is null` branch to the "deny" condition (deny whenever the path doesn't parse at all, regardless of the caller's own linked-person state), e.g. `... and (cv_documents_path_person_id(name) is null or cv_documents_path_person_id(name) is distinct from own_linked_person_id(...))` inside the `not (...)` wrapper - verified by hand against all of TEST A/CONTROL A2/CONTROL A3/TEST B-E's own inputs above that this rewritten predicate denies every one of them that should be denied (A, B, C, D, E) while still allowing CONTROL A2's analogue for a genuinely-linked employee's own real path and leaving owner/admin/member fully unaffected (`is_employee_in_company` false for them, same as today) - not applied to the PR branch itself, offered only as the recommendation text for whoever does.

**Backlog status.** `git fetch origin main` immediately before this pass started and again immediately before pushing this entry both showed `main` unchanged at `09dc56f` - no sibling-session commit landed in between. `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`'s own last finding number was confirmed to be 220 (not assumed) via `grep -n "^### Finding " docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md | tail -5` immediately before assigning 221. All 23 open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#196`) reconfirmed open and unmerged via the GitHub REST API at the start and the end of this pass. The scratch database (`scratch_cvdoc_compound`) was dropped and the Postgres service stopped at the end of this pass; the disposable `refs/remotes/origin/pr/189`/`195`/`196` refs fetched for read-only reference were left in place only as ordinary remote-tracking refs (never checked out as a working tree, never built on, never pushed to) consistent with this segment's own established convention for referencing PR content without touching it.

**Test-coverage addendum (2026-11-08lviii, later pass):** confirmed live that this exact bug is NOT caught by PR #189's own test additions to `test_tenant_isolation.py` either. PR #189 adds a real new test (`[20]`/`part2_storage_employee_gap()`) that correctly checks two DIFFERENT, each correctly LINKED employees can't reach each other's real CV files - but every path in it is well-formed (`cv_documents_path_person_id()` never NULL) and every employee in it is linked (`own_linked_person_id()` never NULL), so it never exercises the double-NULL case above at all. See `docs/specs/System-Status.md`'s `2026-11-08lviii` entry (top of that document) for the live run: a scratch Postgres built from `main`'s 113 migrations plus this exact unfixed `0128` applied, PR #189's own branch copy of `test_tenant_isolation.py` (including its new `[20]`) run against it end to end, result `ALL PASSED`/exit `0` - then TEST A's own malformed-path insert re-run successfully, unchanged, on that same just-certified-green database. A sketched regression test to close the gap (a third, unlinked employee plus a pre-planted malformed-path object added to `[20]`'s own fixture) is given there too. No new Finding number consumed - this is a coverage statement about this already-documented finding, not a new bug.

To verify independently: check out PR #189's branch `fix/cv-documents-storage-employee-gap` read-only (or fetch `refs/pull/189/head`), replay `main`'s 113 migrations plus this one file onto a scratch Postgres, seed a company with one `owner`, one `employee` linked to a real `people` row, and a second `employee` with NO `people` row at all. ## 2026-11-08lxi (standing solution-architect review, background worker): fresh-angle race-condition sweep

### Finding 222 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - a TOCTOU race in `company_principals`' own 100%-ownership cap, `tt_principals_check()` (0050): two concurrent inserts/updates for the SAME company could each pass the "shareholdings would add up to over 100%" check against the same pre-write total and both commit, silently producing a shareholding total over 100% - the same check-then-write shape already fixed for team seats (0113/0114) and pack-request quotas (0115), just on a `SUM` cap over sibling rows rather than a `COUNT` cap, and on a table neither of those prior fixes touches)

**Area:** `app/supabase/migrations/0050_principals_registrations_properties.sql`'s `tt_principals_check()` trigger function (fired `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` on `company_principals`). Fixed in `app/supabase/migrations/0124_principals_ownership_cap_race.sql`.

**Why this angle:** this pass's task brief named three already-exhausted race classes (sibling-code divergence, double-NULL authorization bypass, secrets exposure, label-vs-reality mismatch, CI status) and asked for a genuinely fresh one; it suggested "quota/count check followed by insert... anything with a 'can we add one more' shape that isn't `request_submission_pack_checked()`/`request_general_job_checked()`/`create_company_invite_checked()`." Read every `actions.ts`/`*-actions.ts` file under `app/app/**` (22 base files, 46 once the `tenders/[id]/*-actions.ts` family and `discovery/preferencesActions.ts`/`company/officeActions.ts`/`company/digestActions.ts` are counted) for a check-then-insert "room for one more" shape. Every quota-shaped candidate actually found (team seats, pack-request quotas, trial one-pack-total, one-company-per-user, duplicate-CV-generation, duplicate-submission-pack-request) was already fixed in a locked `_checked()` RPC (0113/0114/0115/0116) or backed by a real unique index with a 23505 catch (migration 0075, `pack_generation_jobs_one_open_key`, `bank_accounts_one_*`, `registration_types_company_slug`) - confirmed by reading each one's own SQL, not assumed from a comment. Broadened the search from "a `COUNT` compared to a cap" to "any aggregate-across-sibling-rows invariant compared to a cap" and found `company_principals`' trigger-enforced 100%-ownership cap has the identical TOCTOU shape, just implemented as a `BEFORE` trigger rather than a Server Action's own three-query sequence, and on nobody's prior checklist because the quota lives in a trigger, not in `app/app/**/actions.ts` itself (`savePrincipal()`, `app/app/company/principals/actions.ts`, just does a plain `.insert()`/`.update()` and lets the trigger raise).

**What was tested and what broke, reproduced live (not reasoned about):** `service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE scratch_principals221'"`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d scratch_principals221` replayed all 113 migrations (`0001`→`0123`) clean. Seeded one company, one owner. Confirmed the live trigger body matches `0050` verbatim (`\sf tt_principals_check`) before touching anything. Temporarily swapped in a throwaway copy of the SAME body with a `pg_sleep(2)` inserted right after the `select coalesce(sum(ownership_pct), 0) ...` read - the identical widening technique `0121`'s own migration comment already used for its own demo, to make the real, normally microsecond-scale race window reliably observable; no logic changed. Ran two real concurrent `psql` sessions (background shell jobs, not simulated) each inserting a DIFFERENT new shareholder for the SAME company at 60% ownership - individually well under the 100% cap, together 120%:
```
Session A: insert ... 'Shareholder A', 60  -> INSERT 0 1 (succeeded)
Session B: insert ... 'Shareholder B', 60  -> INSERT 0 1 (succeeded)
select sum(ownership_pct) from company_principals where company_id = '<co>';
 total_ownership_pct
---------------------
             120.000
```
Both inserts succeeded, no error from either session - a state `tt_principals_check()` exists specifically to make impossible (confirmed the trigger's own logic is otherwise correct: deleted the rows, restored the exact unwidened `0050` body, then ran the SAME two inserts SEQUENTIALLY - the second one correctly raised `shareholdings would add up to 120.000 % - more than 100 %`; only concurrency defeats the check).

**Fix (`0124_principals_ownership_cap_race.sql`):** same pattern as `0107`/`0113`/`0114`/`0115`/`0121` - `perform 1 from companies where id = new.company_id for update;` added before the `sum()` read, locking the company's own row for the rest of the transaction so a second concurrent insert/update for the same company blocks on that lock until the first commits, then correctly sees the first's already-committed share before checking its own. No other logic changed (`person_id` same-company check, the 100% comparison itself, `updated_at`, all byte-for-byte unchanged from `0050`). Re-ran the identical two-concurrent-60%-inserts scenario against the fixed body (same `pg_sleep(2)` widening, now placed after the lock acquisition instead of the read, timed ~0.3s apart so the second call genuinely overlaps the first's sleep): Session B blocked for ~2s on the lock, then correctly saw Session A's already-committed 60% and was refused (`more than 100 %`); final `sum(ownership_pct) = 60.000`, not 120 - exactly one of the two survives, matching the cap. Restored the real (unwidened) fixed function from the actual migration file and confirmed via `\sf` that it matches byte-for-byte.
