### Finding 223 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe - `run_bridges.py`'s `BridgeRunner.run_once()` raised an uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError` straight out of `p.communicate()` the moment any bridge's combined stdout+stderr contained even one invalid-UTF-8 byte, aborting the whole cycle - every OTHER bridge scheduled after the offending one was skipped too, and in `--loop` mode (what the container actually runs) the exception was swallowed by `poll_loop.poll_forever()`'s own generic per-cycle catch with no alert anywhere, since `run_bridges.py`'s `main()` passes it no `alert_source` - the identical consequence, and the identical "no except clause in this method catches it" shape, as the `Popen()`-itself-raising bug this same method was already fixed for on 2026-11-03)

**Area:** `engine/worker/run_bridges.py` `BridgeRunner.run_once()`. Test coverage added in `engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py` (1 new test).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on worker/job-queue. `run_bridges.py`'s own `BridgeRunner.run_once()` already carries an extensively documented history of exactly this bug class - three separate QA passes (2026-10-23, 2026-10-25, 2026-11-03) each closed a different failure channel that used to raise uncaught out of this one method and abort the whole multi-bridge cycle (a hung `soffice` grandchild process not actually killed by a timeout; the generic "worker" alert source burying which bridge actually failed; `subprocess.Popen()` itself raising `OSError` under memory pressure). Reading the method's own two `except` clauses (`OSError` around `Popen()`, `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` around the first `communicate()`) against everything `p.communicate(timeout=self.timeout)` can actually raise showed a third, real channel neither clause guards: `communicate()` with `text=True` and Python's own default `errors="strict"` decoding raises `UnicodeDecodeError` the moment the subprocess's combined stdout+stderr contains a single byte that isn't valid UTF-8.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** A 5-byte child-process payload (`bytes([104,105,0xff,0xfe,10])`, "hi" + two invalid continuation bytes + a newline) through the exact `subprocess.Popen(..., text=True)` / `.communicate()` shape this method uses reliably reproduced `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 2: invalid start byte` - every single time, not an intermittent/environment-dependent failure. Realistically reachable: a bridge's own combined output can include a buyer's malformed document filename echoed into a log line, OCR'd text from a scanned document, or raw byte noise surfaced from a shelled-out tool like LibreOffice/`soffice` (every pack bridge's own docx->pdf step) - any one bad byte anywhere in a whole pass's worth of logging is enough.

**Why this matters.** Identical consequence to the already-fixed `Popen()` OSError case, confirmed by re-reading that fix's own comment: the whole cycle aborts mid-loop (every bridge scheduled after the one with the bad byte is skipped too, not just that one), and in `--loop` mode - what the production container actually runs - the exception is swallowed by `poll_loop.poll_forever()`'s own generic per-cycle catch with only a `print()`, since `run_bridges.py`'s `main()` never passes that call an `alert_source`. A silent, repeating loss (the exact same malformed byte would keep reappearing every cycle, since nothing about the underlying document changes) in the one mode that matters, with no alert anywhere.

**Fix.** Added `errors="replace"` to the single `subprocess.Popen(...)` call this method makes. This is purely a logging/alerting string - the output is never parsed as data anywhere in this method, only logged and/or embedded in a `system_alerts.record()` message - so decoding a malformed byte as the U+FFFD replacement character rather than raising is the correct trade, with no loss of any real information this method actually uses.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_a_bridge_that_writes_invalid_utf8_does_not_crash_the_whole_cycle()`, mirroring the existing `test_a_bridge_that_fails_to_even_start_is_reported_not_silently_lost()`'s own structure: a real two-bridge `BridgeRunner` where the first script writes one invalid-UTF-8 byte to stdout (then exits 0) and the second is a normal `print()` script; asserts `run_once()` itself doesn't raise, both bridges' output is logged (confirming the malformed one's own output survived as a replacement character rather than being lost), and - critically - the SECOND bridge still ran (confirming the cycle wasn't aborted). **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran `test_poll_loop.py` directly - crashed immediately with the exact predicted `UnicodeDecodeError`, traced to `communicate()` inside `run_once()`. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - all tests pass including the new one. `python3 -m py_compile` clean on both files.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: write a two-line script that does `import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"\xff\xfe\n")` and run it through `run_bridges.BridgeRunner([("bad", that_script), ("ok", a_normal_script)]).run_once()` - confirm it returns normally (no `UnicodeDecodeError`) and both bridges' output appear in the log. Run `python3 engine/worker/test_poll_loop.py` from its own directory and confirm "All bridge-loop smoke tests passed."

### Finding 224 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `opportunityBuyerMatch.ts`'s `sanitizePreferredBuyers()` had no minimum-length guard, so a 1-character preferred buyer entry - a plausible real typo, not a contrived input - matched 9 of 10 real-shaped buyer names via the module's own documented bidirectional-substring matching, silently defeating the "sort my preferred buyers first" feature by making almost every Discovery tender look like a preferred match)

**Area:** `app/lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.ts` `sanitizePreferredBuyers()`. Test coverage added in `app/lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.test.ts` (2 new cases).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation wrapped back to discovery. The three main Python discovery files are heavily covered already this session (Finding 200 earlier today), so effort went into the less-examined TypeScript side - `opportunityBuyerMatch.ts` (5 prior mentions). Its own header comment is explicit that matching is "a plain case-insensitive substring check in both directions, not an exact slug comparison" (no canonical buyer list exists to validate against, unlike disciplines) - and `sanitizePreferredBuyers()` already had a length CEILING (`MAX_BUYER_LENGTH`, rejecting absurdly long entries) but no FLOOR at all, despite substring matching being inherently more dangerous the SHORTER the needle is, not longer.

**Confirmed live, not guessed.** Ran `matchesPreferredBuyers`'s own normalisation against 10 real-shaped South African public-sector buyer names ("South African National Roads Agency SOC Ltd (SANRAL)", "Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd", "Rand Water", "Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA)", ...): a 1-character preferred buyer (`"a"` or `"o"`) matched 9 of the 10; a 2-character one (`"sa"`) matched only 2 of the 10 - confirming the single-character case specifically is the degenerate one, not substring matching in general. A company typing a 1-character preferred buyer (an easy, plausible slip - hitting Enter right after the first keystroke, or any upstream input-handling glitch that truncates to one character) would have every single Discovery tender silently sorted as a "preferred buyer" match, with zero real signal behind it - the opposite of what the feature promises, and confusing in a way nothing in the UI would explain.

**Fix.** Added `MIN_BUYER_LENGTH = 2` and the matching `trimmed.length < MIN_BUYER_LENGTH` check alongside the existing `MAX_BUYER_LENGTH` one in `sanitizePreferredBuyers()`'s own filter. Chosen deliberately as the minimal floor that removes only the demonstrated degenerate case: 2 characters is the shortest real abbreviation this file's own header already cites as a legitimate example in spirit (`"SANRAL"`, 6 characters, matching the buyer's full name) and is kept working (confirmed by the new test), while a bare single character is dropped. This does not tighten the module's own deliberately loose substring-matching design in any other way - a genuine 2+ character abbreviation, however short, is still accepted and still matches bidirectionally exactly as before.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added two tests: one confirming a 1-character entry is dropped (alongside a real one, which survives), one confirming a real 2-character abbreviation (`"SA"`) is NOT swept up by the same guard. **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran `node --experimental-strip-types lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.test.ts` directly - failed exactly as predicted on the new single-character test. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - 15/15 pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both clean. Broader regression: every other `*.test.ts` file in `app/` run directly, unaffected; confirmed via grep that this function's only real callers (`OpportunityPreferencesPanel.tsx`, `preferencesActions.ts`, `discovery/page.tsx`) are unaffected beyond the new, narrower input it now rejects.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before writing this entry and again immediately before pushing showed no sibling commits landed in between.

To verify independently: call `sanitizePreferredBuyers(["a", "SANRAL"])` and confirm it returns `["SANRAL"]` (the single-character entry dropped), and `sanitizePreferredBuyers(["SA", "SANRAL"])` and confirm it returns `["SA", "SANRAL"]` (both kept). Run `cd app && node --experimental-strip-types lib/opportunityBuyerMatch.test.ts` and confirm `15/15 pass`.

### Finding 225 (CONFIRMED, FIXED ON AN OPEN PR ONLY - NOT merged/pushed to `main`, money-adjacent per the standing guardrails - moderate-to-severe, revenue-integrity class - `apply_payfast_itn()` had no defence against an EXACT redelivery of an already-fully-applied ITN: a PayFast-side retry or a merchant-dashboard "Resend" of a PAST, already-processed charge silently extends `current_period_end`/resets `current_period_start` a second time, with zero new payment, and compounds with every redelivery)

**Area:** `app/supabase/migrations/0125_payfast_itn_exact_redelivery_idempotency.sql` (new, `apply_payfast_itn()`, redefining 0112's own latest body). Test coverage added in `engine/security/test_payfast_itn_idempotency.py` (new file, 8 checks).

**How this was found.** Fresh angle per this pass's own task brief, option (c): "idempotency of webhook/callback handlers under a genuine duplicate delivery (not just a race, an exact redelivery after the first already completed) - does replaying the identical webhook payload a second time, well after the first fully committed, cause any double-effect?" This segment has a long-running, repeatedly-reconfirmed standing item on `start_payfast_checkout()`'s own revenue-integrity gap, but nothing in this segment's history had looked at `apply_payfast_itn()` - the OTHER half of the same pipeline - from the redelivery angle specifically (prior PayFast-related passes checked the amount-verification check, 0112, and the IS-DISTINCT-FROM/double-NULL sweep, both unrelated). Read `app/app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts` and `apply_payfast_itn()` (0112, the latest body on `main` before this fix) in full first.

**Why a naive "have we already applied this m_payment_id?" check would have been WRONG, and why this bug survived.** `app/app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts` sets `subscription_type: "1"` with `cycles: 0` ("until cancelled") - a genuine PayFast recurring subscription. `m_payment_id` is minted ONCE at initial checkout and reused for EVERY future renewal charge under that subscription's whole lifetime, by design - so `apply_payfast_itn()` being called repeatedly over time for the SAME `m_payment_id`, each time correctly extending `current_period_end` by one more billing period, IS the intended, correct behaviour for a legitimate monthly/yearly auto-renewal. That is exactly why the function never checked "seen this `m_payment_id` as active before?" - it would have broken real renewals. What it also never checked is the ONE field that genuinely is unique per real transaction: PayFast's own `pf_payment_id` (the route's `p_payfast_token`, `pf_payment_id` falling back to `token` - route.ts line 72) - a brand-new charge always gets a new one; an exact redelivery of a PAST charge's ITN carries the identical one again. `apply_payfast_itn()` only ever WROTE into the `payfast_token` column (`coalesce(p_payfast_token, payfast_token)`), never read it back to detect a repeat.

**Confirmed live, not inferred - real scratch Postgres, 115 migrations replayed, `apply_payfast_itn()` called directly (SECURITY DEFINER, no RLS session needed, same as the real route's `supabase.rpc()` call with no signed-in user).** Seeded a company with a trialing subscription (the real `start_company_trial()` trigger's own row), set to `starter`/`monthly` with `payfast_m_payment_id='mpid-...'` (what `start_payfast_checkout()` really does). First `COMPLETE` ITN (`pf_payment_id='pf-token-1'`, `amount_gross=1490`, the real starter/monthly price) correctly activated it: `current_period_end` = now + 31 days. Redelivering the IDENTICAL ITN - same `m_payment_id` AND same `pf_payment_id`, same amount, "arriving" 10 days later (`p_period_end` is always recomputed by the route as `nextPeriodEnd()` = `addMonths(new Date(), ...)` AT CALL TIME per `lib/payfast.ts` - never carried over from the original delivery or derived from anything in the ITN payload or the stored row) - against the pre-fix function on `main`: `current_period_end` jumped from `2026-12-10` to `2026-12-20` and `current_period_start` reset from `2026-11-09` to the redelivery's own "now" - a free 10-day extension of a paid subscription, with zero new payment, that compounds with every redelivery (a THIRD redelivery would push it further still). A genuinely NEW renewal charge for the same subscription (same `m_payment_id`, a DIFFERENT `pf_payment_id`, exactly as PayFast issues for each real charge) correctly continued to extend the period after the fix - confirmed, not assumed, by testing both shapes against the same fixed function in the same run.

**Why this is plausible, not contrived.** PayFast's own merchant dashboard has a documented manual "Resend ITN" action for reconciliation, legitimately used well after a charge already settled; separately, PayFast's documented retry behaviour fires again whenever IT didn't receive our 200 even if we actually processed and returned one (a dropped response on PayFast's side, a proxy timeout, etc.) - a transient network blip, not an attack, is enough to trigger this. There is also no replay-prevention nonce/timestamp on a PayFast ITN at all; the three existing checks (signature, source IP, server confirmation via `eng/query/validate`) all legitimately re-pass on an exact replay of a real past ITN, since they only confirm "this notification genuinely came from PayFast for a real transaction" - not "this is the first time we've seen it." `apply_payfast_itn()` was the only remaining layer that could have caught it, and didn't.

**Fix (`0125_payfast_itn_exact_redelivery_idempotency.sql`).** Before either `'active'`-path branch does anything else, if `p_payfast_token` is non-null, equals the row's OWN currently-stored `payfast_token`, AND the row's current `status` already equals what this ITN would set it to - this is a repeat of an event already fully applied, not a new charge or a new status transition - return as a no-op. A brand-new charge (new `pf_payment_id`) or a first-ever activation (no stored token yet) is unaffected and proceeds exactly as before. The "rescue" branch (0081/0082, for an `m_payment_id` a later checkout attempt has since superseded) is left as a one-time, first-successful-activation path by construction - it already reclaims `payfast_m_payment_id` for that row, making it "current" from then on, so a genuinely duplicate rescue delivery is caught by the SAME new guard on its own next delivery.

**Verified red-then-green, twice.** (1) Hand-patched the running function in a scratch DB with the fix and re-ran the exact scenario above - no-op confirmed, legitimate-renewal case confirmed unaffected. (2) Wrote the real migration file, replayed ALL 115 migrations fresh from empty (`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`, clean), and ran the new `engine/security/test_payfast_itn_idempotency.py` against it (`PAYFAST_ITN_PSQL=... python3 engine/security/test_payfast_itn_idempotency.py`) - **8/8 PASS, 0 failures**. **Red:** ran the identical test file against a second fresh 115-migration replay with migration `0125` itself removed from the replay set (every other migration unchanged) - **4/8 FAIL**, exactly the two no-op checks in both redelivery scenarios (`current_period_end`/`current_period_start` both wrongly advance), the two legitimate-renewal checks still passing (confirming the test isn't just failing everything). **Green:** reran against the real, unmodified 115-migration replay - **8/8 PASS** again. Regression: `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` (`ALL PASSED`) and `engine/compliance/test_principals_registrations.py` (`0 failure(s)`) both re-run against the same 115-migration database this fix lives in - unaffected, confirming migration `0125` doesn't interact with either suite's own fixtures. `apply_payfast_itn()` has no other caller anywhere in `app/` or `engine/` (confirmed by grep) beyond the one route handler, so no other call site needed updating.

**Not pushed to `main` - opened as a PR instead, per this pass's own binding methodology ("money... → PR and STOP, don't merge").** This is this segment's first PayFast/billing-logic CODE change in a long run of passes that have otherwise left every billing-adjacent item (`start_payfast_checkout()`'s own revenue-integrity gap, the yearly pack-quota reset) as doc-only "Sarel's own judgment call" without even a PR - this one crossed from "found" to "fixed and verified," so per the task brief's own explicit instruction for a money-touching fix, it went to a PR rather than either a direct push or a doc-only non-fix. PR branch/number: see this pass's own System-Status.md entry for the exact PR link (not duplicated here to avoid a second place to go stale). Not merged - awaiting Sarel's own review, same as every other open PR in the backlog.

**Backlog status.** `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (fast-forwarded local `main` from `a26109f` to `eaf0713` - two sibling-track commits, `bb2d5ca`/Finding 223 and `eaf0713`/Finding 224, both already correctly attributed and pushed, not this pass's concern) and again immediately before pushing this doc-only commit, both clean - no further sibling commit landed in between. The 23-PR backlog (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#196`) is unaffected and untouched; this Finding's own new PR is a 24th, separate PR, not a competitor to any of them.

To verify independently: `service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE verify225'"`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d verify225` (expect "115 migrations"); `PAYFAST_ITN_PSQL="psql -U postgres -d verify225" python3 engine/security/test_payfast_itn_idempotency.py` (expect "0 failure(s)"). For the red case, replay the same 114 migrations with `0125_payfast_itn_exact_redelivery_idempotency.sql` excluded into a second scratch database and re-run the same test (expect "4 failure(s)", the two no-op checks in each of the two redelivery scenarios).

### Finding 226 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - SANRAL Form B7's live client-side total preview (`subcontracting-plan-form.tsx`) only checked the LOWER bound of SANRAL's policy band, so a total over 100% (more of the contract subcontracted than the whole contract is worth) showed in GREEN ("all good") while the company was typing - the exact opposite of the warning `lib/sanralB7.ts`'s own `checkPlan()` already raises for the identical total once saved, a direct, demonstrated consequence of Finding 202's server-side fix never being propagated to this pre-submission preview)

**Area:** `app/lib/sanralB7.ts` (new shared `totalPercentInRange()` helper), `app/app/tenders/[id]/subcontracting-plan-form.tsx` (the live preview). Test coverage added in `app/lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` (3 new cases).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on SANRAL pack. "text-success" : "text-warning"` - a single lower-bound comparison with no upper bound at all, unchanged since before Finding 202 existed.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Constructed the exact same adversarial case Finding 202 itself used (two Targeted Enterprises at 60% and 55%, total 115%) and traced it through this component's own `total` calculation and the className ternary: `115 >= 30` is `true`, so the live preview renders `text-success` (green) - the company sees a reassuring "all good" signal while filling in the form, then saves, and only on the NEXT page load does `checkPlan()`'s own server-side warning ("more than the whole contract has been allocated; check for a data-entry error") appear. **Verified red-then-green.** Added 3 tests for the new `totalPercentInRange()` function (below minimum -> false, within the acceptable band including both boundaries -> true, over 100% -> false) to the existing `sanralB7.spec.ts` (from Finding 202). **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran `npx vitest run lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` - 3 of 6 failed immediately with `TypeError: totalPercentInRange is not a function`, confirming the function is genuinely new. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - 6/6 pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both clean on all 3 touched files. ### Finding 227 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `engine/cv/generate_cv.py`'s own `_safe_name()` sanitizes a person's free-text `name` for use in an output filename but never truncated it, unlike the identical TS-side convention (`app/lib/safeFileName.ts`'s `.slice(0, 120)`) its own docstring claims parity with - an extremely long name (no length limit anywhere: `people.name` is plain `text not null`, no form-side `maxLength` either) crashes CV generation outright with `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`, and at least one real caller, `engine/pack/harness_pack.py`, does not catch that broadly enough to degrade gracefully)

**Area:** `engine/cv/generate_cv.py` (`_safe_name()`). Test coverage added in `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` (1 new test, 2 assertions).

**How this was found.** Fresh angle for this pass, picked over SA timezone/date-boundary handling and bulk/batch partial-failure sweeps: the task brief's own suggestion (b), "the PDF/DOCX generation pipeline's actual behaviour with extreme-but-valid data... go further than reading code, actually generate a real document with deliberately extreme test data and inspect the real output file." `generate_cv.py` already carries an extensive, dated history of prior QA passes fixing control-character crashes, `None`-vs-missing degradation and path traversal in this exact file - so rather than re-walking that same ground, the angle here was genuinely new inputs: very long field values and non-ASCII text, run through the real builders end to end rather than reasoned about.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Built a real `profile.json` (`company.legal_name` + one `key_people` entry) with `name` set to a 5000-character string - a plausible, not contrived, shape: this project's own comments already note `name` is "free text any company member can set," and it is also a field `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py`'s AI extraction can propose from a misread CV, with no length guard anywhere in the schema or the form. Ran the real CLI, `python3 generate_cv.py profile.json 0 <out_dir> --format sanral_keyperson --detail summary`, exactly as `process_cv_jobs.py`/`harness_pack.py` call it. Pre-fix: crashed with a real, unhandled `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`, traced to `doc.save(docx_path)` - `_safe_name()` sanitizes forbidden characters but passes the full 5000 characters straight through into the final filename (`<name>_<format>_<detail>_<mode>.docx`, longer still in the real worker path which also appends the job's UUID), well past the ~255-byte filename limit most Linux filesystems enforce.

**Root cause - a stated convention that was never actually followed.** `_safe_name()`'s own docstring claims "same sanitizer convention already used for uploaded filenames elsewhere in this project" - true for the character-stripping regex, but `app/lib/safeFileName.ts`'s real implementation also truncates (`.slice(0, 120)`), and the Python side never did. Checked how badly this degrades for each real caller rather than assuming: `engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` wraps the whole job body in a broad `except Exception`, so in the main production worker path this crash is caught, the job is correctly marked `failed` with a clear customer-facing message, and a system alert is recorded - not silent, but still a real, avoidable failure for a legitimate CV request. `engine/pack/harness_pack.py`'s own call site, by contrast, wraps `generate_cv.generate()` in `except ValueError as e:` only (line 157) - an `OSError` is not a `ValueError`, so this exact crash is NOT caught there and propagates out of the per-position loop, aborting the harness's entire pack build for every other position too, not just the one with the long name.

**Fix.** `_safe_name()` now truncates its sanitized result to 80 characters before returning. Chosen shorter than the TS file's 120 deliberately: this function returns only the name *portion* of the final filename - every real caller (`generate_cv.py`'s own CLI, `process_cv_jobs.py`) appends its own `_{format}_{detail}_{mode}[_{job_id}]` suffix and a `.docx`/`.pdf`/`.provenance.json` extension on top - so 80 leaves comfortable headroom for every real suffix this project uses while keeping the full filename well under the 255-byte limit regardless of which caller it is.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `test_person_name_extremely_long_does_not_crash_the_filename()` to `test_generate_cv.py`: asserts `_safe_name()`'s output for a 5000-character input is `<= 80` characters, and that a full `generate()` call with that name writes a real `.docx` instead of raising `OSError`. **Red:** checked out `generate_cv.py` at its pre-fix `HEAD` revision (leaving the new test in place) and re-ran `python3 test_generate_cv.py` directly - both new assertions failed exactly as predicted (`len(base_name)` reported as `5000`; the `generate()` call raised the real `OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`, name and all). **Green:** restored the fixed `_safe_name()`, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`, the new test included. Inspected the real output, not just the exit code: the written `.docx` (119-character filename, confirmed under the limit) opens cleanly via `python-docx` (13 real paragraphs, correct heading text) and the matching LibreOffice-converted `.pdf` opens via `pypdf` (5 real pages) - a genuinely usable document, not just a file that happened to save. Regression: full `engine/cv/test_generate_cv.py` (`0 failure(s)`), plus every other test file anywhere under `engine/` that references `generate_cv`/`_safe_name` - `test_process_cv_jobs.py`, `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py`, `engine/narrative/test_build_docx.py`, `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py`, `engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py`, `test_company_documents.py`, `test_fill_a_forms.py`, `test_fill_docx_forms.py`, `test_make_envelope_covers.py`, `worker/test_poll_loop.py` - all run directly, all `0 failure(s)`/`ALL PASSED`, unaffected.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one function, a length cap, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface) with a verified red-then-green test and a clean full regression run - pushed directly to `main` per this pass's own binding methodology.

### Finding 228 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `app/lib/dates.ts`'s own `daysUntil()`, the single shared "days until a date" calculation the whole Next.js app's deadline/expiry displays and reminder-candidate logic reads, normalized "today" to the HOST PROCESS's own local midnight rather than real Africa/Johannesburg (SAST, UTC+2, no DST) midnight - the exact SA-timezone bug class the Python engine side has independently fixed in at least eight separate files/findings this project's history, in a function this very engine-side fix explicitly cites as the thing it "mirrors")

**Area:** `app/lib/dates.ts` (`daysUntil()`). Test coverage added in `app/lib/dates.test.ts` (1 new test, 2 assertions).

**How this was found.** Fresh angle for this pass, picked per the task brief's own suggestion (a): SA timezone/date-boundary handling, confirmed genuinely untouched this review segment. Oriented by reading `app/lib/dates.ts` in full first - a well-documented file, already explicitly SAST-aware in two other functions (`SAST_DATE_OPTIONS`'s `timeZone: "Africa/Johannesburg"`; `closingDayOf()`'s own `+2 hours` shift, with a comment citing the exact `2026-10-17` incident that motivated it) - but `daysUntil()` itself, directly above `closingDayOf()` in the same file, normalizes "today" with plain `new Date(now); today.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0)`, which sets hours in whatever timezone the running process's own clock uses, not explicitly SAST. Confirmed this matters, not merely cosmetic inconsistency, by checking the actual deployment: no `TZ` environment variable is set anywhere in this repo (grepped `app/`, `engine/`, every `Dockerfile`, every GitHub Actions workflow - zero hits), and this app is deployed on Vercel (`next.config.ts`'s own header comment); Vercel's default Node runtime, like GitHub Actions' `ubuntu-24.04` runners and this very sandbox, defaults to UTC with no DST, 2 hours behind SAST. That makes the host-local-midnight bug class live, not theoretical.

**Confirmed, independently, that this is the identical bug class the Python engine side has already fixed repeatedly - just never ported to the TypeScript function it was modeled on.** `engine/compliance/watch_deadlines.py`'s own `days_until()` carries a comment reading, verbatim: "Mirrors app/lib/dates.ts's daysUntil: midnight-truncated, ceil'd" - and the same file defines a local `SAST = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=2))` constant specifically because, per its own comment, "this worker's container has no TZ set... so it runs in UTC by default. A naive datetime.date.today() is then one calendar day behind the real SAST date for the whole 00:00-01:59 SAST window every single day." Grepping `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md` for this exact bug class turned up at least eight prior, separate, already-fixed instances on the Python side alone (Finding 37 and its siblings: `watch_deadlines.py`, `daily_digest.py`, `watch_new_tenders.py`, `generate_cv.py`/`pdf_merge.py`/`process_pack_jobs.py`, `company_documents.py`, `gov_sources.py`), every one using the identical `SAST = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=2))` pattern - but not one of those passes, nor the later sibling-divergence sweep that explicitly cross-checked `watch_deadlines.py`'s lead-day *thresholds* (`60`/`30` days) against `app/lib/dates.ts`/`vaultDocuments.ts` and confirmed those numbers matched, ever checked whether the TS function's own "today" computation carried the same SAST correctness its Python mirror had already been hardened for. It hadn't: the function this entire Python-side bug class was explicitly modeled on had been carrying the original, unfixed bug the whole time.

**Reproduced live, against the real function, not reasoned about.** `TZ=UTC node --experimental-strip-types` against the actual `app/lib/dates.ts` (no reimplementation): simulated `now = 2026-11-09T23:00:00Z` - `2026-11-10 01:00` in real SAST (already the 10th in South Africa; still the 9th by a bare UTC clock) - inside the exact 00:00-02:00 SAST daily window the Python-side comments name. Pre-fix: `daysUntil("2026-11-09", now)` (a document/registration/tender dated the 9th, i.e. already expired/closed YESTERDAY in true SAST terms by this instant) returned `0` - "today," not yet overdue. Post-fix: `-1`, correctly overdue, matching what the true-SAST calculation independently confirms. This function is the one shared day-count every expiry/deadline surface in the app reads: company document expiry badges (`documentStatus()`/`expiryStatus()` on `/company`), person credential expiry, tender closing countdowns on the dashboard/pipeline/discovery pages, `lib/tenderCompliance.ts`'s own closing-vs-expiry compliance gate, `lib/dispatchTriage.ts`/`lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`'s bucket classification (which uses an EXACT `> 7 days` boundary test), trial-days-remaining on `/billing`/admin customer rows, and the exact-threshold reminder-candidate finders (`lib/deadlineReminders.ts`'s 3-day/1-day thresholds, `lib/complianceDigestCandidates.ts`'s 30/14/7-day thresholds) - all of which fire on an EXACT day-count match, not "within N days," so a single off-by-one during the bad window doesn't just mis-render a badge for two hours, it can make an exact-threshold reminder silently skip its one and only firing day for an item whose deadline happens to fall in that window. Checked the two GitHub Actions crons that actually run these reminder scripts in production (`deadline-reminders.yml` at `04:10 UTC`, `compliance-alerts.yml` at `03:30 UTC`) - both outside the `22:00-24:00 UTC` bad window, so today's actual scheduled sends are not desynced by this specific coincidence of timing, but every live page render (dashboard, pipeline, company vault, tender workspace) during the 2-hour SAST window was genuinely showing the wrong day count/status until this fix, and the reminder scripts would silently mis-fire if their cron times were ever moved into that window without anyone realizing why.

**Fix.** `daysUntil()` now derives "today" from the real `Africa/Johannesburg` calendar date (`now.toLocaleDateString("en-CA", { timeZone: "Africa/Johannesburg" })` → `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, then a UTC-midnight `Date` for that exact calendar day) instead of the host process's own local clock - the same host-TZ-independence `closingDayOf()` already applies for the opposite conversion (timestamp → SAST calendar day), now applied to this function's own "today" too. No other logic in the function changed; every caller's own semantics (whole-day counts, `Math.ceil`, null-for-unparseable) are unaffected.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `daysUntil: the SAST calendar day, not the host process's own local day, decides 'today'...` to `app/lib/dates.test.ts`: asserts `daysUntil("2026-11-09", <2026-11-09T23:00:00Z>)` is `-1` (not `0`) and `daysUntil("2026-11-10", <same now>)` is `0` (confirming the fix doesn't just shift every answer by one, only the boundary day). **Red:** restored the pre-fix `daysUntil()` body (new test left in place), ran `TZ=UTC node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/dates.test.ts` directly - `13 tests, 1 fail` (exactly the new test; the other 12 pre-existing `dates.test.ts` assertions, which don't cross the bad window, still passed). **Green:** restored the fix, re-ran - `13 tests, 0 fail`. Regression: full `TZ=UTC npx vitest run` (`72 files, 558/558`, unaffected - `dates.test.ts` itself is a `node --test` file, outside vitest's `*.spec.ts`-only scope per `vitest.config.ts`'s own comment); every other `*.test.ts` file anywhere under `app/` that could touch `dates.ts`/`daysUntil` run directly via `node --experimental-strip-types --test` - `dashboardStats.test.ts`, `tenderCompliance.test.ts`, `dispatchTriage.test.ts`, plus 25 more (`247 tests` across all of them, `0 fail`); `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors); `npx eslint lib/dates.ts lib/dates.test.ts` (0 errors).

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained TypeScript fix (one function, one line of "today" derivation, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface - `daysUntil()`'s own callers already treat its output as a plain day count and are unaffected by how that count is derived) with a verified red-then-green test and a clean full regression run - pushed directly to `main` per this pass's own binding methodology.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. The 24-PR backlog (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#197`) is unaffected and untouched.

To verify independently: `TZ=UTC node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./lib/dates.ts").then(m => console.log(m.daysUntil("2026-11-09", new Date("2026-11-09T23:00:00Z"))))'` from `app/` should print `-1`. Run `TZ=UTC node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/dates.test.ts` from `app/` and confirm `13/13 pass`, including the new SAST-window test. (Note, standing-review correction 2026-11-09: this line previously, incorrectly, carried Finding 227's own `generate_cv.py` verification text instead of this finding's - a copy/paste slip in the write-up itself, not a code issue; fixed here, no behaviour affected.)

### Finding 229 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, minor-to-moderate - `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py`'s `_send_via_resend()` claimed, in its own docstring, "same sender-profile fallback chain" as `app/lib/resendEmail.ts`'s `sendTransactionalEmail()` - but the real TS function was changed by commit `80d4b6c` (2026-10-24, three days BEFORE this Python file was even created) to drop exactly the cross-profile `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` fallback this Python function still has, so an unset `RESEND_FROM_BIDS` with `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` still set - a partially-configured state the TS side's own header comment explicitly documents as supported - makes Python silently send a Tier-1 (bid pack) email from the Tier-0 address, something the real TS function has never done)

**Area:** `engine/notify/send_pack_ready_email.py` (`_send_via_resend()`). Test coverage added in `engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` (1 new test).

**How this was found.** This pass's own angle, per the task brief's standing carried-forward item: the preceding pass (Finding 228, `daysUntil()`/`days_until()`) fixed ONE instance of "a shared TS util an engine/ comment explicitly cites as 'mirrored'" having an unported fix, but flagged that it had not exhaustively checked every OTHER such "mirrors app/lib/X.ts" comment pair in the codebase. Grepped `engine/` for every comment of that literal shape (`mirror`, `same as the TS`, `TS side`) and found two genuine cross-language, logic-level pairs (as opposed to shared-data-shape or architecture-pattern-only pairs, which don't have a second real implementation to drift from): `watch_deadlines.py`'s `days_until()` (already fixed, Finding 228) and `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s `_send_via_resend()`, which this pass's own docstring reading flagged as worth checking - it names a specific 3-step fallback chain as "the same" as the TS function's, a falsifiable claim about an actual algorithm, not just a shared constant.

**Confirmed the claim was false, against both real functions, not reasoned about.** Read `app/lib/resendEmail.ts`'s real `resolveFromAddress()`: each `SenderProfile` ("system"/"ops"/"compliance"/"scout") resolves its OWN env var independently (`SENDER_PROFILE_ENV_VAR`) and falls back ONLY to that same profile's own hardcoded default (`SENDER_PROFILE_DEFAULTS`) - there is no cross-profile fallback to `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` at all, by deliberate design: `git log`/`git show 80d4b6c` (2026-10-24, "Fix sender-address resolution to match the real env vars Sarel set") shows this was a deliberate removal of an EARLIER blanket-override behaviour, specifically because "a blanket override would silently route Tier 1/2/3 mail through the Tier 0 address instead of their own." `send_pack_ready_email.py` was created three days LATER, on 2026-10-27 (`git log --follow`), so this was never "a later TS fix that didn't get ported" in the `daysUntil()` sense - the Python file's own docstring simply described a fallback chain the real TS function never had, not even on the day this file was written. Reproduced live against both real functions: a temporary `vitest` spec (`lib/__scratch_resendEmail_repro.spec.ts`, mocking only the `resend` npm package's `emails.send`, deleted after use) calling the real, unmodified `sendTransactionalEmail({ ..., from: "ops" })` with `RESEND_FROM_BIDS` unset and `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS="Tier0 <team@tenderready.app>"` - captured `from: "Tender Ready Bids <bids@tenderready.app>"` (`npx vitest run`, 2/2 pass). Calling the real, unmodified (pre-fix) `_send_via_resend()` the same way (`urllib.request.urlopen` monkeypatched to capture the POST body, same discipline this file's own existing test suite already uses) - captured `from: "Tier0 <team@tenderready.app>"`. Same inputs, same claimed "same fallback chain," two different real "From" addresses.

**Why this matters, and why it doesn't matter most of the time.** In normal production this never fires: Sarel has both `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` and `RESEND_FROM_BIDS` (plus `RESEND_FROM_COMPLIANCE`/`RESEND_FROM_SCOUT`) set as real GitHub Actions + Vercel env vars (per `resendEmail.ts`'s own header comment), so `RESEND_FROM_BIDS` is never unset while this function runs. The bug is a latent one: it only reaches a real recipient's inbox the moment `RESEND_FROM_BIDS` is ever unset on its own (an env var rotation, a misconfigured preview/staging environment, a new deployment target) while `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` is still set - exactly the "partially-configured environment degrades per-tier" scenario `resendEmail.ts`'s own header comment documents as a real, supported state, not a hypothetical. When it does fire, the consequence is a wrong "From" sender identity on a real, successfully-sent email (a Tier-1 bid-pack-ready notification going out branded/routed as Tier-0 general mail, or - if `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` is also unset - from a generic `onboarding@resend.dev` address instead of the bids identity) - not a crash, not a lost email, not a security/data issue. Rated minor-to-moderate, not severe, on that basis.

**Fix.** `_send_via_resend()`'s `from_addr` resolution changed from `os.environ.get("RESEND_FROM_BIDS") or os.environ.get("RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS") or "Tender Ready <onboarding@resend.dev>"` to `os.environ.get("RESEND_FROM_BIDS") or "Tender Ready Bids <bids@tenderready.app>"` - dropping the `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` fallback entirely and matching the literal default to the real TS `SENDER_PROFILE_DEFAULTS.ops` value, so the two functions now agree in every env-var configuration, not just the fully-configured one. Docstring rewritten to state the real fallback accurately and record why the old text was wrong. Nothing else in the function changed.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test, `test_send_via_resend_from_address_matches_the_real_ops_fallback_the_docstring_claims()` (`engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py`): calls the real `_send_via_resend()` with `RESEND_FROM_BIDS` unset and `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS` set, `urllib.request.urlopen` monkeypatched to capture the real POST body's `from` field, asserts it equals the real TS ops-profile default. **Red:** ran against the pre-fix body - `1 failure(s)` (exactly the new assertion; captured `Tier0 <team@tenderready.app>`, not the expected bids default - every other pre-existing test in the file still passed). **Green:** fix applied, re-ran - `0 failure(s)`, new test included. Full regression: `python3 engine/notify/test_send_pack_ready_email.py` (`0 failure(s)`, all 9 tests); confirmed via `grep` that `RESEND_FROM_ADDRESS`/`RESEND_FROM_BIDS` are read nowhere else in `engine/` (this is the only Python call site); re-ran both real callers' own test suites unaffected: `engine/general/test_process_general_jobs.py` (`0 failure(s)`) and `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (`0 failure(s)`).

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one function, one fallback chain, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface - this is a notification "From" header, not billing or auth) with a verified red-then-green test and a clean regression run on both real callers - pushed directly to `main` per this pass's own binding methodology.

**Other "mirrors"-comment pairs checked this pass, no issue found (for completeness, not padding):** `personCredentials.ts`'s `TRACKED_PERSON_EXPIRY_FIELDS`/60-day threshold vs. `watch_deadlines.py` - consistent, because `personCredentials.ts` reads `expiryStatus()`, which itself calls the now-fixed `daysUntil()` (Finding 228) - nothing further to port. `app/lib/sanralB7.ts` vs. `engine/sanral_b7.py` (`applicability()`/`check_plan()`) - read both in full; the >100%-total warning (Finding 226's own underlying fix) is already present on BOTH sides, added together in the same prior pass per that fix's own comment - in sync. `app/lib/onboardingScan.ts`'s `KIND_FIELDS`/`DATE_FIELDS`/`NUMBER_FIELDS` vs. `classify_documents.py` - `DATE_FIELDS`/`NUMBER_FIELDS` match exactly; `KIND_FIELDS.id_document` differs (TS lists `id_number`, Python doesn't) but this is intentional, not drift - Python's comment explains `id_number` is matched locally by regex, never by the AI model, and is injected into the final `fields` dict separately (`classify_documents.py` line 531), so the field genuinely is present in the output TS renders from; functionally consistent, just not byte-identical lists for different, documented reasons. `general-workspace.tsx`'s primary-signatory fallback (`filter signatory_capacity, sort by created_at ascending, take first`) vs. `process_general_jobs.py`'s `gather_pack_inputs()` - identical logic, both "first person given a signatory capacity, oldest first." `app/lib/registrations.ts`'s `scopeAllows()` vs. the `0050` migration's trigger-enforced scope rule - logic matches exactly, but `scopeAllows()` itself has zero call sites anywhere in `app/` (confirmed via `grep`) - dead code, zero live drift risk either way. `lib/billing.ts`'s `PLAN_LIMITS`/`PLAN_MONTHLY_ZAR` vs. migrations `0083`'s `tt_plan_limits()`/`0112`'s `tt_plan_price_zar()` (SQL, not Python, so outside this pass's primary TS/Python axis, but checked anyway since the comments explicitly claim parity) - every value read directly from the live migration SQL matches the TS constants exactly (seat/pack limits per tier, Rand pricing per tier/interval); worth a side-note for Sarel's own judgment, not a new Finding: the `0083`/`0112` comments both claim this is "cross-checked by a test," but no such test actually exists (`billing.spec.ts` only asserts TS-internal hardcoded numbers, never queries the SQL functions) - the two sides currently agree, by inspection, but nothing would catch it if they drifted apart in a future pass. `resendEmail.ts`'s own claim to mirror `send_digest_emails.py`'s "never crash, never pretend to have sent anything" rule, and `scoutAnomalyAlerts.ts`'s claim to mirror `check_system_alerts.py`'s "still_occurring" rule - both checked and confirmed to be conceptual/design-parity comments only (no second concrete algorithm in the cited Python file for the citing TS function to have drifted from: `check_system_alerts.py` has no `claim_notification`-based idempotency key at all, and `send_digest_emails.py`'s missing-key handling is a simple skip-don't-crash rule with no fallback chain to diverge on) - not the `daysUntil()`-style bug class, nothing to fix.

### Finding 230 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - bulk/batch partial-failure class - `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`'s `sync_tender_requirements()` wrote one SETUP-sheet position per `client.insert()` call, in a plain for-loop with no shared transaction; a failure partway through one workbook's positions left the EARLIER ones already committed, and the next poll cycle's own "already have positions for this tender?" check is existence-based, not completeness-based, so it then skipped that workbook SILENTLY, forever - permanently stuck on a partial key-positions list, with no further alert and no retry)

**Area:** `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` (`sync_tender_requirements()`). Test coverage added in `engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` (1 new test, `TableAwareFakeClient`); `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py`'s and `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s own fake clients updated to accept the new call shape (both already exercise this function for other reasons and would otherwise have broken on it); `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py`'s real-SQL `PsqlClient.insert()` updated the same way.

**How this was found.** This pass's own fresh angle, picked from the task brief's own suggested list over the already-exhausted sibling-divergence/race-condition/PII/webhook-idempotency angles this review segment had covered: bulk/batch operations - anything looping over multiple rows in a single Server Action or RPC call - for partial-failure handling. Swept every `app/app/**/*actions*.ts` file for a loop-of-writes shape first (`bulkUploadCvs()` in `app/app/people/actions.ts` and `registerOnboardingBatch()` in `app/app/company/document-scan/actions.ts` were the two real candidates - both already correctly handle partial failure: `bulkUploadCvs()` continues past a per-file failure and reports it in its own summary string rather than aborting the whole batch or silently dropping it, and `registerOnboardingBatch()` sends its whole batch as one `.insert(rows)` call, already atomic). Widened the sweep to `engine/`'s own job-processing loops (`process_*_jobs.py`, the `sync_*` functions `process_pack_jobs.py` itself runs every poll) and found `sync_tender_requirements()`: a loop building `tender_requirements` rows (primary SETUP-sheet positions + their ALT slots) from an uploaded blank Technical workbook, one `client.insert()` call per position, inside a `try/except` that already correctly logs+alerts on ANY failure in the whole block - but does nothing about rows already committed before the failure.

**Confirmed live, real scratch Postgres, not reasoned about.** `service postgresql start`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d scratch_bulk230` (114 migrations, matching `main`). Confirmed the real unique constraint live (`\d tender_requirements`: `tender_requirements_tender_position_company_key unique (tender_id, position_code, is_alternate, company_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT`). Simulated the EXACT pre-fix loop as three separate statements (autocommit, one PostgREST request per `client.insert()` call in the real code - confirmed by reading `SupabaseRest.insert()`, each call is its own `urllib.request` POST, no shared transaction across the loop): inserted `PL` (committed), then a 2nd insert with a bad/duplicate `PL` row (modelling one bad SETUP-sheet value or a transient blip on any one of several positions) - **that statement failed, but `PL` stayed committed** (`select position_code from tender_requirements`: 1 row, `PL`). Re-ran the identical 3 rows as ONE bulk `INSERT ... VALUES (...), (...), (...)` instead (what PostgREST sends when a `client.insert()` call's body is a JSON array, not a single object) - **the whole statement failed and ZERO rows were committed.** Same bad data, same constraint - the only difference is whether Postgres is given one failure unit (all 3 positions) or three.

**Why the partial state is permanent, not just "retried a bit late."** `sync_tender_requirements()`'s own `have` set (which workbooks already have positions on file, skip them) is computed ONCE per poll by querying `tender_requirements` for `(tender_id, company_id)` existence - ANY row for that key, not "all of them." Once the partial `PL`-only row above is committed, every future poll's `have` query returns that key as already-done and the function `continue`s past this document without even calling `client.download()` again - no further log line, no further `system_alerts.record()` call, nothing. The Tender Workspace's own Key positions card, `confirm_pack.py`'s human-confirmation gate (every position needs a confirmed person) and `sync_position_suggestions()`'s own candidate ranking all then permanently treat the partial set as the complete one - a real SETUP sheet with, say, 5 positions silently becomes a 1-position tender forever, discoverable only by someone counting rows by hand against the real workbook.

**Fix.** The per-position `for p, alt in rows: client.insert(...)` loop now builds the full list of row dicts first and sends them as ONE `client.insert("tender_requirements", [...])` call (a JSON array body - already how this same file's own `upsert()` calls send `field_provenance` rows, so the REST client already supports it unchanged). A single INSERT statement is atomic in Postgres: a failure now always leaves zero rows for this `(tender_id, company_id)` key, so the existence-based `have` check correctly sees nothing and the next poll cycle retries the whole workbook cleanly, instead of being permanently stuck on whatever subset happened to commit before the failure. `written[key]` and the `[requirements]` log line are unchanged (same data, computed before the call either way); an empty `rows` list (a workbook with zero SETUP positions) skips the call entirely, same as before.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test, `test_sync_tender_requirements_mid_batch_insert_failure_does_not_strand_a_tender_on_a_partial_position_list()` (`engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py`, new `TableAwareFakeClient`): a 3-position SETUP sheet (`PL`/`DS1`/`DS2`) where `DS1`'s own row is rigged to fail insertion on "cycle 1" only, modelling a transient blip; "cycle 2" (the next poll, blip cleared) re-runs `sync_tender_requirements()` against the SAME client/table state. **Red:** reverted only `process_pack_jobs.py` to its pre-fix per-row loop (`git stash` on that one file, test file left in place) - `2 failure(s)`: cycle 1 commits `['PL']` only (the partial per-row result), and cycle 2 never even calls `download()` again (`have` already satisfied) - the tender is stuck on `['PL']` forever, exactly as predicted. **Green:** fix restored - `0 failure(s)`: cycle 1 commits nothing (atomic failure), cycle 2's `download_calls` counter increases (a real retry happened, not a silent skip) and the full `['DS1', 'DS2', 'PL']` list is on file. Also ran the real, unmodified `sanral_fill.Workbook`-driven sample-template test suite, `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` (no synthetic failure injection, just the real `templates/samples/R.396-010-2025.1F_ran.xlsm` SETUP sheet) - `ALL PASSED`, confirming the batched call still reads/writes the exact same rows for a real, unmodified workbook. End-to-end live confirmation: ran `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py` (System-Status.md Gap #8 - "no live Supabase project... can't run in this environment" - turned out to be runnable here with a scratch Postgres, since one is available) against a freshly replayed 114-migration database with real LibreOffice-driven pack generation; its own transcript shows `sync_tender_requirements()`'s batched insert succeeding against the real schema for the real sample workbook (`[requirements] tender ...: 2 position(s) from SETUP (PL, DS1), 2 ALT`, 4 rows in one statement) before the harness's own job later failed on an unrelated, pre-existing gap (`PsqlClient` has no `upsert()` method at all, needed for `field_provenance` - confirmed via `git diff`/`grep` this is untouched by this fix and was already missing; not this Finding, not fixed, left as-is since fixing it would be unrelated scope creep and this harness isn't wired into CI).

**Regression - three other fake/real clients updated to accept the new call shape, each already exercising this exact function for its own reason, each confirmed broken-then-fixed:** `engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py`'s `FakeClient.insert()` (assumed a single dict; `ALL PASSED` after the fix, including its own pre-existing primary/ALT/company-separation/unreadable-workbook tests against the real sample workbook). `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s `Store.insert()` (assumed a single dict via `**row`; confirmed broken first - `TypeError: Store.add() argument after ** must be a mapping, not list` on its own `[16c]` per-company-positions test - then fixed; re-ran BOTH Part 1 (in-memory, no Postgres) and Part 2 (real RLS + `tt_check_same_company`, a freshly replayed 114-migration scratch Postgres, same as CI's own `tenant-isolation-db` job) - `ALL PASSED` on both. `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py`'s real-SQL `PsqlClient.insert()` (built `cols = ", ".join(row)` assuming a single dict; would have raised `TypeError` on a list - fixed to build one `json_populate_recordset`-based bulk INSERT, confirmed working in the live harness run above). None of these three are CI-covered for the exact insert-shape change except `test_sync_functions.py`/`test_process_pack_jobs.py`/`test_tenant_isolation.py` (`bridge-worker-ci.yml` runs all three; `bridge_selftest.py` is not wired into CI) - all now pass either way. `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`, discovery's own fake clients and `engine/worker/fake_supabase.py` each have their own, unrelated `insert()` and are never called by `sync_tender_requirements()` - confirmed via `grep`, not touched.

**Other bulk/batch loops checked this pass, no issue found (for completeness, not padding):** `sync_b7_setup()` (same file) writes exactly ONE row per tender via `client.update()`, not a loop of inserts - no partial-batch surface. `sync_position_suggestions()` (same file) loops over positions but each is its own independent `tender_pack_assignments` row with no existence-gated "skip forever" check analogous to `have` - a failure on one position is caught per-pack by the function's own `try/except` and simply retried next poll (the row for that position just stays stale, not silently treated as done); genuinely different shape, not this bug class. `engine/discovery/watch_tender_updates.py`'s per-company `tender_tasks` insert loop - each company's row is independent (no shared completeness key), a failure for one company doesn't affect any other's; not analogous. `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py`'s and `engine/discovery/taxonomy.py`'s own insert-in-loop calls are self-test/one-off-CLI seeding code, not production job-processing paths.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one function's write strategy, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface - this changes how many HTTP requests one poll cycle's position-sync makes, not any table, policy or billing logic) with a verified red-then-green test, a real-schema live-Postgres repro AND a real-schema live-Postgres regression run (both Parts of `test_tenant_isolation.py`), and all CI-covered sibling test files passing - pushed directly to `main` per this pass's own binding methodology.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened. One pre-existing, unrelated gap surfaced incidentally while live-running `bridge_selftest.py` (its own `PsqlClient` has no `upsert()` method, so a SANRAL pack job's `field_provenance` write always fails in that specific self-test harness) - not acted on, not this Finding, flagged here only so a future pass doesn't mistake it for something this fix caused. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `e36d24c`/Finding 229, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. To verify independently: `service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE verify230'"`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d verify230` (expect "114 migrations"); `\d tender_requirements` and confirm the unique constraint named above. `python3 engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py` from `engine/pack/` (expect `0 failure(s)`, including `test_sync_tender_requirements_mid_batch_insert_failure_does_not_strand_a_tender_on_a_partial_position_list`). `python3 engine/pack/test_sync_functions.py` (expect `ALL PASSED`). `TENANT_PSQL="psql -U postgres -d verify230" python3 engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` (expect `ALL PASSED`). `git log --oneline -1` on `main` should show this pass's own fix commit.

### Finding 231 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - concurrent storage-layer race, not a DB-transaction one - six separate "replace this one document" Server Actions each read the row's current storage path, upload the new file, update the row, THEN delete the path they read at the start; two near-simultaneous submits for the SAME document - a double-click, a slow upload retried, or two browser tabs - both read the same starting path before either writes, so both uploads genuinely succeed and both updates unconditionally succeed too, last commit silently winning the row - permanently orphaning the LOSING request's own just-uploaded file in a private bucket forever, while BOTH users are told "saved")

**Area:** `app/app/company/actions.ts` (`uploadVaultDocument()`), `app/app/experience/actions.ts` (`saveExperienceTags()`), `app/app/company/principals/actions.ts` (`uploadPrincipalDocument()`), `app/app/company/properties/actions.ts` (`savePropertyDocument()`), `app/app/tenders/[id]/vault-quick-fix-actions.ts` (`uploadCoidQuickFix()`), `app/app/company/registrations/actions.ts` (`saveHeldRegistration()`'s certificate-attach step). Test coverage added to each file's own `*.spec.ts` (one new concurrency test per site, 6 total).

**How this was found.** This pass's own fresh angle, picked from the task brief's own suggested list: concurrent storage-layer races, specifically called out as genuinely uncovered this review segment (every race-condition angle so far - double-NULL authorization bypasses, quota-check-then-insert races, exact-webhook-redelivery idempotency - was DB-transaction-level, not storage-layer). Swept every `app/app/**/*actions*.ts` file for the shape "read a row's current storage path, upload a new file, update the row, then delete the old path" (the Document Vault's own standard "replace a document" convention, per `app/company/actions.ts uploadVaultDocument()`'s own header comment, which several sibling files explicitly cite as what they copy). Found six real call sites with the identical shape and the identical gap: every one of them already has the zero-rows-matched/RLS-race fix (`.select("id").maybeSingle()`, checked and fixed in earlier passes - `23b43b4`, `7345243`, and this review segment's own 2026-11-06/07 sweeps), but NONE of them gates the UPDATE on the storage column still holding the value that was read - so the RLS fix (which only protects against a membership being revoked mid-request) does nothing for two requests that both have perfectly valid, unrevoked membership the whole time.

**Confirmed live - a real, deterministic two-request race, not reasoned about.** Built a stateful mock Postgres row (not the sequential response-queue convention this codebase's existing RLS-race tests use, which cannot represent genuine concurrency) for `uploadVaultDocument()`: two calls in flight at once via `Promise.all`, same company, same vault document kind, two genuinely different files. Both calls' own `select(column)` reads land before either call's `upload()` resolves (no artificial delay on the reads; a real, deliberately staggered delay on the two uploads, modelling nothing more exotic than one request's upload round-trip finishing before the other's). **Pre-fix:** both uploads succeed (two distinct, real storage paths); both updates succeed unconditionally (no filter on the column); the row ends up pointing at whichever update committed last; BOTH requests report success to their respective users; the LOSING request's own newly-uploaded file is referenced by nothing (the row doesn't point at it) and deleted by nobody (each request's own cleanup step only ever targets the path it read before EITHER request wrote, which is the ORIGINAL file, not the other request's new one) - a silent, permanent storage leak. Reproduced the identical shape for all five sibling call sites with the same technique, substituting each one's own table/column/update shape.

**Why this is realistic, not contrived.** A double-click on a slow network, a user re-submitting after a spinner stalls (nothing in any of these forms disables the submit button while the Server Action runs), or two tabs open on the same Company Settings/Tender Workspace/Principals/Properties page - all produce two genuinely valid, unrevoked-membership requests racing each other, for documents that include certified ID copies, disability proof, B-BBEE/CIDB/insurance certificates, registration certificates and tender-answer evidence - several of them POPIA-relevant personal documents a company or person believes they have replaced or removed, silently retained in private storage forever, discoverable by nobody and cleaned up by nothing.

**Fix - the same one-line change at all six sites, each already tested for it.** Each update is now scoped with an extra, optimistic-concurrency filter: `.eq(<column>, <the path this request read>)` (or `.is(<column>, null)` when there was none) alongside the existing `.eq("id", ...)`. This makes the UPDATE's own WHERE clause require the row's CURRENT value to still match what this request saw when it started - exactly PostgREST's own real "0 rows matched" behaviour the earlier RLS-race fix already added handling for at every one of these six sites. No new failure branch was needed anywhere: the second request to commit now simply falls into the SAME zero-rows-matched code path the RLS fix already built, which already cleans up that request's own new upload and tells its user to try again, rather than reporting false success. The winning request's behaviour is completely unchanged (its own filter trivially matches, since nothing else has touched the row yet).

**Two related call sites with the identical consequence, NOT fixed this pass - left as a documented gap, not scope creep.** `app/app/company/actions.ts`'s `saveDocumentTemplate()` and `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-actions.ts`'s `uploadTenderDocument()` both have the same "read previous path, upload, write, delete previous" shape, but the write is `supabase.from(...).upsert(row, { onConflict: ... })`, not a plain `.update()` - `upsert()`'s conflict resolution is keyed on the `onConflict` columns, not an arbitrary `.eq()` filter chained afterwards, so the same one-line fix does not apply; closing this properly needs a genuinely different mechanism (e.g. a `SECURITY DEFINER` function doing the compare-and-swap server-side, or restructuring these two call sites to a plain conditional update + insert-on-miss like the other six). Flagged here for a future pass or for Sarel's own judgment call, not fixed now to avoid rushing a schema-adjacent change under this pass's own "small/safe only" guardrail.

**Verified red-then-green, all six sites.** Each site got its own new concurrency test (`*.spec.ts`, a stateful per-table mock rather than the repo's existing sequential-queue convention, since this race specifically requires both requests' reads to land before either write commits): `app/app/company/actions.spec.ts` ("uploadVaultDocument - two concurrent replace requests..."), `app/app/experience/actions.spec.ts` ("saveExperienceTags - two concurrent replace requests..."), `app/app/company/principals/actions.spec.ts` ("uploadPrincipalDocument - two concurrent replace requests..."), `app/app/company/properties/actions.spec.ts` ("savePropertyDocument - two concurrent replace requests..."), `app/app/tenders/[id]/vault-quick-fix-actions.spec.ts` ("uploadCoidQuickFix - two concurrent uploads..."), `app/app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts` ("saveHeldRegistration - two concurrent certificate-attach requests..."). **Red:** each fix was individually reverted in isolation (the rest of the pass's changes left in place) and its own new test re-run - all six failed exactly as predicted (`expected [...] to have a length of 1 but got 2` - both requests reporting success instead of one winning and one being told to retry). **Green:** each fix restored, re-ran - all six pass.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint .` - 0 errors (3 pre-existing, unrelated warnings - an `<img>` tag and an unused import, neither touched this pass). `npx vitest run` (the whole `app/` suite) - 72 files, 564/564 pass, including every existing RLS-race test on all six touched files (confirming the new optimistic-concurrency filter doesn't interfere with the zero-rows-matched handling it now shares a code path with) and every other unrelated suite.

**Pushed directly to `main`** - small, safe, self-contained TypeScript fix across six Server Action files (one additional query filter each, reusing an already-existing failure/cleanup path - no new branch, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface: no migration, no policy, no table, no billing logic touched anywhere), verified red-then-green at every site with a clean full regression run - this pass's own "small/safe" class.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened. One new, clearly-scoped related gap documented above (the two `upsert()`-based sibling call sites) for a future pass or Sarel's own call - not acted on, not blocking this Finding. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `0a2550b`/Finding 230, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. The 24-PR backlog (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#197`) is unaffected and untouched; none of these six files appear on any open PR's own branch (confirmed via `git log --all -- <path>` for each, and by the task brief's own statement that all 23 non-#197 PRs already had a full line-by-line read done earlier this segment with no mention of these files).

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run app/company/actions.spec.ts app/experience/actions.spec.ts app/company/principals/actions.spec.ts app/company/properties/actions.spec.ts "app/tenders/[id]/vault-quick-fix-actions.spec.ts" app/company/registrations/actions.spec.ts` (expect all passing, including the six new "two concurrent ..." tests). `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors). `git log --oneline -1` on `main` should show this pass's own fix commit.
