### Finding 232 (CONFIRMED, FIXED via PR, moderate - continuation of Finding 231 - the two `upsert()`-based sibling call sites Finding 231 itself flagged and left as a documented gap: `saveDocumentTemplate()` and `uploadTenderDocument()` have the identical "replace a document, storage race" shape as Finding 231's six sites, but their write can't take that fix's own `.eq(column, previousPath)` filter)

**Area:** `app/app/company/actions.ts` (`saveDocumentTemplate()`, writes `company_document_templates`), `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-actions.ts` (`uploadTenderDocument()`, writes `tender_answers`). New migration `app/supabase/migrations/0125_document_template_and_tender_answer_upload_race.sql`. Test coverage added to both files' own `*.spec.ts` (3 new tests each, 6 total) - neither function had ANY existing spec coverage before this pass (confirmed via `grep -rl saveDocumentTemplate\|uploadTenderDocument app --include=*.spec.ts` returning nothing).

**How this was found.** This pass's own task brief explicitly named this as a well-scoped continuation of Finding 231, left open specifically because `upsert()`'s conflict resolution is keyed on the `onConflict` columns, not an arbitrary `.eq()` filter chained afterwards - PostgREST's upsert is a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET ...` request with no row-level WHERE of its own. Confirmed both sites still have the exact shape by reading the real, current code (not assumed from Finding 231's own write-up): both read the row's current `storage_path`, upload the new file, write the row via `.upsert(row, { onConflict: "..." })`, then delete the OLD path afterwards - no gate anywhere on the write still matching what was read.

**What closing it properly needed, and why not just "restructure to update()+insert fallback".** Checked how other upsert-shaped races in this codebase were fixed first, per the task brief's own instruction, rather than inventing a new pattern: `0124_principals_ownership_cap_race.sql` closed an identical "no row of its own guaranteed to exist yet" race for `company_principals` (a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger, not an upsert, but the same underlying problem - nothing to lock directly for the very first row) by locking the always-existing PARENT row (`companies`) with `for update` instead. `0117_billing_employee_role_gap.sql` separately established that a `SECURITY DEFINER` function's own writes are NEVER bound by a table's RESTRICTIVE RLS policy (there, `start_payfast_checkout()` silently bypassed `company_subscriptions`' employee-lockout policy) and must re-check the equivalent role condition itself. Both `company_document_templates` and `tender_answers` have exactly this RESTRICTIVE "employee has no access" policy (`0077`) - a naive lift-the-upsert-into-an-RPC fix would have silently reopened the write-access-for-employees gap `0117` already closed elsewhere, since moving the write behind `SECURITY DEFINER` bypasses that policy entirely unless it's re-checked in the function body. Combined both precedents into two new functions (`replace_company_document_template()`, `replace_tender_answer_document()`, migration `0125`): lock the company's own row (`for update`) to serialize concurrent writes for that company (never the shared `tenders` row for the tender-answers case, which would wrongly serialize unrelated companies bidding on the same tender against each other), re-check the row's current `storage_path` against what the caller read before uploading, raise (`P0005`) on a mismatch instead of overwriting, and re-check `is_employee_in_company()` explicitly (`42501`) before writing anything.

**Confirmed live, real scratch Postgres, not reasoned about.** `service postgresql start`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d scratch_upsert_race` (124 migrations, matching `main`'s Finding 231 state) then, separately, a full 115-migration replay including the new `0125` to confirm it applies cleanly end to end. **Red (current, pre-fix shape):** one company, no existing `company_document_templates` row. Two concurrent psql sessions each ran the CURRENT upsert shape by hand (`select storage_path` - none yet - then, after a `pg_sleep(2)` widening the window the same way `0121`/`0124`'s own demos did, `insert ... on conflict (company_id, document_type) do update set ...` with two distinct storage_path values standing in for two different uploaded files) - **both upserts committed with no error.** Exactly one row remained afterwards (`count = 1`); the other session's own distinct storage_path value never appears anywhere in the table - the real file it names would be orphaned in the bucket forever while that session's own caller was told it succeeded. **Green (after applying `0125`):** re-ran the identical two-session scenario calling the new `replace_company_document_template()` RPC instead of the raw upsert - the first call's `for update` lock made the second block until the first committed, then the second correctly re-read the NOW-current `storage_path` (not the stale value both sessions read before either wrote) and raised `'This document was just replaced in another tab or request - refresh and try again.'` (`P0005`) instead of overwriting it. Exactly one of the two writes survived; the losing call got a real, catchable error. Also ran direct sanity checks against both new functions: normal insert (no existing row) then normal update (existing row, matching previousPath) for both tables; switching `company_document_templates` to `ai_guideline` mode with no new upload (doesn't need `p_expected_previous_path` to match, since `p_has_new_upload` is false - no storage-leak risk when nothing was uploaded); a conflict correctly raised on `tender_answers` with a stale previousPath; and the employee-role defense-in-depth check correctly raising `42501` on BOTH functions when called as a seeded `'employee'`-role `company_members` row.

**TypeScript-side changes.** Both Server Actions now call their respective RPC instead of `.upsert()`, passing `p_expected_previous_path` (what was read before uploading) and, for the templates function, `p_has_new_upload` (true only when this request itself uploaded a new file - a plain mode/guideline edit with no new upload never orphans anything in storage, so it skips the check rather than spuriously conflicting with an unrelated concurrent edit). On an RPC error, the EXISTING cleanup-and-retry handling (clean up this request's own just-uploaded file, never touch the still-referenced previous file, surface a message to the user) now surfaces the RPC's own real error message (`error.message || <generic fallback>`) instead of a generic one - the same convention already used by every other RPC-wrapped Server Action in this repo (e.g. `requestSubmissionPack()`'s `request_submission_pack_checked()` call). `uploadTenderDocument()`'s now-unused `userId` destructure was dropped (`answered_by` is set inside the RPC via `auth.uid()`, the same convention as every other `requested_by`/`updated_by` column this repo's SECURITY DEFINER functions already set themselves, never as a parameter).

**Verified red-then-green at the TypeScript layer too.** Since the actual race resolution now happens entirely inside Postgres (the Server Action makes a single RPC call and only ever sees success or a raised conflict, never the race itself), the TypeScript-level tests check the Server Action's own wiring rather than re-simulating concurrency in JS: `app/app/company/actions.spec.ts` gained "saveDocumentTemplate - replace_company_document_template raises a conflict..." (cleans up this request's own upload, never touches the previous file, surfaces the real message), "...succeeds" (deletes the superseded previous file, correct success redirect), and "...switching to a guideline needs no new upload" (`p_has_new_upload: false`, storage never touched at all). `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-actions.spec.ts` gained the mirror three for `uploadTenderDocument()`, plus one for "no previous document on file" (`p_expected_previous_path` is `null`, nothing deleted). All pass.

**Full regression.** `npx tsc --noEmit` (via `npm run typecheck`, includes `next typegen`) - 0 errors. `npx eslint` on all four touched TypeScript files - 0 errors/warnings. `npx vitest run` (the whole `app/` suite) - 72 files, 570/570 pass (564 baseline + 6 new). A full, separate 115-migration schema replay (through the new `0125`) also succeeded end to end, confirming the migration doesn't break anything later in the sequence.

**Escalated to a PR, not pushed directly to `main`.** This needed a new migration (two new `SECURITY DEFINER` functions, including a `for update` lock and an explicit RLS-equivalent re-check) and a write-path restructuring at two Server Action call sites - schema-adjacent and more than the "one additional filter, reusing an existing failure path" shape Finding 231's own six sites were. Per this pass's own binding methodology ("larger/sensitive -> PR via `mcp__github__create_pull_request` and STOP, don't merge"), opened as a PR against `main` rather than pushed directly. Not merged - awaiting Sarel's own review, same as every other open PR this backlog already has.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened; this Finding closes out the one Finding 231 itself left open. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `ede9d9a`/Finding 231, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before opening the PR, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. The 24-PR backlog (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#197`) is unaffected and untouched; neither touched file appears on any open PR's own branch. Both scratch databases used this pass (`scratch_upsert_race`, `scratch_full_replay`) dropped and the Postgres service stopped afterward - nothing left running.

To verify independently: from `app/`, `npx vitest run app/company/actions.spec.ts "app/tenders/[id]/general-actions.spec.ts"` (expect all passing, including the 6 new tests named above). `npm run typecheck` (0 errors). `service postgresql start`; `su postgres -c "psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE verify232'"`; `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d verify232` (expect "115 migrations"); `\df replace_company_document_template` / `\df replace_tender_answer_document` to confirm both functions exist. ### Finding 233 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - resource-exhaustion class, not a crash class - `docx_text()` opens any `.docx` (and any `.doc`'s own LibreOffice-converted `.docx`) directly via `python-docx`, which is itself just a zip container with no size limit of its own; a small, realistic upload (under EVERY existing upload-size cap this app enforces) can decompress to gigabytes inside the SAME in-process worker that is polling the job queue, with no subprocess boundary and no timeout to fall back on the way `pdftotext`/`soffice` already have)

**Area:** `engine/general/requirements.py` (`docx_text()` - the single shared implementation; `engine/cv/extract_cv_fields.py` and `engine/onboarding/classify_documents.py` both import it rather than reimplementing it, so one fix covers all three real call sites: tender-document requirement extraction, CV text extraction, and onboarding document classification). Test coverage added to `engine/general/test_requirements.py` (1 new test, `check_docx_zip_bomb_guard_caps_python_docx_parse()`).

**How this was found - a genuinely fresh angle, not a re-check of ground this segment already covered.** The task brief's own list of already-exhausted angles this segment named sibling TS/Python divergence, double-NULL auth bypasses, secrets exposure, PII masking, CI-status accuracy, quota-check-then-insert races, exact-webhook-redelivery idempotency, extreme-DATA PDF/DOCX crashes (Finding 227 - a too-long NAME value crashing a filename, not a malformed/hostile FILE), SA timezone handling, and both shapes of bulk-operation/storage-replace races (Findings 230-232). None of these is "a file whose own bytes are adversarial," which the task brief separately flagged as untouched: "input validation/sanitization gaps in file uploads themselves... an unexpectedly huge file that isn't caught before a slow operation... times out or OOMs." Read every file-upload entry point's own size/type checks first (`grep` across `app/app/**/*actions*.ts` and `app/lib/*.ts` for `MAX_*_BYTES`/`.size >`/`accept=` - confirmed every upload path already has a real byte-size ceiling, the smallest and most common being `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 4.4 * 1024 * 1024` in `app/lib/vaultDocuments.ts`, reused by company documents, principals, properties, registrations, pack-inputs and narrative-final uploads). Then checked what happens AFTER a file passes that ceiling and reaches the Python engine side for parsing - `engine/general/requirements.py`'s own `collect_documents()` already has an explicit, well-documented decompression-bomb guard (found and fixed 2026-11-03, still in place, re-verified passing) for literal `.zip` tender-pack bundles - but that guard runs ONLY when `collect_documents()` itself sees a `.zip` extension; it is never invoked for a lone `.docx` upload (onboarding, CV) or for a `.doc`'s own LibreOffice-converted `.docx` (both of which ARE zip containers under the hood, opened directly by `python-docx`, with nothing upstream of it checking anything). This asymmetry - one format in this exact threat family gets a guard, a sibling format using the identical container format does not - is what made this worth digging into rather than assuming python-docx was already safe by analogy to the zip-bundle fix.

**Confirmed live, real file, real measured resource usage - not reasoned about.** Built a real, syntactically valid, minimal OOXML `.docx` (`[Content_Types].xml` + `_rels/.rels` + one `word/document.xml`) whose body is 69,000 repetitions of `<w:p><w:r><w:t>` + 50,000 `"A"` characters + `</w:t></w:r></w:p>`, written with Python's own `zipfile` module (`ZIP_DEFLATED`, default settings - no exotic compression method, nothing a real attacker couldn't produce with any ordinary zip tool on repetitive text). Resulting file: **4.37MB on disk** (confirmed via `os.path.getsize` - under the app's own 4.4MB `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` cap on every one of the upload paths above) decompressing to **3.45GB of actual XML** (789:1 ratio - nowhere near the practical ceiling of plain DEFLATE on this repetitive a payload; a single long repeated byte run with no tag interruption every 50KB, or an LZMA-compressed entry, which Python's own `zipfile` reader already supports transparently, would almost certainly inflate further still inside the same 4.4MB budget - not attempted, since the result already below was sufficient to demonstrate the bug). Ran the REAL, unmodified `docx_text(path)` against this file: **red (pre-fix), under a 4GB `ulimit -v` cap modelling a resource-constrained worker container** - `python3 engine/general/test_requirements.py` raised a genuine, uncontrolled `MemoryError` partway through `lxml`'s own parse of `word/document.xml` (confirmed by running the exact same call standalone with `resource.getrusage` instrumentation first, before the memory cap was tightened for the red/green test: **peak RSS ~6.79GB, ~16.9 seconds of CPU**, eventually failing on an UNRELATED internal `libxml2` limit, `XMLSyntaxError: unknown error`, not anything this codebase added). **Green (post-fix)**, same 4GB `ulimit -v` cap: the new guard rejects the file in **0.36 seconds at ~39MB peak RSS** - a clean, immediate `ValueError`, not a multi-second multi-gigabyte spike that merely happens to end in an exception today.

**Why this is strictly worse than the "corrupt/unreadable file" case every one of these three call sites already handles correctly, and worse than the sibling PDF/`.doc` paths.** Every `docx_text()` call site (`requirements.py`'s `read_document()`, `extract_cv_fields.py`, `classify_documents.py`) already wraps the call in `try/except Exception` and reports a clean, user-facing "could not be opened / corrupt or not really a Word file" message - so a bomb that merely raises an exception, eventually, is not itself new. What is new, and what those `except` blocks cannot do anything about, is the RESOURCE SPIKE that happens BEFORE the exception is ever raised: `python-docx`/`lxml` run as plain library calls, in the SAME process and the SAME memory space as the worker's own job-polling loop (`engine/worker/run_bridges.py` and the per-engine `process_*_jobs.py` poll loops) - there is no subprocess boundary to isolate the blast radius, unlike `pdftotext` (`subprocess.run(..., timeout=120)`) and `soffice` (`subprocess.run(..., timeout=180)`), both of which are already time-bounded AND run as a separate OS process, so even a resource-hungry PDF/`.doc` only ever risks killing ITS OWN subprocess, not the worker. If the worker's own container has anything less than several GB of free memory headroom (plausible on a Railway-hosted always-on background worker - no explicit memory limit is set anywhere in this repo's `Dockerfile`/deployment docs, so this is the host platform's own default, not something this review can read directly, but nothing here suggests several GB of slack is guaranteed), the OS's own OOM killer - not this codebase's `try/except` - ends the ENTIRE worker process the moment it crosses that line, taking down whatever OTHER jobs were in flight in the same process along with the one that triggered it. That is a real availability bug, not merely an unhandled-error one: a single malicious or even accidentally-malformed `.docx` upload (company onboarding, a CV upload, or - least trusted of all - a buyer-published tender document fetched from an external OCDS/tender-portal source, the one input to this exact function this codebase does not control at all) can knock the whole fulfilment worker offline mid-queue.

**Fix.** Added `_docx_zip_bomb_guard(path)` to `engine/general/requirements.py`, called at the top of `docx_text()` before `python-docx` ever touches the file. It streams every member of the zip through in 1MB chunks (never trusting the zip's own stated `file_size` header, the identical caveat `collect_documents()`'s own 2026-11-03 guard already documents for the same reason - a crafted zip can misstate it), enforcing the exact same per-member/total byte caps that guard already uses and has already been reviewed and accepted for this threat model (`_ZIP_MEMBER_MAX_BYTES` = 300MB, `_ZIP_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES` = 1GB - reused directly, not reinvented), raising a plain `ValueError` the instant either cap is crossed. Because all three real call sites already catch `Exception` around their `docx_text()` call and report a clean message, this fix adds NO new failure branch anywhere - it only replaces an unbounded resource spike with a fast, bounded rejection that flows into the exact same "could not be opened" message path that already exists. A `.doc` file's own LibreOffice-converted `.docx` is covered automatically, since it is read via the same `docx_text(conv)` call at every site.

**Verified red-then-green.** New test `check_docx_zip_bomb_guard_caps_python_docx_parse()` in `engine/general/test_requirements.py`, built the same way as the existing `check_zip_decompression_bomb_is_capped()` test just above it (same file, same style): builds the 4.37MB/3.45GB bomb docx above, confirms `docx_text()` on it raises a `ValueError` naming the guard rather than succeeding or raising `MemoryError`, and separately confirms a genuinely ordinary small `.docx` (written with real `python-docx`, `doc.add_paragraph(...)`) still reads back its real text unaffected - the guard must not false-positive on a real document. **Red:** `git stash` on `requirements.py` only (test file left in place), re-ran `python3 engine/general/test_requirements.py` under a 4GB `ulimit -v` cap - `1 failure(s)`, exactly the new test, and it failed with a REAL `MemoryError` (not a simulated one) under that cap, confirming the risk directly rather than asserting it secondhand. **Green:** fix restored, same command, same memory cap - `0 failure(s)`.

**Full regression, all three real call sites plus the sibling test files that exercise real `.docx` content end to end.** `python3 engine/general/test_requirements.py` - `0 failure(s)` (including the pre-existing `check_zip_decompression_bomb_is_capped()`, confirming the new guard and the older zip-bundle guard don't interfere with each other). `python3 engine/general/test_general_bridge.py` - `ALL PASSED`, including its own real-filled-`.docx`-readback assertion (a genuine SBD/SANRAL form, filled by `fill_sbd_docx.py`, written back out and re-read through this same now-guarded `docx_text()` - confirms zero false positives on a realistic, legitimate production `.docx`). `python3 engine/general/general_harness.py --no-pack` against the full real sample-tender corpus - `91 clean, 0 flagged, 0 failed` (every sample `.docx`/`.doc`/`.pdf`/`.zip` in the real corpus still reads identically to its stored baseline). `python3 engine/general/test_build_general_pack.py`, `test_fill_sbd_docx.py` - `0 failure(s)` each. `python3 engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py`, `test_process_cv_jobs.py`, `test_generate_cv.py` - `ALL PASSED` / `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/onboarding/test_classify_documents.py`, `test_process_onboarding_jobs.py` - `ALL PASSED` / `0 failure(s)`. `ruff check engine/general/requirements.py engine/general/test_requirements.py` - 20 pre-existing errors, confirmed identical in count and location before and after this change via `git stash`/`ruff`/`git stash pop` (none introduced by this fix). Every file and test command above is already wired into `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` (confirmed via `grep` against the workflow file directly), so this fix is covered by the existing CI job with no workflow change needed.

**Related paths checked, no issue found (for completeness, not padding).** `pdf_text_or_error()` (same file) already runs `pdftotext` with `timeout=120` in its own subprocess - a PDF decompression bomb is bounded by that timeout and isolated to its own process, not this bug class. `convert_with_soffice()` already runs with `timeout=180`, same reasoning, for the `.doc` -> `.docx` CONVERSION step itself (the bug fixed here is specifically about READING the resulting `.docx` afterwards, which this fix now also covers via the shared `docx_text()` call). `collect_documents()`'s own zip-bundle guard (2026-11-03) is unaffected and untouched - re-verified passing, still the right guard for literal `.zip` tender bundles, just never the same code path as a lone `.docx`/`.doc` upload.

**Severity: moderate, not severe.** This is a real availability/DoS vector against the background worker, not a data-integrity, auth, or billing issue, and not a guaranteed outage - whether it actually OOM-kills the whole worker depends on that worker's own host memory headroom, which this review cannot read directly from the repo (no explicit container memory limit is configured anywhere found). Even on a host with ample headroom, the multi-second/multi-gigabyte spike per malicious upload is itself a real resource-exhaustion cost worth closing regardless.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one new helper function, one call added at the top of one existing function, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface - no migration, no policy, no table, no Dockerfile change, no billing logic touched anywhere) with a verified red-then-green test backed by a REAL `MemoryError` under a realistic memory cap (not a simulated/asserted risk), and a clean full regression run across every real call site and every CI-covered sibling test file that exercises genuine `.docx` content - pushed directly to `main` per this pass's own binding methodology.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `164637b`/Finding 232's own docs commit, matching the task brief's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. The 25-item backlog (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#198`) is unaffected and untouched; `engine/general/requirements.py` and `engine/general/test_requirements.py` do not appear on any open PR's own branch (confirmed via `git log --all -- <path>` for both files).

To verify independently: from `engine/general/`, `python3 test_requirements.py` (expect `0 failure(s)`, including `check_docx_zip_bomb_guard_caps_python_docx_parse`). For the live repro under a realistic memory cap: `( ulimit -v 4000000; python3 test_requirements.py )` should still report `0 failure(s)` post-fix; reverting only `requirements.py` (`git stash push -- engine/general/requirements.py`) and re-running the identical command reproduces the pre-fix `MemoryError`/`1 failure(s)`. `python3 general_harness.py --no-pack` (expect `91 clean, 0 flagged, 0 failed`). `git log --oneline -1` on `main` should show this pass's own fix commit.

### Finding 234 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - the SANRAL and non-SANRAL "qualifying experience" renderers each independently re-filtered the Experience Library by document type ALONE, silently dropping the rule's own `since_year` cutoff that `evaluateEvidence()` - the shared, authoritative evaluation both of them sit right next to - already applies, so the exact same tagged items could read as fully qualifying in one place on the same screen while the status/detail text beside it says "missing")

**Area:** `app/lib/experienceEvidence.ts` (new exported `itemQualifiesForRule()`), `app/app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-data.ts` (the non-SANRAL Pack Review "Qualifying experience" item), `app/app/tenders/[id]/compliance-report.tsx` (the SANRAL "Company experience" chip and per-item badges). Test coverage added in new `app/lib/experienceEvidence.test.ts` (5 cases) - no spec file for this module existed before this (confirmed via `find`/`grep`).

**How this was found.** This pass's rotation landed on the non-SANRAL pack. After a full, clean sweep of `lib/generalTender.ts`'s `checkReturnable()`/`questionStates()`/`companyFieldStates()`, `validityAtClosing()`'s SAST-midnight inheritance from Finding 228, the `bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until` generated-column null-safety, `general-pack-review-logic.ts`'s `signatureAnswerStatus()` (already independently correct, same shape as Finding 203's own fix), `pack-inputs-actions.ts`'s `confirmPositionPerson()` union logic (traced and ruled a harmless no-op), and `build_general_pack.py`'s vault-file mapping dicts (the 2026-11-03 `cidb_document_path` gap confirmed still fixed) turned up nothing new, sibling-comparison was applied one level further: `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s own "Qualifying experience" item computes its displayed `value` as `acceptedDocTypes(rule).size > 0 ? experience.items.filter((i) => acceptedDocTypes(rule).has(i.document_type)).length : experience.items.length`, right next to a `note` field populated from `evaluateEvidence()`'s own `detail` - two independently-computed facts about the same items, displayed together, the exact shape Finding 226 (SANRAL B7's live-preview-vs-server-check divergence) already demonstrated is a recurring, real bug class in this codebase. Checking `evaluateEvidence()` itself (`lib/experienceEvidence.ts`) showed its own `qualifyingItems` filter applies BOTH `accepted.has(i.document_type)` AND a private `inSince` check (`!rule.since_year || completion_date's year >= rule.since_year`) - the displayed `value` line applies only the first. Checking every other real caller of `acceptedDocTypes()` for the same shape found two more: `general-workspace.tsx` (the live Tender Workspace screen) already does this correctly, using `evidenceEval.qualifying` - `evaluateEvidence()`'s own returned count - directly, never re-filtering; `compliance-report.tsx` (SANRAL's own equivalent renderer) has the identical bug as `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s, both for its summary chip (`qualifying = items.filter((i) => accepted.has(i.document_type))`) AND its per-item "Counts" badge (`accepted.has(i.document_type) ? <Chip "Counts"/> : <Chip "Not accepted"/>`, with no since_year awareness at all).

**Why this isn't a contrived edge case.** `since_year` is a real, live field read from real tenders' own documents (`engine/discovery/score_outlook.py extract_experience_evidence()`) - `experienceEvidence.ts`'s own module docstring names a specific real buyer using it: "Gauteng DRT: completion certificates since 2000, per project (Sched. A)". A tender stating a `since_year` cutoff rather than a rolling window is exactly the real-world shape this gap silently mishandles, for either a SANRAL tender or a general one (the evidence-rule extraction is family-agnostic).

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Built a real `EvidenceRule` (`since_year: 2020`, `accepted_evidence: ["completion_certificate"]`, `projects_required: 3`) and 3 real Experience Library items (2 completion certificates dated 2023, 1 dated 2015 - before the cutoff). Ran the REAL, unmodified `evaluateEvidence()`: `status: "missing"`, `qualifying: 2`, `detail: "...Only 2 of 3 qualifying item(s)."` - correct, the 2015 item doesn't count. Ran the REAL, unmodified type-only re-filter each buggy renderer used on the exact same 3 items: both returned `3`. Concretely, pre-fix, a user would see (general-pack-review-data.ts) "3 item(s)" as the item's displayed value with "Only 2 of 3 qualifying item(s)" as the note directly beside it - a visible, self-contradicting line - and (compliance-report.tsx) a chip reading "3 of 3 qualifying" rendered in SUCCESS green for a tender whose real functionality score, computed by the same `evaluateEvidence()` elsewhere on the identical page, is actually "missing".

**Fix.** Extracted the combined check `evaluateEvidence()` already had inlined as a private `inSince` closure into a new exported pure function, `itemQualifiesForRule(rule: EvidenceRule, item: ExperienceLite): boolean` (`lib/experienceEvidence.ts`) - the single source of truth for "does this one item actually count toward this rule," reused by `evaluateEvidence()` itself (no behavior change there - same two conditions, same order) and by both renderers that previously re-derived a narrower version of the same question. `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s displayed value now reads `evidenceEval.qualifying` directly - the exact pattern `general-workspace.tsx` already used correctly, so there's nothing left to recompute at all (the now-unused `acceptedDocTypes` import was dropped). `compliance-report.tsx`'s chip and per-item badges now call `itemQualifiesForRule(rule, i)`; the per-item badge gained a third, more accurate state for an item whose document type IS accepted but fails the since_year cutoff ("Accepted type, but before `<since_year>` - doesn't count"), distinct from "Not accepted by this tender" at all - these are two different facts about an item, and conflating them (as the pre-fix binary branch did) would have kept misleading a user checking individual rows even after the summary count was fixed.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added `lib/experienceEvidence.test.ts` (new file, `node --experimental-strip-types --test` convention): `itemQualifiesForRule` rejects a right-type item before `since_year`, accepts one on/after it, always rejects a wrong document type, and accepts any date when the rule has no `since_year` at all; a fifth test confirms `evaluateEvidence()`'s own `qualifying` count agrees with `itemQualifiesForRule()` applied item-by-item on the 2-of-3 adversarial case. **Red:** saved the diff, `git apply -R`, re-ran `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/experienceEvidence.test.ts` directly - immediate import/reference failure (`itemQualifiesForRule` doesn't exist), confirming the function is genuinely new, not a rename. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - 5/5 pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on all 3 touched files. Regression: `npx vitest run lib/sanralB7.spec.ts` (unrelated sanity check, 6/6 - confirms the general toolchain is sound); `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/compileReadiness.test.ts lib/dates.test.ts` (28/28, both files unaffected by this change, run as a broader regression spot-check since neither touches `experienceEvidence.ts`).

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained TypeScript fix across 3 files (one new shared helper function, two call sites changed to use it or its result instead of an independent re-filter) - no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change. Pushed directly to `main`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `164637b`/Finding 232, matching this pass's own stated current state exactly) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. The 24-PR backlog (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#198`) is unaffected and untouched; none of the 3 touched files appear on any open PR's own branch.

To verify independently: from `app/`, `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/experienceEvidence.test.ts` (expect `5/5 pass`). On a tender whose evaluation rules state a `since_year` cutoff with at least one qualifying-type item dated before it, confirm Pack Review's "Qualifying experience" value and the SANRAL Pack Review's own "Company experience" chip both now agree with the status/detail text beside them, rather than showing a higher count. `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors).

### Finding 235 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - resource-exhaustion class, the same shape as Finding 233 but on the .xlsm/.xlsx side - `sanral_fill.py`'s `Workbook.__init__` decompresses EVERY member of an uploaded .xlsm/.xlsx into memory unconditionally, via one dict comprehension, before ANY real workbook-structure check runs, with no subprocess boundary the way `pdftotext`/`soffice` already have)

**Area:** `engine/sanral_fill.py` (`Workbook.__init__` - the single shared implementation every SANRAL-side reader and filler imports: `engine/fingerprint.py`, `engine/fill_tender.py`, `engine/fill_conventional.py`, `engine/fill_financial.py`, `engine/fill_financial_hours.py`, `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`, `engine/discovery/boq_extraction.py`, `engine/pack_generator/suggest_pack.py`, `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py`, `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`, `engine/pack/bridge_selftest.py`, `engine/admin_harness.py`). Test coverage added to `engine/test_sanral_fill.py` (3 new checks).

**How this was found.** Picked up the task brief's own first-listed concrete suggestion for this pass's fresh angle: "XLSX/spreadsheet parsing... check if any xlsx parsing path in this repo has the same gap `docx_text()` just had" (Finding 233, closed immediately before this pass started). Checked for `openpyxl` first (none anywhere in this repo, confirmed via `grep` - this codebase reads/writes `.xlsm`/`.xlsx` entirely through its own hand-rolled zip+XML reader, `engine/sanral_fill.py`'s `Workbook` class, specifically because `openpyxl` silently drops SANRAL's own data-validation/conditional-format extensions and form-control dropdowns, per that file's own header comment). Read `Workbook.__init__` directly: `self.zin = zipfile.ZipFile(path); self.files = {i.filename: self.zin.read(i.filename) for i in self.zin.infolist()}` - every member of the zip is decompressed and held in memory, unconditionally, with no size check anywhere, BEFORE `_map_sheets()`/`_map_controls()` (the first real structure checks) ever run. Confirmed real, untrusted reachability, not just template-filling: `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`'s `classify_workbook()` calls `Workbook(path)` on **every** uploaded tender document whose extension is `.xlsm`/`.xlsx` (both in `app/lib/manualTender.ts`'s `ACCEPTED_EXTENSIONS`, up to its own `MAX_TENDER_FILE_BYTES` = 50MB) at intake - the exact same "a buyer-published or company-uploaded file, not a trusted template" reachability `docx_text()` had. `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` and `engine/pack/assemble_pack.py` also call `Workbook()` directly on a tender's own stored technical/financial submission workbook on every poll cycle, with no try/except around the call at either site (unlike every `docx_text()` call site, which already wraps it) - a bomb there doesn't just spike memory, it's also an unhandled exception.

**Confirmed live, real file, real measured resource usage - not reasoned about.** Built a minimal, syntactically-valid-looking `.xlsm` (`[Content_Types].xml` + one bogus, otherwise-unused member `xl/junk.bin`, 4000 x 1MB of a single repeated byte, `ZIP_DEFLATED` level 9 via Python's own `zipfile`) - **3.89MB on disk** (confirmed via `os.path.getsize`, under both the 4.4MB `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and the 50MB `MAX_TENDER_FILE_BYTES` caps) decompressing to **3.90GB** (~1,030:1 ratio). The bomb member doesn't need to look like a real workbook part at all, and the file doesn't need `xl/workbook.xml` to be well-formed - `self.files = {...}` reads every member in the archive, by name, regardless of whether anything downstream will ever ask for it. Ran the REAL, unmodified `Workbook(path)` against this file: standalone, with `resource.getrusage` instrumentation, it peaked at **~7.84GB RSS and ~13.7s CPU** before eventually failing on an unrelated `KeyError` in `_map_sheets()` (the bomb fixture has no `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` at all - the OOM-magnitude spike already happened before that lookup). **Worse than Finding 233's own docx repro (6.79GB RSS) despite a smaller input file (3.89MB vs. 4.37MB)**, because `python-docx`'s own `lxml` parse at least has to build a DOM as it goes; this class's `dict` comprehension is a flatter, even-less-bounded "read every member fully, unconditionally" step. Under a 4GB `ulimit -v` cap modelling a resource-constrained worker container, the same call raised a genuine, uncontrolled `MemoryError` ("Unable to allocate output buffer").

**Why this is strictly worse than the "corrupt/unreadable file" case most call sites already handle, same reasoning as Finding 233.** `classify_tender.classify_workbook()` already wraps `Workbook(path)` in `try/except Exception`, reporting a clean "could not open as a workbook" message - but that `except` only runs AFTER the spike, identical to `docx_text()`'s pre-fix shape. `process_pack_jobs.py`/`assemble_pack.py` don't even have that: `Workbook(technical)` there is called with no surrounding try/except at all (confirmed via direct read of both call sites), so on these paths a bomb is both a resource spike AND an unhandled exception. All of this runs in-process, in the same worker that polls the job queue, with no subprocess boundary - the identical availability concern Finding 233 raised for `python-docx`.

**Fix.** Added `_zip_bomb_guard(zin)` to `engine/sanral_fill.py`, called at the very top of `Workbook.__init__`, immediately after `zipfile.ZipFile(path)` opens the archive and before `self.files = {...}` reads anything. Streams every member through in 1MB chunks (never trusting a zip's own stated `file_size` - the same caveat `requirements.py`'s own guards already document), enforcing the SAME per-member/total byte caps `_docx_zip_bomb_guard` already uses and has already been reviewed and accepted for this threat model (`_ZIP_MEMBER_MAX_BYTES` = 300MB, `_ZIP_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES` = 1GB - reused as values, not re-derived; `sanral_fill.py` has no import relationship with `requirements.py` in either direction, so the guard function itself is a small, self-contained duplicate of the same streaming logic, not a cross-module import), raising a plain `ValueError` on a breach. Every call site that already catches `Exception` around `Workbook(...)` gets a fast, bounded rejection instead of an unbounded spike with no new failure branch; the two call sites with no existing try/except (`process_pack_jobs.py`, `assemble_pack.py`) already treat any `Workbook(...)` failure as fatal for that job/run (a template that can't be opened can't be filled either way) - this fix does not change that behavior, it only makes the failure fast and bounded instead of a multi-gigabyte spike that then fails anyway.

**Verified red-then-green.** New checks in `engine/test_sanral_fill.py`: builds the 3.89MB/3.90GB bomb fixture above, confirms `Workbook()` on it raises a `ValueError` naming the guard rather than succeeding or raising `MemoryError`, and separately confirms the existing real, committed SANRAL sample (`templates/samples/R.334-030-2025.1F_ran.xlsm`) still opens normally and exposes its real sheets - the guard must not false-positive on a real document. **Red:** `git stash push -- engine/sanral_fill.py` (test file left in place, carrying the new checks), re-ran `python3 engine/test_sanral_fill.py` under a 4GB `ulimit -v` cap - `1 FAILURE(S)`, and it failed with a REAL `MemoryError` ("MemoryError - guard did not run"), not a simulated one. **Green:** `git stash pop` to restore the fix, same command, same memory cap - `0 failure(s)`, all 7 checks (4 pre-existing `set_value()` checks plus the 3 new ones).

**Full regression, every real caller of `Workbook`.** `python3 engine/test_sanral_fill.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_sanral_b7.py` - `ALL PASSED`. `python3 engine/test_fingerprint.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_company_documents.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_fill_financial_hours.py` - `ALL PASSED`. `python3 engine/test_fill_a_forms.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_form_field_audit.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_fill_tender.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/test_fill_financial.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/pack_generator/test_suggest_pack.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/discovery/test_boq_extraction.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/intake/test_classify_tender.py` - `0 failure(s)`. `python3 engine/pack/test_process_pack_jobs.py`, `test_sync_functions.py`, `test_assemble_pack.py` - `0 failure(s)`/`ALL PASSED` each. `python3 engine/test_fill_key_persons_malformed.py`, `test_fill_docx_forms.py`, `test_make_envelope_covers.py` - `0 failure(s)` each. `python3 engine/general/general_harness.py --no-pack` - `91 clean, 0 flagged, 0 failed`. `ruff check engine/sanral_fill.py engine/test_sanral_fill.py` - 16 pre-existing errors, confirmed identical in count before and after this change via `git stash`/`ruff`/`git stash pop` (none introduced). `python3 engine/test_sanral_fill.py` is already wired into `.github/workflows/bridge-worker-ci.yml` (line ~270, confirmed via `grep` against the workflow file directly), so this fix is covered by the existing CI job with no workflow change needed.

**Severity: moderate, not severe.** Same reasoning as Finding 233 - a real availability/DoS vector against the background worker, not a data-integrity, auth, or billing issue, and whether it actually OOM-kills the whole worker depends on that worker's own host memory headroom (no explicit container memory limit confirmed anywhere in this repo, per Finding 233's own still-open side-note). The two call sites with no existing try/except (`process_pack_jobs.py`, `assemble_pack.py`) make the failure mode on THOSE specific paths an unhandled exception rather than a caught one even before the spike - this fix's `ValueError` is itself still unhandled there, but it now arrives in milliseconds instead of after a multi-gigabyte, multi-second spike, which is the actual harm this fix closes; making those two call sites also catch the exception cleanly (matching `classify_workbook()`'s own convention) would be a reasonable follow-up but is a separate, smaller finding, not folded into this fix to keep this pass's own change minimal and reviewable.

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained Python fix (one new helper function, one call added at the top of one existing `__init__`, no RLS/schema/money/worker-image surface - no migration, no policy, no table, no Dockerfile change, no billing logic touched) with a verified red-then-green test backed by a REAL `MemoryError` under a realistic memory cap, and a clean full regression run across every real call site of `Workbook` found in this repo plus every CI-covered sibling test file - pushed directly to `main` per this pass's own binding methodology.
