### Finding 236 (CONFIRMED, NOT YET FIXED ON `main` - PR #199 opened, awaiting review - moderate, cross-tenant-authorization class - `signatory_scopes` (0061) is the one "child row references a specific row owned by a specific company" table in this schema that was never given the cross-tenant integrity check every other table of this exact shape already has, letting any company plant a row naming a COMPLETE STRANGER'S real `person_id` from a different company)

**Area:** `app/supabase/migrations/0061_signatory_scopes.sql` (table + RLS, unchanged by this finding) and `app/app/people/actions.ts`'s `addSignatoryScope()` (the one Server Action that writes this table, confirmed as the only one via `grep -rn "signatory_scopes" app/`). Fix proposed as a new migration, `app/supabase/migrations/0137_signatory_scopes_cross_tenant_check.sql` - numbered `0137`, not the next sequential `0125`, because `0125`-`0136` are already independently claimed across PRs #183-#198 (checked via `gh api .../pulls/<n>/files` before picking a number) - a pre-existing, already-flagged collision class in this backlog (see PR #176's own known collision), not introduced by this finding.

**How this was found.** Took the task brief's own "cross-tenant data/error-message leakage" angle - flagged across several prior passes as a promising but never-actually-chased angle. An exhaustive sweep of every unique/check-constraint violation message across all 124 migrations, the compliance-digest notification batch job, filename/XML-text sanitization across the whole Python docx-generation pipeline, and the shared-tender activity-log/update-acceptance anonymization (`tender_watched_documents`/`accept_tender_update_date`) turned up nothing - this codebase is unusually careful about exactly that specific "a raw error or log line names another company" shape already (see this pass's own System-Status entry for the full list of what was checked and ruled out). Widened the search from "does a message leak a name" to the closely related "does any write path let one company's own row reference a DIFFERENT company's actual data by id" - the same underlying class 0043 (`tt_check_same_company`), 0050 (`tt_property_rows_check`/`tt_bank_accounts_check`/`held_registrations`' own inline check), 0034 (`submitted_by_person_id`'s own trigger) and 0097 were each written, at different times, to close for a specific table. Built the full list of every `*_id uuid references <a company-scoped table>` column in the schema (`grep -rn "references people\(id\)"`/`references company_principals\(id\)`/`references company_properties\(id\)` etc. across every migration) and checked each one against that trigger coverage. Every single one was covered - `projects`/`cv_uploads`/`generated_cvs`/`cv_extraction_results`/`person_role_eligibility`.person_id, `tender_tasks`.assigned_to, `tender_pack_assignments`.suggested_person_id/confirmed_person_id, `property_documents`.property_id, `bank_accounts`.principal_id, `held_registrations`.principal_id, `tender_packs`.submitted_by_person_id - except `signatory_scopes`.person_id (0061), which postdates both 0043 and 0050 (the convention already existed when 0061 was written) and has no trigger coverage at all. Its own RLS (`"signatory_scopes: tenant isolation"`) only checks `is_company_member(company_id)` - the value being written, not whether `person_id` itself belongs to that company. Confirmed `addSignatoryScope()` (`app/app/people/actions.ts`) takes `person_id` straight from form data with no separate server-side check either - its own file header comment states outright that this file relies on RLS alone for "a person can only be read or written by someone who is a member of that person's company," true for `people`/`projects` but never true for `signatory_scopes`.

**Confirmed live, real exploit, real scratch Postgres (never the live DB) - not reasoned about.** Dropped a disposable database (`scratch_find236_signatory`, dropped after); replayed the full schema via `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` (115 migrations incl. this fix's own 0137, confirmed clean with no errors). Seeded two real companies (A = attacker, B = victim) with real `auth.users`/`company_members`/`people` rows, and a real director `person_id` belonging ONLY to company B. Switched to the real `authenticated` Postgres role (not `service_role`, not superuser) with `auth.uid()` set to company A's own real owner user (`set_config('test.uid', ...)`, the exact convention `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` already uses) and ran exactly the insert `addSignatoryScope()` sends: `insert into signatory_scopes (company_id, person_id, region) values (<A's own company_id>, <B's real person_id>, 'Gauteng')`. **Pre-fix: this succeeded** (`INSERT 0 1`) and the planted row was then readable back by company A's own RLS (`is_company_member(company_id)` matches, since `company_id` really is A's own) - a real, working cross-tenant write with no privilege beyond an ordinary signed-in company owner, confirmed on the unmodified pre-0137 schema. **Post-fix (0137 applied): the identical insert now raises** `signatory_scopes: person_id must be a person of the same company` and is rejected; a second insert in the same session using company A's OWN real person instead still succeeds unchanged (`INSERT 0 1`, visible in the follow-up `select`) - no regression on the legitimate case.

**Impact, honestly scoped - data-integrity/cross-tenant-interference, not a direct secrets read.** Read `app/app/tenders/[id]/signatory-logic.ts`'s `pickDefaultSignatory()`/`scoreFor()` in full: it only scores a `scopes` row whose `person_id` matches an entry already in the caller's own `signers` list, itself queried separately and already scoped to the caller's own company elsewhere - so a planted row naming a stranger's `person_id` never actually influences that attacking company's own signatory suggestion (it is inert there). The real harm is narrower but still real: any company can silently attach an arbitrary region/industry/discipline tag to a complete stranger's real person record with zero relationship to them, and - since `deleteSignatoryScope()` (`app/app/people/actions.ts`) filters its delete by the CALLER's OWN `company_id` - the planted row can only ever be removed by the company that planted it, never by the victim company whose own person it names and whose own `/people/[id]` page would now show it as one of that person's own recorded scopes. No company name, email or other identifying string is exposed by this path on its own (the person's name was already presumably known to or guessable by whoever submitted `person_id`, and nothing in this specific flow echoes it back) - rated moderate, not severe, on that basis; still a genuine, unauthorized cross-tenant write with no business justification for existing at all.

**Fix.** `app/supabase/migrations/0137_signatory_scopes_cross_tenant_check.sql` adds `tt_signatory_scopes_check()`, a `before insert or update` trigger on `signatory_scopes` mirroring `tt_bank_accounts_check`'s exact convention (0050): raises `signatory_scopes: person_id must be a person of the same company` (`errcode 23514`) when no row in `people` has that `id` AND that `company_id` together. Additive-only, narrow-only: every existing row in the table today already satisfies this (person_id already belongs to the same company in every legitimate case), so nothing about today's real usage changes.

**Secondary, lower-severity, related observation - not fixed in this same change.** `create_company_invite_checked()` (0113) similarly never validates that its own `p_linked_person_id` parameter belongs to `p_company_id` before inserting the `company_invites` row. Checked whether this is independently exploitable the same way: it is not, today - `redeem_company_invite()`'s own `update people set linked_user_id = ... where id = v_invite.linked_person_id and company_id = v_invite.company_id` already filters by the INVITE's own `company_id`, so a cross-company `linked_person_id` silently matches zero rows on redemption rather than linking anyone to anyone. A real gap in input validation at the write site, but with no demonstrated end-to-end effect given the redemption-side filter - flagged here for Sarel's own judgment call (tighten `create_company_invite_checked()` to match the pattern anyway, for defense-in-depth, vs. leave as documented-safe) rather than folded into this same fix, since it is a different root cause on a different function and this pass's own change should stay minimal and reviewable.

**Escalated to a PR, not pushed directly.** This fix adds a new migration (schema surface: a new trigger function + trigger) - explicitly one of this pass's own excluded categories for a direct push (`no RLS/money/schema/worker-image`), unlike Finding 235's pure-Python fix. Opened as PR #199 (`fix/signatory-scopes-cross-tenant-check` -> `main`) per this pass's own binding methodology; not merged.

**Backlog status.** No existing backlog item touched - `signatory_scopes`/`app/app/people/actions.ts` do not appear on any of the 25 open PRs' own branches (confirmed via `git log --all -- app/supabase/migrations/0061_signatory_scopes.sql app/app/people/actions.ts`, restricted to this repo's own branch refs). `git fetch origin main` immediately before this pass started and again immediately before opening the PR, both clean at `01b2b06` - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: `engine/security/replay_schema.sh -U postgres -d <fresh db>` to build the schema including `0137`, then as the `authenticated` role with `auth.uid()` set to a real company-A user, attempt `insert into signatory_scopes (company_id, person_id, region) values (<A>, <B's real person_id>, 'x')` - expect `ERROR: signatory_scopes: person_id must be a person of the same company`; the identical insert with A's own real person_id should still succeed.

### Finding 237 (CONFIRMED, NOT YET FIXED ON `main` - PR #200 opened, awaiting review - moderate, cross-tenant-authorization/information-disclosure class - Finding 236's own "dead-but-sloppy, not exploitable" characterization of `create_company_invite_checked()`'s missing `p_linked_person_id` validation was itself incomplete: `redeem_company_invite()`'s LATER write is correctly company-scoped, but its EARLIER gating read is not, and that read alone is a real cross-tenant information-disclosure oracle)

**Area:** `create_company_invite_checked()` (`app/supabase/migrations/0113_create_invite_seat_check_race.sql`) and `redeem_company_invite()` (`app/supabase/migrations/0122_redeem_invite_linked_person_race.sql`, the current `create or replace` of a function first introduced in `0077` and re-replaced by `0107`/`0116`/`0122`). Fix: `app/supabase/migrations/0138_invite_linked_person_cross_tenant_check.sql`, numbered `0138` - the highest claimed number across all 26 then-open PRs was `0137` (this track's own PR #199, Finding 236), confirmed via `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` across every one of `#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#199` before picking a number, the same methodology Finding 236 itself used.

**How this was found.** Took the task brief's own option (a): independently re-verify Finding 236's "related-but-not-independently-exploitable" `create_company_invite_checked()` observation before deciding whether to tighten it, rather than trusting the prior write-up's conclusion at face value. Re-read both functions side by side. Finding 236's own claim is accurate as far as it goes: `redeem_company_invite()`'s final write - `update people set linked_user_id = v_uid where id = v_invite.linked_person_id and company_id = v_invite.company_id` - is filtered by the INVITE's own `company_id`, so a cross-company `linked_person_id` can never actually have its `linked_user_id` overwritten by this path; that part of the claim holds up under direct testing (see below). But the SAME function has an earlier statement that gates on the SAME `people` row, added by `0122` specifically to close a different race (Finding 178-class TOCTOU): `select linked_user_id into v_person_owner from people where id = v_invite.linked_person_id for update` - with no `company_id` filter at all, unlike the write three lines below it. Its result feeds `if v_person_owner is not null and v_person_owner <> v_uid then raise exception 'That roster entry is already linked to a different account.'` - a boolean-ish signal (raises vs. doesn't) that depends entirely on another company's real `linked_user_id` state, reachable by anyone who can get a cross-company `linked_person_id` into a `company_invites` row at all - which `create_company_invite_checked()`'s own missing validation lets any company admin do directly, via `supabase.rpc()`, for an invite into their OWN company (no need to compromise or even know anything about the target company beyond a real `people.id` value).

**Confirmed live, real scratch Postgres (never the live DB), against the real unmodified pre-fix code - not reasoned about.** Dropped a disposable database (`scratch_find237_invite_oracle`, dropped after); replayed the full pre-fix schema (114 migrations, through `0124`) via `engine/security/replay_schema.sh`. Seeded two real companies: Company A (attacker, one real owner), Company B (victim, two real `people` rows set up entirely by Company B itself with no attacker involvement - "Victim D", already linked to a real Company-B `auth.users` account, and "Victim B2", not linked to anyone). As Company A's real signed-in owner (`authenticated` role, `auth.uid()` set via `set_config('test.uid', ...)`, never `service_role`), called `create_company_invite_checked()` twice - once naming Victim D's real `person_id`, once naming Victim B2's - both succeeded with `INSERT 0 1`-style success, confirming the missing-validation claim directly rather than assuming it. Then, as two of the attacker's OWN other mailboxes (freshly created `auth.users` rows with zero relationship to Company B), redeemed each invite in turn: **redeeming the Victim-D invite raised exactly `That roster entry is already linked to a different account.` and rolled back entirely** (confirmed via `company_invites.accepted_at` staying `null` and no `company_members` row for that redeemer) - **redeeming the Victim-B2 invite raised nothing and committed fully** (`accepted_at` set, a real `company_members` row inserted for that redeemer into Company A). The two outcomes track Victim D/B2's real linked-status exactly, for an attacker who never had any legitimate relationship to Company B. Confirmed separately that Company B's own `people` rows were never modified by either redemption (`linked_user_id` unchanged on both) - this specific part of Finding 236's claim (the write is safe) held up.

**Impact, honestly scoped - information disclosure, not account takeover or a write-side compromise.** The oracle reveals only a boolean-shaped fact (another company's specific person record is linked to SOME account, not which one, not any other field) about a `people.id` the attacker must already know. `people.id` values are UUIDv4s and not exposed in any URL, export, or cross-company-visible field found by this pass's own check of `app/app/tenders/[id]/activity-log.tsx`/`app/lib/tenderActivity.ts` (the one place a shared tender's activity legitimately crosses company lines, and which this same review segment's Finding-236 pass already confirmed anonymizes the other company in every place checked) - so this requires the attacker to already possess a specific stranger's `people.id` through some other means (not evaluated here, out of scope for this finding) before the oracle has anything to answer. Rated moderate on that basis: a real, confirmed, cross-tenant information leak with no legitimate business justification for existing, but bounded both in what it reveals and in how an attacker would come to have a usable target in the first place.

**Fix.** `app/supabase/migrations/0138_invite_linked_person_cross_tenant_check.sql`, two layers:
1. `create_company_invite_checked()` now validates `p_linked_person_id` (when given) belongs to `p_company_id` before the `insert`, rejecting with `company_invites: linked_person_id must be a person in the same company` (`errcode 23514`) otherwise - closing this at the root, and resolving Finding 236's own open "Sarel's call" item in favor of tightening it, since this pass's own re-verification found it IS independently exploitable (as an information leak), contradicting the "not exploitable" framing.
2. `redeem_company_invite()`'s gating `select ... for update` is now additionally filtered by `and company_id = v_invite.company_id`, matching its neighbouring `update` - defense-in-depth per this schema's own established convention (0043/0050/0034/0097/0137), so even a `company_invites` row that somehow predates fix #1, or any future write path that isn't this RPC, can't resurrect the oracle: a cross-company `linked_person_id` now reads as "no such row" (no exception, normal success) on BOTH the read and the write, consistently.

**Verified red-then-green, both layers independently.** Re-ran the same two-invite scenario against fix #1 alone: invite CREATION itself is now rejected outright (`ERROR: company_invites: linked_person_id must be a person in the same company`) before a cross-company invite can even exist - the strongest possible verification that the root cause is closed. To verify fix #2 on its own merits (in case a row ever exists despite fix #1 - simulated by inserting a cross-company `company_invites` row DIRECTLY, bypassing the RPC's own new check entirely, standing in for a pre-existing/legacy row or a different write path), redeemed it against the fixed `redeem_company_invite()`: no exception, clean success, Victim D's real `people` row confirmed unchanged - the oracle is closed even when the root-cause fix is bypassed.

**Added permanent regression coverage.** `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py`'s `[19]` section (`part2_team_billing_rpcs`) gained two new checks: Company A's owner can't name Company B's person as `linked_person_id` on an invite into Company A's own company (via `create_company_invite_checked()`), and a directly-inserted cross-company invite (bypassing that RPC check, simulating a pre-existing row) doesn't leak the target person's real linked-status when redeemed, with the target's `people` row confirmed still unchanged afterward. **Red:** re-ran the suite against the unmodified pre-`0138` migrations (a scratch copy of `app/supabase/migrations/` with `0138` removed, replayed fresh) - `2 FAILED`, both the two new checks, exactly as expected. **Green:** same suite against the real `0138`-included schema - `ALL PASSED`, including every pre-existing check in sections `[1]`-`[19]` (no regression on the unrelated seat-cap/last-owner/pack-quota/one-company-per-user coverage `[19]` already had, or anywhere else in the suite).

**Escalated to a PR, not pushed directly.** This fix replaces two existing `SECURITY DEFINER` functions via `create or replace function` in a new migration - schema surface, one of this track's own explicitly excluded categories for a direct push (`no RLS/money/schema/worker-image`). Opened as PR #200 (`fix/invite-linked-person-cross-tenant-oracle` -> `main`) per this pass's own binding methodology; not merged, per the standing guardrails.

**Backlog status.** No existing backlog item touched - `create_company_invite_checked()`/`redeem_company_invite()` do not appear on any of the (now 26, prior to this pass's own new PR) open PRs' own branches beyond PR #199's own read-only reference to the same Finding-236 write-up (confirmed via `git log --all -- app/supabase/migrations/0113_create_invite_seat_check_race.sql app/supabase/migrations/0122_redeem_invite_linked_person_race.sql`, restricted to this repo's own branch refs - PR #199 itself does not touch either file). `git fetch origin main` immediately before this pass started and again immediately before pushing the branch/opening the PR, both clean at `0736db2` - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: `engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` with `TENANT_PSQL` pointed at a scratch database built via `engine/security/replay_schema.sh` (including `0138`) - section `[19]`'s two new Finding-237 checks should `PASS`; removing `0138` from the migrations directory before replaying and re-running should make the same two checks `FAIL`. Manually: as a real `authenticated` Company-A owner, `select create_company_invite_checked('<A>', 'x@example.test', 'employee', '<a real people.id belonging to a DIFFERENT company>')` - expect `ERROR: company_invites: linked_person_id must be a person in the same company`.

### Finding 238 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class - a market-intelligence widget's B-BBEE level breakdown had no minimum-sample gate of its own, unlike its two sibling figures in the exact same function)

**Area:** `app/lib/marketTrendLogic.ts`'s `gateMarketTrend()` (the pure honesty-gate logic for migration `0062`'s `market_trend_for_tags()`), rendered by `app/app/tenders/[id]/market-context.tsx`'s `MarketTrendBlock`.

**How this was found.** Fresh-angle pass per this pass's own task brief (frontend/UI correctness, not security/timezone - both already exhausted this segment). Browsed for a calculation shown to the user that could be wrong on an edge case, settled on the market-trend widget (a "historical reference" box on the Tender Workspace showing a discipline's comparable past awards: headline count, price-vs-estimate %, typical bidder count, and a B-BBEE winning-level breakdown) and read `gateMarketTrend()` end to end against its own test file. The function's own doc comment and its existing test suite (`marketTrendLogic.test.ts`) already document and test an explicit design rule, applied twice: the headline award count (`n`) clearing `MARKET_TREND_MIN_SAMPLE` (5) is not enough on its own to show `pctOfEstimate` or `bidderCount` - each is gated AGAIN on its own, often-thinner sub-sample (`pct_of_estimate_n`/`bidder_count_n`), because migration `0062`'s own `pct_rows`/`bidder_rows` CTEs filter out rows with no stated estimate / no recorded bidder count, so a tender with a comfortably-sized `n` can still have almost none of that `n` carrying real data for either figure. The file's own header comment records that the `bidder_count_n` gate was itself a 2026-11-04 fix for exactly this - the caller "wasn't applying the gate to it" originally. The THIRD figure the same function returns, `bbbeeLevelCounts` (built from `0062`'s own `bbbee_rows` CTE, filtered identically: `where winner_bbbee_points is not null`), had no such gate at all - it was passed through unconditionally (`row.bbbee_level_counts ?? {}`), and the SQL function returns no `bbbee_level_n` column to even check against. The sole caller, `market-context.tsx`, only guarded rendering on `bbbeeTotal > 0` (computed by summing the level counts itself at render time) - never on `bbbeeTotal >= MIN_SAMPLE`. The existing test for this field (`"B-BBEE level distribution is passed through as-is, defaulting to empty rather than invented"`) only ever exercised `n` at exactly the default `row()` fixture's `bbbee_level_counts` (which happens to sum to 5, i.e. already at the minimum) - no test exercised `n` comfortably above minimum with a THIN `bbbee_level_counts`, the exact shape the two sibling tests (`"...bidder-count sample does not..."`, `"...pct-of-estimate sample does not..."`) already cover for the other two fields.

**Reproduced against the real, unmodified function - not reasoned about.** `node --experimental-strip-types` against the actual `gateMarketTrend()` (no reimplementation), with a row shaped like a realistic comparable-awards query: `n: 30` (well above `MARKET_TREND_MIN_SAMPLE`), `pct_of_estimate_n: 0`, `bidder_count_n: 0`, `bbbee_level_counts: { "2": 1 }` (only 1 of the 30 awards has a recorded winning B-BBEE level - the realistic case, since most comparable awards won't). Pre-fix result: `trend.bbbeeLevelCounts` = `{"2": 1}` unchanged, which `market-context.tsx`'s `bbbeeTotal > 0` check would render verbatim as "Winning B-BBEE level, 1 award: 2 (1)." directly underneath "Based on 30 comparable past awards tagged ..." - a reader has no reason to assume the B-BBEE line is drawn from a 1-award sample rather than the 30 the headline just stated, since `pctOfEstimate` and `bidderCount` on the SAME line already demonstrate (by their absence, correctly, when their own `_n` is below 5) that this function suppresses figures it can't back with enough data - the B-BBEE line's continued presence at `n=1` reads as "this one DOES have enough data," which is false.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Low/moderate - a UI content-correctness bug on an explicitly-labelled "historical reference only... not a prediction" box, not a security or money-handling defect, and the sample size IS disclosed in the rendered text itself (`"1 award:"`) rather than hidden outright, so a careful reader isn't actively deceived - but the design intent, stated in this exact function's own doc comment and enforced for its two sibling figures, is "below [MIN_SAMPLE], the caller shows nothing rather than a trend built on too few comparable awards," and this third figure was the one place that rule wasn't applied, which could make a company's own sector-level B-BBEE competitiveness look more/less common than it really is based on a single outlier award.

**Fix.** `app/lib/marketTrendLogic.ts`: `gateMarketTrend()` now sums `bbbee_level_counts`' own values and applies the same `>= minSample` gate the other two fields already use, returning `{}` (not the thin breakdown) when the sum is below the threshold - computed in TS since `market_trend_for_tags()` returns no separate `bbbee_level_n` column for it (unlike `pct_of_estimate_n`/`bidder_count_n`), using the exact sum `market-context.tsx` was already computing at render time, just applied before the gate rather than only for the label after it. `market-context.tsx` itself needed no change: its existing `bbbeeTotal > 0` check now only ever sees `{}` (total 0) or an already-gated breakdown (total >= 5).

**Verified red-then-green.** Red: the repro script above, run against the pre-fix function - `bbbeeLevelCounts` returned `{"2":1}` (bug confirmed, script exits 1). Green: identical script re-run after the fix - `bbbeeLevelCounts` returns `{}` (script exits 0, "already gated"). `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/marketTrendLogic.test.ts`: 14/14 pass (12 pre-existing, unmodified in behaviour and still passing, plus 2 new - a too-thin-B-BBEE-sample case mirroring the existing bidder-count/pct-of-estimate sibling tests, and an at-exactly-minimum case confirming the breakdown still shows once its own sum clears 5). `npx eslint app/lib/marketTrendLogic.ts app/lib/marketTrendLogic.test.ts`: clean. `npx tsc --noEmit` on the project: no new errors attributable to this file. `npx vitest run app/lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` (the one other file importing `gateMarketTrend`, via `loadMarketTrend()`): 18/18 pass, unaffected (it never asserts on `bbbeeLevelCounts` directly, and the type returned is unchanged - still `Record<string, number>`, just empty more often on a too-thin sample).

**Pushed directly to `main`, not a PR.** Pure TypeScript logic in a single already-unit-tested pure function plus its own test file - no RLS, no money, no schema/migration, no worker image; squarely the "small/safe" direct-push category this pass's own binding methodology sets out, unlike Findings 236/237 (both required a new migration/`SECURITY DEFINER` change and went to a PR instead).

**Backlog status.** No existing backlog item touched - `marketTrendLogic.ts`/`market-context.tsx` do not appear on any of the 27 open backlog PRs' own branches (confirmed via `git log --all -- app/lib/marketTrendLogic.ts app/app/tenders/[id]/market-context.tsx`, restricted to this repo's own branch refs). `git fetch origin main` immediately before this pass started and again immediately before pushing, both clean at `a6cf502` - no sibling commit landed in between.

To verify independently: `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/marketTrendLogic.test.ts` from `app/` - all pass. Manually: call `gateMarketTrend({ n: 30, date_from: null, date_to: null, pct_of_estimate_n: 0, pct_of_estimate_median: null, bidder_count_n: 0, bidder_count_median: null, bbbee_level_counts: { "2": 1 } })` - `bbbeeLevelCounts` should be `{}`, not `{"2":1}`.

### Finding 239 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class - the SAME shape as Finding 238, one layer up: `/market-intelligence` and `/analytics` rendered `benchmark()`'s five sibling per-field statistics gated only on the headline sample, not each field's own)

**Area:** `app/lib/marketPricing.ts`'s `benchmark()` (the pure award-statistics aggregator built on `public_tender_outcomes`, 0053), rendered by `app/app/market-intelligence/page.tsx` (market-wide view, every buyer) and `app/app/analytics/page.tsx` ("Your own benchmark" section, this company's own matched tenders only).

**How this was found.** Continuing this pass's own task brief's option (a): the same "a SQL-fed function's filtered sub-samples need their own gate, not just the headline count" shape that produced Finding 238 (`marketTrendLogic.ts`'s `gateMarketTrend()`), in a part of the codebase not yet checked. `benchmark()` is the market-pricing module's own sibling to `gateMarketTrend()` - same honesty-rule header comment ("every aggregate carries its own sample size, and below MIN_SAMPLE it is not shown at all"), same shape (one function, several independently-filtered sub-samples: `bidders` from rows with `priced_bidder_count >= 2`, `lowestWon` from rows with `lowest_bid_won !== null`, `winnerVsMedian` from rows with a recorded `winner_vs_median`, `contractSize` from single-winner awarded rows with a priced amount, `winners` from the same single-winner set) - each returning its OWN `n`, separate from the headline `n: rows.length`. Grepped every caller of `benchmark()` (`app/app/market-intelligence/page.tsx`, `app/app/analytics/page.tsx`, `app/app/discovery/page.tsx`, `app/app/pipeline/pricing/market-comparison.tsx` - the last doesn't call `benchmark()` at all, it works per-row). `discovery/page.tsx` does this correctly already (`if (b.contractSize.n >= MIN_SAMPLE) pricingByKey.set(...)` before ever reading `contractSize.p25/median/p75` later) and so does `market-context.tsx`'s own `MetricRow` (passes each field's own `n` into `sampleStrength()` and shows "too few to say (k)" below `MIN_SAMPLE`, per field) - both already correct, and left untouched. `/market-intelligence` and `/analytics` were not: both check only the headline `overall.n >= MIN_SAMPLE` / `ownBenchmark.n >= MIN_SAMPLE` before rendering anything, then display each of `contractSize.median`, `bidders.median`/`p25`/`p75`, `lowestWon`'s won/n percentage, and `winnerVsMedian.median` gated only on that field's own truthiness (`median ? ... : "-"`) or `n > 0` - never on `n >= MIN_SAMPLE`. `/market-intelligence`'s own module comment even claims "every breakdown's `n` is real and MIN_SAMPLE-gated the same way /analytics' own benchmark section is" - true of the `byCategory`/`byBuyer`/`byProvince` breakdowns (correctly `.filter((b) => b.n >= MIN_SAMPLE)`), false of `benchmark()`'s own five fields, which the same page (and `/analytics`) render unconditionally once the much bigger headline `n` alone clears the bar.

**Reproduced against the real, unmodified function - not reasoned about.** `npx vitest run lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` (new test, run against the pre-fix codebase first): 5 rows - `{winner_count:1, winner_amount_zar:1_000_000}` plus four `{winner_count:3}` batch-award rows with no priced bidder count, no `lowest_bid_won`, no `winner_vs_median` - fed to the real `benchmark()`. Result: `b.n = 5` (clears `MIN_SAMPLE`, so both pages' own headline gate passes and renders the section) while `b.contractSize.n = 1`, `b.bidders.n = 0`, `b.lowestWon.n = 0`, `b.winnerVsMedian.n = 0` - every one of the five sibling fields is actually far thinner than the headline that gates whether anything is shown. Confirmed `fieldReliable` did not exist before the fix (`TypeError: fieldReliable is not a function` - both new test cases red) and passes after (`20/20`, including the 18 pre-existing, unmodified-in-behaviour tests).

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Low/moderate, same bracket as Finding 238 and for the same reason: an explicitly-labelled, purely-informational market-intelligence feature ("never guessed, never used to set or suggest your own price" - both pages' own footer text), not a security or money-movement defect, and the real `n` for each field IS available in the rendered caption text in most spots (e.g. "of {n} awards..."), so a careful reader isn't actively deceived about sample size where that caption exists. But two pages, not one, were showing a "Median contract size" (in Rand) or a "Lowest bid won" percentage that could be built on a single data point the moment the page's own much-larger headline count cleared 5 - the exact pattern Finding 238 fixed one function over, now shown to recur across this module's OTHER consumer pages, while the THIRD page using the same `Benchmark` type (`market-context.tsx`) and a FOURTH (`discovery/page.tsx`) already had it right. This is the kind of drift this standing review exists to catch: the correct pattern existed in the same codebase, just not applied everywhere it needed to be.

**Fix.** `app/lib/marketPricing.ts`: added `fieldReliable(n, minSample = MIN_SAMPLE): boolean` - a one-line, exported, documented, unit-tested pure predicate (`n >= minSample`), so every caller states the SAME rule explicitly instead of each re-deriving (or, as found here, omitting) it per page. `app/app/market-intelligence/page.tsx`: gated `overall.contractSize.median`, `overall.lowestWon` (both occurrences), `overall.winnerVsMedian.median`, `overall.bidders.median`/`p25`/`p75`, and `BreakdownTable`'s per-row `contractSize.median`/`lowestWon` on `fieldReliable(field.n)` instead of truthiness/`> 0`. `app/app/analytics/page.tsx`: same fix on `ownBenchmark.lowestWon`, `.bidders.median`, `.contractSize.median`. `market-context.tsx`, `discovery/page.tsx` and `market-comparison.tsx` needed no change - confirmed already correct (the first two already apply the equivalent per-field gate by hand; the third never calls `benchmark()`).

**Verified red-then-green.** Red: new tests in `app/lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` against `fieldReliable` (not yet existing) - `TypeError: (0 , fieldReliable) is not a function`, 2/2 new tests failing, 18/18 pre-existing still passing. Green: after adding `fieldReliable()` - `npx vitest run lib/marketPricing.spec.ts`: 20/20 pass. Full suite: `npx vitest run` from `app/`: 72 files, 566/566 pass (no regression anywhere else in the module graph). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: clean, no new errors. `npx eslint app/market-intelligence/page.tsx app/analytics/page.tsx lib/marketPricing.ts lib/marketPricing.spec.ts`: clean (one pre-existing, unrelated unused-import warning on `analytics/page.tsx`'s `STAGE_META`, not touched by or caused by this fix).

**Backlog status.** `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting this finding's work and again immediately before pushing, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between. Checked PR #164 specifically (the one open backlog item whose own diff touches `app/app/analytics/page.tsx`, for its unrelated Capacity-Unlocked/savings-counter rework): read its full diff - it only touches that file's imports and the top-of-function `Promise.all`/`savingsSummary` wiring (lines ~9-70), nowhere near the "Your own benchmark" `dl` block (lines ~301-306) this fix touches - no line-range overlap, no collision. `git log --all` for `app/app/market-intelligence/page.tsx` and `app/lib/marketPricing.ts` shows no open-PR-branch commits touching either file at all (every hit is already-merged `main` history). Pushed directly, same "small/safe" bracket and reasoning as Finding 238: pure TypeScript + two page-level display-gating edits, no RLS, no schema/migration, no worker image, and the module's own repeated header comment is explicit that these are informational display figures never used to set or suggest a price - not a money-handling code path.

To verify independently, from `app/`: `npx vitest run lib/marketPricing.spec.ts` - 20/20 pass, including the two new tests under `describe("fieldReliable / benchmark's per-field sample gate (Finding 239)")`. Manually: call `benchmark()` with 5 `OutcomeStats` rows where only one has `winner_count: 1` + a priced `winner_amount_zar` and the other four have `winner_count: 3` with no priced bidder count / `lowest_bid_won` / `winner_vs_median` - `b.n` is 5 (clears `MIN_SAMPLE`) while `b.contractSize.n`/`b.bidders.n`/`b.lowestWon.n`/`b.winnerVsMedian.n` are all below it; `/market-intelligence` and `/analytics` now show "-" for each of those fields rather than a figure built on 0-1 data points.

### Finding 240 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class - the dashboard's own "setup checklist" called a company's SARS Tax Compliance PIN "not on file" whenever only its expiry date hadn't been captured yet, disagreeing with the Company vault page reading the SAME row)

**Area:** `app/app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s empty-state "Get set up to bid" setup checklist (`SetupChecklistCard`), specifically its `tax_pin` item; cross-checked against `app/app/company/_components/ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` and `ReadOnlyView.tsx` (the Company vault's own two renderers of the same `companies.sars_tcs_pin*` columns).

**How this was found.** Fresh angle per this pass's own task brief (frontend/UI correctness, not security - the "SQL-fed function, multiple filtered sub-samples" angle that produced Findings 238/239 was swept first and is now exhausted: only two migrations in the whole schema use a `count(*) filter`/multi-CTE shape at all, `0062_market_trend_by_tags.sql` (already fixed, Finding 238) and `0101_telemetry_and_billing.sql`'s `platform_admin_engine_telemetry()` - the latter is an internal, admin-only ops page with no established honesty rule for this shape and already handles a zero-sample average gracefully (`"no completions in the last 7 days"` for `avg_latency_seconds === null`), so not a fresh instance of the bug class; documented as a genuine negative). Looked for a "different completion-percentage/on-file calculation" not yet reviewed, per the brief's own example. `app/components/tt/setup-checklist-card.tsx` had zero prior mentions in either standing doc; its own comment says every item is "composed entirely from already-computed readiness/document-expiry signals (no new completion logic)" - read the dashboard page's own derivation of each of its 6 items against that claim. Five hold up. The `tax_pin` item does not: `const taxRow = documentExpiryRows.find((r) => r.label === "SARS Tax Compliance PIN"); ... done: !!taxRow && taxRow.status !== "missing"`. `documentExpiryRows` comes from `lib/documentExpiry.ts`'s `loadDocumentExpiryOverview()`, whose own `statusFor()` is `daysLeft === null ? "missing" : ...` - i.e. `"missing"` means "no expiry DATE on file", a question answered purely from `sars_tcs_pin_expiry`, never from `sars_tcs_pin_document_path` or `sars_tcs_pin` (the PIN text itself). The checklist item's own label is "Tax clearance (SARS TCS PIN) **on file**" and the surrounding comment claims this reuses the scan "only 'on file or not'" - but what it actually reuses answers a different question ("has a date been captured"), not "is there a PIN/document here at all". The established, correct "on file" rule for this exact field already exists elsewhere in this app, verbatim, in TWO other call sites - `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` and `ReadOnlyView.tsx`, both via `lib/dates.ts`'s `documentStatus(hasFile, dateStr)`: `hasFile = company.sars_tcs_pin_document_path !== null || !!company.sars_tcs_pin || !!company.sars_tcs_pin_expiry` - the SAME three-way "document, or PIN text, or date" rule `documentStatus()` was fixed to need on 2026-10-29 (a file genuinely on file must never read "Not on file" just because its expiry date hasn't been captured/extracted yet). The dashboard's `tax_pin` item independently re-derived a narrower, wrong version of that exact rule instead of reusing it.

**Reproduced against the real, unmodified functions - not reasoned about.** `npx vitest run` (scratch spec, deleted after use) against the real `statusFor`/`daysUntil` (`lib/documentExpiry.ts`/`lib/dates.ts`) and the real `documentStatus()`: for a company that has entered its SARS TCS PIN (or uploaded the letter) but not yet captured an expiry date (`sars_tcs_pin_expiry: null`), `statusFor(daysUntil(null))` returns `"missing"`, so the dashboard's own boolean (`taxRow.status !== "missing"`) evaluates to `false` - checklist shows the item as NOT done, with a "Fix" link. The SAME company, read through `documentStatus(true, null)` (the Company vault's own established rule for this exact ambiguity), returns `{ label: "Needs date verification", tone: "warning" }` - explicitly NOT "Not on file". The dashboard and the vault page disagree about the same company row, in the direction the 2026-10-29 fix exists specifically to prevent.

**Impact, honestly scoped.** Low/moderate - cosmetic/informational (a checklist nudge, not a gate on bidding or compliance scoring), but it's exactly the kind of "the product tells you two different things about the same fact in two different places" bug that erodes trust in the Home cockpit's "get set up" nudges: a company that has genuinely entered its SARS TCS PIN sees a persistent "Fix" link telling them to go re-do something they already did, right after the Company vault page told them (correctly) that it's on file and just needs a date.

**Fix.** Centralised the correct three-way rule as a new exported, documented, unit-tested pure function, `sarsTcsPinOnFile()`, in `app/lib/vaultDocuments.ts` (the file that already owns this field's other per-kind rules, e.g. `vaultDocumentMismatchWarning`). `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` and `ReadOnlyView.tsx` now call it instead of each carrying their own identical inline copy of the same three-clause expression (de-duplication, not a behaviour change there - same boolean result as before). `app/app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s `tax_pin` item now computes `taxPinOnFile = !companyError && !!companyRow && sarsTcsPinOnFile(companyRow)` instead of reading `documentExpiry.ts`'s date-only `status`; the page's existing `companies` query was widened by 3 columns (`sars_tcs_pin`, `sars_tcs_pin_document_path`, `sars_tcs_pin_expiry` - no new round trip) to have the data this needs. The now-unused `taxRow`/`documentExpiryRows.find(...)` lookup for this item was removed; `documentExpiryRows` itself is still used for every other dashboard widget that genuinely wants the date-based `status` (Vault & Compliance Health, Team & CV Bench) - this fix narrows ONE item's own derivation, not that shared data load.

**Verified red-then-green.** Red: added `sarsTcsPinOnFile` to the import list of `app/lib/vaultDocuments.test.ts` before the function existed in `vaultDocuments.ts` (confirmed by stashing the `.ts` change and re-running) - `SyntaxError: The requested module './vaultDocuments.ts' does not provide an export named 'sarsTcsPinOnFile'`, test file fails to even load. Green: with the function restored, `node --experimental-strip-types --test app/lib/vaultDocuments.test.ts`: 12/12 pass, including 4 new cases (nothing on file -> false; document path alone -> true; PIN text alone with no document/date -> true, the exact real-world shape this bug mishandled; expiry date alone -> true). Full suite: `npx vitest run` from `app/`: 72 files, 566/566 pass (one pre-existing, unrelated time-boundary flake in `lib/billing.spec.ts`'s `trialDaysLeft` test reproduced identically on a clean `git stash` of this fix, in isolation, both before and after - confirmed NOT caused by this change). `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `npx eslint app/app/dashboard/page.tsx app/app/company/_components/ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx app/app/company/_components/ReadOnlyView.tsx app/lib/vaultDocuments.ts app/lib/vaultDocuments.test.ts`: clean.

**Backlog status.** `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting this finding's work and again immediately before pushing, both clean at `00fc6e4` - no sibling commit landed in between. Full, proper collision check per this pass's own task brief (not a diff-summary skim): `git diff --name-only <merge-base> <branch>` for all 27 open backlog PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#176`-`#200`) against each of this fix's 5 touched files, using each PR's own real merge-base with `main` (not `main` itself, which falsely flags every file an old, un-rebased branch merely drifted away from as "touched" - the exact trap this track's own prior pass, `lxxvii`, was corrected for on a diff-summary skim). Only one PR's REAL diff (base..branch) touches any of the 5 files at all: `#164`, on `app/app/dashboard/page.tsx` only (adds `fetchCompanySubscription`/`PLAN_MONTHLY_ZAR` imports, a `subscription` Promise.all member, and changes the pre-existing `savings_baseline` item's `href`). Simulated the real merge, not just eyeballed it: committed this fix to a disposable local branch (never pushed), `git merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/pr/164` against it, read the actual conflict markers, then `git merge --abort` and deleted the scratch branch/worktree. Result: this fix's own new/changed lines - the `tax_pin` item's `taxPinOnFile` computation (lines ~348-359) and the widened `companies` select (lines ~196-201) - merged with ZERO conflict markers; PR #164 never touches either. The merge DID conflict on two pre-existing, independent regions neither caused nor touched by this fix: the shared `Promise.all` destructuring line (PR #164's branch predates the `companyError`/`documentExpiryError`/`peopleRowsError` members Findings 164/165 already added to it - a staleness collision that exists regardless of this fix, since PR #164 was never rebased after either of those landed) and the pre-existing `savings_baseline` item's `href`/`companyError`-guard (PR #164 changes `href` to `/company?edit=1#savings-baseline`; unrelated to the `tax_pin` item three entries above it, never touched by this fix). Both are the SAME already-documented PR #164 staleness this track's own prior pass flagged on a different file (`analytics/page.tsx`, Finding 239) - not a new collision this fix introduces, and not something to resolve here per this track's standing guardrail (read-only reference only, Sarel's own call when he merges). Pushed directly to `main`: pure TypeScript/TSX logic + a 3-column widen of an already-RLS-scoped `companies` select on the signed-in user's own row - no RLS change, no money, no schema/migration, no worker image.

To verify independently, from `app/`: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/vaultDocuments.test.ts` - 12/12 pass, including the 4 new `sarsTcsPinOnFile` cases. Manually: a company with `sars_tcs_pin: "1234567"`, `sars_tcs_pin_document_path: null`, `sars_tcs_pin_expiry: null` reads as `done: true` on the dashboard's setup checklist (was `false`) and as `{ label: "Needs date verification", tone: "warning" }` (unchanged) on the Company vault page - the two now agree.

### Finding 241 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class, same shape as Finding 240 one layer up - the bid-readiness SCORE's own `tax_compliance`/`bee`/`cidb` criteria called the same three vault documents "missing" whenever only the document was uploaded and the matching text/level/grading field hadn't also been typed in, disagreeing with the Company vault page's own, already-correct rule for the SAME three columns, rendered on the SAME page)

**Area:** `app/lib/readiness.ts`'s `computeBidReadiness()` (the one pure scoring function behind `BidReadinessCard`, used by the dashboard, the Company page header, the discovery page's "Company profile X% ready" chip, and `/admin/customers`) - specifically its `tax_compliance`, `bee` and `cidb` criteria; cross-checked against `app/app/company/_components/ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` (the Company vault's own renderer of the exact same `companies.sars_tcs_pin*`/`bee_proof*`/`cidb*` columns, rendered on the same page as `BidReadinessCard` itself) and `lib/vaultDocuments.ts`'s `sarsTcsPinOnFile()` (Finding 240's own new centralised function, this same pass's immediately preceding finding).

**How this was found.** Continued option (a) from this pass's own task brief - having fixed the dashboard checklist's `tax_pin` item (Finding 240), checked the checklist's other items against readiness.ts, the thing they read from, per the brief's own "check each item against the canonical source of truth" instruction. `company_basics`/`csd`/`bee` on the dashboard just read `readiness.criteria` directly (no independent re-derivation - trivially consistent, nothing to fix there). But reading `readiness.ts` itself end to end to confirm that, its own `tax_compliance`/`bee`/`cidb` criteria turned out to be a FOURTH independently-derived instance of the exact "is this document on file" fact Finding 240 just fixed three call sites for: `const hasPin = presence(input.taxPin)` - text only, never `input.taxPinDocumentPath` (which didn't even exist as a field on `ReadinessInput`) - and `lib/companyReadinessData.ts`'s `fetchCompanyReadiness()`/`app/app/company/page.tsx`'s own inline `computeBidReadiness()` call both fed it `taxPin: company.sars_tcs_pin` alone, the same narrow rule Finding 240 just fixed for the dashboard checklist. The exact same gap existed for `bee` (`hasLevel = input.beeLevel !== null`, ignoring `bee_proof_document_path`) and `cidb` (`hasGrading = presence(input.cidbGrading)`, ignoring `cidb_document_path`) - both of which DO already have an established three-way (cidb) or two-way (bee) document-aware rule inline in `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`/`ReadOnlyView.tsx` (`cidb_document_path !== null || !!cidb_grading || !!cidb_expiry`; `bee_proof_document_path !== null || !!bee_level`) that readiness.ts never reused.

**Why this one is worse than Finding 240, not just a repeat of it.** Finding 240 was a secondary checklist nudge. This is the headline READINESS PERCENT and "blockers" list itself - and on `app/app/company/page.tsx` specifically, `BidReadinessCard` (showing this score, with these criteria in its blockers) renders directly above `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` (showing the correct, document-aware status for the SAME three columns) on the exact same page render - the clearest possible version of "the product tells you two different things about the same fact in two different places," not even requiring the user to navigate between pages to notice.

### Finding 243 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, UI content-correctness class, same shape as Findings 240/241/242 - a 4th independently-derived instance in the SAME `computeBidReadiness()` function this session already patched twice - the bid-readiness score's `bank_confirmation` criterion called a genuinely-uploaded bank confirmation letter "missing" whenever only the letter's date hadn't been typed in yet, disagreeing with the Company vault page's own, already-correct rule for the SAME column pair, rendered on the SAME page)

**Area:** `app/lib/readiness.ts`'s `computeBidReadiness()` - specifically its `bank_confirmation` criterion; cross-checked against `app/app/company/_components/ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`/`ReadOnlyView.tsx` (the Company vault's own renderer of `companies.bank_confirmation_letter_path`/`_date`/`_valid_until`) and `app/app/company/actions.ts`'s `uploadVaultDocument()` (the generic vault uploader every `VAULT_DOCUMENTS` kind, including `bank_letter`, goes through).

**How this was found.** This pass's own task brief named "sibling-function divergence" and "re-derives a business rule instead of reading the canonical computation" as productive tracks. Having read Findings 240/241/242's own write-ups (all three fixed `tax_compliance`/`bee`/`cidb` in this exact function, in this exact session), checked whether `computeBidReadiness()`'s OTHER expiry-gated criteria had the same shape. `company_basics`/`csd`/`principal`/`people_cvs`/`experience` have no document-path column to conflate with (pure presence/count checks - not applicable). `bank_confirmation` does: it is the one remaining criterion in the function still gated on a single date field alone (`bankConfirmationValidUntil`, i.e. `companies.bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until`) with no document-path OR, never touched by Findings 240-242.

**Why this is real, not hypothetical.** `bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until` is a **GENERATED column** (migration `0014`: `(bank_confirmation_letter_date + interval '3 months')::date) stored`) - it is non-null if and only if `bank_confirmation_letter_date` is non-null. Checked `uploadVaultDocument()` (`app/app/company/actions.ts`, the one Server Action every vault document kind - including `bank_letter` - uploads through): for kind `bank_letter` it writes exactly one column, `companies.bank_confirmation_letter_path = storagePath` (`VAULT_DOCUMENTS.bank_letter.column`) - it **never** writes `bank_confirmation_letter_date`. So "letter genuinely uploaded via the normal product flow, date never typed in (there is no separate date-entry field in that same upload action), `bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until` still null" is the real, reachable state produced by the app's own generic uploader on every single upload of this document kind unless a user separately edits the date field elsewhere - not a contrived edge case. `app/app/company/_components/ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` (line ~129) already has the correct rule for exactly this state: `documentStatus(company.bank_confirmation_letter_path !== null || !!company.bank_confirmation_letter_date, company.bank_confirmation_letter_valid_until, BANK_LETTER_RENEW_SOON_DAYS)` - and `documentStatus()` (`lib/dates.ts`) returns `"Needs date verification"` (a warning, not "Not on file") when `hasFile` is true and the date is null. `readiness.ts`'s pre-fix `bank_confirmation` criterion read none of that - only `bankConfirmationValidUntil` - so it showed the SAME row as a flat "missing" (weight-5) blocker on `BidReadinessCard`, rendered directly above `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx` on `app/app/company/page.tsx`, disagreeing with the correct status two inches below it, the same "two different answers to the same fact on the same page" shape Finding 241 called out for tax_compliance/bee/cidb.

**Reproduced against the real, unmodified function.** New `readiness.spec.ts` cases (kept through the stash below) against the real `computeBidReadiness()`: `{ ...EMPTY, bankConfirmationLetterPath: "co/vault/bank_letter/fnb.pdf" }` (no date, no valid_until - the exact real-upload shape above) → pre-fix `bank_confirmation` criterion: `{ satisfied: false, reason: "missing" }`; `{ ...EMPTY, bankConfirmationLetterDate: <10 days ago> }` (date typed, valid_until not pre-computed in this input shape) → same pre-fix result. `git stash push -- app/lib/readiness.ts` (keeping the 5 new test cases), `npx vitest run lib/readiness.spec.ts` from `app/`: 2 of 15 cases fail against the pre-fix logic (both document/date-alone cases), 13 pre-existing pass. `git stash pop`, same command: 15/15 pass.

**Fix.** Added two new, deliberately *optional* `ReadinessInput` fields - `bankConfirmationLetterPath`/`bankConfirmationLetterDate` - mirroring the Finding 241 pattern exactly (default to behaving exactly as before when omitted by a caller). Unlike tax_compliance/bee/cidb's `hasX`, which had no pre-existing "presence" signal of its own, `bank_confirmation`'s new `hasBankLetter` is `!!input.bankConfirmationValidUntil || !!input.bankConfirmationLetterPath || !!input.bankConfirmationLetterDate` - deliberately including the OLD field in the OR, not just the two new ones, so a caller that hasn't been updated to supply the new fields (every caller, until this same fix updates two of them) sees `hasBankLetter` driven by `bankConfirmationValidUntil` alone exactly as before, with zero behavior change. `satisfied = hasBankLetter && (expiry.current || input.bankConfirmationValidUntil === null)` - same shape as tax_compliance/bee/cidb's own satisfied expression. `lib/companyReadinessData.ts` (`fetchCompanyReadiness()`, feeding the dashboard, Company vault header and discovery page's readiness chip) had its `companies` select widened by the 2 new columns and now passes them through. `app/app/company/page.tsx`'s own inline `computeBidReadiness()` call now passes `bank_confirmation_letter_path`/`_date` - both already present in that file's own `row` select (for `ComplianceDocumentsSection.tsx`'s own rendering), so no new select was needed there, same as Finding 241's equivalent fix. **One caller deliberately left as-is, not silently inconsistent:** `lib/customerRowData.ts` (`/admin/customers`, fed by migration `0098`'s `platform_admin_company_readiness_data()` RPC) has neither new column available - that RPC would need widening, a schema change left for a future pass. Per this track's own standing guardrail against competing with an open PR's own content, this was **deliberately not bundled into PR #201** (Finding 242's own open PR, already widening this exact same RPC for the OTHER three document-path columns) - left undocumented in `customerRowData.ts` itself to avoid touching that file at all (a real `git diff`/merge-simulation collision check below confirms PR #201 does modify `customerRowData.ts`, just not `readiness.ts`'s `bank_confirmation` block); flagged here instead as a second, separate open item for whoever next widens that RPC (ideally the same pass, so it isn't a 3rd migration to the same function).

### Finding 244 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - the CV-review page's own "this project is probably already on file" heuristic, `looksLikeExistingProject()`, false-matched two genuinely unrelated projects whenever the EXISTING project's own text happened to contain the NEW project's contract number as a coincidental substring produced by squashing two adjacent, unrelated tokens together - a different root cause from the bare-year false positive an earlier pass already fixed in this exact function)

**Area:** `app/lib/cvExtraction.ts` (`looksLikeExistingProject()`, new private `projectNumberTokens()` helper). Test coverage added to the existing `app/lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` (1 new case, 6 total).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on CV. A broad sweep of the TypeScript-side CV surfaces (`cv-compare.tsx`, `cv-led-add-person.tsx`/`createPersonWithCv()`, `bulk-cv-upload.tsx`/`bulkUploadCvs()`, `standardCvQueue.ts`) turned up nothing new - each either already has a documented, DB-trigger-backed defense (0043's `tt_check_same_company()` cross-tenant trigger closes the one real-looking gap in `bulkUploadCvs()`'s unvalidated `person_id_<i>`, at the database level, for every writer including the service role) or is already extensively analyzed and intentionally scoped in its own docstring (`queueStandardCvs()`'s own TOCTOU caveat). Moved to `lib/cvExtraction.ts`'s `looksLikeExistingProject()` next - a pure, already-once-fixed function (a 2026-11-06 standing-review pass's own comment and spec file are right there: a bare shared year like "2024" used to false-match two unrelated projects). Rather than re-litigate that already-closed bare-year case, read the CURRENT implementation adversarially for a different root cause the earlier fix didn't touch: the final comparison, `ex.includes(n)`, checks whether a proposed number token is a SUBSTRING of the ENTIRE squashed existing line - and `squash()` strips every separator, including the ones BETWEEN unrelated tokens, so two adjacent tokens in the existing text can concatenate into a longer digit run that coincidentally contains an unrelated proposed number.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Ran the real, unmodified `looksLikeExistingProject()`: `existing = ["SANRAL N1-234/2019 Upgrade of N1 Western Bypass"]`, `proposed = "Joburg Water Contract 1234 Reservoir Upgrade"` - two projects with nothing in common (different client, different scope, different real contract number). Squashing the existing line turns `"N1-234/2019"` into `"n12342019"` - the "N1" and "234" tokens run together with no boundary, and that string happens to contain the literal substring `"1234"`, the proposed project's own, completely unrelated, contract number. Pre-fix: `looksLikeExistingProject(proposed, existing)` returned `true`. Per the function's own header comment and the existing `cvExtraction.spec.ts`'s own framing (restated, not invented here): "its own header comment says this must 'never hide' a genuinely new project - a false positive here is a silent-data-loss risk, not a cosmetic nuisance" - this reproduces exactly that risk: the CV-review page (`cv-review.tsx`) would start this genuinely new project's own "Add this project" checkbox UNTICKED, and a reviewer who trusts the flag rather than comparing the two projects by hand would never add it.

**Fix.** Extracted the number-token extraction (split, digit-presence + 4-char-minimum filter, squash, bare-year exclusion) into a small private `projectNumberTokens()` helper, applied identically to BOTH sides of the comparison - the proposed line (as before) and now, newly, each EXISTING line too - and changed the check from "is the proposed number a substring anywhere in the existing line's fully-squashed text" to "does the proposed number EXACTLY match one of the existing line's own extracted number tokens." This keeps each token's own boundaries intact on both sides, so two tokens that were never adjacent in the real text can no longer accidentally concatenate into a false match, while every already-covered case (an identical whole line, a real shared contract number that happens to embed a year, a genuine non-year 4+ digit number, the bare-year exclusion) is unaffected - each of those relies on an exact token match or a whole-line match, never on the substring-across-concatenation behavior being removed.

**Verified red-then-green.** Added one new case to the existing `cvExtraction.spec.ts` (same file as the 2026-11-06 fix, same style) reproducing the concatenation false-positive above. **Red:** saved the diff to `lib/cvExtraction.ts` only, `git apply -R`, re-ran `npx vitest run lib/cvExtraction.spec.ts` - `1 failed | 5 passed`, exactly the new case (`expected true to be false`), confirming the other 5 pre-existing cases (including the already-fixed bare-year one) were untouched by this change and the new one genuinely reproduces live. **Green:** `git apply` to reapply, re-ran - `6/6 pass`. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (only the pre-existing, unrelated `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` module-resolution errors this session has repeatedly confirmed are an environment gap, not a regression).

**Not escalated to a PR.** Small, safe, self-contained TypeScript fix to one pure function plus its own spec file - no RLS, no migration, no money path, no worker-image change, and the only real caller (`cv-review.tsx`) uses the function's boolean result exactly as before. Pushed directly to `main`.

**Backlog status.** No new backlog items opened by this fix. `git fetch origin main` immediately before starting (clean, `main` at `a1cddfb`, matching the sibling track's own most recent docs commit) and again immediately before pushing this commit, both clean - no sibling commit landed in between.

On the CV-review page, upload a CV proposing a project whose contract number exactly matches a run of digits produced only by two adjacent, unrelated tokens elsewhere in an existing project's own text, and confirm its "Add this project" checkbox now starts TICKED (not pre-unticked as a false "probably already on file").

### Finding 245 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, data-merge-omission class, one layer up from Finding 189's shape (a single source reader missing a field) - `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s `_fold()` copied only 5 of a direct-site release's fields into its matched eTenders-portal row, silently dropping `published_date`/`opening_date`/`procurement_category` whenever the portal's own value for them was null)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s `_fold()` (called from `merge()`'s two fold paths: the ordinary "direct-site release matches an open portal row" case, and the "buyer's own site says still-open, portal has it in the Closed tab" case) - this is the exact lead the immediately preceding pass (`lxxxii`) flagged as unconfirmed and explicitly left for this one to settle with a real reproduction rather than more reasoning about plausibility.

**Settling the lead: a real reproduction, not reasoning.** The prior pass's own write-up (and this pass's own task brief, quoting it) was right about the code: `_fold()`'s field-copy loop was

```python
for f in ("briefing", "province", "tender_type", "description", "scm_reference"):
    if not hit.get(f) and r.get(f):
        hit[f] = r[f]
```

- `published_date`/`opening_date`/`procurement_category` are real, always-present keys on every release dict (`source_http.release()`'s own `base` dict defaults all three to `None`) but none of the three is in that tuple. The open question was whether this is ever actually REACHABLE - it only bites when the portal's own `date_Published`/`category` for a row is genuinely null/missing at merge time, which the prior pass had no live-portal access to confirm. Built the real fixture instead of reasoning about it further: `etenders_portal.normalize()` called on a real-shaped portal row with `"category": None, "date_Published": None` (both genuinely nullable on the live portal schema - `normalize()` just passes them through `sh.clean()`/`sh.iso_sast()`, which return `None` for `None` input, no special-casing) produces a release with `published_date`/`opening_date`/`procurement_category` all `None` - confirmed directly, not assumed:
```
portal published_date: None
portal opening_date: None
portal procurement_category: None
```
Then built the matching direct-site release with the real, unmodified `capetown_procurement.normalize_rfq()` (City of Cape Town is in `BUYER_FAMILY`, so it folds) against a real row shape (same fixture `test_transnet_capetown()` already uses, `CAPETOWN_RFQ_HTML`'s one row), which has real values for all three fields:
```
direct published_date: 2026-10-17T14:20:39+02:00
direct opening_date: 2026-10-17T14:20:39+02:00
direct procurement_category: Clothing, PPE & Accessories
```
Called the real, unmodified `gov_sources.merge({"etenders_portal": [portal_rel], "capetown_procurement": [direct_rel]})` - **RED, confirmed real, not hypothetical:**
```
MERGED listing_sources: ['etenders_portal', 'capetown_procurement']
MERGED published_date: None
MERGED opening_date: None
MERGED procurement_category: None
```
The merged release - which DOES carry the direct-site source in `listing_sources`, so a reader has no signal anything is missing - silently kept the portal's null for all three fields instead of picking up the real value sitting one field over in the very same fold. This is exactly the live-data condition the prior pass flagged: it needs the portal's own row to be missing the field, which `etenders_portal.normalize()` passes straight through whenever the portal's API genuinely returns `date_Published`/`category` as null for that row (nullable in the real schema, not a reader bug - `etenders_portal.py` doesn't invent these values).

**A second, related gap found while fixing the first.** `merge()` has a SECOND fold path - the "buyer's own site says still open, portal has the row in its Closed tab" branch (used for SANRAL's own closing-date extensions, e.g. the module's own `NRA 2026/0754 (A)` example) - that doesn't call `_fold()` at all. It hand-duplicates three of `_fold()`'s five effects (`listing_sources`, `documents`, `direct_documents`) directly inline, and skips the field-copy loop entirely - so this path had the SAME omission, plus it was ALSO missing `briefing`/`province`/`tender_type`/`description`/`scm_reference` (the 5 fields `_fold()` already copied correctly in the ordinary path), not just the 3 new ones. Reproduced the same way, with a frozen clock (the existing `test_merge()`'s own `_FixedBeforeClosing` pattern, needed because `is_closed` is baked in at `sh.release()` construction time against the real wall clock) and a closed portal row with no `date_Published`/`category`: RED, `merged[0]["published_date"]`/`["procurement_category"]` both `None` despite the real SANRAL-site release carrying real values for both.

**Why this matters downstream, not just cosmetically.** `published_date`/`opening_date` feed `gov_sources.published_since()` (keeps a release with no publish date rather than treating it as stale - "unknown is not old" - so a silently-nulled date doesn't wrongly filter a tender OUT, but does make a genuinely-dated tender look undated) and `tender_changes.py`'s own re-advertisement-linking and late-added-addendum detection (lines 167/281/287/298 - `sorted(rels, key=lambda x: (x.get("published_date") or "", ...))` and same-day comparisons that degrade silently when the field is null). `procurement_category` feeds `assess_tender.categorize()` and `tender_enrichment.classify_tags()`/`enrich_release()` (the scope/industry-tag heuristic `attach_scope_enrichment()` attaches to every merged release) - a null category there means a weaker, less specific tag set for a tender that actually has a real category one field away in the same merged row.

**Fix.** Added `published_date`/`opening_date`/`procurement_category` to `_fold()`'s existing field-copy tuple (now 8 fields, same `if not hit.get(f) and r.get(f)` guard - never overwrites a portal value that IS present, only fills a genuine gap). For the second fold path, replaced its hand-duplicated 4-line partial copy of `_fold()`'s own logic with a direct call to `_fold(hit, r, name)` - `hit["closing_date"]` is already set equal to `r["closing_date"]` two lines above that call (the whole point of that branch), so `_fold()`'s own closing-date-disagreement check is a no-op there, not a duplicate of the `status` disagreement the branch already records just above it. Confirmed by hand this doesn't change `listing_sources`/`documents`/`direct_documents` behavior in that path - `_fold()` does exactly what the hand-written lines did for those three, plus now also does the field copy they'd skipped.

**Verified red-then-green.** Both repros above: RED against the pre-fix `_fold()` (fields stay `None` through the fold in both paths), GREEN after (merged release carries `published_date: 2026-10-17T14:20:39+02:00`, `opening_date` likewise, `procurement_category: Clothing, PPE & Accessories` in the first path; `published_date`/`procurement_category` correctly populated in the second). Both repros promoted into a permanent regression test, `test_fold_copies_published_opening_category()` in `engine/discovery/test_gov_sources.py` (registered in its own `if __name__ == "__main__":` block), using the real unmodified `etenders_portal.normalize()`/`capetown_procurement.normalize_rfq()`/`sanral_site()`/`gov_sources.merge()` - no mocking. ### Finding 246 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, cross-source data-attribution class - the fresh-angle lead the `lxxxiii` pass's own fresh-angle sweep explicitly left open: not whether `store_award_outcomes.py`'s `merge()` covers every field, but whether its coalescing RULE for one is itself correct - `winner_amount_zar`'s own fallback could attach ONE source's award amount to a DIFFERENT source's named winner)

**Area:** `engine/discovery/store_award_outcomes.py`'s `merge()` - specifically the `winner_amount_zar` fallback (`if winner_part and not amount: amount = next(p.get("winner_amount_zar") for p in ordered if p.get("winner_amount_zar"))`), immediately below where `winner_part`/`winner` are picked by `SOURCE_PRIORITY` order. This is the exact lead the `lxxxiii` pass's own fresh-angle sweep flagged and explicitly declined to chase without "a concrete reason to suspect one": that pass checked field COVERAGE only (does `merge()` populate every `public_tender_outcomes` column) and found it clean, but never checked whether the RULE deciding which of 2-3 sources' values wins for a given field is itself internally consistent.

**The concrete reason: `winner_name` and `winner_amount_zar` are selected by two DIFFERENT rules that can disagree about which source is authoritative.** Every other field `merge()` fills (`ocid`/`reference`/`buyer`/`title`/`project_type`/`procurement_type`/`province`/`closing_date`/`award_date`/`winner_points`/`winner_bbbee_points`/`attribution`) goes through the SAME `first()` helper - one consistent rule, first non-empty value in `SOURCE_PRIORITY` order (`sanral_awarded` > `sanral_closed` > `etenders_portal`). `winner_name` does NOT go through `first()` - it's taken from `winner_part`, the first (by priority) part that HAS a `winner` at all. `winner_amount_zar` starts from that SAME `winner_part`, but when `winner_part`'s own amount is empty, it falls back to **any part's `winner_amount_zar`, in priority order, with no check that part names the SAME winner.** `part_from_sanral()`/`part_from_portal()` always set `winner` and `winner_amount_zar` together, from the SAME source row - the two fields are the source's own statement "company X won, for amount Y." The fallback breaks that pairing: it can label the row with source A's winner name and source B's winner's amount.

**Confirmed real, not hypothetical.** Real fixture data (`fixtures/award_prices/real_outcomes_2026-10-17.json`, `X.003-080-2024/1`) already shows SANRAL and eTenders genuinely disagreeing on how to WRITE the same winner's name - SANRAL's awarded page says `"Black Torres JV"`, eTenders' Awarded tab says `"BLACK TORRES 96"` (`norm_name()` gives two different strings, `BLACKTORRESJV` vs `BLACKTORRES96` - not a normalization near-miss, genuinely different text). That case doesn't trip the bug today only because BOTH sources also happen to carry the SAME amount (`22681492.44`) directly on their own part, so `winner_part`'s own amount is never empty and the fallback path is never reached - a coincidence of this one fixture row, not a property the code enforces. `summarize_sanral()`'s own `with_contract_amount` counter (already in this file) exists specifically because SANRAL award pages don't always carry a parseable approved-contract-amount even when they do carry `awarded_to` - so a SANRAL part with a real winner and no amount is a normal, already-anticipated shape, not a corner case invented for this finding. Built the real repro directly through `part_from_sanral()`/`part_from_portal()` (no mocking, same builders production code calls):
```python
sanral_rec = {"source": "sanral_awarded", "reference": "N.001-002-2026/1", "title": "Test tender",
              "awarded_to": "Black Torres Builders CC"}                 # no approved_contract_amount_zar at all
portal_rec = {"bid_number": "SANRAL-TEST-1", "title": "Test tender", "buyer": "SANRAL",
              "procurement_type": "Open",
              "awards": [{"supplier": "Delta Roadworks (Pty) Ltd", "amount_zar": 18_500_000.0}]}
row = sao.merge("sanral:N.001-002-2026/1", [sao.part_from_sanral(sanral_rec), sao.part_from_portal(portal_rec)])
```
**RED, confirmed real:**
```
winner_name: "Black Torres Builders CC"
winner_amount_zar: 18500000.0   # Delta Roadworks' own amount, from an entirely different winner
```
The merged, public row stated that "Black Torres Builders CC" won for R18,500,000 - a figure that, on the data actually fed in, belongs to "Delta Roadworks (Pty) Ltd," a different company the eTenders portal recorded as ITS OWN winner for what the outcome-key match treated as the same tender (a stale SANRAL page next to an updated eTenders one after a re-award/appeal is a realistic way for this to arise - South African public-procurement awards being overturned and re-awarded on appeal is a documented, non-rare occurrence, not a contrived shape).

**Why this matters downstream, not just internally.** `public_tender_outcomes.winner_name`/`winner_amount_zar` are read together, by name, on the product's own market-pricing surfaces: `app/lib/marketPricing.ts` (`winnerAmount`, and `sizes`/`normName(r.winner_name)` used to build a company's own win-size distribution for benchmarking) feeding `app/app/tenders/[id]/market-context.tsx` and `app/app/pipeline/pricing/market-comparison.tsx`. A misattributed amount doesn't just sit unused in a database column - it would show a SPECIFIC company name next to a SPECIFIC rand figure it never actually won, and feed that same wrong pairing into the per-company pricing-benchmark numbers a bidder reads to size their own bid.

**Fix.** The fallback now only accepts an amount from a part whose own `winner` field, when present, name-matches (`norm_name()`, the same helper `find_winner()` already uses) the chosen `winner` - or from a part that names no winner of its own at all (never contradicts the chosen one). When no part's amount clears that bar, `winner_amount_zar` stays `None` (safer than a wrong number) and a new note names the excluded source and the OTHER winner its amount actually belongs to, so the gap is visible rather than silently empty - the same "say why, don't go quiet" convention this file already uses for a dropped zero-amount or an unconfirmed `name_token` match. The original, legitimate use of the fallback - the SAME real winner, spelled differently per source, one part missing its own amount - still works: it only required a name-normalized match, which it already has.

**Verified red-then-green.** Two permanent regression tests added to `engine/discovery/test_store_award_outcomes.py` (registered in its own `main()`): `test_amount_fallback_never_crosses_to_a_different_winners_source()` (the repro above) and its mirror, `test_amount_fallback_still_works_for_the_same_winner_spelled_differently()` (SANRAL `"Build Co (Pty) Ltd"` / eTenders `"BUILD CO LTD"` - same company, same amount, must still fill in). `git stash push -- engine/discovery/store_award_outcomes.py` (keeping both new tests), `python3 test_store_award_outcomes.py` → `2 FAILED` (`winner_amount_zar == 18500000.0` instead of `None`; the mismatch note missing) - exactly the first test, the mirror test already passes pre-fix (confirming it wasn't a vacuous addition). `git stash pop`, same command → `0 failure(s)`, all 8 tests. Full existing suite in this file re-run clean (`find_winner()`'s own name/amount/name_token tests, the batch-upsert key-shape test, the zero-amount test) - no regression. `engine/discovery/test_award_prices.py` (the real-fixture merge test, including the `X.003-080-2024/1` Black-Torres case this finding started from) re-run clean - `0 failure(s)`, confirming the fix doesn't disturb the one real row already exercising a cross-source name mismatch. `python3 -m py_compile store_award_outcomes.py test_store_award_outcomes.py test_award_prices.py` clean.
