### Finding 259 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low, cosmetic-but-real display bug in `displayTenderTitle()`) - the gov-source ALL-CAPS "shouting" title fix only title-cased the FIRST run of letters in each space-separated word, so a hyphenated word (`RE-ADVERTISED`, `CO-ORDINATION` - a real, reachable gov-portal title shape, not a contrived example) came out half-fixed - `"Re-ADVERTISED"` - leaving the second half still fully shouting, directly defeating the one thing this display-only transform exists to do

**Area:** `app/lib/titleCase.ts` (`titleCaseWord()`'s final `return` - the generic per-word title-case `.replace()` call). Test coverage added to `app/lib/titleCase.test.ts` (1 new case, two assertions).

**How this was found.** This pass's own continuation of the task-brief-named mention-count-ranking technique on `app/lib/*.ts`: re-ranked every `.ts` file directly under `app/lib` (excluding `*.spec.ts`/`*.test.ts`) by real mention count across both standing docs combined. `app/lib/titleCase.ts` (65 lines) ranked lowest of any file with real logic (1 mention, never independently reviewed as its own unit by this track before). Read it in full against its one real caller, `app/app/discovery/page.tsx:878`'s `displayTenderTitle(o.title)`. The file's own existing test file (`titleCase.test.ts`, 6 cases) covers plain shouted titles, known acronyms, digit-bearing reference codes, and the "already mixed case" no-op path well - but every test case's title is made of space-separated words with exactly ONE run of letters each; none covers a word containing an internal non-letter separator (a hyphen) with letters on both sides.

**The gap, traced, not guessed.** `titleCaseWord()`'s final line was: `word.replace(/[A-Za-z]+/, (run) => run.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + run.slice(1).toLowerCase())` - a regex with no `/g` flag. `String.prototype.replace()` with a non-global regex replaces only its FIRST match. For a word with a single run of letters (`"MAINTENANCE"`, `"SANRAL"`, `"(RFQ10419311)"` - digits/punctuation aside, one letter run) this is correct and indistinguishable from a global replace. For a word with TWO letter runs separated by a non-letter character inside the same space-delimited token - a hyphen is the only realistic case in tender titles - only the first run gets the "capitalize first letter, lowercase the rest" treatment; the second run is returned completely untouched, exactly as it arrived (i.e. still upper-case, since this whole function only ever runs when the source `isAllCaps(title)`).

**Confirmed reachable, not hypothetical.** `RE-ADVERTISEMENT`/re-advertised tenders are a named, recurring real-world shape this codebase already has fixtures and handling for elsewhere (`engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s own test fixtures model exactly this "same Ref No., re-advertised" case; `engine/discovery/tender_changes.py` emits a dedicated `"readvertised"` change-type event for it). More directly: `state/seen_tenders.json` - this repo's own real, live discovery-run state file - contains an actual title, `"SCMU 03 - 2026 2027 RE-ADVERTISED"`, scraped verbatim from a real government portal. `displayTenderTitle()` is called unconditionally on every Discovery-page title (`app/app/discovery/page.tsx:878`), so this exact real title would render with this exact bug today.

**Reproduced RED with the real, unmodified `titleCaseWord()`.** Ran the real function directly against the real title found in `state/seen_tenders.json`, plus a second realistic case:
```
node --experimental-strip-types -e '
import { displayTenderTitle } from "./lib/titleCase.ts";
console.log(JSON.stringify(displayTenderTitle("SCMU 03 - 2026 2027 RE-ADVERTISED")));
console.log(JSON.stringify(displayTenderTitle("APPOINTMENT OF SERVICE PROVIDER FOR CO-ORDINATION OF WORKS")));
'
```
Real output, pre-fix: `"Scmu 03 - 2026 2027 Re-ADVERTISED"` and `"Appointment of Service Provider for Co-ORDINATION of Works"` - in both cases the hyphen's second half is left exactly as scraped, still fully shouting, directly contradicting the rest of the now-Title-Cased sentence around it. Added the same two cases as a new test in `app/lib/titleCase.test.ts`:
```
cd app && node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/titleCase.test.ts
```
Real output, pre-fix: **1 failed, 6 passed** - `AssertionError: expected 'Scmu 03 - 2026 2027 Re-ADVERTISED' to equal 'Scmu 03 - 2026 2027 Re-Advertised'`, confirming the bug was genuinely present, not merely suspected.

**Fix.** Added the `/g` flag to the one `.replace()` call: `word.replace(/[A-Za-z]+/g, (run) => run.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + run.slice(1).toLowerCase())`. This title-cases every letter-run in the word, not just the first, so a hyphenated word gets both sides fixed (`"RE-ADVERTISED"` -> `"Re-Advertised"`). No change to `isAllCaps()`, `KNOWN_ACRONYMS`, or `LOWERCASE_MID_WORDS` - this is a pre-existing, documented, accepted limitation (whole-word-granularity acronym/short-word detection) this fix deliberately does not expand scope into; it only fixes the "second run left fully shouting" defect, which is unambiguously wrong under the function's own stated purpose ("Title Case instead of ALL-CAPS when the source was fully shouted").

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.**
```
cd app && node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/titleCase.test.ts
```
Post-fix: **7 passed (7)** - the new hyphenated-word test and all 6 pre-existing tests pass unchanged. Full regression (every `*.test.ts` in the repo, run individually via `node --experimental-strip-types --test <file>`): 28/29 files ran with no failures across any of them (the remaining file, `app/_components/document-intake/uploadBatch.test.ts`, also passed; the 5 files under `app/tenders/[id]/` report `0 pass / 0 fail` when invoked with the literal bracketed path on the command line - a pre-existing node:test path-globbing quirk unrelated to this change, confirmed unaffected by this fix since none of those files import `titleCase.ts`). `npx vitest run` - **73 files, 584 tests, all pass** (unchanged from the last-recorded baseline - `titleCase.ts` has no `.spec.ts` counterpart, so this fix doesn't move that count). `npx tsc --noEmit` - 0 errors. `npx eslint lib/titleCase.ts lib/titleCase.test.ts` - 0 errors/warnings. `npx next build` - `✓ Compiled successfully`, route list unchanged (confirmed `/discovery` still present, same shape as before).

Pushed directly to `main`: pure TypeScript, a single regex-flag addition plus its accompanying test - no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration.

### Finding 260 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, sibling-TS-vs-Python-function divergence - a confirmed-live false-positive the Python side already fixed, never ported to its TS mirror) - `app/lib/locality.ts`'s `matchLocality()` could award real preference points for an office nowhere near a tender's required locality, because its name-similarity check matched on a bare run of letters rather than a whole word

**Area:** `app/lib/locality.ts` (`normArea()`'s sibling `similar()`/`areaMatches()` - adds `normAreaWords()` and `wordIn()`, changes `similar()`'s signature to take both the bare-letter and space-preserving forms of each name). New test coverage: `app/lib/locality.spec.ts` (this file had zero test coverage before this fix - 6 new cases).

**How this was found.** Continuing this pass's own mention-count-ranking technique on `app/lib/*.ts` (after the task brief's own note that the clean-negative ratio on this directory was rising): re-ranked every unswept `.ts` file directly under `app/lib` by real mention count across both standing docs combined. `app/lib/locality.ts` (126 lines, 2 real mentions - both passing references in feature-list tables, never independently reviewed as its own unit by this track's technique before) ranked among the lowest unswept files with real logic. Its own header comment claims it is "Same rules as `engine/discovery/score_outlook.py`'s own `match_locality()`" - a direct, explicit sibling-divergence claim, so read both functions side by side in full, the exact check this track's own history already treats as a productive lead class ("Sibling-TS-vs-Python-function divergence sweeps" - though that class is marked already-exhausted in general, this specific file/function pair had never actually been diffed against its named Python sibling before).

**The gap, traced, not guessed.** `score_outlook.py`'s own `_norm_area_words()` carries a dated docstring: "confirmed live, 2026-10-21: a company office in 'Kannaland' (Western Cape) matched a tender's own locality row for 'Nala' (a Free State local municipality, nothing to do with Kannaland) because the bare letters 'nala' sit inside 'kannaland' - awarding real preference points for an office nowhere near the required area." The Python side's fix: alongside `_norm_area()` (which strips administrative words then collapses straight to bare letters, no spaces, used for the exact-match and `difflib.SequenceMatcher` typo-tolerance checks), it added a SECOND normaliser, `_norm_area_words()`, which does the same stripping but keeps spaces, and a `_word_in()` helper that requires a whole-word (space- or edge-bounded) substring match - `_area_matches()` only treats a substring containment as a match when it passes this whole-word check, not a bare-letter `in` check.

`app/lib/locality.ts`'s own `normArea()` is the direct TS equivalent of Python's `_norm_area()` - same word list, same bare-letter collapse. But its `similar()` function still used the OLD, pre-fix shape: `if (b.length >= 6 && (a.includes(b) || b.includes(a))) return true;` - a bare-letter `.includes()` check with no word-boundary guard at all, exactly the shape the Python side's own docstring names as the confirmed-live bug it fixed. The TS mirror was never updated with the corresponding fix, so the identical false positive was reachable through `matchLocality()`, called with real company office rows and real tender locality rows (extracted by the same `score_outlook.py` the TS file claims to mirror, stored in `tenders.evaluation_rules.locality`) from `app/tenders/[id]/general-workspace.tsx`, `app/tenders/[id]/compliance-report.tsx`, and `app/tenders/[id]/general-pack-review-data.ts` - every one of the Tender Workspace's own locality-scoring and pack-review surfaces.

**Confirmed reachable, not hypothetical.** Kannaland (Western Cape, under the Garden Route district) and Nala (Free State, under the Lejweleputswa district) are both real, currently-existing South African municipalities with no relation to each other - the exact real-world pair the Python side's docstring names as the confirmed-live case. Any company with an office in Kannaland (or any other district/local-municipality/town name containing "nala" as a bare run of letters) tracking a tender whose locality table scores "Nala" would have been awarded those points incorrectly, exactly as happened on the Python/Discovery side before its own 2026-10-21 fix.

**Reproduced RED with the real, unmodified `matchLocality()`.** Ran the real function directly with the real place names from the Python side's own docstring:
```
cd app && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
import { matchLocality } from "./lib/locality.ts";
const rows = [{ area: "Nala", level: "municipality", province: null, points: 5, system: "90/10", kind: "specific_goals" }];
const offices = [{ id: "1", label: null, office_kind: "head_office", province: "Western Cape", district_municipality: "Kannaland", local_municipality: null, town: null, street_address: null, proof_type: null, proof_date: null, notes: null }];
console.log(JSON.stringify(matchLocality(rows, offices)));
'
```
Real output, pre-fix: `{"status":"matched","points":5,...,"reason":"Office in Kannaland matches \"Nala\" - 5 point(s) under 90/10."}` - a clean false positive, not hypothetical. Added a new test file (this file had none before), `app/lib/locality.spec.ts`, with the same case as its first test:
```
npx vitest run lib/locality.spec.ts
```
Real output, pre-fix: **1 failed, 5 passed** - `AssertionError: expected 'matched' to be 'no_match'`, confirming the bug was genuinely present, not merely suspected.

**Fix.** Added `normAreaWords()` (same administrative-word stripping as `normArea()`, keeps spaces instead of collapsing to bare letters) and `wordIn()` (whole-word/edge-bounded substring check, mirroring Python's `_word_in()`) to `app/lib/locality.ts`. Changed `similar()`'s signature to take both the bare-letter and word-preserving form of each side (`similar(a, b, aWords, bWords)`), kept the exact-match and Levenshtein-ratio typo-tolerance checks exactly as they were (unrelated to this bug - still needed for the real misspelling case, "Dawid Kruper" vs "Dawid Kruiper", TN051/2026's own points table), and replaced the bare-letter substring check with `bWords.length >= 6 && (wordIn(bWords, aWords) || wordIn(aWords, bWords))` - same length-gate side (the office field, matching Python's own `len(vw) >= 6` gate on the office-side word form) and same whole-word requirement as the Python fix. `areaMatches()` updated to compute and pass both forms. No change to `normArea()` itself, `matchLocality()`'s own tie-breaking/province-level logic, or any caller.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.**
```

### Finding 261 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low severity, display/data-shape bug, reachable today via arbitrary date input, not just a future-year wait) - `app/lib/publicHolidays.ts`'s `holidaysForYear()` could return two entries for the SAME calendar date, giving the free deadline calculator a duplicate React key and a misleading "two holidays" row

**Area:** `app/lib/publicHolidays.ts` (`holidaysForYear()` only - no change to `isPublicHoliday()`, `isBusinessDay()`, `addBusinessDays()`, `businessDaysBetween()`, or `sastToday()`, all of which already treated a date as one holiday regardless, via a `Set`). New test coverage: one new case added to the existing `app/lib/publicHolidays.test.ts` (this file already had 13 tests; no new file needed).

**How this was found.** Per the task brief's own suggested fresh angle (a genuinely unswept UI directory, since the engine/-Python mention-count-ranking technique turned out to be already heavily mined for the lowest-mention candidates checked this pass - `cidb_tenders.py`/`dbsa_procurement.py`/`sars_procurement.py`/`generate_action_checklist.py`/`run_discovery.py`/`print_financial.py` all carry extensive prior fix history in their own inline comments or this doc's own history despite a low basename-occurrence count, a mismatch this pass confirmed by reading each one in full before moving on) - pivoted to `app/app/toolkit/`/`app/app/tools/`'s free lead-magnet calculators, reading `DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx` and its backing `app/lib/publicHolidays.ts` end to end again, specifically for the one class of bug this file's own `holidaysForYear()` had never been checked against before: can two of its own entries (10 fixed-date holidays, their s2A Sunday-shift Mondays, 2 Easter-derived dates) ever land on the exact same calendar date?

**The gap, traced, not guessed.** `holidaysForYear()` built its output as a plain, unordered array via unconditional `.push()` calls, with zero dedup before `.sort()`. Wrote a small script implementing the identical algorithm (Meeus/Jones/Butcher Easter + the fixed-date table + the s2A Sunday shift) and ran it across 1994-2100 looking for any year where two pushed entries shared a date - found two distinct real collision shapes: (1) whenever Christmas Day (25 December) falls on a Sunday, s2A's own "the following Monday is a public holiday" rule lands on 26 December - but 26 December is ALREADY Day of Goodwill's own fixed date, so the shift is entirely redundant (that Monday was a holiday regardless) yet still produced a second, separate array entry for the identical date (found at 2033, 2039, 2044, 2050, 2061, 2067, 2072, 2078, 2089, 2095 within that window - next occurrence 2033, only 7 years from today); (2) Human Rights Day (21 March) and Good Friday can coincide on their own, genuinely different grounds (last real occurrence 2008, within the same scan). Confirmed the real, deployed TypeScript function reproduces the same collision, not just the reimplementation.

**Confirmed reachable today, not just a future-year theoretical.** `DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx`'s `upcomingHolidays` computes `holidaysForYear(year)`/`holidaysForYear(year + 1)` from whatever `startDate` the visitor types into the public, unauthenticated `/tools/deadline-calculator` page (no sign-in, no date-range restriction) - typing any date in late 2032 right now shows the 2033 holiday list, so this is reachable immediately by anyone using the live tool today, not only once 2033 actually arrives. The list is rendered with `<li key={h.date}>` - a genuine duplicate React key for the one date, and a misleading display implying two separate non-working days on 26 December 2033 when there is only one. `isPublicHoliday()`/`isBusinessDay()`/`addBusinessDays()`/`businessDaysBetween()` were NOT affected by this - they already dedupe via a `Set` built from the same array - so no deadline/business-day MATH was ever wrong, only the raw list this one function returns and the UI that renders it directly.

**Reproduced RED with the real, unmodified function.**
```
cd app && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
import("./lib/publicHolidays.ts").then(m => {
  const hs = m.holidaysForYear(2033);
  const byDate = {};
  for (const h of hs) { (byDate[h.date] ??= []).push(h.name); }
  for (const [date, names] of Object.entries(byDate)) if (names.length > 1) console.log("COLLISION:", date, names);
});
'
```
Real output, pre-fix: `COLLISION: 2033-12-26 [ 'Public holiday (Christmas Day falls on a Sunday)', 'Day of Goodwill' ]` - confirming the bug was genuinely present against the real function, not merely suspected. Added a new test to the existing `app/lib/publicHolidays.test.ts` asserting exactly one entry for `2033-12-26`:
```

```
Real output, pre-fix (verified by temporarily reverting only `lib/publicHolidays.ts`, keeping the new test): **13 passed, 1 failed** - the new test failed (`AssertionError: expected 2 to equal 1`), confirming the bug.

**Fix.** After building the full `out` array (fixed-date holidays, their s2A shift entries, the two Easter-derived dates, any gazetted `EXTRA_HOLIDAYS`) but before sorting, added a dedup pass: group entries by `date`, and for any date with more than one distinct `name`, join them with `" / "` into a single entry (e.g. `"Public holiday (Christmas Day falls on a Sunday) / Day of Goodwill"`) rather than dropping either side arbitrarily - this keeps every real, distinct reason a date is a holiday visible, while guaranteeing one entry per date. No change to `FIXED_DATE_HOLIDAYS`, `easterSunday()`, the s2A shift condition itself, `isPublicHoliday()`/`isBusinessDay()`/`addBusinessDays()`/`businessDaysBetween()`, or any caller's signature.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with real output.**

```

### Finding 262 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, input-validation gap, reachable today with no special setup - `app/app/tools/bee-preference-points/BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx`'s result validation let two of its three Rand fields silently read as a real R0 amount instead of a missing input, producing a false maximum score with no error shown)

**Why this area.** Per this pass's own task brief, picked the other still-unswept half of the task brief's named fresh candidates (`app/app/toolkit/`/`app/app/tools/`'s remaining two calculators, `B6EstimatorClient.tsx` and `BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx`, plus their backing `app/lib/sanralScoring.ts`/`sanralMatrices.ts`/`preferencePoints.ts` - `preferencePoints.ts`'s own `BEE_POINTS_TABLE` was already excluded per the brief's own note, already checked against its Python counterpart). **`B6EstimatorClient.tsx` + `sanralScoring.ts`/`sanralMatrices.ts`: read end to end, genuinely clean.** This lib turned out to be far more heavily and carefully built-out than its low doc-mention count suggested (an extreme-value optimization replacing a brute-force 2^n search for the "managerial flag unknown" case, explicit handling of sub-6-month pro-rata experience, matrix-to-matrix project exclusion with its own user-facing note, `DS_SPECIALISMS`' regex-matching order checked for false-positive overlap across all 8 specialisms - none found). Checked specifically for the same "stale UI state after a dependent control changes" and "empty-input coerces to a wrong valid number" shapes this pass's real finding (below) turned out to have: `matrixForPosition()` only reads the `specialism` text when `baseCode(positionCode) === "DS"`, so a stale specialism value left over from a prior DS selection is provably inert once the position switches away from DS (confirmed by reading `matrixForPosition()` itself, not assumed); a stale `experienceType` value that no longer matches the new matrix after switching positions degrades gracefully through the existing `excluded`-projects path (the project is left off with an explanatory note, not silently mis-scored) - this is `estimatePosition()`'s own documented, pre-existing behavior, not a gap. The two date `<input type="date">` fields (closing date, project start/end) are naturally immune to the `Number("")` shape below, since `!closingDate` is checked directly against the empty string. Conclusive negative on this half.

**The real finding: `BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx`'s three Rand `CurrencyInput` fields didn't all get the same "reject a non-positive price" guard.** The component's own validation was:
```ts
const cv = Number(contractValue);
const tp = Number(tenderPrice);
const lp = Number(lowestPrice);
if (!Number.isFinite(cv) || !Number.isFinite(tp) || !Number.isFinite(lp) || lp <= 0) {
  return { error: "...", data: null };
}
```
`Number("")` evaluates to `0`, not `NaN` - so clearing a `CurrencyInput` field to blank (the exact flow its own `useLayoutEffect`-driven select-on-focus behavior is built to encourage: focus selects all, user retypes) passes `Number.isFinite` and is silently treated as a genuine R0 amount. `lowestAcceptablePriceZar` already had the extra `lp <= 0` guard - needed by `pricePoints()`'s own division-by-Pmin - but `contractValueZarInclVat`/`tenderPriceZar` had no equivalent guard at all, even though a R0 "your tendered price" is just as semantically invalid as a R0 Pmin, and feeds `pricePoints()`'s formula directly: `Ps = maxPricePoints * (1 - (0 - Pmin)/Pmin) = maxPricePoints * 2`, clamped to `maxPricePoints` - the full, maximum possible price-points score.

**Confirmed reachable today, live, with a real browser - not just read-and-reasoned-about.** Started the real Next.js dev server (`npm run dev`) and drove it with Playwright/Chromium (`playwright-core@1.56.1`, already present in the repo's own tooling) against `http://localhost:3000/tools/bee-preference-points` (the public, unauthenticated page):
```js
await page.locator("#tp").click();
await page.keyboard.press("Control+A");
await page.keyboard.press("Delete");
await page.locator("#lp").click(); // blur tp
```
Real output, pre-fix: the field itself read back `"R 0.00"` on blur, and the page's own rendered text showed `Price points (Ps)\n80 / 80` and `Total (80/20)` - the maximum possible price-points score, with no error message anywhere on the page, as if the visitor had genuinely bid R0 against their own stated lowest-acceptable price. The same probe against `#cv` (contract value) showed the "R50 million threshold -> defaults to the 80/20 system for this value" caption and a full result rendering unchanged, both computed from a silently-assumed R0 contract value. This is reachable by anyone using the live, public, no-signup tool today - no future date, no special input needed, just clearing a field (a completely ordinary thing to do while editing a number).

**Fix.** Extended the existing `lp <= 0` rule to `cv`/`tp` as well: `cv <= 0 || tp <= 0 || lp <= 0` (alongside the unchanged `Number.isFinite` checks), with the error message updated from naming only the lowest-acceptable-price field to naming all three ("Enter valid numbers greater than 0 for the contract value, tendered price and lowest acceptable price."). No change to `preferencePoints.ts` itself - this was purely a UI-level validation gap, not a formula bug (the formula's own existing `lowestAcceptablePriceZar <= 0` throw was always correct; the issue was the client never reaching it with a correctly-invalid `tp`/`cv` in the first place, and never checking `cv`/`tp` at all before calling it).

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with the real page in a real browser.** Pre-fix (above): clearing `#tp` and blurring showed `80 / 80` and `Total (80/20)`, no error. Post-fix, same exact Playwright script, re-run against the hot-reloaded dev server: clearing `#tp` and blurring now shows the error text (`"Enter valid numbers greater than 0..."`) and no `Price points`/`Total` text anywhere on the page. Confirmed the untouched default-input case is byte-for-byte unaffected: a fresh page load (no interaction at all) still renders `Price points (Ps)\n72 / 80` and `Total (80/20)\n92 / 100` - the exact reg-4 worked example this file's own header comment and `preferencePoints.test.ts` both cite (Pmin=R1,000,000, Pt=R1,100,000, Level 1, 80/20 -> Ps=72, total=92) - and clearing `#cv` now also correctly shows the error (previously: no error). Full regression: `npx vitest run` from `app/` - **74 files, 590 tests, all pass** (unaffected - this is a UI-only change, no lib touched). `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/preferencePoints.test.ts` - **12 passed (12)**, unchanged (confirming the formula itself was never the bug). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` - 0 errors. `npx eslint app/tools/bee-preference-points/BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx` - 0 errors/warnings. `npx next build` - `✓ Compiled successfully`, route table and rendering mode unchanged (`/tools/bee-preference-points` still `○` static, `/toolkit/bee-preference-points` still `◐` partial-prerender, same as before this change) - also confirmed the toolkit (signed-in) route still resolves (redirects to login when logged out, as expected, `307`), and that the component's third real call site, `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx`'s embedded "Preference points calculator" card (deliberately given no tender-specific prefill, per that file's own comment - confirmed, not re-litigated), uses the exact same shared component and therefore gets the exact same fix with no separate change needed there.

### Finding 263 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low, input-validation gap, the identical `Number("")===0` shape as Finding 262 but on the sibling lead-magnet calculator Finding 262's own write-up explicitly flagged as a "worth checking" candidate - `app/app/tools/cidb-grade/CidbGradeClient.tsx`'s "Contract/tender value" field silently read a cleared or literally-zero field as a real R0 contract, producing a false "Grade 1CE" minimum-grade answer with no error shown)

**Area:** `app/app/tools/cidb-grade/CidbGradeClient.tsx` only (the `required` `useMemo`'s own guard, plus the one error-message string it gates) - no change to `app/lib/cidbGrading.ts` (`requiredGradeForValue()`/`gradeSufficientForValue()`/`CIDB_GRADING_TABLE` are all still correct; `requiredGradeForValue()`'s own existing `contractValueZar < 0` check was always right, this was purely a caller-side gap one step before it).

**Why this area.** This pass's own task brief, following directly from Finding 262's own write-up: "worth checking whether any OTHER calculator/form in the app has the same unguarded `Number(someInput) <= 0` gap," naming the CIDB grade calculator explicitly as a candidate already checked for Findings 260/261's own *unrelated* bug classes but "not necessarily for THIS specific empty-field-coerces-to-0 shape." Grepped every `CurrencyInput` usage first (`grep -rln "CurrencyInput" app` -> exactly one file, `BeePreferencePointsClient.tsx` itself, already fixed by Finding 262 - no second `CurrencyInput` consumer exists anywhere in the app) and then every other `Number(<form field>)` site gated only by `Number.isFinite`/`Number.isNaN` across `app/` (`grep -rn "Number\.isFinite\|Number("` over every `.ts`/`.tsx`, ~108 hits, read every one). Almost all were already safe by construction - every Server Action in `app/app/{tenders,experience,people,company,admin}/**/actions.ts` that calls `Number()` on a form field first runs it through a `str()`/truthiness guard (`v ? Number(v) : null`, or an explicit `v === "" ` / `levelRaw !== ""` check) *before* calling `Number()`, so `Number("")` never happens on that side at all (confirmed by reading `tenders/[id]/actions.ts:527` (`if (valueRaw) { value = Number(valueRaw); ... }`), `experience/actions.ts:127`, `people/actions.ts:261/715`, `company/principals/actions.ts:82`/`company/properties/actions.ts:39` (both via a shared `num()`/inline guard), and `admin/discovered-opportunities/actions.ts:30` (`if (levelRaw !== "") { ... }`) - all genuinely clean, not assumed). `logistics-actions.ts`'s `estimated_print_hours`/`estimated_transit_hours` and `DeadlineCalculatorClient.tsx`'s "days to add" field both coerce blank straight to `0` with no extra guard too, but checked and ruled out per this pass's own task brief's own caveat ("not every number field needs a `> 0` guard... where zero is a legitimate value is fine") - 0 estimated print/transit hours and 0 working days to add are both real, meaningful answers for their own fields (a same-day digital submission; "the deadline is today"), not evidence of a missing input.

**The real finding: `CidbGradeClient.tsx`'s "Contract/tender value" field, a native `<input type="number">`, had the exact same `Number.isFinite`-only guard Finding 262 fixed on `CurrencyInput`.**
```ts
const numericValue = Number(value);
const required = useMemo(
  () => (Number.isFinite(numericValue) ? requiredGradeForValue(numericValue) : null),
  [numericValue]
);
```
`Number("")` is `0`, not `NaN` - so clearing this field (default state `"9000000"`, but freely editable/clearable like any `<input type="number">`) passes `Number.isFinite` and is read as a genuine R0 contract value. `requiredGradeForValue(0)` is not a bug in that function - `0` correctly falls in the table's own published `0 - R200 000` Grade 1 band, exactly as the function's own header comment says it should for an actually-R0 contract - but a blank field is not an actually-R0 contract, and the component had no way to tell the two apart. The result: the tool showed a real, specific, plausible-looking answer ("Minimum grade required: Grade 1CE") instead of its own existing "enter a valid value" error, for an input that was never actually answered.

**Confirmed reachable today, live, with a real browser.** Started the real Next.js dev server (`npx next dev -p 3100` in `app/`) and drove it with Playwright/Chromium (`/opt/node-tools/node_modules/playwright-core@1.56.1`, the same toolchain Finding 262 used) against `http://localhost:3100/tools/cidb-grade` (the public, unauthenticated page):
```js
await valueInput.click();
await valueInput.fill("");           // select-all + clear, same as Finding 262's probe
```
Real output, pre-fix:
```
BASELINE (default 9000000):
Minimum grade required
Grade 6CE
---
AFTER CLEARING FIELD TO BLANK:
  Shows error message? false
  Shows a 'Minimum grade required' result? true Minimum grade required Grade 1CE
```
No error anywhere on the page - a visitor who clears the field (an ordinary thing to do while editing a number) sees a fully-formed, specific "Grade 1CE" answer that looks exactly as legitimate as a real result, and could reasonably (and wrongly) conclude a Grade 1 contractor can tender for whatever contract they actually had in mind.

**Fix.** Added a `numericValue > 0` guard alongside the existing `Number.isFinite` check (not just `>= 0`, since - per the same reasoning Finding 262 applied to `cv`/`tp` - a real government contract can't actually be worth R0 either, so a literally-typed `"0"` is just as invalid as a blank field), and updated the error copy from "Enter a valid, non-negative contract value." to "Enter a valid contract value greater than zero." so it no longer implies `0` is an acceptable answer. No change to `app/lib/cidbGrading.ts` - `requiredGradeForValue()`'s own `< 0` rejection and its correct `0`-is-Grade-1 table lookup were never wrong in isolation; the gap was entirely the caller never asking the function in the first place when there was really no input.

**Verified red-then-green, myself, with the real page in a real browser.** Pre-fix (above): blanking `#value` showed `Grade 1CE`, no error. Post-fix, same Playwright script re-run against the hot-reloaded dev server:
```
[baseline (default 9000000)] error shown? false | result: Minimum grade required Grade 6CE
[blanked field (post-fix)] error shown? true | result: none
[literal 0 (post-fix)] error shown? true | result: none
[negative value (post-fix)] error shown? true | result: none
[13000001 (expect Grade 7CE, boundary check)] error shown? false | result: Minimum grade required Grade 7CE
[200000 (expect Grade 1CE, inclusive lower boundary)] error shown? false | result: Minimum grade required Grade 1CE
```
Blank, literal `"0"` and a negative value all now correctly show "Enter a valid contract value greater than zero." with no result; the untouched default (`9000000` -> Grade 6CE) and the table's own two cited boundary values (`13 000 001` -> Grade 7CE; `200 000` -> Grade 1CE, confirming the inclusive-lower-bound convention from `cidbGrading.ts`'s own header comment is unaffected) all still resolve exactly as before. ### Finding 265 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low/moderate, silent-data-loss + orphaned-file class, two independent bugs found in the same small block - the standing brief's own named second candidate angle, `app/app/tenders/new/`'s manual-tender-creation flow, UI + server action, not just the `registerManualTender()` validation gap already traced for Findings 254/257's own reachability) - `registerManualTender()`'s own closing-date/closing-time pair only ever checked ONE direction of "both or neither" (a closing DATE typed with no closing TIME, the Form-Field-Audit 2026-10-18 fix); a closing TIME typed with no closing DATE fell straight through with no error at all, silently discarding the typed time and loading the tender with no closing date whatsoever - and, independently, the malformed-closing-date refusal branch returned without calling `cleanup()`, directly contradicting this exact file's own header-comment promise ("On any refusal the uploaded files are removed again so nothing is left orphaned")

**Area:** `app/app/tenders/new/actions.ts` (`registerManualTender()`), `app/app/tenders/new/manual-tender-form.tsx`, new shared helper `app/lib/manualTender.ts` (`parseManualTenderClosing()`), new test file `app/lib/manualTender.test.ts`.

**Why this area.** `engine/narrative/`'s own document-BUILDING logic (`generate_narrative.py`/`build_prompt.py`/`build_docx.py`/`uniqueness.py` - as opposed to its already-checked job-queue bridge, `process_narrative_jobs.py`) was read end to end first, per the brief's first-ranked candidate, and found genuinely clean: all 5 of its own test files (`test_build_prompt.py`, `test_build_docx.py`, `test_uniqueness.py`, `test_generate_narrative.py`, `test_process_narrative_jobs.py`) pass, 0 failures, and the module's own inline comments already document a deep, dated review history (Findings 75/123/126/186/192/253, plus seven separate dated QA passes from 2026-10-22 through 2026-11-07, including a genuine similarity-score-recompute-after-review fix on 2026-11-06). Moved to the brief's second named candidate, `app/app/tenders/new/`'s manual-tender-creation flow (`actions.ts` + `manual-tender-form.tsx` + `page.tsx`), confirmed to have **zero** test files of its own anywhere in the repo before this pass (`find app -name "*.test.*" -path "*tenders/new*"` - no matches) - genuinely unswept territory, not just the one already-traced `registerManualTender()` gap.

**Bug 1, reproduced against the real, unmodified function, not a reimplementation.** Read `registerManualTender()`'s closing-date/time block: `if (input.closingDate) { ...require closingTime too... }` - only the "date present, time blank" direction was ever checked (and only on the server; the client form's own `onSubmit` mirrors the same one-directional check). Nothing anywhere checks "time present, date blank." Reproduced live against the real function with a fake-Supabase/fake-Next scratch harness (a custom Node ESM loader hook resolving this repo's `@/*` alias and standing in for `@/lib/supabase/server`/`next/navigation`/`next/cache`, so the actual, un-copied `registerManualTender()` ran unmodified): called it with `closingDate: "", closingTime: "14:00"` and valid documents - the function proceeded straight to `supabase.rpc("load_manual_tender", { p_closing_date: null, ... })` with **zero validation error returned**, confirmed by capturing the real RPC call's own arguments. The typed closing time is gone with no trace and no warning; the tender loads as if no deadline information was ever given at all, meaning every downstream deadline-dependent feature (closed-tender detection, "days left", deadline reminders) silently never applies to it.

**Bug 2, found while fixing Bug 1, same file's own explicit written promise.** `registerManualTender()`'s header comment states plainly: "On any refusal the uploaded files are removed again so nothing is left orphaned." The malformed-closing-date branch (`if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(input.closingDate)) return { error: ... }`) returned immediately, with no `await cleanup()` call before it - unlike every other refusal branch in the same function (the missing-documents branch, the invalid-closing-time branch, the RPC-failure branch all call `cleanup()`). Reproduced live against the real function with the same scratch harness: called `registerManualTender()` with `closingDate: "not-a-real-date"` and one valid, already-"uploaded" document - got back `{ error: "Closing date isn't a valid date." }` with the fake `storage.remove()` called **zero times**, confirming the already-uploaded document is left orphaned in Storage on this one refusal path, contradicting the file's own stated contract. (A genuinely malformed date string can't reach this branch through the real browser form - `<input type="date">` always emits `YYYY-MM-DD` - but a Server Action is a public POST endpoint reachable directly, bypassing the client entirely, a known Next.js surface; the file's own promise makes no such carve-out.)

**Fix.** Extracted the validation into one new, pure, exported function, `parseManualTenderClosing(date, time)` (`app/lib/manualTender.ts`), used by both `registerManualTender()` and the client form, so the two surfaces can't drift apart on which half of the pair each one checks (the exact root cause of Bug 1 - the client and server each independently encoded only one direction). It rejects either direction of a partial date/time pair, rejects a malformed date or time, and otherwise returns `{ closing: "<date>T<time>:00+02:00" }` or `{ closing: null }` for a genuinely blank pair. `registerManualTender()` now has exactly one `if ("error" in closingResult) { await cleanup(); return {...} }` branch for every closing-date/time refusal, closing Bug 2's gap structurally (every future refusal from this one call site calls `cleanup()`, not by convention but because there's only one path). `manual-tender-form.tsx`'s own `onSubmit` gained the symmetric client-side check too, so the form fails fast before uploading anything, not just on the server round-trip.

**Verified red-then-green against the real, unmodified function (not the extracted copy) for both bugs**, using the scratch harness described above: pre-fix, `closingDate: "", closingTime: "14:00"` reached the RPC with `p_closing_date: null` and no error (RED); post-fix, the same call now returns `{ error: "Enter the closing date too (or leave the closing time blank)." }` and the RPC is never called (GREEN, 0 calls). Pre-fix, `closingDate: "not-a-real-date"` returned an error with `storage.remove()` called 0 times (RED); post-fix, the identical call now calls `storage.remove()` exactly once before returning the same error (GREEN).

**New test coverage**, `app/lib/manualTender.test.ts` (6 cases, `node --experimental-strip-types --test`, matching this repo's own node:test convention - not vitest, since `manualTender.ts` has no existing `.spec.ts` sibling): both blank (closing is `null`, no error), both valid (combined into the `+02:00` SAST timestamp), date-without-time (rejected, pre-existing direction unchanged), **time-without-date (rejected - the actual regression test for Bug 1)**, a malformed date, a malformed time. All 6 pass.

**Full verification suite, all green:** `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors), `npx eslint app/tenders/new lib/manualTender.ts lib/manualTender.test.ts` (0 errors), the full `app/*.test.ts` sweep run the same way CI does it (`find . -name "*.test.ts" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"`, every file individually) - all pass, and `npx vitest run` - 74 files, 590/590 tests pass.

**Backlog collision check - a real, named overlap, resolved by actual merge simulation, not assumed.** `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` for all 28 open PRs, grepping for `tenders/new|manualTender`: **one real hit, PR #195** (Finding 214, migration `0135`, still open/unmerged) - it also touches `app/app/tenders/new/actions.ts` and `app/lib/manualTender.ts`, but for a completely different, unrelated bug (the ".." path-traversal substring-vs-segment false positive in `cleanDocuments()`, moving that function from `actions.ts` into `manualTender.ts`) - confirmed by actually reading its full diff (`gh api repos/.../pulls/195/files`), not assumed from the title. Did a REAL local merge simulation per the standing guardrails: fetched its branch read-only (`git fetch origin pull/195/head:tmp-pr195-check`), committed this fix on a throwaway local branch off `main`, ran `git merge --no-commit --no-ff tmp-pr195-check` against it, read the real conflict markers, then `git merge --abort` and deleted every temp branch/ref (`tmp-my-fix-sim`, `tmp-merge-test`, `tmp-pr195-check`) before finishing. ### Finding 266 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate - `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`'s `runClarificationWindow()` read `tender_tasks` with a plain, unranged `.select()` - the identical PostgREST 1000-row cap this very file's own two sibling stages, `runPrintCutoff()`/`runBriefingReminders()`, were already paginated for, just never applied to this third stage - past the cap, a clarification-window reminder for any task sorting past row 1000 would silently and permanently never fire)

**Area:** `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts` (`runClarificationWindow()`). Test coverage added to the existing `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts.spec.ts` (1 new case, 7 total; also hardened the shared `makeBuilder()` mock itself - see below).

**How this was found.** This cycle's rotation landed on compliance/reminders. A broad sweep of the smaller pure-logic files in this area (`clarificationWindowReminders.ts`, `complianceExpiryReminders.ts`, `companyExpiryFields.ts`, `briefingReminders.ts`, `printCutoffReminders.ts`) found each already correctly scoped and tested - including confirming `complianceExpiryReminders.ts` is deliberately dead code (its own sibling script's header comment explains it was superseded by `send-compliance-digest.ts`'s broader coverage on 2026-10-27, left in place on purpose rather than deleted) and that the "exclude already-decided pipeline stages" bug class across this whole reminder family (deadline/briefing/clarification/print-cutoff) is already closed everywhere, per each file's own dated comment. Moved to the real caller script, `scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`, read in full: its two other stages, `runPrintCutoff()` and `runBriefingReminders()`, each carry a detailed, explicit comment on reading their own shared/public table (`tender_packs`/`tenders`) under the SERVICE ROLE key, summed across every company at once, and both are paginated via `fetchAllRows()`/`.range()` specifically because of PostgREST's 1000-row `db-max-rows` cap (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`). The third stage sitting right below them, `runClarificationWindow()`, read `tender_tasks` - the SAME shared-table-under-service-role shape - with a plain `.select()` and no pagination at all.

**Why this matters, concretely.** `tender_tasks` rows are never deleted once a clarification task is marked done (the status column just flips); summed across every company's own clarification tasks on the platform, this subset only grows over time, the identical "only grows" reasoning both sibling stages' own comments already give for `tender_packs`/`tenders`. `clarificationWindowCandidates()` (`lib/clarificationWindowReminders.ts`) fires on an EXACT day match (10 or 2 days left, no retried window) with the one-time `record_operational_alert_sent` dedupe claim on top - so a task whose row sorts past whatever 1000 rows PostgREST happens to return on a given run doesn't just miss one day's reminder, it misses its ONE qualifying day permanently, with no error anywhere to show why.

**Confirmed live, not inferred.** Read both call sites directly: `runPrintCutoff()`'s and `runBriefingReminders()`'s own `tender_packs`/`tenders` reads both go through `fetchAllRows()`; `runClarificationWindow()`'s `tender_tasks` read was a bare `await query` with no `.range()` anywhere, confirming it genuinely hits the documented, previously-confirmed-live PostgREST cap (`lib/supabasePaging.ts`'s own header comment: "confirmed live 2026-10-23... requesting `.limit(5000)` still only ever returned rows 0-999").

**Fix.** Wrapped the `tender_tasks` read in `fetchAllRows()`/`.range()`, same pattern and same `20_000`-row cap as this file's own two sibling stages immediately above it, preserving the existing `--company-id` scoping filter.

**Verified red-then-green - including hardening the test harness itself to catch this class at all.** Added a new case to the existing `send-operational-alerts.spec.ts`: `POSTGREST_PAGE_SIZE + 5` distinct clarification tasks (each its own company/tender), run with `--dry-run` (to avoid making 1000+ real network calls to the sandbox Resend API this spec file's OTHER tests already show failing with a real `daily_quota_exceeded` 429 in this environment), asserting both `result.candidates` and the collected `dryRunRows` equal the full row count, not a number capped at 1000. Fixed the mock itself first: a direct await (no `.range()`) now returns at most `POSTGREST_PAGE_SIZE` rows, matching the real server's own documented default; `.range(from, to)` continues to slice precisely as before. **Red (with the corrected mock):** saved the diff to `send-operational-alerts.ts` only, `git apply -R`, re-ran - `1 failed | 6 passed`, exactly the new case, the 6 pre-existing cases (across all 3 stages) untouched. **Green:** reapplied, re-ran - `7/7 pass`. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean project-wide (only the pre-existing, unrelated `date-fns`/`react-day-picker` gap). Broader regression: `npx vitest run scripts/` - all 7 script spec files, 47/47 pass.

### Finding 267 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate, open-redirect bypass, reachable today at all 4 real call sites, no special setup - `app/lib/safeRedirect.ts`'s `isSafeRedirectPath()` missed a tab/newline/CR-hidden variant of the exact backslash bypass Finding 57 already fixed, confirmed to cause a REAL cross-origin navigation in a real Chromium tab, not just a theoretical parse mismatch)

**Area:** `app/lib/safeRedirect.ts` (`isSafeRedirectPath()`/`safeRedirectPath()`, the single shared "is this a safe same-origin redirect target" helper). Test coverage extended in the existing `app/lib/safeRedirect.spec.ts` (2 new cases, 10 total).

**How this was found.** The task brief's own two newest named candidates (`app/app/experience/`, the submission-pack review/download UI) both turned out, on checking against this track's own history, to already be genuinely exhausted - `app/app/experience/` has a dedicated 2026-11-07 clean-sweep entry read-in-full in this file; the submission-pack review/download UI lives entirely under `app/app/tenders/[id]/`, already on the task brief's own exhausted list, with no separate `app/app/pack/` directory existing at all. `engine/general/`'s own pack-building logic (`build_general_pack.py`) likewise turned out, on a real grep of both standing docs, to be some of the most heavily-reviewed code in the whole repo (dozens of dated passes/Findings naming it by line). Rather than force a finding into any of these three already-exhausted populations, ran this track's own established fallback (`grep -c` mention-count ranking over a not-yet-covered population, the same technique that found Findings 249-251/257/260) across `app/lib/*.ts`. `safeRedirect.ts` (35 lines, 7 real mentions, all from its own original Finding 57 fix history) stood out as a small, security-relevant file whose own header comment explicitly names the exact browser-URL-parsing quirk it defends against (WHATWG's "backslash is a path separator for a special scheme" rule) - prompting the question of whether a SECOND browser-URL-parsing quirk, not yet covered by that comment or its tests, could bypass the same check.

**The gap.** `isSafeRedirectPath()`'s regex, `/^\/(?!\/|\\)/`, only inspects the single character right after the leading `/`. The WHATWG URL spec's parser (step 1: "remove all ASCII tab or newline from input") strips every ASCII tab (U+0009), LF (U+000A) and CR (U+000D) character from a URL string UNCONDITIONALLY, wherever it sits, before resolving it - confirmed directly against Node's own spec-compliant `URL` (not guessed): `new URL("/\t/evil.com", "https://good.example").href` and `new URL("/\t\\evil.com", ...).href` both return `"https://evil.com/"`. A value like `"/\t/evil.com"` or `"/\t\\evil.com"` passes the existing regex (the character right after the leading `/` is a tab - neither `/` nor `\`), but the value a browser actually navigates to, once it strips that tab, re-forms the exact `"//"`/`"/\\"` bypass shape this file already exists to block. The same holds for `\n` and `\r`.

**Confirmed this is a REAL, live navigation bypass, not just a parser-level curiosity - with a real browser, not jsdom.** Started this repo's own real dev server (`npx next dev -p 3100`) and, via a small temporary scratch route (removed before finishing, never committed) calling `useRouter().push()` - the exact mechanism `app/login/page.tsx`'s `handlePasswordSignIn()` uses on `next` right after a real sign-in succeeds - drove it with Playwright/Chromium (`/opt/node-tools/node_modules/playwright-core@1.56.1`): `router.push("/\t\\evil.example.com")` (pre-fix) produced a real outbound HTTP request to `http://evil.example.com/`, captured directly via Playwright's own `request`/`requestfailed` events (`net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` only because that host doesn't exist / this sandbox has no DNS for it, not because the navigation was refused - confirmed via `page.url()` landing on `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`, i.e. a failed cross-origin load attempt, never a same-origin page). Traced why: Next.js App Router's own navigation code (`node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router.js`) resolves the pushed URL via `new URL(canonicalUrl, ...)` (tab stripped here too) and, on detecting the result is cross-origin, falls back to a real `location.assign(canonicalUrl)` - an API that, unlike `history.pushState()`, is not restricted to same-origin targets. All 4 of this file's own real call sites (`/login?next=`, `/signup?next=`, `app/company/document-scan/actions.ts`'s hidden `return_to` field, `app/app/auth/callback/route.ts`'s own sink) still route through this one shared helper, confirmed by reading each (`grep -rn "safeRedirectPath"  app`) - none duplicate their own check.

**Fix.** Added `stripUrlWhitespace()` (a one-line `.replace(/[\t\r\n]/g, "")`) and apply it to the value before the existing same-origin regex check - mirroring exactly what a browser's own URL parser does first, so the function judges the same string a browser will actually act on. Deliberately not narrowed further: a legitimate in-app path never legitimately contains a tab/CR/LF, so this closes the bypass without rejecting anything real (confirmed: a control case with a tab elsewhere in an otherwise-ordinary path, not reforming `"//"`/`"/\\"` after stripping, still correctly returns `true`).

**Verified red-then-green against the real, unmodified function.** New cases in `safeRedirect.spec.ts` asserting `isSafeRedirectPath()` is `false` for `"/\t/evil.com"`, `"/\t\\evil.com"`, `"/\n/evil.com"`, `"/\n\\evil.com"`, `"/\r/evil.com"`, `"/\r\\evil.com"`, plus a `true` control case for a tab elsewhere in a safe path. **Red:** `npx vitest run lib/safeRedirect.spec.ts` against the pre-fix code - `1 failed | 9 passed` (`expected true to be false`). **Green:** after the fix - `10/10 pass`. Re-ran the exact live-browser repro above against the FIXED code (same scratch route, `safeRedirectPath("/\t\\evil.example.com", "/dashboard")` wired through `router.push()`): `page.url()` landed on `http://localhost:3100/login` (the app's own real "signed out, needs auth" redirect for `/dashboard` - expected, not a bug) and the captured request list contained zero requests to `evil.example.com`, confirming the fix holds in a real browser, not just the unit test. Full regression: `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors), `npx eslint lib/safeRedirect.ts lib/safeRedirect.spec.ts` (0 errors/warnings), `npx vitest run` - **74 files, 593 tests, all pass**, `npx next build` - compiled successfully, full route table unchanged (the scratch test routes were removed before this build, confirmed absent from its output).

**Not escalated to a PR.** A pure-TypeScript, one-helper-function fix plus its own test file - no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration. Not an authorization-bypass/tenant-isolation finding either (nothing here reads or mutates another tenant's data, or bypasses a server-side permission check) - it's the same client-side URL-parsing/input-validation gap class as this file's own original Finding 57, which this track already treated as a direct push (`d2de313`, no PR). Pushed directly to `main`, consistent with that precedent.

**Backlog collision check.** `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` for all 28 open PRs, grepping for `safeRedirect`: zero hits - no open PR touches either changed file.

**Backlog/sibling status.** `git fetch origin main` at pass start showed a new sibling-track (`session_01UMAzowxArab6cV4KurgXNE`) commit, `d8a4653` (Finding 266, `send-operational-alerts.ts`), that had landed since the task brief's stated `7c77674` - confirmed zero file overlap with this fix (`git show --stat d8a4653`: `app/scripts/send-operational-alerts*.ts` + docs only), fast-forwarded local `main` onto it (`git merge --ff-only`, no rebase needed since nothing had been committed locally yet), re-confirmed the real last Finding number by grep (**266** at that point, so this pass's own finding is **267**), then proceeded. Re-fetched again immediately before committing and again immediately before pushing: still `d8a4653` both times - no further sibling commit landed during this pass, so the push was a plain fast-forward.

To verify independently: `node -e 'console.log(new URL("/\t/evil.com", "https://good.example").href)'` (expect `https://evil.com/`, confirming the underlying browser-parser behaviour this fix defends against). `cd app && npx vitest run lib/safeRedirect.spec.ts` (expect `10/10 pass`). Call `isSafeRedirectPath("/\t\\evil.com")` directly and confirm it now returns `false`. `git log --oneline -1` on `main` should show this pass's own fix commit directly on top of `d8a4653`.

### Finding 268 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - low, Host-header-trust gap in one transactional-email link builder - `app/lib/siteUrl.ts`'s `siteUrl()` built "this app's own public base URL" straight from the incoming request's own Host header with zero validation, exactly as client-controlled as a query param or form field, confirmed live with a real spoofed-Host HTTP request against a real running dev server, not just read-and-reasoned)

**Area:** `app/lib/siteUrl.ts` (`siteUrl()`, the one function in this repo that derives "this app's own URL" from the live request rather than an explicit trusted value). New test file `app/lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` (10 cases - this file had none before).

**How this was found.** Finding 267's own task-brief follow-up asked two things: (1) are there other URL/redirect-target validation sites with a similar browser-normalization gap, and (2) does `stripUrlWhitespace()` (or an equivalent) need applying anywhere that reads a `next`/`return_to`-style param directly, bypassing `isSafeRedirectPath()` entirely? Grepped for every direct `searchParams.get("next"/"return_to"/"returnTo"/"redirect"/"redirectTo"/"callback"/"url")` and every `formData.get("return_to")` across `app/` - both candidates checked and ruled out (see pass write-up in `System-Status.md` for the full detail): `app/app/discovery/actions.ts`'s `acknowledgeDowngrade()` reads `return_to` directly and does NOT go through `isSafeRedirectPath()`, but its own regex (`/^\/(discovery|tenders\/[0-9a-f-]{36})(\?[^#]*)?$/`) is fully anchored at both ends against a tiny literal-path allowlist, not a loose prefix check - confirmed directly with real `RegExp.test()`/`new URL()` calls that no tab/CR/LF placement can make it match a cross-origin shape (full detail and exact commands in `System-Status.md`). `app/app/pipeline/actions.ts`'s own `return_to` read is a strict `=== "pricing"` equality check, never used as a path at all. Genuinely exhausted - not a new finding.

Pivoted to the open-ended half of the task brief's own suggestion - "are there OTHER places that parse/validate a URL, path, or redirect target where a similar gap could exist" - broadened past the redirect-target family specifically to any place this app treats a client-supplied value as if it were its own trusted identity. `grep -rn "window.location\|router\.push(\|NextResponse\.redirect"` across `app/` surfaced nothing new beyond what Finding 267 already covers (every dynamic `redirect()`/`NextResponse.redirect()` call target in `app/app/**/actions.ts` is built from a hardcoded path prefix plus a DB-sourced id, never a raw client-supplied full path - checked `proxy.ts`'s own two `NextResponse.redirect(url)` calls too: both only ever set `.pathname` to a literal `"/login"`/`"/onboarding"` on a cloned URL, no user-controlled redirect target there at all). The one genuinely fresh angle this opened: `app/lib/siteUrl.ts` - a file a 2026-11-07 pass's own mention-count sweep had explicitly SKIPPED as "trivial" purely by its 21-line size (`System-Status.md` line ~237: "...and pure trivial/type files (`utils.ts` at 1 line, `demoCompany.ts`/`siteUrl.ts` at 21 lines each)"), never actually read for content. It was never read for this - and it directly fits this pass's own "something the server treats as its own trusted value when it's really client-supplied" theme just as much as a redirect target does.

**The gap.** `siteUrl()`'s own header comment says it returns "this app's own public base URL" - but the implementation read the incoming HTTP request's `Host` header and, whenever present (which is true of essentially every real HTTP request, since `Host` is mandatory under HTTP/1.1), returned `https://<that value>` with **no validation at all** - never checked against any known-good value, not even a substring check. The `Host` header is exactly as attacker-controlled as a query parameter: any raw HTTP client can set it to anything. Confirmed directly, two ways: (1) a `vitest` unit test mocking `next/headers`' `headers().get("host")` to return `"evil.attacker.example"` made the pre-fix function return `"https://evil.attacker.example"` verbatim; (2) a real, live HTTP round-trip - started this repo's own real dev server (`npx next dev -p 3101`) with a small temporary scratch route (`app/app/scratchsiteurltest/route.ts`, removed before finishing, never committed) that calls the real, unmodified `siteUrl()` and returns its value - `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" http://localhost:3101/scratchsiteurltest` returned `https://evil.attacker.example`, a real HTTP response from a real running server, not a mock. The one real caller, `app/app/onboarding/actions.ts`'s welcome email (sent right after a new company is created), builds a clickable "Go to your dashboard" link from this value and emails it to the signed-up user.

Severity is genuinely low, stated plainly rather than inflated to match Finding 267's own "confirmed live cross-origin navigation" bar: (1) the one caller sends the resulting link only to the email address of the same user whose own request triggered it, with no token or other secret embedded in the URL, so there is no credential-leak/account-takeover path through this specific caller, unlike a classic password-reset-poisoning case; (2) whether an external attacker can actually get an arbitrary, unregistered `Host` value to reach this specific Next.js deployment in production depends on Vercel's own edge-routing behaviour, which was not independently confirmed from this sandbox (no outbound access to probe the real `tenderready.app`/`*.vercel.app` production routing, and spoofing `Host` locally against `npm run dev` is not the same guarantee as against Vercel's edge). What IS conclusively confirmed, not inferred, is that the function's own code, as written, applied zero validation and would act on whatever `Host` value reached it - a genuine mismatch between the function's own stated contract ("this app's own... URL") and what it actually computed, and a real inconsistency with how every OTHER email-link builder in this exact codebase already handles the identical need: `scripts/send-deadline-reminders.ts`/`send-discovered-tenders.ts`/`send-operational-alerts.ts` all read `process.env.APP_URL` (confirmed, not assumed - the PR #153 note already on record in this file's own `System-Status.md` history found that fallback itself briefly stale, but it's still an explicit trusted value, never a Host header); `lib/emailBrand.ts`'s own `layout()` default (`appUrl ?? "https://tenderready.app"`) and `scripts/render-email-samples.ts`/`lib/emailTemplateSamples.ts`'s own `APP_URL` constants are both the literal real production domain, confirmed via `grep -rn "tenderready.app" app` (10 real hits, all either the literal domain or an explicit env-var read - `siteUrl.ts` was the one file doing neither).

**Fix.** Added a small known-good-host allowlist (the real production domain `tenderready.app`/`www.tenderready.app` - confirmed as the real domain from the existing `scripts/render-email-samples.ts`/`lib/emailTemplateSamples.ts`/`lib/emailBrand.ts` constants already on record above, not a new guess - plus any `*.vercel.app` deployment, which legitimately covers the production alias and every preview deployment, and `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` for `npm run dev`) and validated the `Host` header against it before trusting it. An unrecognised `Host` now falls through to the function's own pre-existing `VERCEL_URL`/localhost fallback - the exact path this function already took when `Host` was absent - rather than ever being used verbatim. Confirmed the allowlist itself isn't a naive substring check that a crafted value like `"tenderready.app.evil.example"` or `"evilvercel.app"` could slip past (both correctly rejected - see verification below).

**Verified red-then-green against the real, unmodified function, twice over (mocked unit test AND a real live request).** New `lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` (10 cases: trusts the real production domain, trusts `www.`, trusts any `*.vercel.app` host, trusts `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` with a port, rejects a spoofed arbitrary host and falls back instead, rejects a host that merely CONTAINS the real domain as a substring (`"tenderready.app.evil.example"`), falls back to `VERCEL_URL` when the host is unrecognised (same path as when it's absent), and the two pre-existing absent-Host fallback behaviours unchanged). **Red (mocked unit test):** `npx vitest run lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` against the pre-fix code (`git stash` on just this one file, keeping the new test) - `3 failed | 7 passed` (the spoof-trusted case, the substring-bypass case, and the "falls back to VERCEL_URL when unrecognised" case, since pre-fix nothing was ever "unrecognised"). **Green:** after restoring the fix - `10/10 pass`. **Red/green again, live, with a real HTTP request against a real server, not a mock:** pre-fix, `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" http://localhost:3101/scratchsiteurltest` -> `https://evil.attacker.example`; post-fix, the identical request -> `http://localhost:3000` (the function's own existing no-`VERCEL_URL`-set fallback, correct, not a bug), while a request with `Host: tenderready.app` still correctly returns `https://tenderready.app`, and a plain same-origin request (curl's own default `Host: localhost:3101`) still correctly returns `http://localhost:3101` - confirming the fix doesn't narrow any legitimate case. Scratch route deleted and dev server stopped (confirmed via `ps aux`/`pkill`) before any commit; confirmed absent from `npx next build`'s own route table. Full regression: `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors - `.next/types` regenerated via a fresh `next build` after the scratch-route `.next` cache was cleared, so the one transient `LayoutProps`/stale-route-reference error seen mid-cleanup was a build-artifact staleness issue, not a real source error, and did not survive a clean rebuild), `npx eslint lib/siteUrl.ts lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` (0 errors/warnings), `npx vitest run` - **75 files, 603 tests, all pass** (up from 74/593 before this pass, exactly the one new file/10 new tests), `npx next build` (clean, full route table unchanged beyond the already-removed scratch route).

**Not escalated to a PR.** A pure-TypeScript, one-file fix (plus its own new test file) adding input validation to a function that already had a safe fallback path for the "no usable value" case - no RLS, no money path, no hard-stop gate, no worker-image change, no schema/migration. Not an authorization-bypass/tenant-isolation finding either (nothing here reads or mutates another tenant's data, or bypasses a server-side permission check - the one affected caller sends an email only to the account that triggered it, with no secret/token in the link). Same client-side/request-input-trust gap *class* as Findings 57/267, though materially lower severity/blast-radius than either (stated honestly above, not inflated to match their bar) - pushed directly to `main`, consistent with this track's own precedent for that class and severity tier.

**Backlog collision check.** `gh api repos/SarelJvR2024/tender-tool/pulls/<n>/files` for all 28 open PRs, grepping for `siteUrl`: zero hits - no open PR touches either changed file.

**Backlog/sibling status.** `git fetch origin main` immediately before committing and again immediately before pushing: both times still `d015dc4` (this pass's own starting point, Finding 267's docs commit) - no sibling-track (`session_01UMAzowxArab6cV4KurgXNE`) commit landed during this pass, so the push was a plain fast-forward.

To verify independently: `cd app && npx vitest run lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` (expect `10/10 pass`). Mock `next/headers`' `headers()` to return `{ get: () => "evil.attacker.example" }` and call `siteUrl()` directly - expect it to NOT return `"https://evil.attacker.example"`. Or, live: `npx next dev -p 3101`, create a one-line scratch route calling `siteUrl()`, `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" http://localhost:3101/<route>` - expect the function's own `VERCEL_URL`/localhost fallback, never the spoofed host verbatim (remember to delete the scratch route and stop the dev server afterward).

### Finding 269 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, same Host-header-trust class as Finding 268, but materially higher blast radius - `app/app/company/team/page.tsx` re-implemented the exact same unvalidated-Host-header pattern Finding 268 just fixed in `app/lib/siteUrl.ts`, inline, instead of calling it, and the resulting link carries a real, usable company-invite token rather than a tokenless welcome link)

**Area:** `app/app/company/team/page.tsx` (the "Pending invites" section's own invite-link text shown to a company admin, built from `${proto}://${host}/invite/${inv.token}`). No new test file - the fix removes the duplicated logic entirely in favour of calling `app/lib/siteUrl.ts`'s own already-fully-tested `siteUrl()` (10 cases, from Finding 268).

**How this was found.** This pass's own assigned task: follow up on Finding 268's open thread - "whether other request-derived values (`Origin`/`Referer` headers, etc.) are trusted as the server's own identity anywhere else in the app." Grepped every `headers().get(...)`/`.headers.get(...)` call across `app/` (excluding `node_modules`) for `origin`, `referer`, `x-forwarded-*`, `x-real-ip`, `host`, `request.ip` - two real hits outside `siteUrl.ts` itself: `app/app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts`'s `sourceIpLooksLikePayfast()` reads `x-forwarded-for` for a soft, non-decisive IP sanity check (read in full - it's the weakest of 4 PayFast ITN checks by the file's own design, explicitly non-blocking when the header is absent, and the money-affecting decision is gated by signature verification plus a live round-trip to PayFast's own `/eng/query/validate` endpoint requiring the literal response `"VALID"`, which can't be forged by spoofing a header - flagged as a standing recommendation below, not force-fixed, since it sits on a money path and whether to harden it depends on a judgment call about this app's actual Vercel/CDN topology that only Sarel can make); and a direct `h.get("host")` read in `app/app/company/team/page.tsx`, the one other place in the whole repo besides `siteUrl.ts` itself that reads the raw `host` header at all (confirmed exhaustively: `grep -rn '\.get(\"host\"\)' app` - excluding `node_modules` - returns exactly these two files, nothing else).

**The gap.** `team/page.tsx` (lines 69-72, pre-fix) read `headers().get("x-forwarded-proto")`/`headers().get("host")` directly and built `origin` from them with **zero validation** - the identical unvalidated-Host-header pattern Finding 268 fixed in `siteUrl.ts` just one pass ago, independently re-implemented inline in this file instead of calling that fix. Confirmed live, with a real spoofed-Host HTTP request against a real running dev server, that the exact code (copied verbatim into a temporary scratch route, removed before any commit) computes the spoofed value: `npx next dev -p 3102`, then `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" -H "X-Forwarded-Proto: https" http://localhost:3102/scratchteamorigin` returned `https://evil.attacker.example`, a real response from a real server, not a mock. This `origin` is then used at line 142 to build `` `${origin}/invite/${inv.token}` `` - the full invite link rendered in a read-only input for a company admin to copy and send to a prospective teammate. Confirmed `inv.token` is a real, bearer-style secret, not a cosmetic value: `app/app/invite/[token]/page.tsx`'s own `invite_preview`/`acceptInvite` flow grants company membership (as owner/admin/member/employee, per the invite's own stored role) to whoever visits `/invite/<token>` and accepts it - no other check gates that grant beyond the token itself matching an unexpired, unaccepted row.

**Severity, stated honestly, not inflated or understated.** The precondition is identical to, and no more confirmed than, Finding 268's own: whether an external attacker can get an arbitrary, unregistered `Host` value to actually reach this Next.js deployment in production depends on Vercel's own edge-routing behaviour, which this sandbox cannot independently probe (same open caveat, not re-litigated further here). What's different, and worth flagging plainly for Sarel's own risk read even though it doesn't change this pass's own push-vs-PR call (see below): IF that precondition ever holds, the blast radius here is materially worse than Finding 268's - the resulting link carries a real company-membership-granting token, not a tokenless "go to your dashboard" link, so an admin who copies a poisoned link and sends it on to a real invitee would be handing a real secret to whatever domain the spoofed `Host` put in its place, closer in kind (though still gated by the same unconfirmed Host-spoofing-in-production precondition) to a credential/token-leak path than Finding 268's own "email only ever reaches the same user who triggered it" case.

**Fix.** Removed the inline `headers()`/`x-forwarded-proto`/`host` read entirely and replaced it with a call to `app/lib/siteUrl.ts`'s own `siteUrl()` - the exact function Finding 268 already hardened with a known-good-host allowlist and gave full test coverage (10 cases). No new validation logic was written; this fix is purely "stop duplicating the pattern Finding 268 already fixed, and call the fixed version instead," which is also why no new test file was needed - `siteUrl()`'s own existing spec already covers every case this call site now depends on.

**Verified red-then-green against the real running server, not a mock, with the literal pre-fix and post-fix code.** Pre-fix (RED): a temporary scratch route (`app/app/scratchteamorigin/route.ts`, copied verbatim from `team/page.tsx`'s own 3 vulnerable lines, deleted before any commit) against a real `npx next dev -p 3102` - `curl http://localhost:3102/scratchteamorigin` (no spoofing) -> `http://localhost:3102` (correct, unexploited baseline); `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" ...` -> `http://evil.attacker.example`; `curl -H "Host: evil.attacker.example" -H "X-Forwarded-Proto: https" ...` -> `https://evil.attacker.example` (the exact exploitable string). ### Finding 270 (CONFIRMED AND FIXED ON `main` - moderate, a direct bypass of the Finding 268 fix, in the one file it exists to protect - `app/lib/siteUrl.ts`'s own Host-header allowlist checked only the text before a ":" but then returned the RAW, un-stripped header, letting a Host of the shape `"tenderready.app:@evil.attacker.example"` pass the allowlist while every real URL parser resolves it to `evil.attacker.example`)

**Area:** `app/lib/siteUrl.ts` (`siteUrl()`/`isKnownGoodHost()`, renamed `knownGoodHostAndPort()`). `app/lib/siteUrl.spec.ts` extended with 3 new cases (13 total, up from 10 added by Finding 268).

**How this was found.** This pass's own task brief asked to pursue the "duplicated logic that should reuse an already-hardened shared helper instead of its own inline copy" lead Findings 267-269 opened. Re-verified `safeRedirectPath()`'s 4 call sites (`auth/callback/route.ts`, `company/document-scan/actions.ts`, `signup/page.tsx`, `login/page.tsx`) - all 4 already call the shared helper, nothing bare-`startsWith("/")` left (`grep -rn "startsWith(\"/\")"` across `app/` returns only comment text citing the fix, no real re-implementation).
